This report closes the loop by solving the retarded integral equations directly, without passing through the local formulation, and comparing the result with the FDTD-ADE solution under the same physical and material conditions. The two independently implemented, structurally different numerical schemes agree within 0.02-1.3% for the reported reflected and transmitted energy fractions; the absorbed fraction, computed independently in both schemes from the Lorentz damping term rather than merely inferred from 1-R-T, agrees closely between the two methods, to the precision reported. Both solutions are also compared with an exact reference, the Airy formula weighted over the pulse spectrum: the direct solution reproduces it to within 0.3%, and its Richardson extrapolation to all digits shown. The agreement persists for a few-cycle pulse and for a sub-wavelength slab, where naive fixed-point iteration of the integral equations is not a practical convergent strategy. A complementary set of movie-style, nine-frame visualizations is also presented, illustrating the same equivalence directly in the field rather than only in integrated observables. To the author's knowledge, a direct numerical cross-validation of these two formulations in this genuinely time-dependent regime has not previously been reported.

articles.title: All-photonic millimeter-wave and terahertz signal core at room and cryogenic temperatures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Millimeter-wave and terahertz technologies offer new opportunities for high-capacity communications, sensing, and quantum systems, but electronic signal chains above 100 GHz are limited by weak sources, noisy receivers, and lossy interconnects. Photonic approaches mitigate these constraints by enabling chip-scale high-frequency components, yet existing implementations generally retain lossy off-chip electrical or free-space links, hindering dense and compact integration for cryogenic or space-constrained settings. Here, we show a monolithic lithium tantalate photonic chip, termed a signal core, which generates, modulates, routes, and detects continuous-wave signals at discrete frequencies between 100 GHz and 2.5 THz. The architecture integrates high-frequency functional modules on chip and uses exclusively fiber-based optical interfaces. Bidirectional coherent electro-optic conversion enables signal generation, detection, and nanosecond-scale amplitude and phase modulation, while micro-coplanar striplines interconnect the modules into an end-to-end signal chain on a single chip. Our modules achieve single-photon electro-optic coupling rates of g₀/2π=10 kHz and peak drive-power-normalized photon-flux conversion efficiencies of 1.0%/mW for generation and 0.5%/mW for detection. It also operates at 4 K in a dilution refrigerator through the same fiber-only optical links. Together, these capabilities establish an all-photonic platform for millimeter-wave-to-terahertz systems and offer a broadly applicable architecture for applications constrained by electrical-interconnect loss, heat load, and footprint.

articles.title: A Personal History in Quantum Foundations: an Oral History Interview
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This oral history interview provides Yakir Aharonov's personal and conceptual recollections from the 1950s to the 2000s, focusing on his academic trajectory, some of his major contributions to quantum foundations, and his perspective on the development of the field. The interview traces Aharonov's academic career through the Technion, University of Bristol, Brandeis University, Yeshiva University, University of South Carolina, Tel Aviv University, George Mason University, and Chapman University. The interview also traces the development of Aharonov's work and collaborations on the EPR paradox, time-energy uncertainty relations, quantum measurement theory, quantum frames of reference, the two-state vector formalism, weak values, protective measurements, and several other contributions. It includes recollections of meetings and discussions with David Bohm, Niels Bohr, John Clauser, Paul Dirac, Rudolf Peierls, Aage Petersen, and Abner Shimony. Also mentioned: David Albert, Jeeva Anandan, Peter Bergmann, Gideon Carmi, Avshalom Elitzur, Dave Finkelstein, Vladimir Fock, Itzhak Kalugai, Ed Lerner, Joel Lebowitz, Stanley Mandelstam, Yuval Ne'eman, Sandu Popescu, Maurice Pryce, Daniel Rohrlich, Nathan Rosen, Joseph Safko, Paul Singer, Daniele Struppa, Leonard Susskind, Lev Vaidman, Chien-Shiung Wu.

articles.title: Shaping Near Fields of Photonic Modes into Topological Textures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31207v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topological textures of light, such as optical vortices and skyrmions, are attractive for high-density information encoding and light-matter interactions. In the near field, topologies have primarily been realized using polaritonic platforms that inherently tie the platform to the material dispersion, limiting their footprint due to propagation losses and restricting their operating spectral region. Here, we introduce a route to shape near-field topologies through the geometric engineering of a dielectric metasurface supporting a quasi-bound state in the continuum resonance, without the need for polaritonic surface waves. In-plane deformation of our metasurface bars conserves their resonance-driven near-fields locally, so that the metasurface geometry and the polarization of the illuminating light dictate the generated topology. By shaping silicon unit cells into geometries with rotational symmetry, we create optical topologies with controllable topological charge. Using phase-resolved scattering-type near-field optical microscopy, we experimentally characterize high-purity resonance-locked topologies such as vortices in concentric rings and topological charge doublets in Archimedean spirals. In contrast to conventional topological textures, our purely photonic mode-based field textures are stationary standing waves in the radial direction, without relying on surface-wave propagation or polaritonic dispersion, establishing a spectrally and spatially scalable platform for near-field topological photonics.

articles.title: Quartz Crystal Microbalance impedance of discrete adsorbates with lubricated contact
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31220v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a thorough theoretical investigation of the shear force exerted on a horizontal plate undergoing fast (MHz range) longitudinal oscillations in presence of a spherical particle suspended in the liquid at close proximity to the plate. This hydrodynamic problem is relevant toward the analysis of frequency response (i.e., complex impedance) of Quartz Crystal Microbalance (QCM) to discrete (particulate) adsorbates. For low areal density of adsorbates, the contributions of individual particles remain additive, rendering the theory applicable towards quantitative interpretation of the experimental measurements. For adsorbates much smaller than the viscous penetration depth, the closed-form analytical expressions for the complex impedance were derived for particles of arbitrary density, assuming a lubricated contact (i.e., non-localized adsorption). The theoretical predictions were shown to be in an excellent agreement with accurate Finite Element numerical computations. The validity of the theoretical approach was confirmed by QCM measurements conducted for polystyrene nanoparticles in a broad range of sizes, from 32 nm to 510 nm, adsorbing onto gold/silica sensor upon varying the oscillation frequency.

articles.title: Cleaner air strengthens the Pacific trade winds without a detectable change in El Nino
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31236v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Air quality policy will cut aerosol and ozone precursor emissions, and studies disagree on how the tropical Pacific circulation and the El Nino Southern Oscillation (ENSO) will respond. Here we show, in 12 Earth system models with and without air quality controls, that the cuts strengthen the Pacific trade winds and offset half to two thirds of the weakening projected without them. The response is absent with prescribed sea surface temperatures and detectable only after 2040. It is consistent with the Indian Ocean warming relative to the Pacific, which also ranks the responses to cuts made region by region. ENSO amplitude changes by less than a tenth of its value, the smallest change this ensemble could detect. The change implied by the mean state shift is a sixth of that, and an ENSO model trained without the reduced emission runs predicts none. El Nino's regional impacts still change, because the background climate does.

articles.title: Second- and third-order nonlinearities in silicon nitride waveguides via heterogeneous integration of lithium niobate membranes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thick, dispersion-engineered silicon nitride is a leading platform for integrated third-order nonlinear optics, supporting supercontinuum and frequency comb generation. However, it lacks the second-order nonlinearity required by many applications. Here we bond pre-fabricated x-cut thin-film lithium niobate membranes onto finished silicon nitride waveguides as a back-end step, compatible with commercially fabricated waveguides. A single silicon nitride waveguide generates an octave-spanning supercontinuum and, through the lithium niobate membrane, concurrent second-harmonic, sum- and difference-frequency generation. These results open new possibilities for thick silicon nitride photonics, from visible light generation to on-chip f-2f comb self-referencing, a key step towards miniaturised timing and navigation quantum technologies.

articles.title: Multireference Polarizable Embedding for Core-Level Spectroscopy in Aqueous Solution: XPS and XAS of Glycine
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31400v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Core-level spectra in solution are governed by the interplay of core-hole relaxation, electron correlation, specific solute--solvent interactions, and environmental polarization. We report the first application of RASSCF--RASPT2 combined with the fluctuating-charges polarizable embedding to X-ray photoelectron (XPS) and X-ray absorption (XAS) spectroscopy in aqueous solution. The protocol couples a multireference treatment of core-ionized and core-excited states with molecular-dynamics sampling, and is assessed for the carbon and nitrogen K-edges of glycine in the gas phase and in water. The calculated spectra are compared with experiment and with fixed-charges electrostatic embedding. Gas-phase ionization and absorption features are accurately reproduced. In solution, configurational averaging captures inhomogeneous broadening, while XPS peak positions, relative intensities, and widths depend strongly on the solvent parametrization. The best-performing polarizable model improves the spectral profile, although aqueous ionization energies remain overestimated. For XAS, the carbon K-edge is reproduced close to the experimental energy scale, whereas the nitrogen K-edge line shape is recovered after rigid alignment. These results support multireference polarizable embedding as a promising framework for core-level spectroscopy in solution.

articles.title: Modelling wide-swath altimeter observation-error correlations with a regularised diffusion operator
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31409v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Unaccounted-for observation-error correlations have long been known to be detrimental to the quality of atmospheric and ocean analyses produced by data assimilation (DA) systems. While progress has been made over the past decade on modelling inter-channel error correlations, modelling spatial error correlations remains a challenge for large datasets. Common strategies for mitigating the harmful effects of spatial error correlations, such as variance inflation or data thinning, prevent the extraction of valuable small-scale information from the observations. With the emergence of new sources of high-resolution observations, such as those from the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) wide-swath altimeter, the need to address this limitation of DA systems has become increasingly pressing. To do so, we consider a diffusion-based observation-error correlation operator, extending previous work on modelling correlated errors in conventional nadir altimeter data. When observation-error correlation length scales are large, the original method can suffer from an excessive sensitivity of the inverse correlation operator to small-scale perturbations. Since actual estimates of observation-error correlations from SWOT suggest the presence of large length scales, a more robust formulation of the method is required. We present a regularised formulation of the diffusion-based correlation operator that eliminates this excessive sensitivity while preserving computational efficiency. We describe the implementation of the operator for a mesh constructed from SWOT observation locations and demonstrate its application in a global ocean DA system. To validate the new formulation, we perform DA experiments with simulated SWOT observations. These experiments confirm that the regularised correlation operator provides an effective, robust and practical approach for representing wide-swath altimeter observation-error correlations in operational ocean DA systems.

articles.title: Analytical Modeling of Modulated Heating for Three-Dimensional Anisotropic Optical Thermometry of Multilayered Cylinders
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thermally relevant cylindrical geometries are used in a plethora of applications with thermal property differences depending significantly on material complexity. Manu- facturing processes also induce substantial anisotropy ratios resulting in directionally dependent thermal transport. However, for cylindrical specimens, current thermal metrology resolves only isotropic thermal properties, assumes perfect thermal inter- faces, and offers no formulation for temperature spatial dependence. In this work, we present an analytical framework that models the frequency dependent thermal transport of orthotropic arbitrary layered cylinders to be used as a forward model for existing optical thermometry techniques. This formulation captures the effects of non-negligible thermal boundary conductance and offers the first closed-form solution of a projected Gaussian laser, a common form of heating in thermal metrology, hav- ing a finite elliptic spot size on a curved surface. The novel anisotropic cylindrical model was compared with literature derivations involving two-dimensional isotropic transport for cylinders by applying simplifying assumptions. For single- and two- layerisotropicsamples, thethree-dimensionalmodelagreedwithestablishedsolutions with negligible error, while predictions for orthotropic multilayer samples agreed with finite-element simulations within 1.5% across a range of material properties and laser geometries. Comparison with anisotropic planar models identified conditions under which a planar approximation can reduce computation time. These results estab- lish the first forward model for noncontact characterization of anisotropic thermal properties in arbitrarily layered cylinders.

articles.title: Unifying Time-Independent and Time-Dependent Franck--Condon Pictures in Quantum Mechanochemistry via the Linear Coupling Approximation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31426v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum chemistry has achieved impressive results in modeling and interpreting mechanochemical transformations at the molecular level. An essential question, the time profile of force application, has however attracted less attention. Here, the Franck--Condon theory of quantum mechanochemistry, previously formulated for the sudden-force limit, is generalized to arbitrary time-dependent force profiles using the linear-coupling approximation. Solving the driven harmonic oscillator yields a closed-form, time-dependent effective Huang--Rhys factor: a natural measure of vibrational excitations upon force application. It is governed by the Fourier transform of the force derivative and recovers the sudden- and fixed-force limits. At the conceptual level, this linear coupling picture links mechanochemistry to vibronic spectroscopy and Marcus electron theory. For a shock-front force ramp, vibrational excitation is shown to be suppressed in frequency, only low-frequency modes being excited under realistic laser-shock-peening conditions.

articles.title: Nanopillar metasurfaces uniting high optical reflectivity with ultracoherent nanomechanics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31452v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mechanically compliant mirrors are key components in cavity optomechanics. However, the requirements to achieve the best optical and mechanical performance are usually in direct competition. A high reflectivity for tightly focused beams entails thick reflectors, whereas ultracoherent flexural nanomechanics necessitates thin membranes. We eliminate this trade-off by introducing high-refractive-index nanopillar metasurfaces on top of a thin membrane. We pattern a 50 micrometer-diameter array of nanopillars to form a photonic crystal. The flat band behavior of guided resonances in the photonic crystal enables a reflectivity of 99.82(1)% for a tightly focused beam of 7 micrometer waist. The combination of two guided resonances creates a 100 nanometer-wide high-reflectivity band around 1550 nanometer. Simultaneously, the nanopillar patterning realizes a density-modulated phononic crystal that isolates an ultracoherent localized mechanical mode with a Q· f-product of 2· 10¹⁴Hz. The demonstrated nanopillar metasurfaces enable lightweight mirrors for room-temperature quantum optomechanics and for use as levitated mirrors or lightsails.

articles.title: Bridge change-of-measure for propagator estimation of diffusions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30213v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The propagator of one-dimensional diffusions has relevant applications in statistical inference and across many disciplines. Yet it is obtained in closed form only for very few simple models. Here we analyze an importance sampling strategy based on a bridge change of measure to estimate propagators: paths are generated under an auxiliary diffusion whose bridge between the two fixed boundary points is easy to generate, and the target propagator is recovered through a Radon-Nikodym derivative or likelihood ratio correction derived from Girsanov's theorem. This method overcomes the main limitations of the crude Monte Carlo estimator, which relies on binning in state space, introducing bias and becoming inefficient with rare transitions. We apply the method to a range of benchmark processes and show that the bridge-based estimator matches the accuracy of crude Monte Carlo with orders of magnitude fewer sample paths. Finally, we elaborate on discretization schemes for the Radon-Nikodym derivative and on approximations to the best-in-class change of measure, both of which increase the efficiency of the method.

articles.title: Entanglement certification of attosecond light fields with photoelectron interferometry
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31187v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The emergence of entangled quantum optical states in high-harmonic generation raises a fundamental problem about its characterization, namely, how can entanglement of extreme-ultraviolet radiation be certified for attosecond light fields? Here, we provide experimentally accessible separability tests, particularly showing that attosecond photoelectron interferometry provides a direct solution to this problem. This is achieved by a quantum optical treatment of mapping photoelectron interferometry to the measurement of optical correlation functions. This yields a negative-partial-transpose witness for infrared-XUV entanglement and a sufficient witness of genuine multipartite entanglement without auxiliary optical measurements. We evaluate both witnesses on explicit optical states and identify how the protocol can be extended to XUV-XUV entanglement certification. Hence, we establish attosecond photoelectron interferometry as a general framework for entanglement certification across a wide range of optical frequencies.

articles.title: Fixed-Dimensional Latent Flow for Generating Variable-Size 3D Molecules
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.08333v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Molecular size is intrinsically linked to composition, structure, and properties, but most 3D molecular generators treat size as a predefined input rather than a quantity to be generated. We introduce Equivariant-Free Transformer-Autoencoded Latent Flow Matching, a two-stage framework that samples a fixed-dimensional latent vector using flow matching and employs an autoregressive Transformer to determine molecular size, atom types, coordinates, and chemical attributes. Canonical atom ordering and rigid-pose alignment enable Transformers without equivariant layers, while decoded attributes guide bond reconstruction. On PCQM4Mv2, unconditional generation yields 87.9% unique and novel molecules passing sanitization and PoseBusters checks, exceeding baselines with lower end-to-end training and sampling time and higher end-to-end throughput. Across ten target HOMO-LUMO gaps, internal ranking retains 30% of the screened candidates and increases the density functional theory-verified hit rate within 0.1 eV of the target from 25.0% to 52.4%, while largely preserving novelty and diversity. These results demonstrate fixed-dimensional latent generation with autoregressive decoding as a practical approach to molecular design without prespecifying size.

articles.title: Near Chemical Accuracy From Size-Consistent Padé Resummed Møller-Plesset Perturbation Theory
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.25330v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Padé resummation of the correlation energy from Møller-Plesset (MP) perturbation theory is not size-consistent and is therefore seldom used. We present an orbital-based Padé resummation of the MP2 and MP3 self-energy operators, whose trace yields a size-consistent correlation energy. We find that damping the third-order same-spin contribution leads to substantially increased accuracy, with the resulting same-spin damped orbital Padé resummed (SSD-OPMP3) approach attaining near-chemical accuracy (mean absolute error sim 1 kcal/mol) for total atomization energies of non-multireference molecules in the W4-17 dataset against the gold standard CCSD(T) method. Excellent performance surpassing CCSD is also obtained for other molecular datasets such as those containing barrier heights, noncovalent interactions, dipole moments, static polarizabilities, and transition-metal chemistry. SSD-OPMP3 is thus a highly accurate electronic structure method with the same noniterative O(N⁶) cost as MP3, filling a gap in the cost/accuracy hierarchy of wavefunction methods.

articles.title: Enhanced Whispering Gallery Mode Phase Shift using Indistinguishable Photon Pairs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2404.17409v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a theoretical investigation of a whispering gallery mode (WGM) resonator coupled to a Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) and show a bimodal coincidence transmission spectrum when the input state is an indistinguishable photon pair. This is due to the doubled WGM phase shift experienced by the path-entangled state in the interferometer. Further, we model the noise in a WGM resonance shift measurement comparing photon pairs with a coherent state. At least a four-fold improvement in the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is possible, with clear implications for quantum-enhanced WGM sensing.

articles.title: RiboBridge: protein-conditioned de novo RNA binder structure design
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30668v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Designing RNA molecules that bind to target protein structures requires generating both an RNA conformation and its bound complex geometry, without assuming a predefined binding site. Existing approaches generally model these coupled processes within a unified representation, entangling RNA conformation generation with protein-relative placement. In this work, we introduce RiboBridge, a structure-first framework that separates RNA conformational generation from protein--RNA assembly through cross-frame interaction geometry. RiboBridge first proposes multiple candidate RNA-binding interfaces on the protein surface, generates canonical RNA conformations within a pretrained RNA structural latent space (RiboSphere), and then predicts protein--RNA interaction constraints to bridge the independently defined RNA and protein coordinate frames. The resulting interaction geometry is converted into a geometrically consistent protein-relative pose through rigid placement. We evaluate RiboBridge on a temporally split, sequence-filtered, and redundancy-controlled benchmark of 124 protein--RNA complexes. Under post-hoc interface-correspondence evaluation, where native information is used only after generation to select among already generated predicted-pocket candidates, RiboBridge achieves the highest fNAT and DockQ and the lowest interface and ligand RMSDs among compared methods. Component ablations and stage-wise diagnostics further characterize the contributions of RNA conformational generation, interaction prediction, and rigid placement, identifying the main sources of complex-recovery error.

articles.title: XALIGN: A Human-centric Visual Analytics Approach to Understanding AI Explanations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31015v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Explainable AI (XAI) methods are usually evaluated for technical properties such as faithfulness and robustness. In high-stakes application domains, experts also need to check model predictions against established knowledge. Different explanation methods often disagree, and this disagreement is hard to see when each method is inspected separately. We propose XALIGN, a visual analytics workflow and interface that shows rule-based explanations and several feature attribution methods (TreeSHAP, KernelSHAP, and LIME) side by side for the same Random Forest model. Agreements and contradictions between the methods become visible signals that users can explore and compare with domain knowledge. We apply XALIGN in two case studies: the German Credit dataset and a meteorological dataset, in which events derived from ICON model output and Cloudnet observations are classified. In both, the views reveal discrepancies between the rule-based explanation and the attribution methods that a single method would not show. In an expert evaluation with three specialists, participants found XALIGN useful for identifying influential features and for avoiding over-trust in predictions. Linking rules to attributions was harder for the participant without an XAI background.

articles.title: Harmful Responses Are Jailbreak Templates: Transferring Autoregressive Jailbreaks to Diffusion Language Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31331v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) enable flexible masked generation through bidirectional context modeling, but this capability also introduces a distinct jailbreak attack surface. We find that a harmful response to a given query naturally serves as an effective jailbreak template: simply masking a subset of its tokens can induce a dLLM to reconstruct harmful content. Based on this observation, we propose RMT-Jailbreak, a general framework that transfers existing autoregressive (AR) jailbreak attacks to dLLMs through their induced harmful responses. RMT-Jailbreak converts an AR-generated harmful response into a high-mask-ratio template using uniform token retention, and further applies prompt-based safety filtering to mask any remaining visible harmful content. The refined template is then provided to the target dLLM for bidirectional reconstruction. Extensive experiments across multiple AR jailbreak methods and target dLLMs demonstrate the effectiveness and generality of RMT-Jailbreak, revealing strong cross-paradigm transferability of jailbreak attacks.

articles.title: SQuAT: Spherical Lattice Vector Quantization-Aware Training
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31412v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vector quantization (VQ), in particular lattice-based methods, offer strong rate-distortion trade-offs for low-bit large language models (LLMs), yet their behavior under quantization-aware training (VQ-QAT) remains poorly understood. We scale lattice VQ-QAT to billion-parameter LLMs and multi-billion-token training regimes, and introduce SQuAT, a shape-gain VQ-QAT approach trained with a separate straight-through estimator (STE) for the shape and gain. SQuAT decomposes weights into direction and magnitude: normalized directions are quantized using an E₈-derived spherical codebook, while gains are quantized independently with low-bit scalar quantizers. We show that, unlike a standard STE applied to the full quantizer, which ignores the shape-gain structure, these separate STEs induce tangent-space updates for directions, yielding an implicit form of spherical (Riemannian) optimization. To enable scalability, we develop a distributed exact nearest-neighbor assignment scheme, in which workers quantize disjoint weight blocks and communicate only discrete indices, reducing VQ-QAT training time by 12.8× and allowing us to scale it to 10B tokens. Across instruction-tuned LLaMA-3.2-1B/3B, Qwen3-4B, and base Qwen3-1.7B, SQuAT consistently outperforms standard VQ-QAT STE under identical quantizers and initialization, and achieves SOTA VQ-QAT accuracy.
authors: Tycho F. A. van der Ouderaa

articles.title: Why Constrained Updates Still Forget: A Functional-Path Analysis of Continual SFT
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30191v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Supervised fine-tuning adapts language models to specialized tasks but can disrupt previously acquired behavior. Existing approaches constrain parameters, gradients, or replay objectives, yet the connection between the protected object, the intervening trajectory, and retained outputs remains unclear. We develop a functional-path account that decomposes old-loss changes along realized updates into the controlled direction, gradient staleness, probe mismatch, and finite-step effects. The account yields a conditional refresh budget and identifies the restoring direction supplied by informative replay. Matched QLoRA interventions separate constraint granularity from placement before or after Adam: placement strongly affects retention across the studied code-label audits, whereas the granularity interaction depends on the endpoint. Checkpointed generation separates endpoint recovery from higher sampled-path accuracy, and matched replay schedules reveal loss exposure concealed by final scores. A sequential-task comparison extends this distinction to backward transfer: subspace regularization and projection improve average retention while trading off different old tasks; supervised replay protects both more consistently in this setting. Additional response interfaces distinguish content gains from exact-response retention. These findings connect update-level protection to task-wise behavior and motivate mitigation through explicit functional anchors, trajectory evaluation, and joint old/new auditing.

articles.title: Vision Transformers for Estimating Irradiance Using Data Scarce Sky Images
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30940v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Accurate estimation of diffuse horizontal irradiance (DHI) is critical for optimising photovoltaic system performance and energy forecasting yet remains challenging in regions lacking comprehensive ground-based instrumentation. Recent advancements using Vision Transformers (ViTs) trained on extensive sky image datasets have shown promise in replacing costly irradiance measurement equipment, but the scarcity of long-term, high-quality sky imagery significantly restricts practical implementation. Addressing this critical gap, this study proposes a novel dual-framework approach designed for data-scarce scenarios. First, calculated atmospheric parameters, including extraterrestrial irradiance and cyclic time encodings, are integrated to represent sky conditions without utilising any instrumentation. Next, a sequential pipeline initially predicts synthetic global horizontal irradiance (GHI) and uses it as a feature, to refine DHI estimation. Finally, a dual-parallel architecture simultaneously processes raw and overlay-enhanced fisheye sky images. Overlays are generated through unsupervised, physics-informed cloud segmentation to highlight dynamic sky features. Empirical validation is performed using data from the Chilbolton Observatory, chosen for its temperate climate and frequent cloud variability. To simulate data-scarce conditions, models are trained on a single month (e.g., January) and evaluated across a temporally disjoint, full-year test set. Under this setup, the sequential and dual-parallel frameworks achieve RMSE values within 2-3 W/m² and 1-6 W/m², respectively, of a state-of-the-art ViT trained on the complete dataset. By combining physics-informed modelling with unsupervised segmentation, the proposed method provides a scalable and cost-effective solution for DHI estimation, advancing solar resource assessment in data-constrained environments.

articles.title: Prompt Sensitivity in Tool-Augmented Model Comparisons
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31148v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Language models are compared on question-answering benchmarks that pose each question in one wording, and a reworded question can change which of two models scores higher. We ask whether giving the models tools makes such comparisons more stable. An accuracy gain cannot answer this, because tools change several steps between the question and the scored answer at once. We propose a matched protocol that separates those steps: the answer readout, reasoning, the decision to call, the tool's answer, and the report supplied without a call. We apply it to six open models in five domains under five wordings. We find that tools raise accuracy where a program answers the question and widen the wording sensitivity of many pairwise comparisons. The widening follows how often a model calls, and call frequency follows the wording for some models and not others. It also depends on the interface and the instructions: a native tool-calling interface and a second tool description leave no detected widening in molecules, and sensitivity persists where tools return intermediate results. These findings show that deterministic reports do not guarantee stable comparisons. We recommend reporting call frequency and comparison stability under several wordings beside accuracy.

articles.title: AfterDeleteBench: Auditing Post-Deletion Information Persistence in LLM Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31366v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many LLM agents maintain external persistent memory and derive additional state from past interactions, such as summaries. Deleting an original memory record therefore need not remove information carried by its descendants. We introduce AfterDeleteBench, a controlled behavioral audit for this failure mode in fixed-weight LLM agents. For each synthetic secret, we compare an exposed-then-deleted agent with an otherwise matched agent that was never exposed to the secret, allowing post-deletion recovery to be attributed to the original exposure. In our primary setting, a single query recovers the deleted secret from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct in roughly two thirds of cases, while matched never-exposed controls have zero recovery. Crucially, recovery does not require a surviving verbatim copy: when the complete secret string is absent and only separately stored components remain under a public composition rule, exact reconstruction succeeds in 62-99% of cases across Qwen, Mistral, and Phi-3. We also show that the response interface is part of the measurement system: target-bearing replies can be scored as failures when the requested format and parser are misaligned. Finally, we separate reconstruction from write-back and fresh-session recall. Provenance-aware closure eliminates observed recovery in the tested positive-baseline settings, whereas an exact-literal write filter blocks reinsertion but cannot erase information already present. Together, these results show that source deletion should be evaluated behaviorally at the level of the agent and its memory system, not only as a storage operation.

articles.title: MCP vs CLI for AI Agents: A Comparative Analysis of Tool Integration Strategies for Autonomous Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30157v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents require interfaces to interact with external systems such as files, APIs, databases, and cloud services. Two competing paradigms have emerged: CLI (Command Line Interface), where agents execute shell commands directly, and MCP (Model Context Protocol), a structured JSON-RPC protocol providing governed, typed tool access. This paper presents a comparative analysis across 14 evaluation dimensions, supported by worked examples, security assessment against established compliance frameworks, and economic modeling. Our analysis indicates that CLI provides superior efficiency for single-user, local-only workflows, while MCP addresses requirements that CLI fundamentally cannot satisfy, including fine-grained access control, credential isolation, structured audit, and multi-tenant governance. We further examine how progressive disclosure techniques eliminate MCP's historical weakness (context window overhead), yielding token efficiency comparable to CLI while preserving its architectural benefits. A hybrid architecture is recommended for production systems. This analysis draws upon academic, government, and industry sources including NSA formal guidance (CSI U/OO/6030316-26), OWASP security standards, and economic modeling from BCG and Gartner.

articles.title: Feedback That Backfires in Games: Do LLM Players Repeat the Move They Just Watched Fail?
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30205v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When an LLM agent's move fails, the harness writes the move and the failure message into the transcript and asks again. In tool calling, this record makes small models more likely to repeat the failed action. We test whether the same holds in games (Sokoban, Connect Four, Othello), where a move can fail by being illegal or by being legal but losing, both verified exactly. On fixed probe items built by perturbing a correct move, the record backfires: pooled over 8 instruction-tuned models (135M-1.7B) it makes the failed move more likely (corrective gain G = -1.38 nats per token), through the move's surface form, for illegal moves but not for losing ones, and not for every model. An exploratory analysis shows what sets the sign: after the record, the failed move's log-probability barely depends on how likely it was before (slope 0.18). Moves the model would not have played become more likely, and greedy decoding starts to produce them; moves it was about to play become less likely, but greedy decoding still repeats 38% of them. A description of the failure that omits the move string keeps the model's preference instead. Along the OLMo 2 1B post-training ladder the inversion is present in the base model and largely removed at the DPO stage. RAGEN's default models invert in RAGEN's own Sokoban format before any RL. A "do not repeat" instruction does nothing, a clean retry is the worst harness, and a decoder ban stops exact repeats but not illegal play. All measurements ran in float32 on a free Colab GPU, which first reproduced the original paper's number.

articles.title: Faithful Latent Harm Monitors Work No Better Than the Models Own Behaviour at a Matched False Alarm Rate
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30727v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models have been reported to encode the harmfulness of a request separately from their decision to refuse it, and latent safety monitors such as Latent Guard build on this report by classifying prompts as harmful from the internal activations of the model, with the aim of catching harmful intent even when the model complies. Whether these representations give a signal of harm that survives distribution shift and is independent of model behaviour is unclear. We test this on out-of-distribution prompts made by rewriting existing harmful and benign requests with surface rewording, persuasive framing and jailbreak-style wrappers. Across 15 instruction-tuned LLMs and 38 activation-based readers, we compare harm detection with that of TF-IDF and sentence-embedding classifiers, with independently trained safety classifiers, and with the refusal of each model. Activations are read at the last token of the user instruction, where the model has read the whole request, and at the last chat-template token before the reply, where the planned response can be represented. Because models disagree about which prompts to refuse, we can separate a signal of the harmfulness of the prompt from a signal of the refusal decision of the model. At the end of the instruction, the representation is largely independent of the refusal behaviour of each model but degrades under distribution shift, so that a TF-IDF classifier ranks harm better than the original Latent Guard in every model we test, and linear and MLP probes do about as well as sentence-embedding classifiers trained on the same examples. The representation just before generation detects more, catching 44 percent of harmful prompts at a matched false-alarm rate against 32 percent for the refusal of the model, but that gain follows the refusal decision itself, and part of it comes from refusals that string-matching evaluation misses.

articles.title: Subgoal-aware Memory Graph for GUI Agent
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31307v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: GUI agents aim to automate complex user tasks by interacting with mobile interfaces, but ef- fective decision-making in long-horizon set- tings requires reusing prior experience rather than relying solely on the environment ob- servations. Existing memory-based methods typically store experience either at the single- action level or as entire trajectories. Single- step actions are often too fine-grained to carry meaningful semantics, since the success of an individual action does not necessarily imply progress towards the overall goal. In contrast, whole trajectories are often too coarse-grained and difficult to reuse across different tasks. We propose a subgoal-aware memory graph that distils past trajectories into structured, reusable evidence at the level of subgoals. We define a subgoal as consecutive actions shar- ing a single intent, the granularity at which progress toward the task becomes meaning- ful. To reduce redundancy and support cross- task reuse, we organise subgoal experiences as nodes in a graph, where related memories can be merged, extended, and retrieved based on the environment observation. On SPA-Bench, our method improves success rate by 11.11% over the baseline.

articles.title: MemPlan: Memory-Conditioned PDDL Planning for Partially Observable Text Environments
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30379v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM agents are flexible in language interaction, but using them as long-horizon planners is costly and prone to hallucinated or invalid actions. This paper targets a different role for LLMs: constrained bridges between language and symbolic planning. We propose MemPlan, a memory-conditioned PDDL planning framework for partially observable interactive text environments. MemPlan keeps the PDDL domain fixed and reconstructs the PDDL problem at each step from parsed observations, candidate hypotheses, and interaction memory. Positive graph memory assigns relevance-based action costs to candidate hypotheses for missing objects, locations, or conditions, guiding the planner toward more plausible checks. Negative memory records execution-refuted assumptions and compiles them into exclusion constraints, preventing repeated attempts at candidates already contradicted by feedback. A unified schema-conditioned language--symbol interface, trained offline with supervised fine-tuning, connects text environments to the planning loop through observation-to-fact parsing and symbolic-action-to-command grounding. Experiments on TextWorld, ALFWorld, and Robotouille show that MemPlan improves task completion and step efficiency over language-only and PDDL-aware baselines, while substantially reducing online token cost compared with LLM-planning baselines such as ReAct. The same fine-tuned interface is also reused across TextWorld task types without task-specific fine-tuning. Our code and data are available at: https://github.com/tewiSong/MemPlan.

articles.title: Multi-Tool Selection for Robotic Systems: Comparing Semantic Retrieval and LLM
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31013v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Natural-language interfaces allow users to command robotic systems without interacting directly with mission planners or robotics middleware. Their reliable use depends on robot tool routing, defined here as the selection of the smallest complete subset of predefined executable capabilities required to satisfy a request. This task is particularly difficult for compound instructions, where incomplete selection may omit necessary sensing or monitoring capabilities, while excessive selection may expose irrelevant tools. We compare four routing strategies: three progressively refined ChromaDB-based methods - fixed-threshold retrieval, relative-distance retrieval, and clause-aware aggregated retrieval - and a cloud-hosted 120-billion-parameter language-model baseline. The methods are evaluated on 164 manually annotated prompts organised into three complexity levels, from direct single-tool requests to compound requests requiring at least three tools. Using exact-match accuracy, completeness, precision, a completeness-weighted composite score, and routing latency, CDB-v3 achieves the best macro-average score among the retrieval-only methods, with 0.7822, compared with 0.8869 for the large-model baseline. Although the LLM provides higher routing quality, CDB-v3 exhibits substantially lower latency and can be deployed locally without requiring cloud connectivity. These results identify a quality-latency trade-off between direct large-model selection and clause-aware semantic retrieval for privacy-sensitive, connectivity-constrained, and resource-constrained robotic systems.

articles.title: Harm Is Behavioural, Moderation Is Lexical: How Language and Culture Decide Whom Automated Safety Systems Protect and Whom They Silence
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31047v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Content warning: this paper quotes slurs and hateful statements from published test suites; the racial slur among them is masked. Automated systems decide at scale which messages are harmful, and they decide unevenly. Classifiers label African American English as offensive up to twice as often as other English, the accounts of prominent drag queens can score as more toxic than those of white nationalists, and safety behaviour that holds in English collapses in low-resource languages. We argue that over-flagging and under-protection share one cause: deciding harm from vocabulary and surface form rather than from what a message does. We organise the evidence into seven failure modes and argue, as testable hypotheses, that harmful behaviours (a request for secrecy, a demand for payment, an attempt to isolate someone) travel across languages better than the words that express them. We propose an evaluation protocol that makes the gap between the best- and worst-served language communities a headline result, and show that the naive gap is inflated under equal service and that its usual bootstrap interval is unreliable. Applied to five open systems in eleven languages, from a keyword lexicon to two current multilingual guard models, the protocol finds that none reaches native-speaker accuracy at separating harmful function from harmless form (51 of 55 system-language pairs fall short); that greater capability raises discrimination in nine languages while leaving Arabic and romanised Hindi near chance, so the gap between the best- and worst-served languages grows with capability; that one system both over-flags and under-protects the same language most; and that a language a system reads worst can look the most fairly treated when only false positives are reported.

articles.title: CoWriter: Guiding Methodological and Synergetic Human-LLM Co-Authoring
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31277v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While LLMs have transformed text generation, standard chat-and-canvas interfaces often reduce human authoring to quite passive supervision, causing review fatigue, over-reliance on AI, and the sidelining of the human role in long-form, source-grounded writing. Prior systems typically address isolated writing phases, leaving comprehensive end-to-end human-LLM collaboration largely unexplored. In this paper, we introduce CoWriter, a proactive agentic scheme that adapts expert human (co-)authoring methodologies from cognitive science to flexibly steer the entire writing workflow while actively encouraging the user to engage. In an exploratory user study, compared to a standard LLM baseline, authors using CoWriter better expressed their perspectives and maintained a higher sense of document ownership, supported quantitatively by 2.2× more successful agent engagements. Furthermore, external reader judges rated the resulting texts higher in "human touch" qualities like storytelling and integrating unique personal experiences. Overall, our results demonstrate that proactively engaging users through established human practices is beneficial for effective LLM-supported co-authoring, providing useful methodologies, techniques and insights for future research on collaborative agents.

articles.title: Trapped in a Soundproof Box: How CO2 Levels Influence Speech Quality Assessment and Response Behaviour
articles.abstract: Standardised tests to assess speech quality, such as the listening tests of Recommendation P.800 of the International Telecommunication Union Telecommunication Standardization Sector (ITU-T), require controlled experimental environments to ensure reliable subjective ratings. However, poor ventilation in soundproof booths can lead to increased carbon dioxide (COtextsubscript2) concentrations, which may affect cognitive function and judgement. This study investigates whether COtextsubscript2 levels affect speech quality ratings and response behaviour in listening tests. We conducted a classic mean opinion score (MOS) listening experiment while continuously measuring COtextsubscript2 concentrations in a non-actively ventilated sound booth. Our analysis reveals three key findings: (1) Higher COtextsubscript2 levels significantly reduce response time, suggesting a shift towards more impulsive decision making. (2) Speech quality ratings are systematically affected, with poorer samples rated more favourably and higher quality samples rated less favourably at elevated COtextsubscript2 concentrations. (3) Response variability decreases under high COtextsubscript2 conditions, suggesting reduced sensitivity to quality differences. These findings highlight a previously overlooked factor in speech quality research, suggesting that ambient air quality may introduce bias into subjective ratings. We discuss the implications for experimental design and the need for controlled ventilation in perceptual studies to ensure data validity.

articles.title: Interface Bond Performance of Concrete-Filled Galvanized Steel Tubes Strengthened with Internal Circular Rings: A Taguchi–Grey Relational Study
articles.abstract: Efficient transfer of longitudinal shear at the steel–concrete interface is required for composite action in concrete-filled steel tubular members, particularly near connections and other regions where load is introduced primarily through one component. This study evaluates the bond response of M40 concrete-filled galvanized steel tubes and quantifies the improvement produced by a single welded internal circular ring located near the top, middle, or bottom of the specimen. A Taguchi L9 orthogonal array was used to vary tube diameter (33.7, 42.2, and 48.3 mm), wall thickness (2.6, 3.2, and 4.0 mm), and length-to-diameter ratio (12, 14, and 16). Push-out tests were performed after 28 d of curing, and ultimate average bond stress was calculated from the peak load and nominal steel–concrete contact area. Unstrengthened specimens developed 0.878–1.899 MPa, whereas the top-, middle-, and bottom-ring series reached 1.86–2.85, 2.13–3.36, and 2.58–3.85 MPa, respectively. Relative to the unstrengthened series, the mean bond stress increased by 60.3% with a top ring, 85.6% with a middle ring, and 121.8% with a bottom ring. The bottom ring exceeded the middle and top positions by 19.5% and 38.4%, respectively, on a mean basis. For the top and middle positions, L/D produced the largest range in the response means; for the bottom position, diameter was dominant. Recalculated larger-is-better grey relational analysis identified D = 42.2 mm, t = 4.0 mm, and L/D = 12 as the best tested combination, while the factor-level optimum was D = 48.3 mm, t = 4.0 mm, and L/D = 12. The results demonstrate that ring position is a primary design variable because a ring close to the loaded end promotes mechanical interlock and mobilizes a larger resistance to core slip.

articles.title: Study on the Effect of Preparation Methods on the Performance of Ag-Cu Bifunctional Catalysts for NH₃-SCO
articles.abstract: Ammonia selective catalytic oxidation (NH₃‑SCO) can purify NH₃ waste gas, yet monometallic Ag/Al₂O₃ shows excellent low‑temperature activity but poor N₂ selectivity with abundant N₂O byproducts. Herein, a series of 10 wt.% Ag‑5 wt.% Cu bifunctional catalysts were prepared via different impregnation routes and metal loading sequences to balance catalytic performance. Performance tests reveal that co‑impregnated Ag‑Cu/Al₂O₃‑C retains high low‑temperature activity with limited selectivity improvement, while two‑step Cu‑first Ag‑Cu/Al₂O₃‑T slightly sacrifices conversion efficiency but achieves over 90% N₂ selectivity over the full temperature range. Multiple characterizations prove Cu occupies surface hydroxyl sites, reduces surface active oxygen and modulates Ag aggregation. In‑situ DRIFTS indicates Ag/Al₂O₃ follows the low‑selectivity imide pathway, whereas Ag‑Cu/Al₂O₃‑T shifts reactions toward the N₂⁻ route and partially reduces bidentate nitrates to restrain NO₂ formation. This work clarifies the structure‑activity correlation and provides an optimized preparation strategy for high‑efficiency NH₃‑SCO catalysts.

articles.title: Experimental investigation of the effects of operating factors on the internal temperature of ultra-large tires using direct measurements at the Muruntau open-pit mine
articles.abstract: This paper investigates the effects of operating factors on the thermal condition of 50/80R57 Bridgestone MasterCore VREM E1A tires installed on Komatsu 860E-1K haul trucks under the sharply continental climatic conditions of the Muruntau open-pit mine in Uzbekistan. Full-scale field tests were conducted on five haul trucks operating with payloads of 225–230 t. The internal tire temperature was measured directly using needle-type thermocouples at nine control points located near the tread–breaker interface. The thermocouple measurements were comparatively evaluated against data obtained using an infrared pyrometer and the KODA monitoring system. The results showed that temperatures in the tire shoulder zones were 3–7°C higher than those in the central tread region, while the rear tires operated at temperatures averaging 5–8°C higher than those of the front tires. Multiple regression models incorporating haul distance, operating speed, longitudinal road grade, and ambient temperature explained 97.6% of the variation in front-tire temperature and 90.5% of the variation in rear-tire temperature. Under operating conditions characterised by an ambient temperature of 36°C or higher, a mean speed of approximately 15 km/h, and a longitudinal road grade of approximately 4%, each additional kilometre of haul distance increased the internal tire temperature by an average of 2.79°C. The calculated haul distance corresponding to the critical temperature of 105°C was approximately 5.8 km. The implementation of the developed organisational and technical recommendations for improving tire utilisation at the Muruntau mine reduced operating costs by UZS 1013 per kilometre. Based on the estimated annual operating volume, the resulting annual economic benefit amounted to UZS 607.8 million per haul truck.

articles.title: Constructed a stable coordination polymer for highly efficient and selective capture of thorium
articles.abstract: The efficient separation of thorium (Th) from chemically similar rare earth elements (REEs) is technically challenging. In this work, a stable coordination polymer (Ni-tfc-CP) was fabricated by adopting the strategy of in-situ incorporation of hydrophobic groups. Ni-tfc-CP exhibits excellent structural stability over a wide pH range of 2–11 and under high-temperature conditions up to 247°C. The abundant carboxyl oxygen active binding sites on the surface of Ni-tfc-CP, provides favorable environment for Th(IV) uptake. The maximum adsorption capacity was calculated to 518.9 mg g⁻¹, by fitting the equilibrium data to the Langmuir model. Moreover, it showed an ultra-fast adsorption rate and reached equilibrium within 5 minutes. Notably, competitive tests confirmed the superior selectivity of Ni-tfc-CP for Th(IV), with a high distribution coefficient of 6×10⁵ mL g⁻¹. This study provides meaningful guidance for the rational development of functional materials toward nuclide separation.

articles.title: Linear Control System of a 6-DOF Parallel Motion Platform for Controlled Dynamic EEG Phantom Experiments with Actuator Dynamics
articles.abstract: This paper presents a Type-1 linear controller for a six-degree-of-freedom Stewart motion platform intended for controlled dynamic electroencephalography phantom experiments. The platform is intended to provide repeatable mechanical motion so that electrode signals can later be compared under static and dynamic conditions. A simplified task-space model is formed about a nominal equilibrium pose. First-order actuator dynamics represent input lag, and one integral error state is added for each controlled coordinate. The resulting model contains 24 states: 12 platform states, six actuator states, and six integral states. A null-space method is used to formulate the state-feedback gain for prescribed closed-loop eigenvalues. An analytical controllability check establishes rank 24 for the augmented model. TheMATLAB responses approach the prescribed translational and rotational step commands with approximately zero steady-state error. The rotational responses also show substantial transient motion, including roll overshoot. These results demonstrate tracking within the simplified linear model; the command amplitudes do not establish the validity of a small-motion approximation for a physical platform. The study provides an initial control framework for future experiments on motion artifacts, signal quality, and source-localization stability. Physical actuator allocation, workspace limits, and experimental electroencephalography validation remain to be addressed.

articles.title: Characteristics of GaAs Thin Films Grown by MOVPE Using Triethylgallium (TEGa) and Tertiarybutylarsine (TBAs)
articles.abstract: Gallium arsenide (GaAs) growth by metal-organic vapor phase epitaxy (MOVPE) is typically achieved by using arsine (AsH₃) and trimethylgallium (TMGa) as precursors. However, this study explores the growth of high-quality, undoped homoepitaxial GaAs thin films using triethylgallium (TEGa) and tertiarybutylarsine (TBAs) as alternative precursors. The thin films were characterised using Nomarski optical microscopy, high-resolution X-ray diffraction (HRXRD), photoluminescence (PL) and temperature-dependent Hall measurements. The growth temperature significantly influenced the properties of the epitaxial films. A smooth surface morphology was observed in undoped GaAs epilayers grown at temperatures above 600°C, whereas films grown at or below 575°C exhibited a rougher surface morphology. All layers displayed n-type conductivity, except those grown at 550°C, which showed p-type conductivity, with a carrier concentration of (:6:×:10¹⁶) (:cm⁻³) and a mobility of approximately (:298:cm²/V·s) at room temperature. The lowest carrier concentration (:(sim1.5:×::10¹⁵:cm⁻³)) and highest mobility ((:5147:cm²/V·s)) at room temperature were achieved at growth temperatures of 600°C and 650°C, respectively. Additionally, low-temperature (5.4 K) PL measurements showed a reduction in defect-related emissions with increasing growth temperature, further supporting improved material quality at higher temperatures.

articles.title: Improving the Efficiency of Pumping Equipment by Enhancing the Cooling System of a Submersible Pump Motor
articles.abstract: Submersible pumping units used in the in-situ leaching (ISL) technology of the Kyzylkum region may be subject to electric motor overheating caused by insufficient fluid flow velocity around the motor, the formation of mineral deposits on the housing surface, and continuous operation in an aggressive environment. These factors lead to premature degradation of the winding insulation and reduced efficiency of the pumping equipment. This paper proposes a technical solution — a cooling jacket installed on the suction nozzle of a submersible pump — and develops a mathematical model of heat transfer in the annular channel between the motor housing and the jacket. The model is based on forced convection theory and accounts for the Reynolds and Nusselt numbers, the hydraulic diameter of the annular gap, and the dependence of the heat transfer coefficient on flow velocity. Numerical calculations were performed for two pump models, USK 408/42 and URN 6 25/14, operating in wells with diameters of 159 mm and 195 mm, respectively. The results show that the cooling jacket increases the fluid velocity along the motor of the USK 408/42 pump from a subcritical value (about 0.17 m/s) to 0.69 m/s, and provides velocities of 0.59–1.43 m/s for the URN 6 25/14 pump; at a fluid temperature of 40 °C, the calculated overheating of the USK 408/42 motor surface relative to the fluid decreases from 9.4 °C without a jacket to 2.4 °C with a jacket inner diameter of 113 mm. It is shown that the main function of the jacket is to ensure longitudinal flow along the motor, which may not be achieved without a jacket. Conjugate CFD simulation in SolidWorks Flow Simulation showed a reduction in the mean motor surface temperature of 12.6 °C (7.0 °C according to the analytical model) and in the maximum temperature inside the motor of 16.5 °C. Laboratory tests on the SGU-TsNS-012-6LR-PK test bench with a Chimp QDX3-20-0.55(Y) submersible pump and jackets of 220–240 mm diameter qualitatively confirmed that the motor surface temperature decreases as the jacket diameter decreases and the flow rate increases (overheating reduced from 14.2 to 0.5 °C). The capital cost of the jacket is about USD 37 per pump, which is negligible compared with the cost of motor repair; the effect of the jacket on energy consumption remains to be verified experimentally.

articles.title: Atmospheric Heat Retention and Weakening Urban–Rural Thermal Contrast Driven by Surface Characteristics in the Indo-Gangetic Plains
articles.abstract: Rapid urbanization, coupled with regional climatic and topographic constraints, has intensified the SUHI effect. This study employs an integrated methodological approach, utilizing Partial Least Squares (PLS) Regression, to identify and decouple the urban and atmospheric drivers influencing SUHI. The method is applied to, one of the world’s most densely populated and highly environmentally constrained region, Indo-Gangetic Plains (IGP). Yearly as well as seasonal daytime and nighttime SUHI intensities are analysed for seven major cities of IGP by comparing two distinct five-year pentad windows spanning two decades (early: 2000–2004 and late: 2020–2024), alongside consecutive yearly seasonal monitoring across 2020–2024. Results reveal persistent nocturnal mean (max) SUHI dominance in the range of 2.12°C – 2.67°C (3.59°C – 4.61°C) in the recent pentad, exceeding daytime intensities across all cities and periods. Daytime urban–rural LST contrast has gradually narrowed, particularly during the pre-monsoon as rural moisture deficits, bare soils, and peri-urban expansion weaken daytime rural evaporative cooling. Also, pixel level seasonal SUHI assessment reveals anomalous behaviour; daytime SUHI exhibits spatial variance in Agra, Prayagraj, and Patna, whereas nighttime SUHI remains commonly positive for all cities (~ 95% of urban pixels). PLS regression analysis indicates that the built-up expansion is a primary year-round positive warming driver, while water bodies provide consistent daytime SUHI mitigation. Crucially, vegetation cooling is relatively weaker during the daytime but effectively reduces nighttime SUHI, and relative humidity largely plays as a mitigator except for post-monsoon daytime. We also observe that, persistent nighttime warming aligns with regional basin topography, synoptic flow channelling, and aerosol-mediated thermal retention. These findings emphasize the necessity of season- and diurnal-specific urban mitigation strategies tailored to shifting regional baselines.

articles.title: Synergistic effect of nano-silica and copper grains on the superhydrophobicity and corrosion resistance of silane coatings on carbon steel
articles.abstract: Q235B carbon steel is one of the most widely used structural materials in the field of industrial engineering. However, the corrosion failure problem in harsh service environments restricts its service life and application safety. Existing anticorrosive coatings generally have defects such as high preparation costs, complicated processes, and poor eco-friendliness. In order to address these issues, this study utilized a simple chemical displacement deposition and silane synergistic modification method to prepare a superhydrophobic composite anti-corrosion coating on carbon steel. The experiment focused on investigating the effects of the doping strategy and concentration of nano-silica on the micro-nano morphology, surface wettability, and electrochemical protection effect of the coating. The results demonstrate that the direct doping of nano-SiO2 in the deposition solution destroys the physical continuity of the surface structure, leading to a negative impact on the overall hydrophobicity and corrosion resistance of the coating. After process optimization, a uniform micro-nano hierarchical rough structure can be constructed on micron-sized copper grains by chemical deposition for 50 s combined with a silane modification solution containing 0.3 wt% nano-SiO2. Under this optimal condition, the static water contact angle of the coating reaches 160°. Electrochemical tests indicate protective properties, exhibiting an approximately 4.5-fold enhancement in polarization resistance and a nearly 75% reduction in corrosion current density relative to the bare substrate, which suppresses the interfacial corrosion kinetics. Furthermore, under long-term continuous immersion in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution (> 500 h), the coating maintained a physical and chemical shielding barrier, halving the cumulative macroscopic corrosion rate compared to the unprotected steel. The composite preparation scheme proposed in this study provides a simple and reliable technical reference for the low-cost anti-corrosion treatment of carbon steel components.

articles.title: Influence of hydroxyl nest structure of all-silicon supports on efficient propane dehydrogenation over PtZn catalysts
articles.abstract: To investigate the effect of hydroxyl nest structure on the performance of PtZn bimetallic catalysts for propane dehydrogenation (PDH), four all-silica materials, namely S-1, S-β, MCM-41 and SBA-15, were selected as supports and a series of catalysts were constructed by co-impregnation loading PtZn bimetallic catalysts. Catalyst structures were characterized by means of XRD, N2 adsorption-desorption, FT-IR, XPS, etc. The characterization results indicated that the PtZn/S-1 catalyst had the highest content of hydroxyl nests, and the abundant hydroxyl groups on the support surface could provide stable anchoring sites for the PtZn active component, significantly increasing the exposure of Pt0. The activity test results showed that the PtZn/S-1 catalyst exhibited optimal catalytic performance under reaction conditions of 600℃ and WHSV = 13.39 h-1: propane conversion of 29.1%, propylene selectivity of 96.8%, and initial propylene generation rate of 0.79 mmol/g-1·min-1. The study shows that the hydroxyl nest structure of the all-silicon support is a key factor in regulating the dispersion and exposure of the PtZn active center, and provides theoretical support for the structural design of highly efficient PDH catalysts.

articles.title: Predictive Modelling of the Mechanical Strength of Wire Arc Additive Manufactured Metal Parts
articles.abstract: Predictive modeling of the mechanical strength of parts produced via Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing (WAAM) is critical for advancing the technology from prototyping to demanding structural applications. Traditional data-driven models often lack accuracy outside their training datasets, creating a need for frameworks that incorporate fundamental physics. This paper presents a predictive modeling approach that integrates first-principles models to predict the yield strength of WAAM-fabricated components. By modeling the core thermal history, solidification kinetics, and phase transformation mechanisms, the framework establishes a direct link between process parameters such as heat input, travel speed, and cooling rate to the final microstructural evolution. The first-principles approach offers an analytical-physical framework to simulate the transient temperature fields and subsequent grain growth during multi-layer deposition. This metallurgical data serves as the foundation for a mechanistic strength model based on Hall-Petch grain size strengthening, solid solution hardening, and dislocation density evolution. Validation will be done against experimental data from WAAM-printed steel specimens. The first principles model demonstrates superior predictive accuracy and generalization capabilities compared to purely empirical methods which use dataset such as those generated from experimental investigation or with a combination with transient thermo-mechanical finite element (FE) simulations. The findings will provide a robust tool for real-time quality control, process optimization, and the accelerated qualification of high-performance WAAM components as well as a reliable digital twin framework for WAAM.

articles.title: OQMD: Single-Qubit Rotation Control Improves Low-CNOT Multiclass Quantum Classification
articles.abstract: Near-term variational classifiers incur substantial error and latency from two-qubitgates, yet practitioners often assume that additional entangling depth is the defaultroute to higher accuracy. This work studies Optimal Quantum Measurement Decoding(OQMD): optimizing how quantum outcomes are mapped to classical labels by train-ing a readout layer before measurement, jointly with the variational circuit, withoutadding CNOTs. Experiments use trainable triple single-qubit rotations as one con-crete, hardware-native realization of OQMD; other single-qubit parametrizations fitthe same classical outer loop. On the Iris benchmark with a 30-point stratified testsplit, the best observed 0-CNOT configuration with OQMD reaches 83.33% accuracy,with a 96% accuracy at 9 CNOTs, exceeding the best 18-CNOT controls (56.67%)and the best 18-CNOT configuration with OQMD (66.67%) under a common proto-col. A six-point CNOT-depth series from 0 to 18 (fixed optimizer, iteration budget,random-seed count, and ZXZ readout) shows that the highest raw scores need notoccur at the largest template, so aggregate complexity is not summarized by CNOTcount alone. Because run-level accuracies are discrete and non-Gaussian, we empha-size best-observed scores and, where a global comparison of pooled runs is required,Mann–Whitney U tests rather than parametric tests on means. Across architectures,OQMD shows statistically consistent but magnitude-dependent gains: large peak liftson minimal circuits coexist with a small pooled mean shift on complex 18-CNOT runs(p ≈ 0.03) that is not “universal” in the sense of uniformly large practical effects.

articles.title: Baseline-relative evaluation of lap-time and tyre-degradation models for Formula 1 race strategy
articles.abstract: Race-strategy decision support in Formula 1 rests on forecasts of next-lap time and tyre degradation. Published models report small errors but rarely report what a trivial forecast achieves on the same laps, so their accuracy cannot be separated from the strong autocorrelation of consecutive laps. This study supplies that comparison using 167,083 laps from the public FastF1 interface, and finds that constructing the baseline fairly matters as much as reporting it. Gradient-boosted models were trained on 2019–2022, frozen, and evaluated with the race as the unit of inference. Against a persistence forecast the advantage is 15.1%, but 3.2% of comparisons span a pit stop, where persistence compares laps on different tyres: the gain reaches 30.6% in a stint's first five laps against 10.2% later. Against a stint-aware baseline carrying a compound offset across stops it is 12.1% (race-level p = 0.0065), and 13.2% on all green-flag laps without outcome-based filtering. A nested ablation shows the advantage comes from predicting a residual from the previous lap: all three residual configurations beat the baseline by race-level test, and no absolute one does. For degradation, a stint-referenced target subtracts a within-stint constant, so its persistence forecast is identical to the lap-time one and any lap-time model's degradation error equals its lap-time error; the target cannot distinguish degradation knowledge from lap-time knowledge at a one-step horizon. With the evaluation season fixed and five seeds averaged, pre-regulation and same-era training perform alike (11.9%, 12.2%) and pooling both is best (16.1%).

articles.title: Regrets, I've Had a Few: Approximating (Subgame-Perfect) Nash Equilibria via Deep Regret Actor-Critic
articles.abstract: This paper introduces the Deep Regret Actor-Critic (DRAC) algorithm to approximate (Subgame-Perfect) Nash Equilibria in continuous general-sum games. Standard actor-critic methods struggle in these settings, as concurrent utility maximization induces severe non-stationarity. DRAC resolves this by shifting the optimization objective to regret minimization, allowing for a Centralized Training with Centralized Execution architecture that coordinates joint policy updates while enforcing individual rationality to prevent collusion. It employs a Monte Carlo solver that samples unilateral deviations against fixed opponent actions, creating a stationary target landscape. A dual-head Critic maps this stationary landscape by independently predicting the best-response utility and the resulting regret. By minimizing this predicted regret, the Actor drives the joint strategy profile toward an unexploitable equilibrium. Empirical evaluations in a sequential Cournot oligopoly and a proportional prize contest confirm convergence to the analytical equilibria. Compared to Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG), our algorithm consistently achieves lower exploitability and approximates the analytical equilibrium quantities more precisely. JEL Classification: C45 , C63 , C72 , C73

articles.title: Battery circularity for community shared energy storage system: the new city-district of Dietenbach in Freiburg, Germany
articles.abstract: In the coming decades, the need for the end-of-life (EoL) management of retired electric vehicle (EV) batteries is projected to raise especially in the countries that have achieved a rapid market uptake of EVs. This will create a huge challenge to develop appropriate strategies for sustainable EoL management of batteries. The focus of discourses and actions has largely been on providing purchase incentives and necessary infrastructure for the use phase of EVs, lacking a battery circularity perspective to meet the environmental and safety challenges of retired EV batteries. This study will apply insights from different strands of literature to address this gap, especially in a complex context when a range of sectors are technically and physically coupled with each other. In the light of battery circularity, the energy infrastructure planning for the new city-district of Dietenbach in Freiburg is studied to provide some practical insights into the role of battery circularity in using second-life batteries (SLBs) in the community shared energy storage (CSES) systems. The results show that SLBs provide affordable and environmentally responsible energy storage alternatives and the community groups, e.g., collaborative housing groups in Dietenbach are well suited as carriers for applying the battery circularity in the CSES models, which can be used as a solid platform to initiate and develop the notion of solar-based SLBs. Then, one of the key preconditions for sustainable CSES is to establish a uniform set of standards, guidelines and regulations for safe collection and transportation and reliable use of SLBs.

articles.title: The Geometric Product of í µí²� Vectors: a Grade-Spectrum Theorem, Exact Second Moments, and a Two-Scale Cut-off for Random Versors
articles.abstract: Let (:X=a₁cdots:aₙ) be a product of nonzero vectors in the Clifford algebra of (:Rd), and let (:ρ:Xin:Oleft(dright)) be the orthogonal map it represents. We show that the squared coordinates of (:X) are read off from (:ρ:X) by single determinants, (:XI²=left|Xright|²detleft(left(Id+ρ:XDIright)/2right)), where (:DI) is the diagonal sign matrix of the blade (:eI). The formula holds for all versors, odd ones included. Its grade-wise form, (:sum:ₛparallel:⟨X⟩ₛparallel:²ts=left|Xright|²detleft(left(left(1+tright)Id+left(1-tright)ρ:Xright)/2right)), refines the spin-character identity (:⟨X⟩²=detleft(left(Id+ρ:Xright)/2right)) for unit (:X). For even versors the coordinate formula is equivalent to a consequence of Shirokov’s reconstruction of spin group elements from minors, and in dimension three it gives the squared components in Shepperd’s quaternion extraction. As consequences, the grade energies are a Krawtchouk transform of the exterior-power traces of (:ρ:X), and the grade profile is a complete conjugacy invariant with mean (:left(d-trρ:Xright)/2) and variance (:left(d-trρ:X²right)/4).
