These results empirically support the LCA hypothesis and underscore the need to simulate the brain's mechanisms and generate adaptive, entangled modules for AGI. They also expose the shortcomings of conventional artificial neural networks (ANNs) that depend on vast, opaque parameters. By combining ANN-based AI with probability-wave-based entangled brain simulations, machine learning enables the creation of human-like processing units (HPUs). Such HPUs promise more efficient and robust AGI, particularly for embodied intelligence and robotics.

articles.title: Scalable Stress-Constrained Topology Optimization: A Super-resolution and Simultaneous Approach Based on Machine Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28703v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large-scale topology optimization (TO) remains computationally demanding, especially for stress-constrained problems. To address this challenge, we propose the simultaneous neural topology optimization (SNTO) framework where we represent state, adjoint, and design variables with custom neural networks (NNs) whose parameters are jointly optimized within a single optimization loop that leverages continuous adjoint analysis and automatic differentiation. This optimization minimizes a multi-component loss function that combines the design objective, an aggregation of the local stress constraints, and the potential energy functionals. Our NNs have a unique architecture that accelerates convergence while enabling the networks to capture sharp gradients and boundaries which are critical to stress-constrained TO. To achieve scalability to millions of degrees of freedom (DoF), we develop a hardware-aware training scheme in which the design domain is partitioned into subdomains that are distributed across multiple GPUs. To control peak GPU memory usage, we further slice each subdomain into smaller regions whose loss gradients are evaluated sequentially and accumulated to update the NN parameters. Unlike domain decomposition approaches, our partitioning naturally ensures field continuity across the subdomains and does not require the introduction of additional terms into the loss function. For validation, we first evaluate the proposed framework on various 2D stress-constrained benchmarks and compare our results to a conventional finite element-based approach, showing that SNTO produces super-resolution designs with sharper boundaries, smaller gray areas, and lower volume fractions. We then consider large-scale 3D problems with up to eight million collocation points and distribute the training over up to eight GPUs.

articles.title: STAR-XPC: Set Transformer for Estimating X-ray Transmission in Polymer Composites
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28709v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evaluating the energy transmission ratio of an X-ray beam through a polymer composite is a challenging task in radiation shielding studies. The reference solution with Monte Carlo transport simulation is highly accurate but computationally expensive: each of our reference simulations is capped at 4×10⁹ photon histories and a 20,000 s (over 5 hours) time limit, while closed-form analytical methods fail to represent such complex scenarios. We present an artificial neural network model that maps the unordered multi-set of molecular constituents, their mass fractions, and four bulk physical descriptors directly to the transmission ratio I(t)/I₀ in 1-3 milliseconds. The model is a Set Transformer, which makes it permutation invariant by construction and accepts mixtures of different sizes up to 11 constituents within a fixed-size padded set. Each constituent is embedded with a chemistry-pretrained transformer language model, ChemBERTa. In our proposed method, training data are produced by an automated PENELOPE/penEasy pipeline using the radiation source at 30, 80, 100, and 120 kV tube voltages over polyethylene-based shielding composite slabs of thicknesses spanning 0.15-2.5 mm. After preprocessing, the dataset contains n = 4697 simulated configurations on which a leakage-free, jointly stratified 10-fold cross-validation is performed, attaining mean squared error MSE = (1.12 ± 0.56)×10⁻⁴, normalized-MSE percentage NMSE% = 0.0294% ± 0.0147%, and R² = 0.9988. The corresponding per-sample percentage errors give an alpha-trimmed (α = 0.10) absolute percentage error (APE) of 1.66% and a median APE of 1.15%. Our model's inference is several orders of magnitude faster than the underlying Monte Carlo simulation (sub-millisecond per query vs. several hours for the reference run) with effective accuracy in predicting I(t)/I₀.

articles.title: A General Topological Symmetry Index for Critical Orbits In Neural Network Loss Landscapes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A systematic understanding of the global structure of neural-network loss landscapes remains challenging due to their high dimensionality. Symmetries arising from network architectures and learning objectives provide a way to investigate aspects of this structure. Although a growing number of studies have drawn attention to these symmetries, a systematic characterization of them, as well as of the critical orbits they give rise to, remains incomplete. To address this gap, in this work we establish a topological symmetry index, based on the methodologies from the family of equivariant degree theories, to decode these symmetries. The frameworks apply to arbitrary network architectures and include methods applicable to degenerate critical orbits. The index detects the isotropy of the critical points and quantifies the corresponding net topological contributions. Several examples, including softplus MLPs, Transformers, and equivariant neural networks, are presented to illustrate the computations.

articles.title: Combating Catastrophic Forgetting in Continual Domain Adaptation via Knowledge Recasting
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28892v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adapting language models to new domains during post-training risks degrading previously acquired capabilities, a phenomenon commonly known as catastrophic forgetting. Existing mitigation methods largely treat forgetting as a consequence of excessive model drift. They therefore constrain updates by preserving old outputs, replaying old data, or regularizing changes to parameters and representations so that the updated model remains close to its previous state. We take a different view: Rather than pulling the updated model back toward its old state, we translate the new domain into the model's pre-existing knowledge space, making unfamiliar knowledge learnable through familiar procedures. Therefore, we propose Skill Schema Transport (SST), a post-training framework that transports new knowledge into the model's existing skill space. SST abstracts each example type into a skill schema, preserving its essential operations, dependencies, and verification steps while removing domain-specific surface forms. By recasting new examples as instances of reusable procedures, SST turns knowledge update from trajectory memorization into procedural reuse. In continual domain adaptation settings, SST consistently reduces forgetting while improving generalization to related tasks. Across two 3B instruction-tuned backbones, SST improves average final performance on streamed domains by 2.53 to 5.75 points over sequential post-training. It also lowers max-drop forgetting in all evaluated settings, with the largest reduction from 42.41 to 7.10 points on the Qwen-3B MATH stream, while substantially recovering the OOD degradation induced by sequential updates.

articles.title: From Weather to Enhanced Weathering: Weather Foundation Models for Carbon Dioxide Removal at Operational Scale
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28973v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Enhanced Rock Weathering (ERW) is a carbon removal solution with the potential to remove gigatons of CO₂ per year, but quantifying that removal today requires dense soil sampling and laboratory analysis. We evaluate five weather Foundation Models (FMs) as frozen encoders feeding lightweight decoders, under a leave-one-field-out protocol on 5,192 chronosequences from 264 fields across Brazil and the US. To our knowledge, this is the first holistic evaluation of weather FMs for ERW and the largest evaluation on operational ERW data. We find that across weather FMs, representations transfer to ERW: our best model, TerraNova-ERW, built on Aurora 1.5, positively orders measurements within fields it has never seen. Zero-shot prediction of a new field's mean removal is not yet feasible, and we attribute this to data scale: the same architecture excels on sim10⁵ natural-weathering sequences, anchoring the scale we expect ERW data must reach. Few-shot prediction, blending the model with a few samples per field, is supported today: TerraNova-ERW recovers over 60% of the highest-removal fields with two samples per field, roughly halves the samples needed to estimate a field's mean removal, and can cut sampling on our densest fields by 28-98%.

articles.title: SSMCGM-Stream: A Streaming State-Space Model for Personalized Diabetes Management
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28976v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Continuous glucose monitoring supports diabetes management but requires forecasting models that are accurate, interpretable, and efficient enough for real-time deployment. We present SSMCGM-Stream, a streaming state-space model that maintains a personalized hidden state updated with each incoming glucose reading to provide constant-time forecasting, physiologically structured counterfactual reasoning, and interpretable forecasts through hidden-state attribution. Built on this foundation, SSMCGM-Agent delivers risk-aware, natural-language decision support by translating forecasts, explanations, and counterfactuals into grounded recommendations through a guarded language-model interface. Evaluated on the T1DEXI cohort, SSMCGM-Stream achieves forecasting performance comparable to strong neural baselines while substantially reducing computational cost, enabling continuous on-device diabetes decision support.

articles.title: ExpEvolve: Structuring and Reusing Experience for Open-Ended Discovery
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evolutionary coding agents such as AlphaEvolve are one of the notable successes in using Large Language Models (LLMs) to build AI Scientists. These agents tackle open-ended scientific problems by iteratively improving and evolving programs, leveraging the prior knowledge and reasoning capabilities of LLMs. Despite their success, mutations over programs are mostly low-level upon surface heuristics, without a persistent unit of control. In contrast, science compounds through ideas. In this work, we propose ExpEvolve, which injects idea-level extraction and control into evolution: it discovers and leverages the high-level factors from programs that explain scoring differences among different programs. We characterize theoretical conditions on when discovery with idea factors improves sample efficiency. We also build a practical framework to show that the extracted high-level idea factors are helpful for guiding exploitation from experience and exploration when discovery comes to a plateau. Across 11 open-ended mathematical tasks, ExpEvolve significantly improves the final performance and sample efficiency up to 5.0x. The improvements also transfer to 4 other LLMs and to 6 machine learning tasks from MLS-Bench. Analysis shows that ExpEvolve can discover idea-level factors to provide better exploration and exploitation for evolutionary discovery.

articles.title: YingLan: A Multimodal Ocean Foundation Model for Unified Representation Learning from Heterogeneous Observations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29313v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal ocean modeling remains challenging due to substantial heterogeneity in data structures, physical semantics, and spatiotemporal characteristics across satellite imagery, gridded oceanographic fields, and buoy observations. Existing approaches largely focus on task-specific ocean modeling, while learning transferable representations from heterogeneous observations remains an open problem. To address this challenge, we propose YingLan, a multimodal ocean foundation model that integrates physics-attribute-conditioned dynamic encoding, Spatiotemporal Increment Coupling (STIC), and ocean-state evolution-aware pretraining. Specifically, the dynamic encoding mechanism generates adaptive input projections conditioned on physical semantics and observation characteristics, enabling flexible representation of heterogeneous ocean variables. STIC models multiscale spatiotemporal dependencies through cross-scale interactions of latent temporal increments. The pretraining strategy further combines masked observation reconstruction with temporal evolution objectives to facilitate the learning of coherent ocean-state representations across different prediction horizons. YingLan is implemented using MindSpore and trained on Huawei Ascend 910B NPUs, demonstrating its compatibility with domestic AI computing infrastructure. In a seven-day sea surface salinity (SSS) forecasting task conducted in the Shenzhen coastal waters, YingLan achieves an average RMSE of 0.687508 PSU, corresponding to relative error reductions of 0.58%, 5.31%, and 12.42% compared with LangYa, XiHe, and GloNet2, respectively. These results provide initial evidence of the model's effectiveness in regional ocean forecasting, while broader cross-task and cross-regional evaluations remain necessary to assess its generalization capabilities.

articles.title: BrainCodes: A Lightweight EEG Foundation Model over Discrete Neural Codes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29320v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models increasingly emphasize model scale, potentially limiting their deployment on resource-constrained devices and in everyday environments. We argue that transferable EEG features can instead be learned with a compact architecture and introduce BrainCodes, a lightweight foundation model pretrained through self-supervised learning on more than 800 hours of recordings from over 1,000 participants. Our architecture combines a quantization-based neural tokenizer with a spatiotemporal encoder that supports arbitrary electrode configurations. The pretraining objective explicitly encourages representations that capture spatial connectivity through channel positional encoding, and sensitivity to narrowband neural oscillations through an auxiliary training objective. Our model matches or surpasses the state of the art across diverse neurophysiological monitoring tasks, including sleep staging, attention assessment, and cognitive load estimation. BrainCodes transfers effectively to low-resource wearable devices while using up to 97% fewer trainable parameters than comparable architectures. Beyond predictive accuracy, our evaluation framework characterizes the geometry and invariances of learned EEG representations across measurable spatial, temporal, and spectral signal properties.

articles.title: Cross-Area Transfer Learning for VLC-based Indoor Localization with a Transfer Efficiency Score
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29638v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Indoor localization systems are critical for Industry-4.0 applications. Visible Light Communication (VLC)-based systems offer advantages such as immunity to electromagnetic interference, high accuracy, and energy efficiency, but their performance is hindered by environmental variability across deployment areas. This paper presents a transfer learning (TL) framework for VLC-based indoor localization that enhances cross-area robustness while reducing data requirements. Using real-world measurements from four distinct areas of a Bosch manufacturing facility, we show that fine-tuning a deep neural network (DNN) pre-trained on source area data with only 40% of target-area measurements recovers 97% of full-data performance, thereby reducing the amount of target data needed. We further introduce the Transfer Efficiency Score (TES), a composite metric that identifies the most effective source models for transfer without exhaustive evaluation. Guided by TES, the framework selects the best source model, yielding localization errors as low as 40.9 cm with success rates above 86%. Validation on an unseen area confirms its generalization capability, with a 3.28 cm mean error achieved using the TES-selected source model. Overall, the proposed framework provides a scalable and data-efficient pathway for industrial VLC localization, substantially reducing deployment costs and computational burden while maintaining high accuracy in diverse and dynamic environments.

articles.title: Orbitol: Crystal Generation on Wyckoff Orbits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30086v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative models propose crystalline materials by learning composition and geometry, but unconditional sampling gives no direct control over the space group, which constrains whether responses such as piezoelectricity are symmetry-allowed. We present Orbitol, a crystal generator built on the Crystalite diffusion Transformer that replaces atom tokens with Wyckoff-orbit tokens. Given a space group and a collection of occupied Wyckoff positions, Orbitol generates the atom type and free coordinates of each orbit together with a compatible lattice, so every valid structure is invariant under the operations of the requested group. It generates structures two to three orders of magnitude faster than the symmetry-aware baselines at the evaluated settings. On MP-20, 13.8% of Orbitol's attempts yielded stable or metastable, unique and novel structures that retained the requested space group after relaxation, compared with 10.8% for SGFM, the next best model. We also introduce SPARC, a score that combines retention of the raw detected space group with agreement between the retained-group and training distributions. Finally, we used Orbitol to generate candidates in piezoelectric crystal classes. Of the structures selected by internal screening, 89% passed our density functional theory checks, and 79% also matched no Materials Project or Alexandria entry with the same space group. Their median figure of merit was nine times that of the piezoelectric materials computed in the Materials Project, and 24% of the new candidates ranked in that set's top 10%.

articles.title: Solar System Surface Technosignatures: Searching for Signs of Artificial Design on Extraterrestrial Terrain
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28687v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Artificial radio emissions have historically been a major focus of technosignature searches. Here, we apply an anthropological lens to expand this scope to surface technosignatures: non-random, intentional patterning on planetary terrain, similar to long-lasting human-made landscapes and monuments on Earth. On geologically inactive bodies such as the Moon and Mars, artificial traces and patterns could potentially remain visible for hundreds of millions of years. We discuss two recent developments that make this search timely: high-resolution imaging datasets, such as those produced by the HiRISE camera on the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO), and ML-based anomaly-detection methods. Finally, we list two possible approaches to developing a model capable of searching for these surface technosignatures: a supervised and an unsupervised one. Complemented by LiDAR, ground-penetrating radar, and reflectance spectroscopy, these methods would enable the first quantitative upper limits on surface technosignatures while yielding ancillary benefits for planetary science.

articles.title: Scaling in Games: Continued Pre-Training For Embodied Agents In Diverse Virtual Worlds
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28698v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scaling data, diversity and model capacity has improved embodied learning in physical environments, where diverse experiences remain grounded in shared physical laws. Whether these gains extend to virtual worlds with different visual styles, dynamics, controls, and objectives remains unclear. We investigate this question through a controlled study of continued pre-training (CPT) across three axes: data volume, diversity, and model size. Our 120 training configurations span four model sizes from 0.8B to 27B, six data budgets from 50 to 1,600 hours, and five mixtures ranging from Minecraft-only data to diverse multi-world corpora. We assess performance and generalization using three-level validation losses and gameplay benchmarks from in-corpus worlds to unseen worlds. Our results show: (1) more data improves in-corpus performance, diversity improves transfer to related worlds with limited gains in distant worlds, and model size improves data efficiency but generalizes worse to distant worlds under single-world training; (2) we observe an early interface phase with broad cross-world benefits and a later world phase with gains narrowed to in-corpus and related worlds, and fit an empirical scaling law relating validation loss to data volume, diversity and model size; and (3) our models are competitive with Minecraft specialists and frontier models in 3D worlds, and perform best in real-time settings. However, the limits of imitation and persistent gaps in distant worlds suggest that building generalist embodied agents requires richer training stages beyond continued pre-training.

articles.title: GPU-Accelerated Construction of the Gabriel Graph: Parallelization Strategies and Applications to Large-Margin Classification and Graph-Based Clustering
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28759v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Gabriel graph is a proximity graph widely used in computational geometry and geometric machine learning, underlying large-margin classifiers and, as we show in this work, density-aware clustering methods. Its construction, however, has cubic time complexity O(N³) in the naive formulation, which severely limits its use on datasets beyond a few thousand samples. This paper presents a set of GPU parallelization strategies, implemented in CUDA, that make Gabriel graph construction practical at scale. We introduce (i) an implicit closed-form mapping from a linear thread index to the corresponding vertex pair (i,j), which removes the need for an explicit O(N²) adjacency structure and lets every thread locate its pair in constant time and constant memory; (ii) a two-pass, bitmask-based, atomically-compacted edge-list construction that produces a dense edge array proportional only to the number of edges actually found; and (iii) a thread-coarsening strategy in which each thread evaluates several candidate pairs, trading launch and scheduling overhead against load balance. We evaluate these strategies on the acceleration of a Gabriel-graph-based large-margin classifier (NN-clas) and on a novel Gabriel-graph clustering algorithm that identifies connected components on a residual graph and performs GPU-parallel Union-Find with hierarchical edge-based merging. On 14 public benchmark datasets, the GPU implementation reduces Gabriel graph construction time by two to nearly four orders of magnitude relative to a sequential CPU baseline (up to 8484x), without loss of classification accuracy, and the proposed clustering method is statistically competitive with DBSCAN on the topological validity index Dunn while eliminating the need for an explicit density radius parameter.

articles.title: One Policy, Many Styles: Where to Aggregate Preferences for Steerable Humanoid Control?
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28925v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern robotic agents are increasingly expected to support steerable control, where a single policy can adjust its behavioral style at runtime under changing user preferences. Preference-conditioned reinforcement learning provides this interface, but conditioning alone does not ensure that a requested behavior change is strong, does not leak into unrelated behaviors, and does not compromise task performance. Our evaluation combines Preference Reward Responsiveness (PRR) with coverage and utility metrics. We use these measures to compare reward-level, advantage-level, loss-level, and PCGrad-based aggregation across two humanoid-control frameworks. No aggregation level performs best across all environments and criteria. Experiments show that aggregating objectives early produces a wider range of behavioral responses but greater unintended changes in other objectives, while aggregating them later improves control precision at some cost to responsiveness.

articles.title: Can Quantum Layers offer Performance and Security Advantages in Vision-Language Models?
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28964v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As quantum computing moves from the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era toward early fault-tolerant quantum computing (EFTQC), quantum-enhanced AI is shifting from a conceptual idea to experimental research. Quantum components are expected to extend the capabilities of existing AI systems, yet it remains unclear how such components will help within large multimodal models. In this study, we try to answer that question for vision-language models (VLMs) using classically simulated quantum layers. With LLaVA-OneVision as the backbone, we evaluate 4- and 8-qubit basic-ring and strongly entangling circuits at four insertion and four replacement locations. Insertion adds quantum layers to the classical model, while replacement substitutes them for classical components. Using the same setup, we compare performance and computational cost between classical and quantum-classical hybrid models. On the Visual Spatial Reasoning dataset, inserting a quantum layer after the visual projector reaches 80.7% development accuracy, 2.28 percentage-points above classical full fine-tuning. Replacing the final decoder feed-forward sublayer retains 79.22% accuracy with 13.07 million fewer trainable parameters. Quantum insertion can thus improve accuracy, and selective replacement can reduce parameters. These benefits depend strongly on where the quantum layer is inserted or which classical component it replaces: earlier replacements lower accuracy, and fewer parameters do not reliably shorten training or reduce computation. To assess potential security benefits, we evaluated the robustness of quantum-classical hybrid models under six attack settings. Overall, our study maps where quantum layers help and hurt within VLMs, offering a starting point for hybrid VLM design; whether these gains generalize remains open. The code is available at https://github.com/TITANS-Lab-Artifacts/QuantumVLM.

articles.title: From Common Information to Canonical Correlation Analysis and Beyond: Bridging Information Theory, Signal Processing, and Machine Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28978v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many problems in signal processing, machine learning, and neuroimaging provide several jointly observed measurements of one process, each mixing a component common to all of them with a component private to itself, and require the common component to be recovered without supervision. This problem has been studied in several communities, largely independently. Statisticians proposed canonical correlation analysis (CCA), introduced by Hotelling in 1936. Information theorists proposed two notions of common information, due to Gács and Körner and to Wyner. Engineers developed subspace methods for sensor arrays and multiuser communications to design multiview receivers. This tutorial presents the main results and tools each community developed for this problem in a single exposition, and explains the connections that emerge where they meet, distinguishing exact equivalences from special cases and analogies. We develop the information-theoretic foundation from first principles. We then introduce CCA and its extension to several views, followed by the engineering thread from blind multiuser detection to CCA as a blind receiver. Next, we turn to nonlinear CCA, covering kernel, deep, and probabilistic formulations, the conditions under which the common factor is identifiable, and connections to self-supervised learning. We conclude with a discussion of further extensions and open directions. The exposition is self-contained, so that readers from each of these communities can follow the parts developed by the others.

articles.title: Our Own Jev: Typed Decisions in One Forward Pass, from an In-House Judge to Open LoRA Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29052v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A typed decision maps evidence, a question and a fixed set of options to a probability for every option, computed in one forward pass, by reading a language model's logits or a small head over its hidden states, instead of generating and parsing text. The commercial system Jev popularised this System~1 interface, and open reproductions have followed. We report two uses of the pattern. emphPart I describes an in-house System~1 judge that triages about 148K agentic coding session records for a training corpus. It replaces a frontier LLM judge that cost on the order of 1,000 per pass and whose stored labels matched a fresh two-judge consensus on only 26.9% of the sessions where the two judges agreed; a self-hosted frozen backbone with a rank-16 LoRA adapter and a pointer head answers three typed questions in one forward pass, judges 1,000 sessions in about three minutes of one GPU, about 0.06 at a reference rate and roughly 1% of the frontier judge's cost, and keeps every session inside the organisation. emphPart II asks whether a readout that adds no parameters can be competitive and whether training one helps. Applying the public Eikos recipe and corpus of about 25K decisions to three further backbones (1B, 2B and 35B), we read the frozen output layer of a LoRA-adapted decoder. On the 111 public hard items of JevBench our single-seed 35B, developed with those items in view, scores 79.3%, not significantly different from the commercial reference (73.0%, unadjusted p=0.12) and ahead of five open systems after Holm--Bonferroni correction; our 2B is ahead of all four kev checkpoints on the leaderboard. A single-seed ablation finds no detectable benefit from training the 26 letter rows of the output layer, and a retrain on a later corpus release moves the 2B's hard-tier accuracy by 11.7 points, which shows how little small evaluations resolve.

articles.title: Region-Aware Multi-View Inspection Using Deep Learning and Domain-Informed Decision Fusion
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29398v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Automated optical inspection of precision components with tiny surface defects remains challenging when different regions of the same component exhibit different defect characteristics and, therefore, different acceptance criteria. This paper presents a region-aware, dual-model inspection framework that combines instance segmentation of localized seat-region defects with image-level classification of global shaft-region anomalies. Rather than treating these two model detections as sufficient evidence for component rejection, a deterministic decision fusion layer that formalizes industrial Standard Operating Procedures is applied to the model outputs to make the final component level decision. A PLC-synchronized imaging system acquires 18 seat and 18 shaft images over a full 360-degree rotation to provide multi-view circumferential coverage. The framework was evaluated on 380 automotive fuel injector needles, covering representative operational defect types, using identical model predictions in all configurations. Direct model-output aggregation via simple union logic (where any single-view detection flags a rejection) identified all 104 non-conforming components but produced a component level false rejection rate of 57.6%. Inclusion of a complete decision layer maintained the observed non-conforming (NOK) recall of 100% while reducing the false rejection rate to 10.9%, corresponding to an 81.1% reduction in false-positive component decisions. The results demonstrate that formalized manufacturing acceptance criteria can complement sensitive visual models by translating frame-level detections into practical and traceable component-level decisions.

articles.title: When Thoughts Become Memory: Unifying In-Context Learning and Fine-Tuning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29419v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We are the first to give a certified rule for whether unseen data belong in a pretrained model's context or its weights, built on an exact law for their information value. That value, the code length saved on held-out queries, equals in expectation the bits stored about the query, plus a prior repair, minus a decoding loss, for any model, architecture, dataset and task. The law's ceilings certify the choice from one measurement, and an anytime-valid test makes it from held-out queries, with error controlled whenever it stops. Every certificate the ceilings issue on a trained transformer, TabPFN, an occupancy network and a stereo network is correct. The test picks TabPFN over XGBoost and a trained surrogate over an in-context learner on airfoil pressure, calls the better of GPT-2's cache and fine-tune in 61,948 of 64,000 query streams over 32 comparisons, and errs in at most 3.3% of null streams. The law also diagnoses when learning in context helps and when it does not. Deleting part of a context is held-out validation of that part in any model, and adding parts one at a time traces the learning curve in context: one patch that sees a shape feature cuts an occupancy network's code length there a hundredfold, while eight that miss it nearly double it, and one camera that sees the surface beats four in a stereo network. Ranked by this label-free valuation, a kriging learner's three best support cars beat four drawn at random, and on a yes-or-no claim the valuation recovers a published evidence adjudicator, with AUROC 0.91.

articles.title: PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agents via Machine-Checked Integrity Theorems and Scalable Community Trust
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28987v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Persistent memory is a largely undefended surface for injection and poisoning, and the same risk limits memory sharing among agents. We present PerMIT, a memory architecture with provable integrity guarantees under an explicit trust assumption: only user-typed inputs and values confirmed at a gate are trusted. PerMIT mediates the release and use of untrusted environment-derived values through a finite memory interface, while preserving agent-driven multi-turn planning and tool choice. Over this finite interface, we prove two integrity theorems that are also machine-checked in Lean 4, which together ensure that environment-derived memory reaches a sensitive action only if confirmed at the gate and influences the agent's behavior only through what the gate displays. Every attack in our threat model thereby reduces to a single auditable decision, which a human, an LLM verifier, or both can make in practice. On Trojan Hippo, PerMIT records zero observed attack success with self-verification and lightweight verifiers. Because each confirmation is a logged verdict on exact content, endorsements accumulate across users, and sufficiently endorsed items become community-confirmed with no further verification required. Under explicit assumptions, we prove and corroborate in simulation a co-scaling property: as the community grows, the risks of promoting poison and of wrongly evicting benign knowledge fall, while per-user verification effort does not rise. On τ²-bench, communities of up to 90 autonomous agents use PerMIT to build shared knowledge bases with no direct memory injection promoted, and the resulting knowledge significantly improves new agents on held-out tasks, suggesting a path toward agents that safely self-improve at test time.

articles.title: PHD-Hand: A Printable Humanoid Dexterous Hand with Linkage-Driven 3-DOA Digits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29030v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Currently, dexterous humanoid robot hands are widely considered the final hardware bottleneck that hampers generalist robots from physically assisting people at home and work. As conventional tendon-driven designs suffer from high cost, demanding maintenance, poor reliability, and short durability, alternative linkage-driven designs have increasingly gained attention. Despite their potential to avoid the weaknesses of tendon-driven hands, integrating multiple degrees of actuation (DOA) in a single digit with linkage drivetrains is a challenge for design and fabrication. Only a few studies have managed to present functional humanoid hands that are completely linkage-driven and have at least three DOAs per digit without compromising actuator placement and other design preferences. Our work introduces a new linkage-driven hand featuring a unique flexure hinge. Together with elastic drive rods made of spring steel, the linkage drivetrains are significantly simplified. Unlike other linkage-driven designs of similar dexterity, our design does not require many miniature moving parts. As a result, the hand can be fabricated easily with a budget 3D printer. This not only significantly lowers the barrier to entry for using and developing dexterous humanoid robot hand functions, but also allows the hands to be sized much closer to regular human hands. The design offers desirable kinematic advantages as well. A prototype is evaluated for grasping and object manipulation. In addition, this paper presents our latest findings on kinematics and control of the hand.

articles.title: ORSMT: Unleashing the Potential of Satisfiability Modulo Theories for Semantic Verification and Repair in LLM-Based Optimization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29145v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models increasingly automate optimization modeling from natural language problems, producing written mathematics, solver code and a returned report. Verifying one optimization problem across these artifacts requires semantic comparison: unequal models can attain the same objective, equivalent models can use different auxiliary variables, and mutually consistent artifacts can omit the same source requirement. ORSMT provides a typed semantic interface and exact SMT relation queries. It aligns observable decisions, projects auxiliary variables, proves or refutes feasible region and objective relations, localizes refutations to implicated rows or domains and links source texts when available. It then reconstructs one artifact from another, and each adopted candidate passes the required relation checks. Across 3,034 problems and six generator sizes, ORSMT improves the model-code match rate in all 72 benchmark and generator combinations before selection. Protected selection raises the aggregate rate from 43.2% to 88.2% and the share that are both correct and matched from 25.2% to 40.2%. On the 1,905 refuted outputs, certified voting under the shared fallback makes 50.9% of outputs correct and matched, compared with 44.8% for ReLoop and 49.4% for Opt-Verifier. A separate one-round source revision followed by exact reconstruction restores a model-code match for 84.4% of the refuted pairs.

articles.title: SP-HLM: Sparse-Pose-Driven Motion Generation and Whole-Body Control for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30044v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires an effective interface between high-level task policies and whole-body control. Existing interfaces typically rely on a single action representation for both task intent and whole-body coordination. This may burden the high-level policy or leave one aspect underspecified. We present SP-HLM, a framework built on a sparse-pose-driven interface. The interface combines five task-critical body poses with a learned latent motion prior to represent spatial intent and whole-body coordination in complementary forms. SP-VLA, a vision-language-action model, first predicts task-relevant sparse poses and finger joint positions from multimodal observations and language instructions using asynchronous action-chunk inference. Given these sparse targets, SP-MGM, a motion generation model trained through two-stage distillation, reconstructs coordinated full-body motion in real time. A pretrained motion encoder maps this motion to a compact latent representation. SP-GMT, a general motion tracker, then integrates the explicit sparse targets with this implicit motion prior for whole-body control. Experiments in simulation and on a real humanoid robot demonstrate improved motion tracking, whole-body coordination, and loco-manipulation success over existing approaches. Additional results and videos are available on our hrefhttps://sp-hlm.github.io/textcolorblueproject page.

articles.title: Modeling Capillary Heterogeneity in Geological CO2 Storage via Finite-volume Discretization with Interface Conditions
articles.abstract: Capillary heterogeneity plays an important role in determining CO2 plume migration paths and the amount of CO2 that can be stored in geological formations, yet standard numerical simulation schemes require excessive grid refinement to accurately resolve capillary-driven trapping at material interfaces. In this work, we present a finite-volume scheme for immiscible two-phase flow that incorporates discrete interface conditions to enforce local capillary equilibrium at rock-type boundaries. The enhanced scheme,referred to as PPU-C, is based on the standard Phase-Potential Upwinding (PPU) method and utilizes a local nonlinear solver at each material interface to enforce capillary pressure continuity and flux conservation. We extend prior formulations by improving the efficiency of the local solver, incorporating capillary pressure and relative permeability hysteresis, and implementing the scheme within the open-source GEOS simulation framework for direct application to geological carbon storage problems. The method is compared to PPU through four numerical examples of increasing complexity: a 1D gravity segregation case, its 3D extension both in drainage-only and hysteretic settings, and a 2D domain with multiple barriers. Finally, we conclude with a field-scale 2D cross-section based on the SPE-11B benchmark. Results show that PPU-C significantly improves the accuracy of predicted capillary and residual trapping volumes on practical grids with a modest computational overhead that does not exceed 25% in our tests. These findings demonstrate that the use of interface conditions is a practical and efficient numerical technique to accurately model capillary heterogeneity in large-scale CO2 storage simulations.

articles.title: Mechanical Performance and High-Energy Photon Attenuation of a Slag-Based Geopolymer Concrete Incorporating Calcined Brezina Dam Sediments
articles.abstract: This study investigates a slag-based geopolymer concrete incorporating calcined sediments collected from the Brezina dam in Algeria, with a focus on mechanical performance and the potential attenuation of high-energy photons. Ground granulated blast-furnace slag (GBFS) was used as the principal precursor, while calcined sediment and silica powder formed the secondary binder fraction. Four mixtures contained 0, 10, 20, or 30% calcined sediment in the secondary binder fraction. The sediment was dried, ground, sieved to 80 μm, and calcined at 750 ◦C for 5 h. The alkaline activator comprised sodium silicate and 12 M sodium hydroxide, with a reported sodium-silicate-to-sodium-hydroxide mass ratio of 2.5. Specimens received an initial heat treatment at 70 or 80 ◦C for 6, 8, or 10 h, or at 90 ◦C for 6 h, followed by maturation at ambient conditions. The reported results indicate that the 10% and 20% sediment mixtures generally exhibited better mechanical performance than the 0% and 30% mixtures. For the 10% mixture, compressive strength increased from 44.74 MPa after 6 h to 58.41 MPa after 10 h at 80 ◦C; the corresponding values for the 20% mixture were 41.13 and 55.50 MPa. Monte Carlo simulations using GATE/Geant4 for a 6-MV flattening-filter-free photon beam yielded a half-value layer (HVL) of 9.94 cm and a tenth-value layer (TVL) of 27.19 cm for the geopolymer mix. These values were close to those reported for the reference standard concrete (10.11 and 27.69 cm, respectively), while barium-rich concrete showed lower HVL and TVL values. The results support further investigation of calcined dam sediments as a locally available constituent of geopolymer concrete; however, the radiation-shielding findings are simulation-based and require experimental validation.

articles.title: Spontaneous Excitonic Mass Generation in Graphene Monolayers
articles.abstract: Coulomb interactions among graphene's massless Dirac fermions are unusually strong, making graphene a unique testbed for correlated quantum phases and interacting field theories. Among the predicted phases is an excitonic insulator, in which strong interactions drive spontaneous electron-hole pairing and condensation into a superfluid ground state. This transition has evaded experimental observation because unscreened long-range Coulomb interactions renormalize and enhance the Dirac velocity, keeping graphene in a weakly coupled semimetallic regime. Here, we overcome this constraint by decorating graphene with nanoscale metals that screen long-range interactions and suppress velocity renormalization. Scanning tunnelling spectroscopy down to 150 mK reveals a hard spectral gap (2Δ ≈ 14 meV) that emerges strictly at the Dirac point and is strongly susceptible to doping, temperature, and magnetic field --- signatures of a many-body rather than single-particle gap. The gap closes at an anomalously low critical temperature (Δ/kBTc ≥ 100), consistent with a Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless transition, and coincides with a charge-density wave at q = K' - K that reflects intervalley excitonic pairing. Together, these results provide strong evidence for spontaneous excitonic mass generation in graphene, a correlated insulating phase long predicted but never before observed.

articles.title: Intermolecular potential of singlet O4H+ ion II
articles.abstract: The displacement of proton cutting through the OO bridge seen in the established geometry of singlet O 4 H + ion, (a proton-bound dimer of molecular O 2), is focussed by constructiing the relevant ab initio potential energy curves computed at the state of the art multi reference configuration interaction level of accuracy with the augmented correlation consistent triple zeta basis set. The curves are presented for two possible conformers (cis and trans) with distinctly varying profile as a function of back and forth the motion of proton across the bridge along with the detailed account of their modelling. The model can be used to compute absorption and emission spectrum associated with the cis-trans interconversion subject to the Franck Condon principle. The reported spectrum has the potential to serve as a finger print for easy recognition when an experimental electronic spectrum is going to be available. At the moment, no such spectrum exists.

articles.title: Nanoscale Architecture Unifies Electron and Dislocation Transport in Metals
articles.abstract: Thermal transport and plastic deformation in metals are usually treated as separate processes. Here, we show that a stable nanoscale architecture can place a common limit on both. Using a bulk nanostructured Cu–Ta alloy, we identify a dense network of interfaces spaced about 15 nm apart that constrains the motion of electrons and dislocations. This architecture produces a broad thermal-conductivity plateau from about 175° to 375°C, with temperature-dependent behavior returning only when the intrinsic electron transport length becomes comparable to the interface spacing. The same nanoscale spacing also interrupts dislocation motion before high-velocity behavior can develop. Because the Cu–Ta structure remains stable across temperature and loading conditions, these effects can be directly linked to a single persistent structural length scale. These results establish nanoscale architecture as a common design parameter for controlling thermal and mechanical behavior in bulk metals.

articles.title: C³M-OMMT Twin: A Causal Process–Structure–Property Digital Twin for Morphology-Aware Mechanical Optimization of OMMT-Modified PLA in Fused-Filament Fabrications
articles.abstract: The rising need for mechanically reliable and dimensionally stable biodegradable parts made using fused filament fabrication has led to an increased interest in developing organo modified montmorillonite (OMMT) reinforced Polylactic Acid (PLA), however recent research have been primarily focused on how changes to the percentage of fillers used in combination with changes to printing parameters affect the overall physical properties of PLA/OMMT while excluding important relationships such as; the degree of clay exfoliation, melt flow behavior, heat-induced bonding between layers of polymer, topological structure of voids formed during processing, and local fracture sites. In response to these limitations, this study will present C³M-OMMT Twin, a Digital-Twin pipeline that addresses all three critical aspects of OMMT/PLA additive manufacturing including cause/effect relationships of composition and processing conditions, crystallography, and morphologies. ExfoRheo-MAP uses data from X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) to generate a dispersion-intercalation-rheology state vector representing degree of clay exfoliation or aggregations. This physically based representation allows researchers to directly assess and compare the degree of clay dispersion or aggregation across different samples. ThermoBond-Sense will use both the thermal history generated through reconstruction of layer-by-layer heating-cooling cycles and the inter-road healing generated from varied nozzle temperatures, print speeds, layer heights, and raster angles to predict the formation of bonds between adjacent roadways. The goal is to develop a predictive model for determining the optimal levels of each variable necessary for creating materials with consistent bonding characteristics throughout their entire thickness. MorphoFrac-3D will integrate information collected via Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM), micro-computed tomography (micro-CT), and strain field analysis to create a defect-clay-interface graphs. Additionally, it includes a new index called the Clay Void Interface Fracture Susceptibility Index to enable researchers to assess susceptibility to localized failure at specific locations within the samples. CauPSP-Net will couple the graph produced by MorphoFrac-3D with physics-informed causal learning to differentiate between direct and morphology-mediated effects on tensile, flexural, and impact performance of OMMT/PLA composites. ConBayes-Pareto will identify uncertainty-calibrated optimums for material-process combinations. CounterTwinV will validate the predictions made by C³M-OMMT Twin experimentally. It is anticipated that the optimized region developed using this pipeline will be able to increase tensile strength by up to 59–65 MPa, modulus by up to 3.5–4.0 GPa, and flexural strength by up to 88–96 MPa while simultaneously decreasing the void fraction created during processing by up to 35–55% as compared to baseline values in practical scenarios. The development of this sequential architecture will provide researchers with a means of improving prediction accuracy, reduce reliance on trial-and-error experimentation, expose potential failure mechanisms, and define a manufacturing window for producing high-quality, reproducible, and sustainable composite components.

articles.title: Sustainable synthesis of Na2FeSiO4 using rice husk-derived silica: effect of calcination temperature on phase formation and electrical properties
articles.abstract: Na2FeSiO4 is a promising cathode material for sodium-ion batteries; however, using conventional silica sources, such as tetraethyl orthosilicate (TEOS), as precursors in its production increases synthesis costs and limits the process's sustainability. This study investigates a waste-derived approach using rice husk-derived silica as an alternative precursor for Na2FeSiO4 synthesis. The effects of calcination temperature on phase formation, morphology, direct optical band gap, and electrical conductivity were systematically evaluated. Na2FeSiO4 was synthesized via a sol–gel method using NaOH, Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, rice husk-derived silica, and C6H8O7·H2O at a molar ratio of 2:1:1:1, followed by calcination at 500 – 800 °C for 10 h. The samples were characterized using FTIR, TG/DTA, XRD, SEM/EDS, UV–Vis DRS, and an LCR meter. Na2FeSiO4 was identified as the dominant phase, with SiO2 and Na2SiO3 as secondary phases. Increasing the calcination temperature enhanced the formation of the Na2FeSiO4 phase, lattice reorganization, and microstructural consolidation, while the direct optical band gap increased from 2.38 to 2.87 eV. Conversely, electrical conductivity decreased with increasing temperature while remaining on the order of 10-5 Sm-1, with the highest value observed at 500 °C. These findings demonstrate the potential of rice husk-derived silica as a sustainable and cost-effective precursor for Na2FeSiO4.

articles.title: Torrential flooding across a humid Appalachian watershed: historical reconstruction and sub-watershed susceptibility
articles.abstract: Torrential floods remain poorly documented in the humid Appalachian regions of eastern North America, where flood management has traditionally focused on large rivers, snowmelt, and ice-jam flooding. This study examines the spatial variability of torrential flood susceptibility among 86 level-2 sub-watersheds of the Chaudière River watershed (Québec, Canada) by integrating historical reconstruction, catchment morphometry, land-use analysis, and GIS-based multicriteria mapping. Documentary sources covering 1900–2023 identified 53 distinct flood dates and 185 event–locality records. Events occurred predominantly in July and August and were associated with thunderstorms, prolonged rainfall, and tropical or post-tropical weather systems. The analysis revealed substantial morphometric heterogeneity among recurrently affected catchments rather than a uniform physical signature. Historical descriptions and generally low catchment-scale Melton values were consistent with predominantly flood-driven torrential activity, although sediment-rich processes within smaller tributaries cannot be excluded. Settlement surfaces increased between 2000 and 2020, but their hydrological effects were not directly quantified. A susceptibility index combining slope, land cover, and substrate-based runoff potential showed partial correspondence with documented flood occurrence. The proposed approach provides a regional screening framework for identifying catchments requiring detailed hydrological and geomorphological investigation, rather than a predictive assessment of flood probability or risk.

articles.title: Infrastructural Embedding: How Domestic Institutional Configurations Shape Divergent Cross-Border Infrastructure Packages
articles.abstract: Why do providers entering the same infrastructure system make different contributions? Historical-institutionalist international political economy (IPE) links domestic structures to external economic strategy, while infrastructure-finance and infrastructure-power research documents variation in financing models, risk allocation, and network power. This article explains how domestic institutional configurations shape provider contributions through infrastructural embedding: organisational actors apply prior mandates and capacities to outward roles, extend established arrangements across borders, and commit them to defined project components. Process tracing of the Benguela-Lobito rail-logistics system compares China Eximbank and contractor-led railway reconstruction, U.S. development-finance support for Angola’s selected private concessionaire, and E.U.-linked preparation of a logistics platform. Angolan decisions establish project and operating authority, while entry stage defines the task available to each provider. Domestic configurations organise the actors, instruments, and responsibilities through which each task is performed. The evidence shows policy finance paired with contractor delivery, U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) lending and assurance added to an operating concession, and E.U.-linked resources organised around Caála preparation through a multi-level interface. The comparison advances historical-institutionalist IPE by explaining how domestic configurations form divergent package architectures at project level.

articles.title: Deep Learning-Based Non-Destructive Seafood Freshness Assessment: A Systematic Review of Sensing Technologies, Validation, and Deployment Readiness
articles.abstract: Seafood freshness assessment is essential for quality control, shelf-life management, and supply-chain decisions, yet conventional sensory, chemical, and microbiological measurements are often destructive or laboratory-dependent. This systematic review synthesizes evidence on deep learning (DL)-based non-destructive seafood freshness assessment, focusing on sensing modality, model architecture, predictive performance, reference-standard validity, methodological robustness, and deployment readiness. Scopus and Web of Science records published in English from 2021 to 2026 were screened. Of 1,057 identified records, 306 remained after filtering and deduplication; 32 full texts were assessed and 28 studies were included. Four technology families emerged: red-green-blue (RGB) computer vision; hyperspectral, near-infrared, Raman, and fluorescence spectroscopy; colorimetric or fluorescent intelligent sensors; and multimodal or olfactory-sensor fusion. Reported performance was often high, with classification accuracies above 95% and regression R² values above 0.90 in several studies, but comparisons were limited by heterogeneous species, freshness labels, datasets, and validation designs. Studies anchored to total volatile basic nitrogen (TVB-N), total viable count/aerobic plate count (TVC/APC), K-value, thiobarbituric acid reactive substances (TBARS), or biogenic amines provided stronger freshness validation than storage-time or visual-class labels alone. Methodological appraisal classified 22 studies as some concern and six as high concern, with no study classified as low concern. Mobile, edge, portable-sensor, and robotic implementations show translational promise, but external and industrial validation remain limited. Technological maturity therefore depends on biological validity, independent validation, computational feasibility, and real-world deployment, not predictive accuracy alone.

articles.title: Integration of Sentinel-2 Imagery and Field Spectroscopy for Vegetation Spectral Analysis
articles.abstract: Remote sensing plays a key role in precision agriculture and vegetation monitoring due to its specifications to provide rapid and efficient large-scale observations. This field involves the analysis of reflection, absorption, and emission of radiation of different surface features in function of different wavelengths of electromagnetic spectrum. The aim of this study is to evaluate the consistency between spectral signature extracted from Sentinel-2 imagery and collected using a field spectrometer. For this purpose, a statistical comparison was executed using Pearson correlation coefficient (r), coefficient of determination (R²) and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of a specific sampling points. The results indicate that it was an agreement between satellite and field measurements, showing a high values of R² (> 0.90) and a low value of RMSE. Overall, the findings confirm that compared to the spectrometer measurements, the sentinel-2 imagery could accurately differentiate the spectral characteristics of vegetation. On the other hand, the results demonstrate the reliability of Sentinel-2 imagery for vegetation monitoring and highlight its integration with field spectroscopy for improved calibration and validation.

articles.title: Influence of Annealing Treatment on Electrical Steel Characteristics and Electric Machine Performance
articles.abstract: This study experimentally investigates the effect of two annealing routes on the magnetic, core-loss, and electrical characteristics of electrical steel used in a BLDC Motor. Three conditions were evaluated: Sample A subjected to a multi-stage controlled annealing process, Sample B subjected to a high-temperature rapid annealing process, and Sample C retained in the as-cut condition as the untreated reference. Compared with Sample C, Sample A showed a 2.44% increase in (:Bᵣₘₛ), a reduction in (:Hᵣₘₛ), and an increase in permeability. Sample B produced a comparable improvement of 2.20% in 𝐵rms at 50 Hz and 1.5 T. The average core loss decreased from 5.90 W/kg for Sample C to 4.90 W/kg for Sample A and 5.10 W/kg for Sample B. The line inductance increased from 104.90 (:μ:)H to 109.38 (:μ:)H and 107.15 (:μ:)H, respectively, while winding resistance remained nearly unchanged. The short-circuit current decreased from 52.36 A for Sample C to 48.15 A for Sample A and 49.85 A for Sample B. These results demonstrate that annealing significantly influences the magnetic and electrical behaviour of the BLDC Motor core.

articles.title: Oxidation-Induced Directional Iron Exsolution Awakens Interfacial Kinetics in Non-Stoichiometric Polyanion Cathodes
articles.abstract: Non-stoichiometric polyanion cathodes possess intrinsically favorable bulk-ion-diffusion potential, yet they often remain trapped in a kinetically dormant state. Using non-stoichiometric sodium iron phosphate (NFP) as a model system, we introduce mild thermal oxidation as a thermodynamic perturbation strategy. This treatment drives the directional exsolution of high-energy lattice Fe species toward the particle surface. Analysis of this reconstruction process reveals the underlying origin of the sluggish electrochemical response: the kinetic limitation does not arise primarily from the bulk framework, but rather from local Na/Fe antisite defects at the interface, which impose severe steric obstruction and kinetic barriers and thereby block trans-phase ion-transport pathways. Fe exsolution effectively removes these cationic blockages and simultaneously reconstructs a conductive interfacial network enriched in mixed-valence Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺ species and vacancies. By eliminating the interfacial mass-transfer bottleneck, the intrinsic solid-solution Na-storage capability of the framework is released, delivering an initial discharge capacity of 130 mAh g⁻¹. This work elucidates a microscopic mechanism for actively reconstructing local defects through thermodynamic regulation and provides new interfacial-kinetic insight into activating the intrinsic electrochemical activity of metastable frameworks.

articles.title: Tuning the Electromagnetic Response of Co₂Y Hexaferrites through Ni–Zn Substitution and Graphite Addition
articles.abstract: Tuning the magnetic resonance while maintaining sufficient dielectric loss is important for improving microwave absorption in Y-type hexaferrites. In this study, the effects of simultaneous Ni–Zn substitution and graphite addition were investigated in Ba2Co2−xNix/2Znx/2Fe12O22 (x = 0.0–2.0). The powders were synthesized by the citrate sol–gel method and characterized using X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, and magnetometry. Complex permittivity and permeability were measured over 1–18 GHz for paraffin composites containing 80 wt% filler, and the reflection loss (RL) was calculated using transmission-line theory. The coercive field decreased from 651 to 45 Oe with increasing x, while the magnetic resonance frequency showed a nonmonotonic variation. The permeability spectra were well described by a distributed Kittel–Gilbert model with a lognormal resonance-frequency distribution. The fitted median resonance frequency increased from 3.04 GHz at x = 0 to 10.08 GHz at x = 0.5 and then decreased to 2.57 GHz at x = 2. The x = 2 composite showed an effective absorption bandwidth (EAB; RL ≤ − 10 dB) of 3.7 GHz at a thickness of 4.5 mm. Adding 8 wt% graphite relative to the filler mass increased the EAB to 4.0 GHz at a reduced thickness of 3.0 mm, with a minimum RL of − 38 dB at 5.1 GHz and 4.0 mm. Overall, the results show that Ni–Zn substitution can effectively tune the magnetic resonance, while a controlled amount of graphite can improve impedance matching and absorption at lower thicknesses.

articles.title: The Representability Gap: Massive-Graviton Physics Cannot Be Held by Virtual-World Physics Engines but Survives the Low-Precision Number Formats of Artificial Intelligence
articles.abstract: Background. The graviton, the hypothetical quantum of gravity, is often invoked in speculation about future artificial intelligence (AI) and immersive virtual worlds, yet a single graviton is widely regarded as undetectable and its only quantified observable property is an upper bound on its mass. Whether massive-graviton physics could even be represented inside the computational systems that run virtual worlds and AI has not been tested.  Methods. Two computational experiments with known truth were run. Experiment 1 asks whether the Yukawa correction implied by a graviton at the current 90% credibility bound (mg ≤ 2.42 × 10−23 eV/c2) is representable in six floating-point formats, using a 60-digit reference, a naive in-format evaluation, and a velocity-Verlet orbit integrator of the kind used in physics engines. Experiment 2 injects the massive-graviton dispersion phase into noise-free inspiral waveforms and measures, for each format, the ratio between the time-and-phase-aligned dispersion residual and the rounding error, and the test AUC of a neural-network discriminator trained on rounded inputs (90 training runs).  Results. The correction is unrepresentable at every virtual-world scale: it first becomes storable in float64 at 5.4 × 108 m and in float32 at 1.25 × 1013 m (about 84 AU). Naive in-format evaluation manufactures phantom corrections up to 9 × 1016 times the true value, and a float32 orbit at 1 AU deviates by 834 km where the true effect is 8 m. In AI formats the opposite holds: at the bound every format, including 8-bit FP8, preserves the residual (representational SNR 9.7 to 2 × 107), with representational floors 3 to 4,500 times below the bound for formats from FP8 to float32; classifier accuracy did not degrade with precision.  Conclusions. Precision is the binding constraint for virtual-world engines but not for AI, where noise and learnability bind first. Any claim that a graviton-scale effect appears in a simulated world should be accompanied by an explicit representability check.

articles.title: Intelligent Signature Verification System Using Hybrid Deep Learning with WOA-GGO Driven Feature Selection
articles.abstract: The paper-based signature verification continues to be important despite increasing adoption of digital repositories, creating a demand for accurate and reliable signature verification systems. Biometric authentication provides a secure and efficient solution compared to conventional verification methods such as identity cards and magnetic strip cards. This paper proposed a hybrid signature verification framework to improve the verification accuracy through effective feature selection and score level fusion. The framework consists of four main stages. First, preprocessing is performed using an improved median filtering process and image resizing technique to obtain the high quality signature images. Next ResNet, global and local features are extracted from the preprocessed images. In the feature selection stage, a hybrid Walrus Optimization Algorithm integrated with Greylag Goose Optimization (WOA-GGO) is used to identify the optimal features. Finally, signature verification was performed using the hybrid deep learning model combining RNN and Bi-LSTM. An improved score-level fusion technique integrates the outputs of both classifiers to produce the final verification result. The proposed framework was evaluated using the GPDS 1-150 and CEDAR datasets. Experimental result shows that the RNN + Bi-LSTM model achieved maximum accuracy values of 0.973 and 0.971 performing better than LinkNet, LSTM, EfficientNet, Bi-GRU, LeNet and Bi-LSTM. The effectiveness of the proposed framework was also validated through various performance and statistical analyses.
authors: CH V K N S N Moorthy

articles.title: Input-Architecture Synergy in Precipitation Nowcasting: Assessing the Need for Physical Anchors using the ANDeL Framework as a Case Study
articles.abstract: High-resolution precipitation nowcasting in West Africa requires forecasting approaches that can represent rapidly evolving convective rainfall while using information from atmospheric and land-surface variables, yet it remains unclear whether the relative performance of autoregressive (AR) and non-autoregressive (NA) deep-learning architectures depends on the atmospheric and land-surface information provided as input. This study examines whether degradation in AR forecasts depends on input composition rather than being an inherent property of recursive forecasting. Using a 17-configuration ablation experiment, we systematically compare AR and NA models across precipitation-only, atmospheric, land-surface and combined input configurations. We found AR performance decreased substantially for several configurations containing highly variable atmospheric or the full multivariate inputs, NA models exhibited greater robust performance to these configurations suggesting that their non-recurrent forecasting structure may be less sensitive to the accumulation of input-related errors. Conversely, configurations incorporating slowly varying soil moisture or static land-surface information produced some of the strongest AR results, with the precipitation plus soil moisture configuration achieving the highest mean CSI (0.2087) among the configurations evaluated. For heavy rainfall, the soil-moisture AR configuration also maintained higher spatial skill than its NA counterpart across the evaluated lead times, coinciding with reduced spatial spreading in the forecast examples. The results therefore support a data-aware approach to architecture selection in which the usefulness of AR and NA forecasting depends not only on forecast horizon but also on the composition and temporal characteristics of the available inputs.

articles.title: Alcohol-Mediated Controlled Cationic Photopolymerization of Vinyl Ethers for Programmable Additive Manufacturing
articles.abstract: Photopolymerization-based additive manufacturing has become a powerful platform for fabricating complex functional materials; however, the development of controlled cationic photopolymerization systems remains limited by the reliance on specialized chain-transfer agents and the lack of versatile resin-design strategies. Herein, we report an alcohol-mediated photoinduced controlled cationic polymerization of vinyl ethers and demonstrate its application in high-resolution digital light processing (DLP) 3D printing. Readily available alcohols function as chain-transfer regulators to control cationic chain growth through terminal acetal formation, enabling the synthesis of poly(vinyl ether)s with tunable molecular weights under mild photoirradiation. The resulting polymerization exhibits rapid curing while maintaining effective control over polymer network formation, allowing direct translation into DLP printing. By independently varying the crosslinking density, vinyl ether structures, and alcohol regulators, the mechanical properties of the printed materials can be programmed over a broad range while preserving excellent printing fidelity and fabrication efficiency. Furthermore, the compatibility of this strategy with structurally diverse, commercially available, and industrially accessible vinyl ethers and alcohols enables the preparation of degradable networks, polyurethane-like elastomeric materials, and other functional polymer systems through modular resin design. This work establishes alcohol-mediated controlled cationic photopolymerization as a general, cost-effective strategy for molecularly programming polymer networks and substantially expands the chemical space available for photopolymerization-based additive manufacturing.

articles.title: Sparse Mamba Decoder for Quantum Error Correction: Efficient Defect-Centric Processing of Surface Code Syndromes
articles.abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is essential for building fault-tolerant quantum computers, requiring decoders that are simultaneously accurate, fast, and scalable. Most state-of-the-art neural decoders achieve high accuracy but process the full dense syndrome array of size O(d2R) regardless of the actual error rate, where d is the code distance and R is the number of measurement rounds. At physically relevant error rates (p ≈ 0.1%), fewer than 5% of syndrome entries contain active detection events—yet existing decoders process the entire syndrome volume. We introduce the Sparse Mamba Decoder (SMD), a defect-centric neural decoder that processes only the k active detection events using a 13-dimensional feature representation per defect and a Mamba state-space backbone, achieving O(k) complexity. Across depolarizing, uniform circuit-level, SI1000, and Google Sycamore experimental benchmarks, SMD reduces the MWPM logical error rate by up to 49% at d ≤ 5 under SI1000 noise, runs 95–467× faster than the Tesseract near-MLD decoder and 232–463× faster than Belief Matching, and maintains nearly constant latency (24–57 μs) across d = 3–9 under uniform circuit-level noise. On the Sycamore experimental dataset, the SMD ensemble matches or slightly surpasses the dense Mamba decoder of Lee et al. All results are obtained on commodity NVIDIA GPUs with 7.5–16M parameters, without specialized accelerators.

articles.title: Predictive Degradation Modelling of Solar Encapsulants: A Deep Learning Approach to IEC 61215 Thermal Cycling
articles.abstract: The operational lifespan of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems relies heavily on the thermo-mechanical stability of Ethylene-Vinyl Acetate (EVA) encapsulants. However, evaluating long-term durability using traditional accelerated physical aging protocols, such as IEC 61215 thermal cycling, is highly resource-intensive and often fails to capture complex, nonlinear degradation kinetics. To bypass these limitations, this study introduces a computational machine learning framework to forecast the structural degradation of mica nanoclay-reinforced EVA nanocomposites. A high-fidelity, physics-informed synthetic dataset (1,220 data points) was generated to model tensile strength decay and microcrack density evolution across four formulation variants (0, 1, 3, and 5 wt.% mica nanoclay) over a simulated 1,500-cycle exposure horizon (-40°C to + 85°C). A Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) recurrent neural network and a Random Forest (RF) ensemble regressor were deployed to map these defect evolution parameters. Both architectures demonstrated exceptional predictive accuracy, with the RF achieving an R² of 0.994 and the LSTM achieving an R² of 0.993. The computational models mathematically validated that an optimal 5 wt.% filler concentration significantly delays crack coalescence, extending the 50% mechanical endurance limit. This data-driven approach fundamentally accelerates the reliability-driven design of next-generation, environmentally resilient photovoltaic modules without the need for multi-month destructive testing.

articles.title: From Soft to Hard Constraints in Physics-Informed Extreme Learning Machines: Analysis and Algorithms
articles.abstract: Physics-informed extreme learning machines (PIELM) cast the numerical solution of partial differential equations (PDEs) as a single linear least-squares problem by fixing the hidden-layer weights at random, yet the standard soft-constraint formulation augments the PDE residual system with boundary equations, requiring a single coefficient vector to reconcile two competing objectives. A Gram-matrix eigenvalue analysis reveals that this competition suppresses boundary influence along directions where the PDE block dominates, and that uniform row scaling cannot reduce the resulting spectral spread. To eliminate this structural imbalance, we embed Dirichlet boundary conditions directly into the trial function via a lifting term and a boundary-vanishing distance function, so that the resulting least-squares system involves only the interior PDE residual while the one-shot closed-form structure is preserved. Boundary conditions are thereby satisfied to machine precision without entering the coefficient solve. Across seven Dirichlet benchmarks covering Helmholtz, Poisson, Kovasznay Navier--Stokes, wave, and nonlinear reaction equations on convex, non-convex, and curved domains, the hard-constrained formulation yields identically zero boundary residuals and reduces relative L² errors by up to seven orders of magnitude under identical random bases and collocation layouts, at comparable computational cost. The code and data accompanying this manuscript will be made publicly available at https://github.com/xgxgnpu/Physics-informed-vibe-coding/tree/main/HC-PIELM.

articles.title: On-board International Space Station Verification of Autonomous Emulsification Lab-on-Chip Payload: TIGERS-X Project
articles.abstract: Sustained deep-space exploration under space programs places critical constraints on pharmaceutical and nutritional resupply, motivating fluid-processing systems, including emulsification, that can operate reliably in microgravity. Conventional terrestrial emulsification relies on high-shear, buoyancy-assisted processes unavailable in free fall, while passive, capillary-driven static mixers offer a compact, low-power alternative better suited to spaceflight constraints. This paper reports the design, ground verification, and on-orbit validation of TIGERS-X, a low-cost, teleoperated lab-on-chip experiment cube for the International Space Station (ISS). Ground testing, including chemical safety, electromagnetic compatibility, and structural verification, confirmed compliance with ISS pressurized-payload requirements. TIGERS-X uses multi-channel Tesla-valve microfluidic devices and optical diagnostics to observe oil-water mixing and emulsification behavior, operating under ground control via YAMCS-based command and telemetry with no astronaut interaction required beyond installation and removal. Across a 10-day flight campaign, TIGERS-X returned near-real-time video of fluid behavior under sustained microgravity, resolving a duration and environment inaccessible to prior parabolic-flight studies. Quantitative colorimetric analysis revealed substantial, geometry-dependent oil-water phase redistribution within short microfluidic channel lengths, extending prior ground- and parabolic-flight-based findings to realistic orbital conditions.
