articles.title: Acoustic control of Rayleigh-regime liquid-jet breakup using a through-hole MHz transducer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29899v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This experimental study demonstrates MHz-order acoustic control of Rayleigh-regime liquid-jet breakup using a compact through-hole lithium niobate thickness-mode transducer integrated at the nozzle exit and driven near its 6.7 MHz resonance. Jet dynamics were measured by high-speed shadowgraphy at 50,000 fps, and breakup lengths were obtained from instantaneous jet-length records using an autocorrelation-based method that identifies statistically separated breakup events. Acoustic actuation produced visible interfacial corrugations and reduced the normalized breakup length, L_b/d, for both water and glycerol--water jets. In water, the response was threshold-like at low Weber number and weakened as the jet velocity increased to We ~ 50. A reduced-order threshold correlation, fit to the water amplitude and velocity sweeps, captured this abrupt shortening and the subsequent loss of actuation efficacy. More viscous glycerol--water mixtures shortened immediately at low forcing, indicating a distinct acoustic-coupling regime rather than a universal collapse of the water response. A wetting-control experiment showed that liquid spreading at the nozzle base can also shorten the jet, so the measured response reflects coupled radiation-pressure forcing, capillary-wave feedback, and wetting-mediated disturbance injection. Resolved droplet tracking further showed that MHz excitation changes the visible gate-crossing droplet population, although sub-resolution mist and micron-scale atomization were not measured. These results establish through-hole MHz actuation as a compact route for modifying free-surface jet breakup and provide a repeatable image-analysis protocol for experimental-fluid-mechanics measurements.

articles.title: Electrically Pumped Quadratic-Soliton Mode-Locked Laser in Lithium Niobate Nanophotonics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30079v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Femtosecond mode-locked lasers are the workhorse of modern photonics, enabling optical atomic clocks, frequency combs, precision spectroscopy, and ultrafast signal processing. Bringing them onto nanophotonic chips promises miniaturized ultrafast systems, yet combining femtosecond pulse generation with electrical pumping remains a major challenge, rooted in a trade-off between the speed and energy efficiency of mode-locking mechanisms. Kerr-based mechanisms offer nearly instantaneous response but typically require high intracavity peak powers that are difficult to achieve with nanophotonic-compatible semiconductor gain. Conversely, semiconductor saturable absorbers enable strong nonlinear responses at low energies but are limited by their slow carrier dynamics. Here we break this trade-off by introducing quadratic-soliton mode-locking based on a quadratic nonlinear interferometer (QNLI): an effective saturable absorber built from cascaded second-order nonlinearity in periodically poled lithium niobate nanophotonics, with a measured sub-20 fs response time. Through hybrid integration with an electrically pumped semiconductor gain element, we demonstrate a self-starting quadratic-soliton mode-locked laser with femtojoule pulse energies, operating in single- and multiple-soliton states. Quadratic solitons arise through the QNLI's dissipative and dispersive nonlinear response, which we confirm with a modified complex Ginzburg-Landau equation in agreement with measurements. By combining soliton formation with intracavity electro-optic modulation, we generate 750 fs pulses with flat-top spectra. Our engineerable, ultra-energy-efficient, electrically powered laser provides the critical source for fully integrated ultrafast photonic circuits in lithium niobate nanophotonics that natively offers electro-optic control, quadratic wavelength conversion, pulse compression, and spectral broadening.

articles.title: Pushing beyond the memory barrier in propagation algorithms with randomization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28845v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Performant classical tools for simulating quantum circuits are important for benchmarking and supporting upcoming quantum devices. Pauli propagation offers promising capabilities, but deep circuits usually cause a rapid growth in the number of Pauli strings and can quickly exhaust the available memory. In this work, we introduce a randomized protocol that combines a specialized resampling schedule, merging, and a controlled amount of bias to keep the propagating Pauli sum within any prescribed memory budget. Additional computational resources can then be spent on embarrassingly parallel repetitions that systematically improve the estimate. Building on the open-source library PauliPropagation.jl, we show that 1) increasing memory of each simulation reduces the error systematically more than outside averaging, 2) resampling just enough to apply the next gate delays variance accumulation and gives better error-per-time trade-offs than more aggressive resampling, and 3) a small, controlled bias is crucial in cutting down variance and pushing far beyond unbiased randomization. The resulting framework can reproduce deterministic calculations while requiring several orders of magnitude less memory.

articles.title: Bounds on Attainable Rate Modulation in Fermi's Golden Rule
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29404v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Controlling transition rates is a central objective across quantum optics, condensed-matter physics, and chemical physics, encompassing processes such as spontaneous emission, energy and charge transfer, spin relaxation, and chemical reactions. Although Fermi's golden rule provides a powerful framework for calculating such rates of weakly coupled transitions, conventional calculations require the interaction to be specified in advance; the range of rate responses attainable over a broader interaction space remains unknown. We formulate spectral-overlap golden-rule rates as quadratic forms of the interaction and derive rigorous bounds on rate modulation over a specified interaction space. As an example, application to energy transfer from a donor to a molecular vibration coupled to an optical cavity reveals that enhancement and suppression depend jointly on the interaction and cavity detuning, including continuous reversal of the rate response for a fixed interaction. The same approach may elucidate rate control for other golden-rule processes, including excitation-energy transfer, nonadiabatic electron transfer, nonradiative electronic transitions, vibrational and spin relaxation, and spontaneous emission.

articles.title: Photon Correlations Control Quantum Fisher Information in Coherent Multidimensional Spectroscopy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29422v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coherent multidimensional spectroscopy probes interactions and dynamics of molecular systems through nonlinear optical signals. Quantum light excitation has been explored as a means of controlling these signals, raising the question of how excitation-light correlations affect the precision of molecular parameter estimation from the emitted signal. In this work, we show that photon-number correlations and two-photon coherence play distinct roles in encoding molecular information in the emitted rephasing signal. In the weak-emission regime and within the single Schmidt pair approximation, we derive a normally ordered information law in which the joint photon-number moment and the squared magnitude of the two-photon coherence weight the amplitude and phase sensitivities of the molecular response, respectively. For matched temporal modes and mean photon numbers in each input mode, two-mode squeezed vacuum enhances both weights relative to coherent excitation, whereas independent displaced squeezing preserves the amplitude weight but reduces the phase weight. The background population and its parameter dependence also affect the total quantum Fisher information, which therefore cannot be inferred from the coherent mean-field signal alone. We derive a leading-order bound on its enhancement over coherent excitation when the background population is nonnegative and common to the compared sources. These findings provide criteria for selecting excitation sources according to how the target molecular parameter affects the amplitude and phase of the response.

articles.title: A Broadband Room-Temperature Design for the Einstein Telescope
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29863v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The unique underground location of the Einstein Telescope (ET) is expected to substantially suppress seismic and gravity-gradient noise, providing a favorable environment for gravitational-wave detection at low frequencies compared with surface-based observatories. The baseline ET design aims to achieve broadband sensitivity through a xylophone configuration, in which separate cryogenic and room-temperature interferometers are optimised for low- and high-frequency gravitational-wave detection. However, achieving the target low-frequency sensitivity introduces substantial technical complexity caused by vertical suspension thermal noise, vibrations of the cryocooler, and detuned optical configuration. In this paper, we demonstrate an alternative, entirely room-temperature, fully resonant, single-interferometer architecture that addresses these challenges and achieves broadband sensitivity superior to that of the conventional ET xylophone configuration. Using mature fused-silica suspension technology, recent advances in optical coatings, and novel inertial isolation, we show that 4-m-long fused-silica fibres can meet the required suspension thermal-noise performance. We further demonstrate that vibrations, optical rigidity, and quantum back-action noise can be controlled through appropriate design of the interferometer, test mass suspensions, optical seismometers, and quantum states.

articles.title: Superconducting parametric amplifiers based on arrays of unequal Josephson junction elements
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29901v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Impedance matching is a crucial feature of an amplifier used to increase its instantaneous bandwidth and is typically achieved using static LC resonators. Here we show an approach to impedance matching in parametric amplifiers using arrays of unequal Josephson-junction-based elements (rf/dc SQUIDs, SNAILs, etc). The elements act either as small-footprint flux-tunable inductors forming an impedance-matching circuit, or 'active' amplifier elements which result in amplifier gain. We develop an analytical theory describing these systems, predicting a quasi-non-periodic amplifier frequency and gain modulation with applied flux and the broadening of gain bandwidths. We demonstrate this in devices using arrays of flux-focused SNAILs where flux biasing varies across the array. We find instantaneous bandwidths of 200 MHz with >17 dB of gain centred at sim5.4 GHz in a device without a static impedance matcher. This broadening of amplifier bandwidth is stable with >100 MHz bandwidth at 17 dB gain across >1.2 GHz tunable bandwidth. Our analytical model captures flux dependence and qualitatively reproduces gain-bandwidths giving confidence in our understanding of these systems and allowing operational figures of merit to be optimised in future devices.

articles.title: Topographically Forced Stationary Waves Can Explain the Near-Surface Zonal Winds Observed by Huygens on Titan
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29930v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Titan's equatorial superrotation is associated with climatological retrograde (westward) near-surface winds at low latitudes, as consistently simulated by Titan general circulation models. However, the Huygens probe measured prograde (eastward) near-surface winds, contrary to the expected circulation. We investigate whether these observations reflect localized forcing by large-scale topography, using paired three-dimensional dry simulations with and without topography in the Titan Atmospheric Model. We find that topography generates longitude-locked, vertically structured zonal wind anomalies that reproduce key features of the Huygens wind profile in the lowest few kilometers. Helmholtz and spectral analyses show that this structure arises from the superposition of several vertically varying low wavenumber modes. A predominantly rotational, topographically forced stationary zonal wavenumber s=1 response provides a major eastward anomaly throughout the lowest 2 km, whereas a locally divergent s=4 response consistent with a gravity wave, opposes it near the surface. Weaker s=2 and s=3 responses also vary vertically and contribute eastward anomalies near the surface. Combined with the retrograde zonal-mean circulation, these modes produce a Huygens-like profile characterized by prograde flow within the lowest 1 km and shear toward retrograde flow aloft. The paired simulations establish their topographic origin, while coherence with the corresponding terrain-forcing components demonstrates that the responses remain phase locked to the forcing. Similar but weaker stationary responses are simulated near the planned Dragonfly landing site, providing baseline expectations for interpreting its future atmospheric measurements. This study demonstrates how large-scale topography can generate localized departures from Titan's zonal-mean circulation and highlights the importance of stationary waves.

articles.title: Hyperfine structure splitting for the triplet 2³S(L = 0)-state in the two-muonic helium {}³He μ₂ atom
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.33059v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The hyperfine structure splitting for the triplet 2³S(L = 0)-state in the two-muonic helium {}³He μ₂ atom is determined to high accuracy. Such a structure arises as a result of hyperfine (or spin-spin) interaction between the triplet two-muonic shell and non-zero spin of the central helicon nucleus. Our result for the hyperfine structure splitting is Δ approx 5.1623403103010 · 10⁷ MHz, where the standard uncertainty has been evaluated as ± 10 Hz.

articles.title: Fast Evaluation of the Sixth-Order Time-Convolutionless (TCL6) Master-Equation Generator
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.18806v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Higher-order time-convolutionless (TCL) master equations provide systematic corrections for non-Markovian dynamics in open quantum systems, but their time-ordered integrals become increasingly costly to evaluate. Direct quadrature of the Hadamard-reduced sixth-order (TCL6) generator at all Nₜ sampled times requires O(Nₜ³) operations at fixed system dimension. We derive an exact reduction for a finite-dimensional system coupled through one Hermitian operator to a stationary centered Gaussian bath. By separating operator coefficients from scalar time-dependent spectral densities, the complete TCL6 time series is reduced to cumulative sums and first-order recurrences, one-dimensional causal convolutions, and an exact dyadic recursion for interlocked sums. With the algorithm, evaluating the complete TCL6 time series requires O(Nₜlog²Nₜ) operations. These reductions enable fast, practical simulations of non-Markovian dynamics involving multiphonon and multiphoton processes in open quantum systems.

articles.title: Online Open-World Wafer Defect Discovery using Hyperdimensional Computing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28949v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional wafer defect analysis relies on offline, closed-world classifiers that fail to detect novel, unseen defect signatures emerging during continuous semiconductor manufacturing. To address this, we propose WaferHDC, an online open-world wafer defect discovery framework based on hyperdimensional computing (HDC). The memory-centric architecture of WaferHDC enables rapid anomaly detection and grouping of recurring failures into compact hypervector representations. This allows the memory space to dynamically scale with new defect modes without retraining a static classifier or archiving entire raw wafer history. WaferHDC first models normal spatial distributions, then dynamically groups recurring failures into persistent defect memory without labels or predefined class counts. It outperforms the strongest online baseline by 13.3 p.p. in adjusted Rand index and 10.5 p.p. in normalized mutual information on the industry-standard WM-811K dataset. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of WaferHDC for continuous and open-world wafer defect analysis.

articles.title: Nominate-then-Adjudicate: LLM-Assisted One-Pass and Per-Instance MIP Solver Tuning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29391v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mixed-integer programming solvers expose hundreds or even thousands of parameters whose best setting varies per instance, yet per-instance search is prohibitively expensive. We frame this as configuration for heterogeneous Big Data optimization workloads and propose a nominate-then-adjudicate pipeline built around two design choices. First, a fixed portfolio is sampled once and reused across instances, removing per-instance configuration search at inference; on the evaluated families, the resulting shortlist retains substantial oracle headroom, making selection within it the empirical focus. Second, the fixed 20-feature representation can map structurally different instances to the same vector, preventing a feature-only selector from distinguishing them even when they prefer different configurations. The foundation model receives no task-specific weight updates, and selection is one-pass: one model call and no solver calls at inference. The study represents structural Variety through distinct formulation families and decision Value through solver-performance outcomes; the one-call, zero-solve protocol specifies the decision interface and leaves end-to-end latency unmeasured. Among comparisons exceeding a 20% practical-difference threshold, the complete adjudicator records 538 wins and 185 losses against the top nominee, while its win rate against the default rises from 84.9% to 90.2%. Against per-instance configuration baselines under a matched one-pass protocol it leads the cluster-level methods and the best-performing evaluated per-instance baseline, ISAC+.

articles.title: Automating ML for Science: Can Frontier Agents Climb Scientific Hills in the Wild?
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28763v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Frontier coding agents are increasingly framed as end-to-end automated researchers, and ML for science offers a demanding test of that promise: improving a scientific model often requires domain insight beyond routine ML engineering. We introduce Agent4Sci, a long-horizon testbed for measuring how far today's agents can improve the published best models on scientific ML benchmarks, spanning 20 benchmarks across 11 domains. Rather than ranking agents on a leaderboard, Agent4Sci asks what kinds of progress agents can make on these tasks under in-the-wild conditions, and where they fall short. Empirically, today's frontier agents advance the published best on every benchmark, with Claude Opus reaching 10.4% mean relative improvement and no run flagged for academic misconduct. These gains, however, come almost entirely from a bag of ML-engineering tricks rather than research-level insight. Trajectory analysis surfaces three recurring limitations in this setting: novelty miscalibration, resource under-utilization, and rapid collapse into local engineering sweeps. Lightweight plug-in skills for research ideation, experiment management, and scheduled checklists raise Claude Opus from 10.4% to 20.1% and Codex from 4.4% to 8.1%, while yielding more diverse, domain-relevant interventions. Agent4Sci gives the community a way to track and push frontier agents from ML engineering toward domain insight on real-world ML-for-science problems. Code and data are available on GitHub (https://github.com/maszhongming/agent4sci) and Hugging Face (https://huggingface.co/datasets/MingZhong/agent4sci).

articles.title: Combining Long-Term Memory and LLMs Comes at a High Cost: From Prompt Injection to Persistent Compromise
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28810v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The widespread adoption of generative artificial intelligence in recent years has brought a parallel rise in prompt injection and jailbreak attacks. By embedding malicious instructions, these exploits manipulate language models to bypass intended behavior and operational boundaries. In traditional chatbots, such attacks are confined to a single session because state memory is not preserved across conversations. However, persistent memory features in modern conversational interfaces enable cross-session attack propagation, establishing a threat vector known as memory injection. This work explores this emerging vulnerability in leading LLM-as-a-service platforms, highlighting its real-world severity and the need for countermeasures. While existing literature focuses on violations tailored to specific platform features, we present a general threat model. We demonstrate that all NIST attack goals are collectively achievable across ChatGPT Instant 5.3, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Gemini 3 Flash under this model. We also show that memory injections can exploit multiple attack vectors, including personal memories, projects, skills, organization instructions, and Model Context Protocol (MCP)-connected resources. Our findings reveal that all evaluated services can be manipulated to persistently spread disinformation, generate harmful content, or simulate offline unresponsiveness, even in fresh sessions. In the particular case of Claude, shared-memory features allow an attacker to compromise multiple users within an organization and also exfiltrate user prompts. To address these vulnerabilities, we derive defense mechanisms from our proposed threat model and foundational cybersecurity principles. Our analysis indicates that nearly half of these mitigations remain unimplemented across the target services. Datasets and attack artifacts are available at https://github.com/PedroBarcha/Memory-injection.

articles.title: HyperDrone: Simulation-to-Reality Transfer at Millions of Frames per Second
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28950v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present HyperDrone, an extremely fast quadrotor simulator focused on high-performance batch rendering that is more than 20x faster than existing state-of-the-art batch quadrotor simulators. HyperDrone combines highly optimized multirotor dynamics with HyperLux, a new ray-tracing engine that supports Nvidia OptiX, Vulkan, Apple Metal and WebGPU backends that takes full advantage of modern ray-tracing hardware, capable of running both components entirely on the GPU. HyperLux renders RGB, depth, semantic/instance segmentation, surface normals and optical flow observations at configurable levels of fidelity, including reflections, realistic lighting, motion blur, anti-aliasing, and Physically Based Rendering (PBR). Even in the highest-fidelity settings, HyperLux achieves millions of Frames Per Second (FPS) on consumer-grade GPUs while rendering realistic 3D scenes. We demonstrate the merits of HyperDrone by training a vision-based yaw-control policy purely in simulation and transferring it to a real small-scale quadrotor (Crazyflie) with a camera, running completely onboard.

articles.title: Compressing Onboard Language Models for Space Robots under a Behavioral-Fidelity Requirement
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29302v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Language models are being explored as the interface through which space robots interpret operator commands and select among verified skills. Running them onboard calls for low-bit compression, and flight use adds requirements that generic post-training quantization leaves implicit: a fixed memory budget and storage format, a static artifact under configuration control, and behavior close to the full-precision model validated on the ground. We treat compression as a ground-segment step and study QSelect, which composes one static low-bit model from compatible AWQ, GPTQ, and AutoRound checkpoints by assigning each linear module to one quantizer family and scoring every substitution at the final next-token distribution. The default fidelity mode needs no labels or tuned thresholds and accepts a substitution only when the forward KL divergence from the BF16 reference decreases; an optional target-adapted mode adds answer likelihood on a small labeled set. On DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, and Llama-3.2-3B at 3 and 4 bits, composed models reach lower mean held-out perplexity than every single-family model in all six settings, and the fidelity mode lowers perplexity and KL further. In a matched scaffold, final-output scoring gives lower held-out KL than representation-similarity scoring in all 12 paired runs. With labels from training or development splits of the evaluated task families, the target-adapted mode raises 3-bit pooled accuracy on the two Llama models by 4.3 and 4.5 points over the best single-family model. At 3 bits, unquantized embedding and output layers make up 43-46% of the packed artifact. All evaluations use general-domain benchmarks on a ground GPU; space-domain tasks and flight hardware are left to future work.

articles.title: Causal Discovery via Transformed Low-Rank Quantile Surfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.16931v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose Low-Rank Quantile Surfaces (LRQS), a bivariate causal model in which, in the causal direction, an unknown monotone transformation of the conditional quantile surface admits a low-rank functional decomposition. LRQS subsumes location-scale noise models and post-nonlinear heteroscedastic noise models, while allowing multiple quantile bases to represent changes beyond location-scale effects. We prove generic identifiability of LRQS: the transformed quantile surface is low rank in the causal direction, whereas reverse representability under the corresponding constraints occurs only for exceptional, fine-tuned cause marginals. We provide a nonparametric causal score using a fitting procedure that alternates between rank-constrained approximation of discretized quantile surfaces and isotonic estimation of the unknown monotone transformation. Experiments on synthetic mechanisms with higher-rank distributional shape variation and strong nonlinear distortions, together with standard bivariate benchmarks, show that LRQS is especially effective when conditional distributional shape or observation distortion goes beyond existing location-scale assumptions.

articles.title: Charts as Epistemic Actions for Experience-Driven Agentic Data Analysis
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30072v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data agents built on ReAct-style loops now execute complex analytical workflows over structured data, yet their intermediate reasoning still runs almost entirely through text. Human analysts instead move between numbers, tables, and charts, reading visual evidence to expose trends and anomalies that text summaries drop. We ask whether charts can serve as internal epistemic actions inside a data agent's reasoning loop, and how to teach an agent to use them. We first build probe{}, a suite of 200 controlled tasks under four matched interface conditions, and find a persistent gap between what agents can read and what they choose to use. Agents score as well from self-generated charts as from numeric output, yet plotting access alone does not translate into consistent use. Task slices show that charts lead on temporal, pattern, and anomaly reasoning, while text leads on precise reading and conditional verification. We then propose method{}, which distils two families of experience from conditioned trajectory rollouts. One family records how to select and verify analytical operations, and the other records when to invoke text, charts, or both. A trajectory judge scores outcomes and labels intermediate steps, and a validation gate admits only experience that improves held-out performance. On three held-out benchmarks with four LLM backbones, method{} raises analytical accuracy and visual evidence quality over matched baselines, and backbones that never drew charts begin using them, all without touching model parameters.

articles.title: The CIDOC CRM Periodic Table: Documentation You Can Test to Support the Adoption of Scientific Research Ontologies for the Humanities
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28650v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The CIDOC CRM family is not only a schema for museum collections. Its extensions formalise the apparatus through which research knowledge is produced and justified: CRMsci models scientific observation and measurement, CRMdig the provenance of digital processes, CRMinf inference and belief. Together they constitute a schema for research data, and the obstacle to their adoption is documentary rather than theoretical: four normative documents, four code conventions, and eighty-nine typed links crossing document boundaries. This paper presents the CIDOC CRM Periodic Table, a single-page browser rendering 131 classes and 480 property entries from CIDOC CRM 7.1.3, CRMsci 3.2, CRMdig 5.0 and CRMinf 1.2.1 as one navigable surface, with two inference facilities: a one-step triple builder admitting only the class-property combinations licensed by declared domains, ranges and the subclass closure, and a multi-step path finder enumerating property chains between two classes. Because all loaded models are merged into one code-keyed dictionary before the hierarchy closures are computed, both resolve chains that cross model boundaries; we document the addition of CRMsci and the three cross-model tests it made possible, and report preliminary uptake signals from 56 months of analytics, with the reading they support.

articles.title: Who Verifies the Builder? Toward Independent Assurance for Agent-Produced Software
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28667v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coding agents can now implement a specification, write and run tests, repair failures, and declare the result ready for release. When the same agentic system produces both the software and the evidence of its correctness, a passing test suite is no longer independent evidence: visible tests become an optimization target, code and tests may share one misinterpretation of the specification, and the builder's own tests may simply be incomplete. This paper argues that agent-produced software requires an assurance plane that is structurally independent of the build plane. We characterize four gaps between stakeholder intent and production (requirement, conformance, evaluation, and model gaps) and identify which of them verification can close. We propose a framework that separates building from verifying, introduces a Verification Contract stating what must be demonstrated before release, and organizes verification in a specification-first phase without access to the implementation and an implementation-aware phase based on mutation analysis, property-based testing, and fuzzing, with an assurance report that leaves the release decision to a human. We evaluate the framework in a pre-registered study on three stateful services, two of them written by third-party models, and an EvalPlus pilot. The builder's programs were correct, but its own tests missed subtle interactions: a verifier in a fresh context detected more of the 46 seeded faults than the builder's tests (Holm-corrected p = 0.006) and surfaced the ambiguities of the specification, at the price of rare false oracles. A verifier from another provider did not add detection.

articles.title: StyleStream 2.0: Fast and Controllable Streaming Voice Style Conversion
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28940v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Voice style conversion (VSC) aims to transform a source utterance to match the timbre, accent, and emotion of a target voice while preserving linguistic content. StyleStream 1.0 introduced the first streamable zero-shot VSC system with state-of-the-art conversion quality, but remained limited in two ways: approximately 1s end-to-end latency on consumer hardware, and the lack of a text-based interface for designing or editing target voices. We present StyleStream 2.0, a fast and controllable streaming VSC framework that addresses these limitations. To reduce latency, we train a few-step pixel MeanFlow model and further fine-tune it with autoregressive feedback inspired by Self Forcing, improving robustness under streaming inference. This reduces end-to-end latency to 520~ms on a consumer GPU, a 2x speedup over StyleStream 1.0, while maintaining conversion quality. To enable controllable style manipulation, we remove the mel-spectrogram context and instead route target style information through a compact style embedding. In this embedding space, we train a unified text-conditioned flow matching model that supports both text-based voice design, which maps natural language prompts to voice styles, and instruction-based voice editing, which modifies a specific attribute of a source utterance while preserving the rest. Experiments show that StyleStream 2.0 achieves the strongest target style fidelity on VSC, voice design, and voice editing, while remaining competitive on intelligibility and non-edited attribute preservation.

articles.title: GRAFT: Restoring the Missing Sampling Interface in Continuous Diffusion Language Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29136v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Continuous diffusion language models generate a whole sequence in parallel, never drawing a single word at any intermediate step; only the final step turns embeddings into text. Models such as ELF now report autoregressive-level quality at a fraction of the sampling steps of discrete-token diffusion models, and this design principle -- no step-wise discretization -- is what their own ablations credit for the gain. We show that this same principle carries a hidden cost: a collapse of the lexical long tail. Measured against held-out human text, ELF's output matches the human rate on common words almost exactly, yet its rarest words appear at only 0.30x the human rate, a gap that does not close from 105M to 652M parameters and that no sampler setting these models expose can reach. A same-size GPT-2, in contrast, spans zero to above the human rate by its decoding rule alone. We trace the difference to what continuous diffusion models lack: with no step that ever draws a discrete word, every step is instead driven by an average over the candidates still in play, and averaging a rare candidate together with the common word competing for its slot lands on the common word. An autoregressive model avoids this because its decoding rule samples one candidate rather than averaging over all of them. We propose GRAFT, a training-free method that grafts this missing choice back onto a frozen model: while the model is still undecided, GRAFT commits the rare words the average would otherwise discard, then regenerates the sequence from scratch with those commitments held in place. Across three ELF scales and on LangFlow, an independent continuous dLLM, GRAFT restores the rare-word share of generated text from 0.42-0.77x the human rate to 0.82-1.10x, a relative gain of 34-109%, and moves the entire word-frequency profile closer to human on every model tested, by 2.7x on ELF-B and 12x on LangFlow.

articles.title: Conflicted Records: Typed Adversarial Contracts for Auditable LLM Output Quality Enforcement
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29669v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM-generated records increasingly populate production information systems where they are treated as data assets subject to the same quality expectations as records from operational databases. A single such record can simultaneously satisfy and violate a quality rule: a grounded fact adjacent to a hallucination, a useful answer adjacent to a stereotype. Classical data cleaning cannot resolve this because the two judgments are incompatible over the same span; a single LLM judge cannot either, since it shares the training biases that produced the conflict. Existing interventions such as prompt engineering, chain-of-thought, and RLHF reduce surface error rates but provide no audit trail and cannot distinguish genuine remediation from blanket suppression. The question is whether a deterministic check over structured inter-agent records can catch the defects that referential checks alone miss. We present BiasGuard-D: two adversarial roles drawn from distinct model families exchange typed claim documents, a three-model quorum adjudicates by majority vote, and a combined referential-plus-semantic invariant validates the verdict. The semantic component fires on verdicts referential checks miss; removing the iterative loop drops invariant satisfaction sharply. The deliberation layer transfers from stereotype to hallucination remediation on HaluEval QA with only role-framing changes, raising right-answer recovery by 49 percentage points; the triage gate required a cross-family second auditor to maintain recall on objective hallucination. Every claim, vote, and instruction is stored as a typed record giving operators a provenance trail auditable under emerging AI regulations.

articles.title: Schiff Base Polymer and Its Reduced Derivative: Synthesis and Comparative Adsorption toward Cu(II)
articles.abstract: Schiff bases are well-established as strong ligands for heavy metal ions due to their electron-rich nature. Herein, a Schiff base-derived adsorbent was facilely synthesized via polymerization of p-phenylenediamine and glutaraldehyde, followed by reduction, for efficient Cu(II) removal.SEM observations revealed uniform spherical particles with diameters ranging from 0.3 to 1.5 µm.. FTIR analysis indicated the formation of imine linkages and their partial reduction during the hydrothermal treatment. TGA and acid-stability tests further demonstrated that the reduction treatment enhanced the stability of the polymer in acidic media, although its thermal stability decreased slightly.Batch adsorption experiments under varying pH, initial Cu(II) concentration, and contact time revealed that the poly-Schiff base and its reduced derivative exhibited maximum adsorption capacities of 138.30 and 234.17 mg·g⁻¹, respectively, both achieving over 76% of their equilibrium capacities within 30 minutes. Comparative FTIR and XPS analyses before and after adsorption indicated that while the poly-Schiff base adsorbed Cu(II) mainly through electrostatic attraction and coordination, the reduced adsorbent additionally facilitated the reduction of Cu(II) to Cu(I), which thus enhanced its adsorption performance.

articles.title: Recalibrated Nitrogen-Oxide (NOx) Emission-Index Model for Hydrogen Combustion Aircraft Engine Performance Analysis
articles.abstract: Aviation contributes to climate change through both cotwo and non-CO2 effects. Hydrogen can eliminate direct in-flight CO2 emissions, but its combustion still produces nitrogen oxides (NOx). Reliable NOx prediction during early engine development remains challenging because detailed models are computationally demanding, whereas reduced-order models have limited validation. This study evaluates and recalibrates an existing p3T3-based NOx emission-index model using combustor-inlet pressure, temperature, and equivalence ratio as inputs. Additional experimental and computational data compiled from the literature reveal substantial deviations in the original model across different combustor designs and operating conditions. Recalibration increases the cross-validation coefficient of determination (R²) from 0.54 to 0.77. A lognormal uncertainty distribution is also derived to quantify variability in the model predictions. The updated model is implemented in MAPLE and applied to a representative hydrogen-powered A320 mission. The recalibrated model predicts higher NOx emissions than the original model, although the predictions remain lower than those for kerosene combustion under corresponding conditions. Substantial uncertainty remains, highlighting the need for broader validation data. The proposed model provides a computationally efficient approach for uncertainty-aware NOx estimation in hydrogen aircraft-engine performance analyses.

articles.title: Design-Point Transfer With Conformal Calibration for SRAM Reliability Sign-Off Across PVT Conditions
articles.abstract: SRAM yield requires per-cell failure probabilities of  10-6 to 10-12 at every process, voltage, and temperature (PVT)  condition. We evaluate cross-PVT estimators against importance sampling (IS) truth at all 242 unseen conditions of a SkyWater  130-nm foundry bitcell and an ASAP7 7-nm FinFET cell (read  and write), cross-checked by plain Monte Carlo and a second IS  proposal. A Gaussian tail with the exact margin moments errs by  up to 11.9 decades, so moment surrogates fail through tail shape,  not extrapolation. Extrapolating per-lobe reliability indices is  accurate for the FinFET cell but unsafe by up to 1.9 decades for  the planar cell, whose failure direction rotates across PVT. We  transfer each lobe's design point, correct it with one SPICE run  per lobe, which removes the first-order error, and calibrate the  result: split-conformal margins, computed from IS on a random  subset of the sign-off conditions, bound the probability of an  unsafe acceptance at a randomly selected condition (a marginal,  not grid-wide, guarantee), and undecided conditions escalate to  IS. With 20 calibration conditions (nominal risk 0.15), no  calibrated decision was unsafe, and the minimum operating  voltage read from the conformal upper limit lay −1 to +34 mV  from IS, whereas FORM, the unguarded transfer, and moment  surrogates were unsafe by up to −7, −10, and −219 mV. Signed  off this way, a 1-Mb macro targeting 99.9 % yield reached at  least 99.88 %, versus 99.66 % with FORM-class estimators and  near zero with moment surrogates, using 3.1–4.9 times fewer  SPICE runs than IS everywhere.

articles.title: Does hiding the post-processing from a memory-limited eavesdropper raise the noise tolerance of QKD? Timelocked advantage distillation and the 20% barrier
articles.abstract: Advantage distillation (AD) raises the finite-key threshold QBER of decoy-state BB84 from 9.5% to 17.3% [1]; asymptotically two-way post-processing tolerates 20%, and Bae and Ac´ın showed that an adversary who stores her probes until the AD parities are announced attains this limit, while one forced to measure each probe beforehand is held off until the 25% entanglement limit. We ask what a quantum computational timelock on the post-processing announcements can buy for this protocol, treating the parities, the block partition and the bases separately. Hiding the parities buys nothing: we prove that for every block size the best measurement made before the parities are known attains the adaptive Helstrom value, so the key length in the min-entropy accounting is the collective-attack value, 17.66% at 1014 pulses against the 17.30% certified by the entropic- uncertainty bound of Ref. [1]. Hiding the partition is different: the protocol of Ref. [1] partitions the sifted key at random after the quantum phase, so an adversary whose memory is shorter than the time between the probes of a block cannot bring them together. Modelling her by role-blind per-probe measurements, an assumption we state rather than derive, the Helstrom benchmark, which a numerical search over identical measurements does not improve at odd block sizes, gives 20.8% (Shannon) and 20.7% (min-entropy) at b= 9, 19.4% and 20.6% in a post-selection sensitivity check, with 25% as asymptote. Whether a memory holding many probes without the partition can do better is open; at up to six probes a joint measurement recovers most of the adaptive value, so at these sizes the gain rests on locality. Hiding the basis leaves the BB84 guessing probability unchanged at one- and two-bit blocks and, for six-state, shrinks the memoryless gain by an order of magnitude at two- and three-bit blocks.

articles.title: A Stabilized Mixed Hybrid Finite Element Framework for Large-Deformation Poromechanics with Torsion: Application to Transmural Perfusion and Vascular Hemodynamics
articles.abstract: Intramyocardial perfusion and wall mechanics involve finite deformations, tissue anisotropy, and interstitial fluid flow subject to combined chamber pressurization and torsion. In standard displacement-based finite element formulations,nearly incompressible solid matrices and steep pressure gradients frequently induce volumetric locking, pressure oscillations, and degraded flux fields across the wall. To address this, a mixed hybrid finite element method (MHFEM) is formulated for large-strain Biot poromechanics in cylindrical coordinates with coupled out-of-plane torsional shear (ur,uθ, uz). Fluid flux is discretized using lowest-order Raviart-Thomas spaces (RT0), while Lagrange multipliers on element boundaries enforce normal flux continuity and exact local mass conservation. An exact, one-dimensional analytical solution for an inflated and twisted thick-walled porous cylinder is derived to evaluate asymptotic convergence and quantify fluid pressure, solid deformation, and shear stress. Axisymmetric simulations under physiological and hypertensive conditions indicate that torsional twist reduces peak endocardial fiber stress by 45.5%, relieving compressive drivers of subendocardial vessel collapse. In models of concentric hypertrophy with elevated systolic cavity pressures (180 mmHg), the mixed hybrid scheme maintains smooth, monotonic pore pressure distributions (L2 error = 0.01%),whereas standard Q1/P1 formulations exhibit spurious pressure oscillations and elevated volumetric errors (L2 = 12.75%).

articles.title: Quantification of sidewall defects and surface passivation strategies in blue InGaN/GaN micro light emitting diodes
articles.abstract: The efficiency of GaN-based micro-light-emitting diodes (µLEDs) degrades severely as the device size decreases, a phenomenon known as size-dependent efficiency droop. This degradation is primarily driven by an increased surface-to-volume ratio, where plasma-induced damage during dry-etching generates non-radiative recombination centers at the mesa sidewalls. To clearly elucidate the impact of these process-induced defects, this study investigates the physical extent of sidewall damage and its quantitative effect on the recombination dynamics of blue InGaN/GaN µLEDs across a size range of 5–100 µm. Spatially resolved micro-cathodoluminescence (MCL) mapping reveals a distinct damaged region approximately 1 µm along the mesa periphery. Furthermore, electrical characterization confirms that leakage current scales inversely with diode diameter, a challenge that is effectively mitigated through KOH wet etching and SiO2 passivation. By correlating the size-dependent shift in peak quantum efficiency current density (Jpeak) with the MCL-measured damage width using a modified ABC recombination model, we quantitatively extracted the defect density of the sidewall region. Our analysis indicates that the density of non-radiative recombination centers within the 1 µm-thick sidewall region is approximately 10–20 times higher than that of the bulk material. These results provide a rigorous physical basis for understanding the "efficiency cliff" in µLEDs and underscore the critical need for defect management in the sub-10 µm regime.

articles.title: Monitoring Air Pollution Dynamics of NO2 and SO2 in Sri Lanka Using Sentinel-5P from 2019 to 2024
articles.abstract: Air pollution monitoring in developing nations is constrained by sparse ground-based infrastructure, making satellite remote sensing an essential alternative. This study analysed the spatiotemporal dynamics of nitrogen dioxide (NO2) and sulfur dioxide (SO2) across all 25 administrative districts of Sri Lanka from 2019 to 2024 using Sentinel-5P TROPOspheric Monitoring Instrument (TROPOMI) Level-3 satellite data integrated with Geographic Information Systems (GIS). Monthly raster maps were generated from Near Real-Time (NRTI) and Offline (OFFL) datasets processed through Google Earth Engine, with column densities converted to estimated surface concentrations in parts per billion (ppb). Results revealed persistently elevated NO2 concentrations in the western coastal corridor (Colombo, Gampaha, and Kalutara), attributable to high traffic density, urban growth, and industrial activity. SO2 hotspots were concentrated around industrial point sources in Puttalam and Kalutara, particularly near thermal power generation facilities. Both pollutants exhibited pronounced seasonal variability driven by southwest and northeast monsoon patterns, with lower concentrations recorded during high-rainfall months. A marked reduction in NO2 was observed during the 2020 COVID-19 lockdown period, corroborating the anthropogenic origin of urban emissions. Comparison of NRTI and OFFL products demonstrated complementary utility for short-term event detection and long-term trend analysis respectively. These findings provide a cost-effective, spatially comprehensive framework for national air quality management and environmental policy planning in Sri Lanka.
authors: P. G. R. N. I. Pussella

articles.title: From spatial attribution to mesh decisions in nonlinear moisture-threshold calculations
articles.abstract: This study links local flux sensitivity to mesh selection for moisture-threshold calculations in a synthetic coupled heat and moisture model. The analysis addresses three practical questions: where a flux change affects the endpoint, how that influence varies with the diffusion law, and how the tested meshes compare in reference difference under recorded CPU budgets. Coupled tangent propagation and a face-resolved adjoint provide consistent endpoint derivatives, with a maximum relative difference of 3.7×10⁻⁷ in six matched checks. A kernel for a fixed constitutive perturbation changes by less than 0.17% under the final spatial refinement in three cases. Cross-law tests resolve surface concentration and signed cancellation, providing a spatial basis for comparing mesh choices. The cost comparison charges recorded pilot, construction and solve stages, including unsuccessful attempts. In the baseline exponential case, surface grading has lower recorded cost and a smaller reference difference than the tested goal strategy. The goal grid gives a smaller finest-grid reference difference for the strong positive-floor case. A derivative-guard test separates endpoint improvement from constraint satisfaction and detects time sensitivity in the difficult exponential case. A conservative synthetic control quantifies a 9.77% endpoint increase from latent cooling. The study provides an interpretable, cost-accounted procedure for assessing numerical drying endpoints within the tested constitutive laws and operating conditions.

articles.title: Sustainable application of natural dyes on wool fibers pretreated with Chitosan/Propolis Nano composite and its antimicrobial Characteristic
articles.abstract: Natural dye derived from madder root extract was used for dyeing wool because it is eco-friendly and non toxic.. The wool fibers were treated with chitosan/propolis nano composite, before being colored with a natural madder dye using microwave and ultrasonic methods. The fastness properties, color strength, color data was measured for treated and untreated fibers. and the results indicated that the treated fibers exhibited higher results than the untreated fibers. Dye concentration, time of dyeing and pH factors of the dyed wool fibres were investigated. The results showed that wool fibres treated with the tested composite exhibited higher results than the untreated.. Chitosan and propolis nanocomposites exhibit antibacterial properties against some dangerous pathogens. The results showed that the morphologies and microstructure of the treated and untreated wool fibers were examined using scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The surface of the raw wool fibers is rough. The treated wool fibers swelled in comparison to the untreated fibers. The diameter of the fibers increased due to treatment. The antimicrobial activity of the natural dye under examination was good, and the antibacterial activity of the natural dyes under study was improved by the composite. The aim of this study is the production of smart textile fibers used for manufacture of hand loom carpet.

articles.title: Microwave-Plasma-Engineered Ti3C2TX -TiO2 -SnO2 Heterostructures for Room-Temperature Hydrogen Sensing
articles.abstract: Hydrogen, as a high-density and zero-carbon energy carrier, is crucial for global clean energy transition, yet its ultralow ignition energy and wide explosive concentration range (4–75%) impose critical demands on gas sensing technologies. Conventional metal oxide semiconductor sensors suffer from high operating temperatures and limited low-concentration detectability, while pure MXene materials are restricted by ambient oxidation and layer agglomeration. To address these issues, we synthesize a ternary Ti3C2TX-TiO2-SnO2 composite via LiF–HCl hydrothermal etching of Ti3C2TX MAX followed by microwave plasma chemical vapor deposition oxygen–argon plasma modification with varied MXene/SnO₂ ratios and O2/Ar volume ratios. The phase composition, microstructure, and surface chemical states are characterized by X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, respectively. Results demonstrate that the optimal MTS-1-15%-40min sample, processed under low-oxygen plasma (O2/Ar = 15:85), well preserves the layered Ti3C2TX conductive framework while inducing controlled surface oxidation to TiO2 and constructing high-density TiO2–SnO2 n–n heterojunctions with abundant oxygen vacancies and Ti3+ defects. This optimized heterostructure achieves a room-temperature response of 32.36% toward 1000 ppm H₂, an ultralow detection limit of 1 ppm, excellent selectivity against interfering gases, good humidity tolerance up to 50% RH, and outstanding long-term stability over 17 days with 94.5–97.5% retention. The enhanced performance arises from the synergistic interplay of oxygen vacancy-enhanced gas adsorption, the high-conductivity MXene electron transport channel, and heterojunction-modulated carrier dynamics. This work offers a viable plasma-assisted strategy for room-temperature, low-power hydrogen detection.

articles.title: Target-Induced Stimuli-Responsive Liquid Crystal for Colorimetric Detection of Aflatoxin B1 via MnO 2 Nanosheet- Mediated Catalysis
articles.abstract: Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) poses a severe threat to global food safety, necessitating the development of rapid, label-free, and simple detection strategies. This study presents a novel colorimetric biosensing platform for AFB1 detection based on target-induced stimuli-responsive liquid crystal (LC) emulsions and MnO2 nanosheet (MnO2 NSs)-mediated catalysis. Within this system, glutathione (GSH) is encapsulated in sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS)-stabilized LC droplets to serve as a responsive gate. In the absence of AFB1, a specific aptamer electrostatically sequesters the cationic surfactant hexadecyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB), preserving the integrity of the LC droplets and allowing the intact MnO2 NSs to efficiently catalyze the oxidation of 3,3’,5,5’-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) into a yellow chromophore. Conversely, the presence of AFB1 triggers specific aptamer-target binding, which releases CTAB to interact with the LC interface, causing the rapid ejection of the encapsulated GSH. The released GSH subsequently reduces and decomposes the MnO2 NSs, preventing TMB oxidation and generating a distinct “color-off” signal. Under optimized conditions, this sensor exhibited a linear dynamic range from 0.2 to 1.0 ng/mL with a calculated limit of detection (LOD) of 0.73 ng/mL. Furthermore, the platform demonstrated exceptional specificity against other common mycotoxins and achieved satisfactory recovery rates ranging from 92.18% to 108.23% in diverse real food matrices, including sunflower seeds, soy milk powder, and milk. Validated by high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), this simple, cost-effective, and highly responsive strategy offers a robust visual tool for the real-time monitoring of AFB1 in practical food applications.

articles.title: Multi-Wavelength Speckle Illumination Digital Holography for Parasitic-Reflection Suppression and Macroscopic Topography Reconstruction
articles.abstract: Digital holography enables full-field surface reconstruction with high axial sensitivity, but coherent illumination makes it susceptible to parasitic reflections. We present a multi-wavelength method using spatially diverse speckle illumination to suppress reflections from axially displaced interfaces while extending the unambiguous height range. At each wavelength, phase-shifting holograms are recorded for independent speckle realizations. The reconstructed object fields are calibrated with matching mirror-reference fields and coherently averaged. Owing to the finite axial correlation length of the speckle field, contributions from the selected reconstruction plane are preserved, whereas displaced contributions decorrelate and are progressively suppressed. Measured axial correlation widths for illumination numerical apertures of 0.02, 0.04, and 0.08 agree well with theory. For a microscope slide, averaging 100 realizations at an illumination numerical aperture of 0.08 reduces normalized amplitude noise and phase noise by factors of approximately five and six relative to plane-wave illumination. For a coin viewed through a coverslip, spatial height noise decreases from 54.3 µm to 5.1 µm while preserving surface features. Three gauge-block surfaces spanning 20.5 mm are reconstructed with mean relative heights agreeing with nominal values within 2 µm. The method retains numerical refocusing without mechanical axial scanning.

articles.title: Influence of microstructure on the erosive-wear resistance of JIS SKH57 high-speed tool steel
articles.abstract: Recently, to improve the service life of components used in surface treatment equipment under severe wear environments, high Cr cast irons are increasingly being replaced by cast steels with compositions equivalent to Mo-based high-speed tool steels. The purpose of this study was to investigate the relationship between the erosive-wear resistance and microstructure of JIS SKH57, a representative high-speed tool steel manufactured by self-hardening mold casting. The microstructures of the as-cast, as-quenched, and tempered samples were examined using scanning electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction, and differential scanning calorimetry. It was demonstrated that a slower cooling rate after solidification resulted in the formation of various secondary carbides within the matrix, in addition to primary carbides precipitated along the grain boundaries. Crucially, tempering at 525°C significantly enhanced the wear resistance of the experimental cast steel, which is primarily attributed to the prominent secondary hardening effect. The erosive-wear mechanism was further discussed in terms of surface hardening, which is associated with increased dislocation density and the volume of strain-induced martensitic transformation from retained austenite.

articles.title: The Al-Mizan Al-Mutakamil Relational Framework: Discrete Scale Operators, Galactic Kinematics, and Cosmological Expansion
articles.abstract: I present a unified, rigorous theoretical formulation of the Al-Mizan Al-Mutakamil rela-tional framework. I replace continuous particle dark matter halos and a fine-tuned cosmo-logical constant with a discrete relational scale-step operator acting on baryonic angular-momentum flux tensors. I derive the Mizan Master Equation governing state evolution across discrete scale steps k ∈ N, obtain the continuum limit of the non-local scale-step kernel Rk(r, Rc, k), and calibrate the framework globally against 175 rotationally supported galaxies from the Spitzer Photometry and Accurate Rotation Curves (SPARC) database us-ing solely the observed baryonic mass distribution Mbar(r). With strictly three global scalar constants—an amplitude normalization A0 = 5.234951 (log10 A0 = 0.7189), a mass-scaling exponent γ = −0.138325, and a relational scale-step ratio exponent KGlobal = 0.978294—I achieve a median galaxy-by-galaxy RMS residual of 0.1157 dex and a global mean residual bias of −0.0079 dex across approximately 3400 radial data points, matching the empiri-cal intrinsic scatter floor of the Radial Acceleration Relation. The negative mass-scaling power γ naturally accounts for the elevated mass discrepancies of low-surface-brightness dwarfs without artificial dark-matter cores. I further derive the dual-trace scale factor of the Al-Musi’a expansion sector, rectify the algebraic derivation of the cosmic acceleration transition time tacc (a¨ = 0), obtain the exact physical root xacc = (√33 − 5)/4 · Ωm/Ωv, and demonstrate that the transition occurs at zacc ≈ 2.15. Numerical evaluation of the AlMizanCosmologyPipeline against DESI BAO and RSD data yields enhanced comoving distances and a suppressed peak fσ8(z) ≈ 0.295. I construct the covariant relational stress-energy tensor from the off-diagonal coherence operator, prove its conservation, and supply a thermal decoherence mechanism that accounts for the observed mass–gas offset in systems such as the Bullet Cluster. All equations, proofs, tables, and quantitative predictions are retained without omission.

articles.title: Contact resistance and wave damping limit thermal-wave impedance matching in layered Maxwell–Cattaneo–Vernotte conductors
articles.abstract: At very short times heat can propagate as a damped wave with finite speed, as described by the Maxwell–Cattaneo–Vernotte (MCV) equation. We give a closed-form Laplace-domain solution for a finite layered slab under a surface temperature step, with a thermal contact (Kapitza) resistance Rc at the interface, in a 2 × 2 matrix form that applies to any number of layers. At short times the temperature front is reflected at an interface according to the thermal-wave impedance Z = e/ √ τ , where e is the thermal effusivity and τ the relaxation time, so two materials can transmit the front without reflection even when their effusivities differ. The front carries only a fraction exp(−Σ) of the applied step, where Σ is half the transit time measured in relaxation times, so this matching matters only at times comparable with τ. Contact resistance enters the front coefficients only through the product ZRc. For gold films, measured contact resistances give ZRc of about 10 to 200, so the contact controls the reflection. The MCV and Fourier models can still predict reflections of opposite sign: −0.12 and +0.46 for gold on sapphire. A finite-volume solver reproduces the predicted front amplitude to within 1%.

articles.title: Equatorial Atmospheric Variability Modulates Carbon and Energy Fluxes in a Wallacean Tropical
articles.abstract: Wet tropical montane forests are critical components of the global carbon cycle; however, conventional seasonal indices often oversimplify the responses of these forests to climate anomalies. Prevailing perspectives suggest that extreme droughts, such as those induced by the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO), consistently reduce the carbon sink capacity of tropical forests. This study challenges this generalization by applying a novel methodological approach: space–time wavenumber–frequency filtering of high-resolution eddy covariance data (2013–2017) from Tropical rain forest Lore Lindu, Indonesia. This technique enables the separation of high-frequency synoptic influences from the Madden–Julian Oscillation (MJO), Kelvin Waves (KW), and Equatorial Rossby Waves (ERW) from background climate conditions. The findings indicate weak daily coupling between carbon assimilation and Latent Heat Flux (LE), with gross primary production (GPP) variability more strongly linked to incoming shortwave radiation. Surface-layer soil moisture from ECWWF ERA5-Land remained relatively high throughout most of the observation period, further supporting the conclusion that short-term carbon flux variability at this site is primarily driven by energy availability. Convective phases associated with the MJO and ERW coincided with reduced incoming radiation and lower GPP. In contrast, the GPP response to Kelvin Wave passage varied with background ENSO state: during the 2015–2016 El Niño, positive GPP anomalies were observed around peak KW passage, whereas under normal and La Niña conditions, the response was predominantly negative. These results underscore the significance of high-frequency equatorial atmospheric variability in modulating ecosystem carbon and energy fluxes and suggest that synoptic-scale processes can alter ecosystem responses within broader seasonal climate anomalies.

articles.title: Characterising Surface Urban Heat Island in Ibadan, Nigeria: Hot- Spot Clustering and Relationships With Vegetation and Land Cover
articles.abstract: Rapid, often unplanned, urban growth in Nigerian cities is reshaping the surface energy balance and intensifying urban heat. This study characterises the Surface Urban Heat Island (SUHI) of Ibadan, one of the largest cities in West Africa, using Landsat thermal remote sensing, and examines how Land Surface Temperature (LST) relates to vegetation and to the spatial clustering of surface heat. LST and NDVI were derived for the 2025 dry season from Landsat 8 and 9 Collection 2 Level 2 Surface Temperature data, assembled as a cloud-masked median in Google Earth Engine, and all analysis was carried out in ArcGIS Pro. A metropolitan urban core was compared against a surrounding rural ring; the heat island was measured both as an urban-minus-rural difference and along urban-to-rural transects; the LST-NDVI relationship was quantified, and statistically significant heat clusters were identified with the Getis-Ord Gi* statistic. Mean LST across the study area was 35.03 degrees C, ranging from 27.84 to 47.60 degrees C. The urban core averaged 39.77 degrees C against 34.73 degrees C for the rural ring, giving a SUHI intensity of 5.04 degrees C, and the transect profiles showed surface temperature peaking over the built-up centre and falling toward the vegetated periphery. LST and NDVI were strongly negatively correlated (r = -0.93, R2 = 0.86), with the regression LST = 43.8–18.7 x NDVI. Hot-spot analysis identified statistically significant heat clustering over 25.1 percent of the study area, dominated by a high-confidence hot core covering about 345 square kilometres, while significant cold clusters (27.7 percent) occupied the vegetated surroundings. Mean LST by land cover ranked built-up (39.35 degrees C) and bare land (38.12 degrees C) warmest and vegetation (33.60 degrees C) and water (31.76 degrees C) coolest, a built-up to vegetation contrast of 5.75 degrees C. These results identify where targeted greening and cooler surfaces would deliver the greatest relief, and provide an evidence base for heat-aware urban planning in Ibadan.

articles.title: Crystal structure and electrochemical analyses of a multi-component cocrystal of cobalt(II) complexes of pyridine-2,6-dicarboxylic acid: Improving energy storage performance of hybrid device using redox active Electrolyte
articles.abstract: A cobalt(II) cocrystal consisting of mononuclear, dinuclear and trinuclear complexes, with the overall composition, [Co13(Pydc)10(PydcH)6(H2O)24].14H2O (1) (Pydc2− = Pyridine-2,6-dicarboxylate) has been synthesized and its structure been established by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. The crystal structure of the compound shows that it is an aggregate of seven complexes, including: two mononuclear [Co(Pydc)(Pydc-H)]− complexes, four dinuclear species {two of each type, [Co2(Pydc)2(H2O)5] and [Co2(Pydc-H)2(H2O)5]2+} and a trinuclear [Co3(Pydc)4(H2O)4]2− complex. To unearth the practical electrochemical applications of compound 1, three and two-electrode assemblies were utilized to construct the cell. Fabrication of a battery device, constituting of Co cluster with activated carbon (AC) demonstrated the specific capacity of 99.3Cg− 1, energy density 20.4 Whkg− 1 and power density 825 Wkg− 1. Dunn’s method was employed to distinguish between capacitive and diffusive controlled mechanisms. The capacitive behavior of asymmetric Co//AC cell was enhanced by adding a redox active species, such as K4[Fe(CN)6], which exhibited the specific capacity of 99.3Cg− 1, energy density 35.3 Whkg− 1 and power density 1280 Wkg− 1. The cyclic stability of 97% was achieved even after 5000 GCD cycles. Depending on the good initial findings of the electrochemical analysis, the electrode qualifies as a promising candidate for an efficient electrode material for ultra-modern reserves of energy application.

articles.title: Battery-Aware Finsler Geometry for Energy-Optimal Routing of Electric Vehicles
articles.abstract: The increasing adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) has created a need for route-planning strategies that account not only for travel distance but also for battery consumption, acceleration tendency and road-gradient effects.Conventional shortest-path methods generally represent transportation cost through scalar edge weights and may therefore overlook directional differences in EV energy demand. In this work, a battery-aware Finsler-geometric framework is developed for energy-aware EV route optimization. The road environment is represented as a differentiable manifold, and adirection-dependent Finsler-type cost function is constructed from a Riemannian travel component and normalized energetic corrections associated with battery demand, desired-speed variation, and uphill motion. A physically interpretable EV energy model is first formulated by considering inertial, rolling-resistance, aerodynamic and gravitational forces together with drivetrain efficiency and regenerative braking. The physical battery energy, acceleration-related energy, and uphill gravitational energy are then evaluated independently for the resulting trajectories. The proposeddirectional acceleration term is interpreted as a first-order surrogate based on the directional variation of a prescribed desired-speed field, rather than as the instantaneous vehicle acceleration itself. A numerical experiment compares distance-based, physical-energy-based and Finsler-based routing strategies on the same directed grid. The results show that the shortest route may require substantially greater battery energy, whereas the proposed Finsler-based route provides a direction-dependent compromise between travel distance, battery demand, acceleration tendencyand road-gradient effects. The proposed framework is presented as a numerical Finsler-type route-selection model whose regularity and positivity are verified on the computational domain used in the experiment.

articles.title: Saddlepoint Approximation and Central Limit Theorem for Densities in high dimensions
articles.abstract: We study the saddlepoint approximation (SPA) for densities of sums of high-dimensional random vectors, allowing the dimension d to grow with the sample size n. For averages of i.i.d.random vectors in mathbb R^d, we obtain an explicit non-asymptotic bound for the multiplicative SPA error whose leading term is of order d²/n. This improves on the generic d⁴/n rate in recent work of Tang and Reid. In the natural central region |x|lesssim(d/n)¹/², we obtain a further refinement. We prove that the leading SPA error is essentially constant throughout this region, up to O(d⁵/²/n³/²). This allows us, at the cost of computing a single Gaussian Monte Carlo integral, to estimate the SPA error in the central region and use the resulting value as a multiplicative correction to obtain a more accurate SPA. As further corollaries to the main SPA bound, we derive a local central limit theorem with explicit multiplicative error and, on the natural high-dimensional central region, a cubic-corrected Gaussian approximation with multiplicative error O(d²/n). We also obtain a more general SPA theorem that applies, in particular, to averages of independent but not necessarily identically distributed random vectors. We further give readily verifiable sufficient conditions for the SPA assumptions, reducing the main high-dimensional Fourier condition to one-dimensional estimates for tilted marginals. These conditions apply, in particular, to arbitrary isotropic log-concave densities, uniformly well-conditioned affine transformations thereof and their convex mixtures, as well as to distributions obtained by smoothing with Gaussian or log-concave noise. The results are illustrated by multivariate generalized Laplace distributions and by a likelihood problem for averaged images with Gaussian-mixture noise.

articles.title: Limited contribution of novel Carbon Dioxide Removal and Geological Carbon Storage to reducing peak warming
articles.abstract: Novel carbon dioxide removal options and geological carbon storage will be necessary for achieving the Paris Agreement’s long-term climate targets1, but are characterized by low current deployment2–4 and near-term upscaling challenges5–7. Here we use the REMIND Integrated Assessment Model with a wide representation of carbon removal technologies and informed by intertemporally consistent upscaling pathways for carbon storage to assess upscaling-constrained mitigation pathways limiting warming to 1.5°C. We find that, even under highly optimistic assumptions, geological carbon storage and novel carbon removal contribute only 32–51 GtCO₂ cumulatively by 2050 - approximately one year of current global CO₂ emissions - and reduce peak warming at most by about 0.025 °C. This limited effect arises because cumulative deployment remains small during the initial quasi-exponential scale-up phase. By contrast, cumulative contributions increase to 300–875 GtCO₂ by 2100, corresponding to 0.14–0.39 °C of post-peak temperature decline. Rapid scale-up can still enable net-zero CO₂ emissions around mid-century, but cannot substitute for immediate and deep emissions reductions in limiting peak warming.

articles.title: PayGuard AI: An Explainable Hybrid Framework for Corporate Payment-Anomaly Detection and Working-Capital Decision Support
articles.abstract: Corporate Accounts Payable processes involve high transaction volumes, diverse suppliers, and complex payment conditions, creating challenges for manual fraud screening. Existing detection methods commonly prioritise classification performance while providing limited interpretability, uncertainty quantification, or financial decision support. This study introduces PayGuard AI, an explainable hybrid framework integrating business rules, Isolation Forest anomaly detection, logistic regression, Bayesian uncertainty estimation, bootstrap review-exposure analysis, and Monte Carlo working-capital simulation. The framework was evaluated on 5,600 synthetic supplier-payment transactions containing a 5% controlled anomaly rate across seven categories. On held-out data, the hybrid achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.982 versus 0.989 for rules alone, but higher average precision (0.770 versus 0.680); its precision, recall, and specificity were 0.848, 0.667, and 0.994, respectively. Sensitivity varied by anomaly type, with weak detection of exact and near duplicates. The statistical models provided interpretable feature associations and approximate posterior uncertainty estimates. Bootstrap resampling produced a mean aggregate review exposure of approximately 302,564 synthetic monetary units (SMU), while Monte Carlo analysis illustrated uncertainty across Days Payable Outstanding scenarios. PayGuard AI offers a proof-of-concept approach that combines transaction screening, interpretability, uncertainty representation, and financial decision support. Real-world validation and organisational calibration are still needed before operational deployment.

articles.title: Realization of decoherence-induced average symmetry-protected topological phases on quantum processors
articles.abstract: Symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases are conventionally formulated for pure states protected by exact symmetries. In open quantum systems, however, decoherence generates mixed-state ensembles in which average symmetry can instead emerge only after averaging over microscopic trajectories. In this work, we realize decoherence-induced average SPT (ASPT) order on programmable quantum processors. Starting from a one-dimensional cluster SPT, we engineer sublattice-selective Pauli-Z dephasing through ancilla-assisted quantum circuits. We diagnose the loss of strong symmetry through the decay of the symmetry charge, while the engineered channel preserves the corresponding symmetry at the ensemble level. Moreover, a two-replica Rényi-2 string correlator measured through destructive SWAP readout remains nontrivial, revealing the ASPT structure encoded at the density-matrix level. We further show that the engineered dephasing redistributes spectral weight among reduced-stabilizer sectors while preserving the characteristic twofold pairing of the half-chain entanglement spectrum. These results establish a gate-based route to engineering and probing ASPT order and demonstrate structured decoherence as a programmable resource for realizing mixed-state topological quantum matter.

articles.title: A Passive Voltage Spike Suppression Strategy for High-Frequency Link Inverters Based on Primary-Side Resonance
articles.abstract: To mitigate the voltage spikes triggered by the resonance between transformer leakage inductance and parasitic capacitance of switching devices in high-frequency link (HFL) inverters, this paper proposes a primary-side resonance suppression passive voltage spike suppression strategy for high-frequency link inverters. This scheme suppresses the resonant spike amplitude by reshaping the excitation waveform on the primary side of the transformer, without adding extra active devices and complex control logic, and completes the compensation for duty cycle loss at the same time. A 1kW experimental prototype has been developed for verification tests. The proposed scheme reduces the voltage spike from 800V to 530V with a self-loss of only 1W, which is lower than that of the traditional RC snubber. The hybrid scheme integrated with the feedback transformer passive snubber circuit can further suppress the voltage spike to 460V. The results show that the proposed scheme achieves excellent voltage-spike suppression performance with low power losses. Moreover, it requires neither complex auxiliary control algorithms nor additional drive circuits, thereby offering high engineering feasibility and cost effectiveness for medium- and low-power photovoltaic high-frequency-link inverter applications.
