articles.title: Quantum control as renormalization group flow
articles.title_zh: 作为重正化群流的量子控制
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26154v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Renormalization Group (RG) establishes relations between effective descriptions of physical systems at different scales; in Hamiltonian RG, these relations induce a flow in the space of Hamiltonians. In direct correspondence, we design an RG framework for quantum control by constructing a flow in the space of time-dependent Hamiltonians. A prescribed control subspace, selected to contain only experimentally accessible terms, forms the fixed-point manifold, while the flow preserves the target unitary and monotonically reduces the Hamiltonian weight outside this subspace. Exploiting the freedom in constructing the flow, we introduce flow-equation engineering to enhance the versatility of the framework for diverse control problems, including time-periodic and open-interval smooth protocols with prescribed endpoints. We provide two disparate applications to exhibit the utility of our approach: (i) Nonperturbative Floquet engineering beyond the regime of validity of high-frequency expansions, which we demonstrate by constructing an implementable time-periodic protocol for the Haldane model; (ii) Accessible fast-forward driving from unit-fidelity counterdiabatic evolution, which we showcase for large transverse-field Ising chains away from the adiabatic regime by compressing the long-range multibody adiabatic gauge potential into the original time-dependent Ising control schedules. Our control RG framework reveals a unifying perspective on Hamiltonian engineering and unitary quantum control, and can serve as an organizing principle behind seemingly disparate nonequilibrium quantum dynamics.
articles.abstract_zh: 重整化群（RG）建立了不同尺度物理系统的有效描述之间的关系；在哈密顿量 RG 中，这些关系引起哈密顿量空间中的流动。在直接对应中，我们通过在时间相关的哈密顿量空间中构建流来设计量子控制的 RG 框架。选择仅包含实验可访问项的规定控制子空间形成定点流形，而流保留目标酉并单调减少该子空间外部的哈密顿权重。利用构建流的自由度，我们引入流方程工程来增强框架针对各种控制问题的多功能性，包括具有指定端点的时间周期和开区间平滑协议。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 重整化群（RG）建立了不同尺度物理系统的有效描述之间的关系；在哈密顿量 RG 中，这些关系引起哈密顿量空间中的流动。在直接对应中，我们通过在时间相关的哈密顿量空间中构建流来设计量子控制的 RG 框架。选择仅包含实验可访问项的规定控制子空间形成定点流形，而流保留目标酉并单调减少该子空间外部的哈密顿权重。利用构建流的自由度，我们引入流方程工程来增强框架针对各种控制问题的多功能性，包括具有指定端点的时间周期和开区间平滑协议。我们提供了两个不同的应用程序来展示我们方法的实用性：（i）超出高频展开有效性范围的非微扰 Floquet 工程，我们通过为 Haldane 模型构建可实现的时间周期协议来证明这一点； （ii）单位保真度反绝热演化的可访问快进驱动，我们通过将远程多体绝热规范势压缩到原始的时间相关伊辛控制计划中，展示了远离绝热状态的大横向场伊辛链。我们的控制 RG 框架揭示了哈密顿工程和酉量子控制的统一视角，并且可以作为看似不同的非平衡量子动力学背后的组织原则。

articles.title: Sidewall Metrology Protocol for Superconducting Qubit Devices
articles.title_zh: 超导量子位器件的侧壁计量协议
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26223v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Sidewall morphology is a potentially important factor influencing superconducting qubit performance, yet its quantitative characterization remains challenging due to the absence of standardized measurement protocols. In this work, we develop a scanning probe microscopy-based measurement framework for the quantitative characterization of superconducting qubit sidewalls. The framework introduces a refined root mean square lateral sidewall roughness descriptor and a new curvature-equivalent radius for quantifying vertical sidewall morphology. The descriptors and measurement procedures are applied to different components of qubit devices, forming the basis of a proposed sidewall characterization protocol. This provides a foundation for quantitative comparisons of fabrication processes across laboratories, enabling future investigations of correlations between sidewall geometry and qubit performance.
articles.abstract_zh: 侧壁形态是影响超导量子位性能的潜在重要因素，但由于缺乏标准化的测量协议，其定量表征仍然具有挑战性。在这项工作中，我们开发了一种基于扫描探针显微镜的测量框架，用于超导量子比特侧壁的定量表征。该框架引入了一个精细的根均方横向侧壁粗糙度描述符和一个新的曲率等效半径，用于量化垂直侧壁形态。描述符和测量程序应用于量子比特设备的不同组件，形成了所提出的侧壁表征协议的基础。这为跨实验室制造工艺的定量比较奠定了基础，为将来研究侧壁几何形状与量子比特性能之间的相关性奠定了基础。

articles.title: Optical vortex bullets with large angular momenta
articles.title_zh: 具有大角动量的光学涡旋子弹
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26289v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate three-dimensional spatiotemporal optical vortex solitons (light bullets with a toroidal shape) carrying higher-order orbital angular momentum in Kerr media with anomalous group-velocity dispersion and a transversely localized Gaussian profile of the linear refractive index. Stationary vortex bullets with topological charges (winding numbers) 1≤ ell ≤ 4 are obtained as numerical solutions of the three-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger equation, and their existence, structure and stability are systematically analyzed. In terms of atomic Bose-Einstein condensates, these solutions represent matter-wave solitons with embedded vorticity. We examine the dependence of the solution families on the propagation constant, the depth and width of the guiding profile, and ell . It is found that the increase of ell  requires one to use a stronger or wider waveguiding potential to sustain localized states satisfying the Vakhitov-Kolokolov (VK) stability criterion. VK-complying and non-complying branches of vortex-soliton families are separated by a degenerate Townes branch. Direct simulations reveal that, although the guiding profile substantially suppresses the collapse and extends the propagation distance of vortex bullets, their robustness is ultimately limited by azimuthal instabilities, whose growth is enhanced for values of ell . These results demonstrate that engineered refractive-index landscapes significantly enlarge the stability domain of spatiotemporal vortex bullets and provide guidelines for supporting optical bullets carrying large orbital angular momenta.
articles.abstract_zh: 我们研究了三维时空光学涡孤子（环形形状的光子弹） ，其在Kerr介质中具有高阶轨道角动量，具有异常的群速度色散和线性折射率的横向局部高斯剖面。将具有拓扑电荷（绕组数） 1 ≤ ell ≤ 4的静止涡流子弹作为三维非线性薛定谔方程的数值解，对其存在性、结构和稳定性进行了系统分析。就原子玻色-爱因斯坦凝聚体而言，这些解代表具有嵌入涡度的物质波孤子。我们研究了溶液族对传播常数、导向轮廓的深度和宽度以及ell的依赖性。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 我们研究了三维时空光学涡孤子（环形形状的光子弹） ，其在Kerr介质中具有高阶轨道角动量，具有异常的群速度色散和线性折射率的横向局部高斯剖面。将具有拓扑电荷（绕组数） 1 ≤ ell ≤ 4的静止涡流子弹作为三维非线性薛定谔方程的数值解，对其存在性、结构和稳定性进行了系统分析。就原子玻色-爱因斯坦凝聚体而言，这些解代表具有嵌入涡度的物质波孤子。我们研究了溶液族对传播常数、导向轮廓的深度和宽度以及ell的依赖性。研究发现， ell的增加需要使用更强或更宽的波导电位来维持满足Vakhitov-Kolokolov （ VK ）稳定性标准的局部状态。涡孤族中符合VK标准和不符合VK标准的分支由退化的Townes分支隔开。直接模拟表明，尽管导向剖面基本上抑制了坍塌并延长了涡流子弹的传播距离，但它们的鲁棒性最终受到方位不稳定性的限制，方位不稳定性的增长对于ell值来说是增强的。这些结果表明，工程折射率景观显着扩大了时空涡流子弹的稳定域，并为支撑携带大轨道角动量的光学子弹提供了指导。

articles.title: Ultrafast Proton-Induced Collective Dynamics Regulated by Water-Mediated Hydrogen-Bond Networks in Liquids
articles.title_zh: 由液体中水介导的氢键网络调节的超快质子诱导集体动力学
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26387v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Photoinduced proton dynamics in liquids couple molecular reactions to nonequilibrium charge transport, yet the role of alkyl C-H sites as proton sources remains poorly understood. Combining optical-pump terahertz-probe spectroscopy with real-time time-dependent density-functional-theory simulations, we investigate ultrafast proton dynamics following strong-field ionization of liquid ethanol and hydroxyl-free ethyl acetate. Isotope-substitution and control experiments support the identification of alkyl C-H groups as the proton source. The released protons induce quasi-free-electron localization on a timescale of hundreds of femtoseconds, manifested as a characteristic V-shaped transient in terahertz absorption. In ethanol-water mixtures, trace water enhances hydrogen-bond-network connectivity and facilitates proton transfer to ethanol O-H sites, suppressing the transient absorption dip. These findings identify photoactivated C-H sites as proton sources in liquids and reveal how hydrogen-bond networks regulate the ensuing proton and electron dynamics, linking local bond cleavage to the ultrafast charge response of the surrounding liquid.
articles.abstract_zh: 液体中的光诱导质子动力学将分子反应与非平衡电荷传输结合起来，但对烷基C-H位点作为质子源的作用仍然知之甚少。我们将光泵太赫兹探针光谱学与实时时间依赖性密度函数理论模拟相结合，研究液态乙醇和无羟基乙酸乙酯强场电离后的超快质子动力学。同位素取代和对照实验支持烷基C-H基团作为质子源的鉴定。释放的质子在数百飞秒的时间尺度上诱导准自由电子定位，表现为太赫兹吸收的特征V形瞬变。在乙醇-水混合物中，微量水增强氢键-网络连接性，并促进质子转移到乙醇O-H位点，抑制瞬态吸收倾角。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 液体中的光诱导质子动力学将分子反应与非平衡电荷传输结合起来，但对烷基C-H位点作为质子源的作用仍然知之甚少。我们将光泵太赫兹探针光谱学与实时时间依赖性密度函数理论模拟相结合，研究液态乙醇和无羟基乙酸乙酯强场电离后的超快质子动力学。同位素取代和对照实验支持烷基C-H基团作为质子源的鉴定。释放的质子在数百飞秒的时间尺度上诱导准自由电子定位，表现为太赫兹吸收的特征V形瞬变。在乙醇-水混合物中，微量水增强氢键-网络连接性，并促进质子转移到乙醇O-H位点，抑制瞬态吸收倾角。这些发现确定了光激活的C-H位点作为液体中的质子源，并揭示了氢键网络如何调节随后的质子和电子动力学，将局部键切割与周围液体的超快电荷响应联系起来。

articles.title: Coupling Evaporation, Chemical Reactions, and Crystallization: A Population-Balance Framework Applied to Two-Step Perovskite Crystallization
articles.title_zh: 偶联蒸发、化学反应和结晶：应用于两步钙钛矿结晶的群体平衡框架
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26591v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A limited understanding of how evaporation couples to crystallization pathways hampers control over the formation of solution-processed perovskite photoactive layers. Identifying these mechanisms-and learning how to select and tune them-is essential for achieving the desired crystal morphology and, ultimately, improving solar-cell performance and stability. To investigate crystallization pathways in evaporating thin films, we develop a simple and general zero-dimensional population-balance model that couples evaporation, chemical reactions, and crystallization. We use the model to explore a range of parameters for a solvent-solute system that follows a two-step crystallization pathway: solvent evaporation first induces formation of a crystalline precursor, which subsequently recrystallizes into the final phase. The model predicts the evolution of the film composition during drying and provides quantitative LaMer curves. Based on these results, we introduce a vocabulary of "supply limitations" and "rate limitations" that enables the interpretation of crystallization kinetics in terms of the governing process conditions.
articles.abstract_zh: 对蒸发如何与结晶途径耦合的有限理解阻碍了对溶液处理钙钛矿光活性层形成的控制。识别这些机制并学习如何选择和调整它们对于实现所需的晶体形态并最终提高太阳能电池性能和稳定性至关重要。为了研究蒸发薄膜中的结晶途径，我们开发了一种简单而通用的零维群体平衡模型，该模型将蒸发、化学反应和结晶结合在一起。我们使用该模型来探索遵循两步结晶途径的溶剂-溶质体系的一系列参数：溶剂蒸发首先诱导结晶前体的形成，随后再结晶成最终相。该模型预测干燥过程中膜成分的演变，并提供定量的LaMer曲线。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 对蒸发如何与结晶途径耦合的有限理解阻碍了对溶液处理钙钛矿光活性层形成的控制。识别这些机制并学习如何选择和调整它们对于实现所需的晶体形态并最终提高太阳能电池性能和稳定性至关重要。为了研究蒸发薄膜中的结晶途径，我们开发了一种简单而通用的零维群体平衡模型，该模型将蒸发、化学反应和结晶结合在一起。我们使用该模型来探索遵循两步结晶途径的溶剂-溶质体系的一系列参数：溶剂蒸发首先诱导结晶前体的形成，随后再结晶成最终相。该模型预测干燥过程中膜成分的演变，并提供定量的LaMer曲线。基于这些结果，我们引入了“供应限制”和“速率限制”的词汇，可以根据控制工艺条件解释结晶动力学。

articles.title: Average lower bound on magnetic double-well tunneling with asymptotically large well separation
articles.title_zh: 具有渐近大井分离的磁性双井隧穿的平均下限
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26637v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study tunneling between two identical, smooth, compactly supported potential wells in a constant perpendicular magnetic field, with the coupling and magnetic field fixed and the well separation tending to infinity. For a sufficiently small positive magnetic field, we prove lower bounds on the hopping coefficient and on the splitting of the two lowest eigenvalues outside a set of separations of density zero. If the well centers are separated by 2d₁ and the magnetic field strength is bλ, the lower bounds have the form e^-bλ d₁²-Cd₁¹⁺δ for every fixed δin(0,1). No radial or reflection symmetry of the single-well potential is assumed. The proof combines the explicit Landau resolvent kernel with a complex analytic estimate for logarithmic averages of the hopping coefficient.
articles.abstract_zh: 我们研究了在恒定垂直磁场中两个相同、光滑、紧凑支撑的电位井之间的隧穿，其中耦合和磁场固定，井分离趋向无穷大。对于足够小的正磁场，我们证明了跳跃系数和密度为零的一组分离之外的两个最低特征值的分裂的下限。如果阱中心间隔为2d * ，磁场强度为bλ ，则对于每个固定的δin (0,1) ，下限的形式为e ^ -bλ d * -Cd * ¹ * δ。不假定单孔电位的径向或反射对称性。该证明将显式Landau分解核与跳跃系数对数平均值的复杂分析估计相结合。

articles.title: Challenging Atomistic Foundation Models on Disordered Carbons
articles.title_zh: 具有挑战性的无序碳原子基础模型
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26701v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Foundation machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) promise broad transferability, yet their out-of-domain reliability is hard to establish. Here, we use pure and O/H-containing disordered carbon spanning multiple phases, competing hybridisations and porous frameworks to stress-test six popular foundation MLIPs. We first screen all six on density functional theory (DFT) energy and force errors and binding curves, then subject four to melt-quench-anneal molecular dynamics and evaluate the resulting structural observables. Binding curves and O/H-containing trajectories reveal unphysical extrapolation and dynamical failures that low DFT energy and force errors fail to reveal. Of the models tested, MACE-MH-1 is the most consistently robust, with low DFT errors and stable MD. Despite differing architectures, OMAT-based models share structural biases, highlighting the importance of training coverage. All four models generate structures of nanoporous carbon that reproduce the principal experimental and specialised carbon potential signatures. Incorporating O/H leaves short-range order largely unchanged but shifts pore-size distributions towards larger pores. These results emphasise the need for application-specific validation and extend molecular dynamics modelling of nanoporous carbon towards experimentally realistic structures.
articles.abstract_zh: 基础机器学习原子间势（ MLIP ）具有广泛的可转移性，但其域外可靠性很难确定。在这里，我们使用跨越多个阶段的纯含O/H无序碳、竞争性杂交和多孔框架来对六种流行的基础MLIP进行压力测试。我们首先筛选所有六个关于密度泛函理论（ DFT ）的能量和力误差和结合曲线，然后对四个进行熔融淬火-退火分子动力学，并评估所得到的结构可观测值。绑定曲线和包含O/H的轨迹揭示了低DFT能量和力误差未能揭示的非物理外推和动态失效。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 基础机器学习原子间势（ MLIP ）具有广泛的可转移性，但其域外可靠性很难确定。在这里，我们使用跨越多个阶段的纯含O/H无序碳、竞争性杂交和多孔框架来对六种流行的基础MLIP进行压力测试。我们首先筛选所有六个关于密度泛函理论（ DFT ）的能量和力误差和结合曲线，然后对四个进行熔融淬火-退火分子动力学，并评估所得到的结构可观测值。绑定曲线和包含O/H的轨迹揭示了低DFT能量和力误差未能揭示的非物理外推和动态失效。在测试的模型中， MACE-MH-1是最稳定的，具有低DFT误差和稳定的MD。尽管架构不同，但基于OMAT的模型共享结构偏差，突出了培训覆盖率的重要性。所有四个模型都会产生纳米多孔碳的结构，再现主要的实验和专门的碳电位特征。结合O/H使短期秩序基本保持不变，但将孔径分布转向更大的孔隙。这些结果强调了对特定应用验证的需求，并将纳米多孔碳的分子动力学建模扩展到实验上逼真的结构。

articles.title: A boundary integral method for computing electron repulsion integrals in heterogeneous dielectric environments
articles.title_zh: 一种计算非均匀介电环境中电子排斥积分的边界积分方法
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26745v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a boundary integral method for evaluating electron repulsion integrals (ERIs) in dielectric environments of piecewise constant permittivity. This generalizes conventional bare-Coulomb ERIs by incorporating screening from structured dielectric surroundings, such as the substrates and/or encapsulating layers present in modern two-dimensional-material devices. We formulate the problem as a second-kind boundary integral equation for the induced surface charge on the dielectric interfaces, and discretize it with a Nyström method on adaptively refined panels. The incident potential generated by each smooth orbital source density is evaluated by a Fourier truncated-kernel method in or near to its source box, and by fast multipole method (FMM) accelerated quadrature farther away. The linear system is solved by a Krylov iteration also accelerated by the FMM. We focus on cuboidal device geometries, and retain efficiency at high aspect ratios via close-to-touching panel quadratures. We further develop a distributed pipeline that computes the full ERI tensor, comprising thousands of orbital pairs, embedded in a single dielectric geometry. We demonstrate the method on an effective three-layer graphene slab over a Si/SiO₂ heterojunction, focusing on the central graphene layer represented by 198 p_z-like orbitals, retaining the 2613² non-negligible entries of the 198⁴-sized ERI tensor. The model is resolved on 1.3 million surface unknowns, achieving a relative error of 0.004%, at a cost of 22 node-hours.
articles.abstract_zh: 我们提出了一种用于评估分段恒定介电常数介电环境中的电子排斥积分（ ERI ）的边界积分方法。这通过结合来自结构化介电环境的筛选来推广传统的裸库仑ERI ，例如现代二维材料器件中存在的衬底和/或封装层。我们将问题公式化为介电界面上感应表面电荷的第二类边界积分方程，并在自适应细化面板上使用Nyström方法对其进行离散化。每个光滑轨道源密度产生的入射电位通过在其源盒内或附近的傅里叶截断核方法进行评估，并通过快速多极法（ FMM ）加速正交到更远的地方。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 我们提出了一种用于评估分段恒定介电常数介电环境中的电子排斥积分（ ERI ）的边界积分方法。这通过结合来自结构化介电环境的筛选来推广传统的裸库仑ERI ，例如现代二维材料器件中存在的衬底和/或封装层。我们将问题公式化为介电界面上感应表面电荷的第二类边界积分方程，并在自适应细化面板上使用Nyström方法对其进行离散化。每个光滑轨道源密度产生的入射电位通过在其源盒内或附近的傅里叶截断核方法进行评估，并通过快速多极法（ FMM ）加速正交到更远的地方。线性系统由同样由FMM加速的Krylov迭代求解。我们专注于立方体器件几何形状，并通过接近触摸的面板正交保持高纵横比的效率。我们进一步开发了一种计算完整ERI张量的分布式流水线，该流水线包括嵌入在单个介电几何体中的数千个轨道对。我们在Si/SiO ₂异质结上的有效三层石墨烯板上演示了这种方法，重点关注由198个p_z样轨道表示的中央石墨烯层，保留了198英寸大小的ERI张量的2613 ²不可忽略的条目。该模型在130万个表面未知数上进行解析，实现了0.004%的相对误差，成本为22个节点小时。

articles.title: Gate-Switchable Josephson Diode Effect in Graphene via Magnetochiral Anisotropy
articles.title_zh: 石墨烯中的栅极可切换约瑟夫森二极管效应（通过磁性各向异性）
articles.abstract: arXiv:2312.02692v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Josephson diode effect originating from magnetochiral anisotropy has thus far been realized primarily in conventional two-dimensional electron gases. Here, we propose a graphene-based Josephson junction as a broadly gate-tunable platform for nonreciprocal supercurrent transport. We demonstrate that the nonreciprocal critical current not only reverses its sign when graphene is switched from n- to p-type doping via electrostatic gating, but its efficiency can also be continuously tuned from zero up to sim 40%. This gate-controlled polarity switching and efficiency modulation---unique to the chiral nature of Dirac fermions in graphene---has no counterpart in conventional semiconductor systems, positioning the graphene Josephson diode as a highly versatile component for advanced superconducting circuits.
articles.abstract_zh: 迄今为止，源自磁性各向异性的约瑟夫森二极管效应主要在传统的二维电子气体中实现。在这里，我们提出了一种基于石墨烯的约瑟夫森结，作为非互易超电流传输的广泛栅极可调平台。我们证明，当石墨烯通过静电栅极从n型掺杂切换到p型掺杂时，非互易临界电流不仅会逆转其符号，而且其效率也可以从零持续调整到SIM 40%。这种栅控极性开关和效率调制--这是石墨烯中狄拉克费米子手性特性的独特之处--在传统半导体系统中没有对应物，将石墨烯约瑟夫森二极管定位为先进超导电路的高度通用组件。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 迄今为止，源自磁性各向异性的约瑟夫森二极管效应主要在传统的二维电子气体中实现。在这里，我们提出了一种基于石墨烯的约瑟夫森结，作为非互易超电流传输的广泛栅极可调平台。我们证明，当石墨烯通过静电栅极从n型掺杂切换到p型掺杂时，非互易临界电流不仅会逆转其符号，而且其效率也可以从零持续调整到SIM 40%。这种栅控极性开关和效率调制--这是石墨烯中狄拉克费米子手性特性的独特之处--在传统半导体系统中没有对应物，将石墨烯约瑟夫森二极管定位为先进超导电路的高度通用组件。

articles.title: Surface-extended Andreev bound states emerging from intrinsic surface superconductivity of PtBi₂
articles.title_zh: 从PtBi ₂的本征表面超导性中出现的表面延伸的Andreev结合态
articles.abstract: arXiv:2507.13843v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Intrinsic topological superconductivity remains one of the central open questions in condensed-matter physics. The three-dimensional Weyl semimetal PtBi₂ has recently been shown by angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy to host a superconducting gap that opens exclusively on its Fermi-arc surface states and exhibits a nodal structure, making it a promising platform for exploring unconventional and potentially topological superconductivity. However, despite these momentum-resolved insights, the real-space spectroscopic signatures of unconventional superconductivity in PtBi₂ remain unclear. Here, using scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy, we reveal a sizable and spatially homogeneous gap (Δ > 10,meV) on atomically pristine terraces of PtBi₂. Within this gap, we detect surface-extended in-gap states exhibiting pronounced atomic-scale spatial modulation. Analysis of the tunneling spectra indicates that these states are most consistently interpreted as Andreev bound states within a superconducting gap. Further phenomenological modeling shows that their characteristic spectral features are naturally captured by a chiral pairing scenario. Our results establish a direct real-space connection between the superconducting gap and surface-extended quasiparticle states in PtBi₂, and provide new insight into the nature of its unconventional surface superconductivity. These findings highlight PtBi₂ as a versatile platform for exploring exotic quasiparticle excitations and potential Majorana physics.
articles.abstract_zh: 固有拓扑超导性仍然是凝聚态物理学的核心开放性问题之一。三维Weyl半金属PtBi ₂最近通过角度分辨光发射光谱显示，它具有超导间隙，该间隙仅在其费米弧表面状态上开放，并表现出节点结构，使其成为探索非常规和潜在拓扑超导性的有前途的平台。然而，尽管有这些动量解析的见解，但PtBi ₂中非常规超导性的真实空间光谱特征仍然不清楚。在这里，使用扫描隧道显微镜和光谱学，我们在PtBi ₂的原子原始梯田上揭示了一个相当大的空间均匀间隙（ Δ > 10 ， meV ）。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 固有拓扑超导性仍然是凝聚态物理学的核心开放性问题之一。三维Weyl半金属PtBi ₂最近通过角度分辨光发射光谱显示，它具有超导间隙，该间隙仅在其费米弧表面状态上开放，并表现出节点结构，使其成为探索非常规和潜在拓扑超导性的有前途的平台。然而，尽管有这些动量解析的见解，但PtBi ₂中非常规超导性的真实空间光谱特征仍然不清楚。在这里，使用扫描隧道显微镜和光谱学，我们在PtBi ₂的原子原始梯田上揭示了一个相当大的空间均匀间隙（ Δ > 10 ， meV ）。在这个间隙内，我们检测到表面延伸的间隙内状态，表现出明显的原子尺度空间调制。对隧穿光谱的分析表明，这些状态最一致地被解释为超导间隙内的Andreev束缚状态。进一步的现象学建模表明，它们的特征光谱特征自然地被手性配对场景捕获。我们的结果在PtBi ₂中的超导间隙和表面延伸的准粒子态之间建立了直接的实际空间联系，并为其非常规表面超导性的性质提供了新的见解。这些发现突出了PtBi ₂作为探索奇异准粒子激发和潜在Majorana物理学的多功能平台。

articles.title: Nonlinear Landau levels in the almost-bosonic anyon gas
articles.title_zh: 近玻色子任意子气体中的非线性朗道能级
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.14679v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the quantitative description of a many-particle gas of interacting abelian anyons in the plane, confined in a trapping potential. If the anyons are modeled as bosons with a magnetic flux attachment, and if the total magnetic flux is small compared to the number of particles, then an average-field description becomes appropriate for the low-energy collective state of the gas. Namely, by means of a Hartree-Jastrow ansatz, we derive a two-parameter Chern-Simons-Schrödinger energy functional which extends the well-known Gross-Pitaevskii / nonlinear Schrödinger density functional theory to the magnetic (anyonic) self-interaction. One parameter determines the total number of self-generated magnetic flux units in the system, and the other the effective strength of spin-orbit self-interaction. This latter interaction can be either attractive/focusing or repulsive/defocusing, and depends both on the intrinsic spin-orbit interaction and the relative length scale of the flux profile of the anyons. Densities and energies of ground and excited states are studied analytically and numerically for a wide range of the parameters and align well with a sequence of exact nonlinear Landau levels describing Jackiw-Pi self-dual solitons. With increasing flux, counter-rotating vortices are formed, enhancing the stability of the gas against collapse. Apart from clarifying the relations between various different anyon models that have appeared in the literature, our analysis sheds new light on the many-anyon spectral problem, and also exemplifies a novel supersymmetry-breaking phenomenon.

articles.title: A chemical avenue to manipulate field-reentrant superconducting rivalries in infinite layer nickelates
articles.abstract: arXiv:2511.22026v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recently, preliminary magnetic field-reentrant superconductivity manifested in high-temperature (Tc) Eu-doped infinite-layer (IL) nickelates, beyond analogous discoveries exclusively in low-Tc systems. This evokes intriguing fundamental issues about potential quantum-phase boundary and criticality between unconventional superconductivity and field-reentrant-one, which are inexplicable owing to formidable challenges in growing IL-nickelates towards later-series rare-earths. Herein, we open up chemical avenues to enable effective growth of (RE1-yRE'y)1-xEuxNiO2 (RE/RE': Pr, Nd, Sm, Gd, Dy), giving rise to discoveries of RE-4f-related quantum competition between high-Tc and reentrant superconductivity. Robust magnetic-field-reentrant superconductivity with uniaxial anisotropy is observed at superconducting-dome boundaries, stemming from Eu2+-4f7 associated competition between magnetic-fluctuation promoted pairing and exchange-field interactions. Their quantum-criticality is further modulable via RE(RE')-magnetism, which either reinforces reentrancy or elevates Tc (40.1 K) with more robust critical-current-density (~266 kA/cm2 at 2 K) beyond Sr-/Ca-doped counterparts. Our synthetic route enables the establishment of an ideal platform via IL-nickelates for studying 4f-related unconventional superconductivity and quantum-criticality.

articles.title: Linear Ensemble-Constrained Quantum Monte Carlo: From Dilute Fermi Gas to Flat-Band Ferromagnetism
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.08552v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a finite-temperature canonical-ensemble determinant quantum Monte Carlo algorithm that enforces an exact fermion number and enables numerically stable simulations of correlated lattice fermions. We propose a stabilized QR update that reduces the computational complexity from standard cubic scaling O(β N³) to linear scaling O(β N Nₑ²) with respect to the system size N, where Nₑ is the particle number. This yields a dramatic speedup in dilute regimes (Nₑ ll N), opening unbiased access to large-scale simulations of strongly correlated low-density phases. We validate the method on the dilute Fermi gas with onsite Hubbard interactions, observing the suppression of the fermion sign problem in the dilute limit. Furthermore, we apply this approach to a one-dimensional flat-band system, where the canonical ensemble allows for precise control over filling. We reveal a ferromagnetic instability at low temperatures in the half-filling regime. Our linear-scaling approach provides a powerful tool for investigating emergent phenomena in dilute quantum matter.

articles.title: Dualities and Topological Classification of the S=1 Pyrochlore Spin Ice
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.03852v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive dual descriptions of the trivial paramagnetic, Z₂-deconfined, and Z₂-confined U(1) Coulomb phases of the S=1 pyrochlore spin ice. In the monopole-free limit, the system can be effectively mapped onto 3D XY and Ising loop-gas models depending on the spin anisotropy, which provides theoretical estimates for the phase boundaries, while a macroscopic flux vector classifies the topological sectors via geometric parity rules. Thermal unit monopoles permit endpoints of both directed spin loops and unoriented vacancy loops. The resulting relevant symmetry-breaking fields in the dual XY and Ising descriptions predict rounded crossovers near the monopole-free critical points. Monte Carlo simulations support this monopole-induced rounding.

articles.title: A large nonmagnetic aluminum-and-Viton vacuum chamber suitable for vacuum pressures down into the extremely-high-vacuum (XHV) regime
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24262v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A recently constructed large nonmagnetic vacuum chamber is described and characterized. The vacuum chamber was machined from 19-inch cubes of aluminum and are sealed using dual Viton O-rings (with the interspace between the O-rings evacuated by a separate vacuum pump). 17-inch-diameter openings on all six sides allow for easy access to the experimental apparatus and for vacuum pumps with very large pumping speeds. These 17-inch holes were bored straight through the aluminum cube, resulting in an interior volume of 100 L (almost 90% of the total volume of the 19-inch cube). The 17-inch openings are sealed with 19-inch-diameter aluminum flanges. The system is modular in that the cubes can be connected to one another to form larger vacuum systems. The chamber is designed to allow for vacuum pressures of 10⁻¹² torr. In many respects (including nonmagnetic properties, outgassing rate after low-temperature baking, weight, cost, ease of machining, and ease of baking due to the chamber's high thermal conductivity) this system is superior to standard stainless-steel metal-sealed CF vacuum systems and is highly recommended for use by others.

articles.title: UDL-RT: A unified differentiable all-sky microwave radiative transfer model with learnable parameterizations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24627v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Radiance-based retrievals and data assimilation require radiative transfer models (RTMs) to simulate radiances and quantify their sensitivities to atmospheric and surface conditions. Conventional RTMs often rely on separately maintained forward, tangent-linear, and adjoint codes, complicating model development and extension. Here, we present the Unified Differentiable and Learnable Radiative Transfer model (UDL-RT), a PyTorch-based framework for all-sky microwave radiative transfer that couples neural-network (NN) parameterizations of gaseous absorption, hydrometeor bulk scattering properties (BSPs), and ocean surface emissivity with an explicit radiative transfer solver in a unified differentiable computational graph. Automatic differentiation directly computes Jacobians with respect to input variables, reducing the model maintenance burden. The NN parameterizations offer flexible representations of complex nonlinear relationships. For example, the NN gas-absorption parameterization reduces the standard deviation of brightness-temperature (TB) errors by approximately 60-85% in the water-vapour channels compared with linear regression. Moreover, UDL-RT propagates loss gradients to trainable parameters to optimize physical parameterizations against observations, with GPU-accelerated batched computation supporting efficient iterative learning. Using Microwave Humidity Sounder-2 (MWHS-2) observations, we optimize the snow BSP parameterization through gradient-based learning. The optimized parameterization improves agreement between simulated and observed TB distributions and reduces the systematic bias and skewness of observation-minus-background (O-B) departures. Overall, UDL-RT integrates radiance simulation, sensitivity analysis, and parameterization optimization within a unified framework, supporting future remote sensing retrieval and data assimilation applications.

articles.title: Strategic Origins of Network Structure
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24792v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The structure and dynamics of complex networks are intimately linked. Despite immense progress in statistically characterizing these systems, a generalized mechanistic framework explaining why specific mesoscale structures emerge remains elusive. Here we introduce the game-graph equilibrium, the stable rest point of a payoff-driven partner-choice dynamic, analogous to a Nash equilibrium. This reveals network structure as the fossilized record of strategic interaction. We prove analytically that two-type games have exactly four network topologies, which are their exhaustive thermodynamic phases: assortative, disassortative, and two core-peripheries. This result generalizes to K^K topological classes for K-type interactions. Furthermore, four distinct Nash equilibria produce core-periphery topologies, yet their payoffs reveal whether the underlying dynamic is cooperative or exploitative. To recover the generating dynamics from observed networks, we develop mechanistic inference by constraining a block model to lie on a low-dimensional, game-theoretic manifold. Applied to real-world networks, the model yields interpretable quantities, distinguishes states that look identical to conventional methods, predicts network topologies it has never seen without retraining, and controls its own complexity without hand-tuned penalties. Networks such as international trade are well described by the model despite the hard constraint, suggesting that real-world systems are organized by payoff-driven partner choice. Our framework resolves a foundational ambiguity by offering a precise, mechanistic definition of communities: strategic equivalence.

articles.title: Low-Field J-Coupling Spectroscopy Measured with a Diamond Nitrogen Vacancy Spectrometer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24815v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nitrogen vacancy centers in diamond (NVs) are point defects well suited to quantum sensing of magnetic fields. NV spin states can be initialized and read out optically with high spatial resolution, enabling detection of pL-scale volumes of nuclear spins. Using Coherently Averaged Synchronized Readout (CASR), standard NMR spectroscopy techniques such as free decay, spin echo, and PGSE have been performed with Hz-scale spectral resolution using NV-diamond sensors. However, using NV detection for conventional high-resolution NMR at multi-tesla fields is challenging due to the need to manipulate NV electronic spins at resonance frequencies 100 GHz or higher. Low-field J-coupling spectroscopy provides an alternative path to chemical resolution in a regime more easily accessible to NVs. Here, we demonstrate homonuclear and heteronuclear J-coupling spectroscopy using an NV-NMR spectrometer based on permanent magnets operating at sim890 kHz proton Larmor frequency (bias magnetic field sim21 mT). This field strength enables chemical characterization based on J-coupling using sequences such as Synchronized Echo (SyncE) and Spin-Echo Double Resonance (SEDOR), which do not require the strong chemical shift dispersion and pristine field homogeneity of high-field NMR. The frequency range is easily detected by NVs using standard XY dynamical decoupling sequences and is well-suited for applying Overhauser DNP, which can boost proton signal by two orders of magnitude. We acquire initial NV-NMR measurements of T₁, T₂, and Overhauser DNP in glycerol before advancing to SEDOR spectroscopy of methanol-¹³C and a methanol-¹³C/acetonitrile-2-¹³C mixture at sample volumes sim50 pL, in which we demonstrate measurement of ¹J_CH couplings and resolution between species. We also acquire a homonuclear J-coupling spectrum of a natural-abundance propylene carbonate sample.

articles.title: Scaling laws for contamination traversal times during vacuum breaks in superconducting accelerators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24876v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A sudden loss of vacuum in a superconducting radio-frequency (SRF) accelerator drives warm gas into the evacuated beamline, where it propagates through interconnected SRF cavities cooled by liquid helium, causing surface contamination, intense heat deposition, and dangerous pressure buildup. Yet predicting how such a failure propagates through realistic multicell cavities has remained difficult because compressible gas dynamics, condensation and cryogenic heat transfer are strongly coupled. Here we develop and experimentally validate a multidimensional computational framework that resolves these processes, and apply it to a full-scale nine-cell SRF cavity. We find that the repeated cell geometry produces staircase-like gas-front propagation, as impingement, recirculation and localized cryopumping strongly retard the bulk flow within each cell. Across a broad range of breach sizes, the cavity traversal time follows a robust power-law scaling with leakage area, providing quantitative guidance for the response time of beamline isolation and protection systems. The simulations also reveal a geometry-confined Mach disk whose position and size track the advancing gas front, suggesting that its acoustic emission could potentially enable rapid, non-invasive detection and localization of vacuum failures. These findings pave the way for a new generation of predictive diagnostics and protection strategies to safeguard large-scale superconducting accelerators.

articles.title: Large Language Model Steering of Acousto-Optic Tweezer Arrays
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.25014v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Controlling quantum hardware requires choosing and revising experimental strategies as nonlinear response, coupling, and drift limit calibration. We experimentally investigate a general-purpose large language model (LLM) as a human-in-the-loop strategy layer for a neutral-atom tweezer platform. Through step-by-step interaction with experimental feedback, the LLM guides a transition from multiplicative row--column correction to a drift-corrected local response-matrix method when separable feedback stalls. Deterministic software performs image analysis and numerical updates, while an experimentalist verifies and authorizes each waveform. For a 10×10 crossed-acousto-optic-deflector array, this workflow reduces the Gaussian-peak coefficient of variation from 20.30% to 1.57% in 30 candidate-update rounds. The experiment demonstrates feedback-informed strategy selection on a physical quantum-control subsystem, rather than direct generation of control parameters alone. These results highlight the potential of LLMs to guide control optimization across diverse quantum platforms by adaptively formulating and refining experimental strategies.

articles.title: Design and synthesis of laser inscribed flexible Bragg gratings containing silicon oxynitride-doped silicon thin film for authentication applications with the insights from X-Ray Absorption Spectroscopy and Quantum Mechanical Calculations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.25382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Silicon-on-insulator is mostly the main driving material system for the field of silicon photonics, including PICs, due to high index contrast and compatibility with current semiconductor manufacturing processes [1]. A recent example is silicon oxynitride-doped silicon [2] discovered recently by our group, offering to set a new position for the fields of silicon photonics with a precise control of refractive index from 2.1 to 2.5 together with the photosensitivity property at different wavelengths. In this study, we demonstrate that the synthesis of silicon oxynitride-doped silicon can be performed on a flexible substrate for the fabrication of Bragg gratings (BG) at low temperatures below 100 degrees Celsius that are emerging for advanced applications. Their use in preserving ultra-fast lasers inscribed micro-information has been demonstrated numerically and experimentally due to its multispectral reflection behaviour from the ultraviolet (UV) to the near-infrared (NIR) regions. The unique structural characteristics of silicon oxynitride-doped silicon were studied at the Si L, O K and N K edges using soft X-ray absorption studies. The quantum mechanical calculations provide the potential formation mechanism of SiON-doped Si, whereas the crystal structure prediction for bulk Si3N4-xOx was conducted using the particle swarm optimization method in combination with density functional theory (DFT).

articles.title: A Unified Interface Neural Network for Elliptic Interface Problems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.25409v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a Unified Interface Neural Network (UINN) framework for elliptic interface problems with discontinuous coefficients. A single shared network provides a unified representation of the solution in both subdomains, while a projection--correction construction embeds the solution and flux jump conditions directly into the neural trial space. This design aligns with the classical numerical principle of incorporating interfacial physics into the approximation basis to construct interface-unfitted numerical methods. The jump conditions are therefore satisfied exactly for any network parameters. Compared with methods based on separate phase networks and numerical formulations with interface penalty terms, UINN provides a unified representation with exact enforcement of interfacial jump conditions and interface-penalty-free optimization. Those features streamline the numerical formulations and can enhance training robustness. Numerical experiments on smooth interfaces at modestly large and high coefficient contrasts demonstrate UINN's solution accuracy, near-machine-precision satisfaction of the interface jump conditions, and enhanced robustness.

articles.title: Yielding-dependent Taylor dispersion in electrokinetic-magnetohydrodynamic Casson microflows
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.25433v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Longitudinal dispersion in a yielding fluid depends on the velocity distribution and on how the flow is maintained. We study a neutral tracer in pressure-assisted electrokinetic and magnetohydrodynamic flow of a Casson fluid through a slit microchannel. The nonlinear stress and velocity equations determine the yielded layers, the unyielded core and the axial flow. Mei's multiple-scale homogenization of the advection-diffusion equation then separates transverse relaxation, mean drift and longitudinal spreading, yielding the Taylor-Aris auxiliary problem and effective diffusivity. An exact pressure-driven solution gives cubic decay of the mean velocity and eighth-power decay of the dispersion enhancement near flow arrest. Under fixed pressure and electrical forcing, increasing the yield parameter from Y=0 to 0.7 moves the optimum Hartmann number from Haₚ=0.696 to 2.634, while the corresponding normalized diffusivity decreases from D_Tmathrm C=1.454 to 1.015. At fixed mean throughput and Haₚ=1, the trend reverses: D_Tmathrm C increases from 1.000433 to 1.002311. The homogenized energy identity traces this difference to the velocity departure from the sectional mean, including that within the unyielded core. Analytical limiting solutions, direct concentration calculations, numerical convergence studies and a coupled Casson shear test support the reduced-flow predictions. An electrolyte-based dimensional assessment identifies the magnetic optima as theoretical forcing states for representative aqueous microchannels. These results are relevant to predicting longitudinal tracer spreading in microchannels carrying fluids with a yield stress, whether pressure or throughput is controlled.

articles.title: Concurrent two-scale topology optimization of printable bone scaffolds via rectified-flow generation and exact latent-space refinement
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.25565v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bone scaffolds must reconcile a macroscale mechanical response with microscale geometric feasibility, yet conventional approaches to their design restrict attainable constitutive properties. This work presents a concurrent two-scale topology optimization framework; a conditional rectified flow generates periodic lattice microstructures, which are then refined in latent space by exact finite-element homogenization sensitivities. The resulting unit-cell geometries and their spatial assignments are jointly optimized under mechanical and feature-size constraints. In a distal rabbit femur benchmark, all eight flow-started refinements produce printable cells with maximum relative errors under 1% across six prescribed engineering moduli. Constructing the implant from a single tiled cell reproduces intact whole-femur compliance within 0.1% and regional strain energy within 0.35% under four loading conditions. In human femoral reconstruction, multiscale concurrent optimization produces a cortical mid-shaft scaffold with porosity 63% while satisfying the compliance constraint within 2% under walking and stair-climbing loads. It achieves an 84% porosity on a proximal cancellous scaffold with strain-energy deviations below 0.25% under the same loads. Analysis of the learned representations reveals distinct architectural families in latent space. Further, the attention heads of the rectified-flow transformer specialize for spatial shifts -- learning the analogue of a finite-difference stencil -- and coordinate symmetries, with ablations showing their influence on generated topologies. These results establish a route to printable, mechanically constrained scaffold designs. The framework is general enough for extending to many other multiscale structural design applications including topology-microstructure co-design in metal additive manufacturing.

articles.title: A General Treatment of Coupled Cavity Resonators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.25648v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider several cavity resonators whose resonant frequencies and electromagnetic fields are known, and suppose that they are coupled through apertures. How can the resonant frequencies and resonant electromagnetic fields of the resulting coupled-cavity resonator be expressed in terms of the original resonant frequencies and electromagnetic fields? This is a problem frequently encountered in radio-frequency systems for accelerators. One example is a multicell cavity used in high-energy electron accelerators. In this note, the resonant frequencies and resonant electromagnetic fields of such coupled cavities are examined as generally as possible, based only on Maxwell's equations and boundary conditions. Specifically, the response function of a cavity as viewed from its coupling ports, namely, its admittance matrix, is derived, and a formulation is developed to express the coupled resonant electromagnetic fields using this matrix. The resulting formulation shows that the coupled resonant modes can be described in terms of overlap integrals between the resonant modes of the cavities and the waveguide modes at the coupling apertures. It also shows that the coupled resonant frequencies are given by the zeros of the determinant of a matrix constructed from the admittance matrices. The results thus obtained are applied to simple systems to confirm the validity of the formulation. Numerical calculations based on this formulation are also carried out for periodic systems in an attempt to derive dispersion relations.

articles.title: All-Dielectric Tight-Binding Photonics via a Band-Gap Vacuum
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.25655v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tight-binding photonics bridges condensed-matter physics and optics, providing a powerful framework for engineering band structures and topological phases with light. For photons, however, the vacuum is gapless, so resonators in air carry radiative tails that produce spurious long-range couplings. Here we embed resonators in a photonic band-gap vacuum (BgV), a photonic crystal whose band gap plays for photons the role vacuum plays for bound electrons. The BgV localizes each resonance exponentially, so designed short-range couplings define the lattice Hamiltonian. We thereby experimentally realize a faithful Benalcazar-Bernevig-Hughes Hamiltonian in an all-dielectric photonic crystal, resolving corner resonances and their orbitals in microwave measurements. Unlike the vacuum surrounding electrons, the BgV is itself designable, controlling relative couplings and closed-loop interference through its band dispersion and Bloch modes. Full-wave calculations and extracted models show that uniformly modifying the BgV, with all resonators fixed, switches the quantized polarization of a two-dimensional Su-Schrieffer-Heeger lattice and converts a zero-flux lattice into a π-flux one. We also numerically realize three-dimensional pyrochlore and hyperhoneycomb lattices with space groups Rbar3m and C2/c, the latter a nodal-loop semimetal with topological drumhead surface states. These results establish the BgV as a designable vacuum for all-dielectric tight-binding photonics in two and three dimensions.

articles.title: Effect of Physical Barriers on High-Harmonic Generation in Liquid-Phase
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26045v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-harmonic generation (HHG) in liquid-phase systems presents fundamental differences from gas and solid phases, notably a reduction in the harmonic cutoff, its apparent independence from laser parameters, and the appearance of a second plateau. In this work, we introduce a one-dimensional quantum model that incorporates physical boundaries to simulate the effect of solvation shells in liquid water by means of a complex absorbing potential (CAP). By systematically varying the position, width, and strength of the CAP, we explore how these physical constraints influence the HHG spectrum. Our findings confirm that spatial confinement, specifically the physical truncation of electron trajectories, is the primary factor governing the cutoff in liquid-phase HHG. This confinement leads to a cutoff that is independent of laser intensity and wavelength, aligning with experimental observations and existing hypotheses proposed by Mondal et al. in 2023 and 2026. Furthermore, by implementing a semi-transparent CAP, we successfully reproduce the less intense second plateau observed in liquid-phase HHG. Time-frequency analysis confirms that this characteristic spectral feature is driven by partial wave-packet transmission through the solvation shells, which allows a surviving fraction of electrons to undergo longer continuum excursions. Our one-dimensional approach successfully isolates the fundamental role of physical boundaries in liquid-phase HHG, providing a clear and intuitive understanding of the underlying physics.

articles.title: Intermolecular Packing and Cooperative Stabilization in Nucleotide Monophosphate Crystals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26068v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine the known polymorphs of cytidine 5^prime-monophosphate (CMP) using dispersion-corrected density functional theory. The monoclinic phase is predicted to be the most stable, lying 1.76 and 3.00 kcal/mol per molecular unit below the orthorhombic and triclinic forms, respectively. Monoclinic CMP contains a ribose-based H-bonding motif along the crystallographic vecb direction, comprising alternating intra- and intermolecular interactions, motivating an investigation of cooperative stabilization along this pathway. We employ chain-of-molecules (COM) and chain-of-slabs (COS) models to quantify the direction- and size-dependent stabilization and extend the analysis to the corresponding 5^prime-monophosphates of thymidine, uridine, adenosine, and guanosine. Successive dimer-addition energies reveal the strongest size-dependent cooperative stabilization along the vecb direction, whereas growth along veca and vecc exhibits substantially weaker size dependence. Among the nucleotides examined, adenosine 5^prime-monophosphate shows the strongest chain-growth stabilization in the COM model, whereas the uridine variant shows the strongest stabilization in the COS model. Guanosine 5^prime-monophosphate exhibits the weakest response in both models. Minimal-basis iterative stockholder (MBIS) analysis further supports molecular polarization along the growing assemblies. These results demonstrate how nucleobase identity and the surrounding crystal environment modulate direction-dependent cooperative stabilization associated with extended hydrogen-bond networks.

articles.title: Reinforcement Learning Controllers for Fusion Scenario Development
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26138v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scenario development, the design of the waveforms that take a tokamak discharge from breakdown to flat-top, is still an iterative, labour-intensive process. Every candidate scenario has to be simulated with a controller in the loop, and the classical shape and current controllers need low-level actuator references. So the process is iterative and includes a number of trial-and-error steps. We propose to replace the per-scenario controller tuning by a single goal-conditioned reinforcement-learning controller trained once, in advance, against a free-boundary equilibrium and transport simulator. A scenario is then specified only by the target waveforms of the physical quantities of interest (plasma current, line-averaged electron density, LCFS shape, x-point positions), and the controller produces the coil-current and fueling commands that realize them. We demonstrate the approach on an EAST plasma-current ramp-up: the controller takes over a small limited plasma, ramps the current and the density, grows the cross-section, forms two x-points and holds a double-null diverted configuration against sampled shape targets for the rest of a 1.2 s episode. The neural network controller is trained using TQC algorithm. On 1024 test scenarios sampled from a low-discrepancy scrambled Sobol sequence in 11-dimensional target space, the controller forms the divertor in 86% of the cases, holds it for more than 0.5 s in 67% and reaches the end of the episode in a diverted state in 58%, with flat-top tracking errors of a few kA in plasma current, sim 0.15×10¹⁹ m⁻³ in density, sim 2 cm in position and sim 8 cm in x-point location; the failures concentrate at the high-current density (J) region which is believed to be physically or from engineering perspective not feasible within ohmic mode.

articles.title: Characterization of the R14374-10 photomultiplier tube for the Pacific Ocean Neutrino Experiment
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Pacific Ocean Neutrino Experiment (P-ONE) is a planned cubic-kilometer-scale neutrino telescope that will be deployed in the Pacific Ocean, leveraging deep-sea infrastructure operated by Ocean Networks Canada (ONC). The first detector line will deploy 320 3-inch Hamamatsu R14374-10 photomultiplier tubes (PMTs) to detect Cherenkov light produced by charged particles propagating through water, as well as light from calibration sources and optical backgrounds. This article presents the systematic characterization of all PMTs to be integrated into the first detector line prior to deployment, ensuring compliance with all detector acceptance criteria. All PMTs satisfy the specified performance criteria: the average transit-time spread (TTS) was measured to be 1.73± 0.15,ns, and the average charge resolution at a gain of num5e6 was 0.43± 0.03,pC; the average after-pulse rate was measured to be around 6,%. The integrated P-ONE data acquisition (DAQ) system was also tested and cross-validated against a laboratory digitization system. The second part of the paper presents an in-depth characterization of a subset of six PMTs, focusing on the key properties required for detector simulations, including linearity, after-pulse rate, quantum efficiency, and relative collection efficiency. PMT linearity was measured at a gain of num5e6 using the complete P-ONE readout electronics, and the response was found to remain linear for signals up to 150 photoelectrons. After-pulse contributions from Cs⁺, He⁺, and other ions were identified in the subset. The peak quantum efficiency was measured to be 27.0±0.7,% at 395,nm. Using measurements of the relative detection efficiency, the collection efficiency was found to differ by a wavelength-independent offset of 10--15% across the measured wavelength range.

articles.title: Leaky-Wave Antenna for Non-Invasive Continuous Glucose Monitoring
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26317v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-invasive continuous glucose monitoring requires sensing techniques capable of delivering stable, accurate, and real-time quantification of glucose-induced dielectric variations. This paper presents a microwave-based methodology that employs a leaky-wave antenna (LWA) to launch localized traveling electromagnetic waves and estimate glucose concentration through phase measurements at a fixed operating frequency. The LWA architecture enhances electromagnetic coupling with the material under test through controlled energy leakage, enabling strong linearity and high phase sensitivity within the physiological permittivity range (relative permittivity 68-70). In vitro measurements using fetal bovine serum-glucose samples demonstrate a total phase shift of 8.51 degree across glucose concentrations from 50 to 255 mg per liter. Preliminary in vivo experiments conducted on two human subjects show strong correlations between measured S11 phase and reference glucose levels (r=0.939 and r=0.906), confirming the potential of the LWA-based sensing mechanism to track dynamic glycemic variations in a proof-of-concept setting. These results highlight the potential of the proposed approach for practical, continuous, and non-invasive glucose monitoring.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal spherical Gaussian pulses
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe a class of electromagnetic Gaussian modes with spherical spatiotemporal structure that remains invariant during propagation through anomalously dispersive media. The angular profile of the modes is given by spherical harmonics, whose quantization axis can be freely chosen. As a result, the modes support spatiotemporal orbital angular momentum (OAM) configurations with longitudinal and transverse components set by the orientation of the quantization axis. Superpositions of these modes generalize the familiar solution of a chirped pulse that simultaneously focuses and compresses to arbitrary angular structure. The modes are derived through a series of unitary transformations that map the dispersive paraxial wave equation onto a Schrödinger equation with a 3D isotropic harmonic potential. These transformations facilitate the identification of conserved operators for mixed longitudinal and transverse OAM.

articles.title: Observation and control of polariton noise in a thermal Rydberg atom electrometer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26479v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The establishment of metrics and control of fundamental noise sources in quantum sensing is a long-standing goal in quantum science and technology. We report on the observation of polariton-mediated optical noise in a thermal Rydberg atom vapor and demonstrate its active control and suppression using a radio-frequency field in Rydberg electrometry. The noise exhibits structured amplification and reduction across the Rydberg electromagnetically induced transparency resonance. This reveals a nonlinear slow-light feedback mechanism in which the polariton medium stores and releases probe-field energy. We show that the reference radio-frequency field used in Rydberg heterodyne receivers can also tune the medium into an operating regime where high electromagnetic-field responsivity coincides with reduced optical noise. This operating-point control enables optimization of the electric-field sensitivity within the constraints imposed by Rydberg-polariton physics. These results establish polariton noise as a previously unrecognized intrinsic noise source in thermal Rydberg vapors and the corresponding control method as a crucial aspect of continued efforts to achieve fundamental sensitivity limits in Rydberg electrometry.

articles.title: A mixed leading variable physics-informed neural network for nonsmooth dynamics simulation in contact systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26495v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-accuracy computation of nonsmooth dynamics is a challenging problem in systems with multiple frictional contacts. This study proposes a general physics-informed neural network framework, termed the mixed leading variable physics-informed neural network (MLV-PINN). By using the governing equations and contact-friction laws as physical constraints, this framework provides common solution approaches for computing nonsmooth dynamics not only in discrete systems but also in continuum systems. Specifically, the network represents accelerations, normal contact forces and friction margins as independent outputs and determines them simultaneously, without first reducing the dynamics to discrete velocity-impulse complementary subproblems. A composite physics-informed loss is constructed from the equations of motion in their original form, contact-friction complementary conditions and a friction-margin consistency relation. To improve stick-slip state identification during PINN optimisation, a mixed leading variable combining relative tangential velocity and acceleration is introduced to reformulate the tangential complementary conditions. Four benchmark simulations cover one-dimensional (1-D) nonsmooth dynamics involving single-contact stick-slip, 1-D nonsmooth dynamics involving multi-contact stick-slip, two-dimensional (2-D) nonsmooth dynamics with coupled normal contact-separation and tangential stick-slip, and 2-D nonsmooth dynamics in a continuum system involving moving contact on an elastic beam. Benchmark comparisons show substantial reductions in displacement and velocity errors relative to the corresponding conventional methods at large time steps. These results, together with an ablation study and tests involving friction-velocity slopes, long-time integration and loss weights, illustrate the computational accuracy and support the broad applicability of the proposed framework.

articles.title: Single-Mode Laser Arrays with Size-Invariant Loss Discrimination
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26578v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In conventional coupled oscillator lattices and laser arrays, expanding the active volume inevitably causes spectral crowding and degrades spatial uniformity, posing a long-standing barrier to high-power single-mode operation. We uncover a dissipative selection mechanism in sparse star networks that decouples modal selectivity from lattice size constraints. By engineering dissipative auxiliary couplings between a central hub and N peripheral resonators, the system establishes an exact star-Laplacian symmetry. This enforces a target eigenstate that is immune to all lossy channels while maintaining equal amplitude across all main nodes. All competing eigenstates break this symmetry, driving the auxiliary loss and opening a persistent, size-independent modal loss gap that prevents multi-mode competition. Realistic microring simulations validate the robustness of this dark-state isolation under electromagnetic dispersion and mechanism extension to arbitrary arrays is allowed when meets the system's exceptional point. By exploiting graph topology to bypass multi-mode competition, this work establishes a general route toward scalable high-power single-supermode laser arrays and robust state selection in coupled non-Hermitian systems.

articles.title: NIR-probe transient absorption on rubrene microcavities demonstrates no changes to singlet fission by strong coupling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Strong light-matter coupling has been proposed to control singlet-exciton fission, yet reported effects remain controversial due to the prevalence of cavity-induced optical artifacts in transient absorption measurements. Here, we investigate singlet fission in dielectric microcavities containing rubrene by probing in the near-infrared region, outside the cavity stopband, to eliminate mode-filtering artifacts. Across contrasting cavity quality factors (Q = 90 and 1150) and a range of exciton-photon detunings (+20 to -110 meV), we find that the underlying kinetics are virtually identical to uncoupled films. Although minor spectral changes occur, transfer matrix simulations reveal these stem purely from mirror interference rather than modified photophysics. Transient electron paramagnetic resonance further confirms that high-spin triplet dynamics remain unperturbed. Together, these findings establish a widely applicable experimental framework for evaluating molecular photophysics in microcavities, revealing that singlet fission remains unaltered in strongly coupled rubrene.

articles.title: Commercial building decarbonization across countries: Future emission trajectories and mitigation priorities
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26696v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With energy-related carbon dioxide emissions remaining at high levels, decarbonizing commercial building operations across key economies is critical for achieving global climate targets. This study assesses future operational carbon trajectories, mitigation potential, and the driving factors of this potential in commercial building operations across 16 countries from 2024 to 2060 by combining a Kaya-based emission model and Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis. The key findings indicate that (1) under the business-as-usual scenario, China's commercial building operational carbon emissions are projected to peak at 1150 (+-120) million tonnes of carbon dioxide (MtCO2) in 2033 (+-5 years), while the remaining countries exhibit differentiated carbon lock-in levels, with the highest level in the United States at 470 (+-89) MtCO2. (2) The total emission reduction potential increases from 352 MtCO2 in 2030 to 1119 MtCO2 in 2050 and stabilizes at 1123 MtCO2 in 2060, with China, the United States, and Japan contributing 84.7%-88.9% of the total potential. (3) By 2060, the mitigation potential from energy intensity reduction is concentrated mainly in China and the United States, reaching 52 and 32 MtCO2, respectively; end-use decomposition further identifies space heating and appliances as key targets for decarbonizing commercial building operations. In summary, this study characterizes future operational carbon trajectories and clarifies the drivers and end-use priorities of mitigation potential in commercial building operations, providing cross-country evidence for differentiated strategies for long-term commercial building decarbonization.

articles.title: Magneto-Rayleigh-Taylor instability driven by a rotating magnetic field: Cylindrical liner configuration
articles.abstract: arXiv:1711.08891v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose using a directional time-varying (rotating) driving magnetic field to suppress magneto-Rayleigh-Taylor (MRT) instability in dynamic Z-pinches. A rotational drive magnetic field is equivalent to two magnetic-field components, Θ and Z, that alternate in time, referred to as an alternate Theta-Z-pinch configuration. We consider the finitely thick cylindrical liner configuration in this paper. We numerically integrate the perturbation equation to stagnation time based on the optimal background unperturbed trajectories. We assess the cumulative growth of the dominant mode selected by some mechanism at the beginning of an implosion. The maximum e-folding number at stagnation of the dominant mode of an optimized alternate Theta-Z-pinch is significantly lower than that of the standard Theta- or Z-pinch. The directional rotation of the magnetic field contributes to suppress the instabilities, independent of the finite thickness. The finite thickness effect plays a role only when the orientation of the magnetic field varies in time whereas it does not appear in the standard Theta- or Z-pinch. The rotating frequency of the magnetic field and the thickness of liner are both having a monotonic effect on suppression. Their synergistic effect can enhance the suppression on MRT instability. Because the MRT instability can be well suppressed in this way, the alternate Theta-Z-pinch configuration has potential applications in liner inertial fusion. This work is supported by the NSFC (Grant Nos. 11405167, 51407171, 11571293, 11605188, and 11605189) and the Foundation of the China Academy of Engineering Physics (No. 2015B0201023).

articles.title: Parameter misspecification in physics-informed neural networks: A closed-form audit and its limits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23948v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are trained to minimize the residual of a prescribed equation, so a low training loss does not indicate whether a coefficient in that equation was specified incorrectly. This study evaluates what can be inferred about the encoded parameter from the trained network alone. When the residual is linear in the parameter, written as A - ν B, the least-squares estimate hatν = AtopB/BtopB is obtained from a single evaluation of the frozen network, without retraining or reference data. Its accuracy depends on how closely the network satisfies its own equation, quantified by a normalized residual ρ. Recovery error is associated with ρ (log-log correlation 0.72 across 36 convection-diffusion networks), and empirical exponents of 0.63 to 1.20 across three equations decompose into one half plus a measurable angular term. For Burgers' equation, a single-model test based on a block-bootstrap standard error flagged 3 of 300 correctly specified networks (observed false-alarm rate 1%), all 2% misspecifications at a practical budget, and two thirds of 1% misspecifications after convergence. For the self-similar blowup rate of the Córdoba-Córdoba-Fontelos equation, where the rate also enters the architecture, the estimator recovers about half of the misspecification, whereas ρ increases approximately quadratically and distinguishes a 0.2% error. When the incorrect rate enters both the equation and the architecture, errors of up to 2% were not detected at the precision reached. At practical budgets, the raw loss can be lower for the misspecified model, a scaling effect that ρ does not share.

articles.title: Critical magnetic Reynolds number of the weakly-collisional turbulent dynamo in supersonic plasmas
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24394v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Weakly-collisional plasmas are found in several turbulent astrophysical environments, such as the Intra-galaxy-cluster medium (ICM) and the solar wind, where magnetic fields can be amplified by the turbulent dynamo. The onset of dynamo action is determined by the critical magnetic Reynolds number, rm Rmᵣₘ cᵣᵢₜ, above which turbulent motions amplify magnetic energy. Although rm Rmᵣₘ cᵣᵢₜ has been studied extensively in collisional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) turbulence, its value in supersonic weakly-collisional plasmas remains unknown. Here we determine rm Rmᵣₘ cᵣᵢₜ using three-dimensional hybrid particle-in-cell (HPIC) simulations of solenoidally driven turbulence with a sonic Mach number approx 2. We vary the magnetic Reynolds number over rm Rmapprox31-1000 and consider two initial plasma magnetisations, characterised by initial Larmor ratios rᵣₘ Lₐᵣₘₒᵣ, ₀/Lᵣₘ bₒₓ=1 and 100. We find that the magnetic energy grows exponentially at sufficiently large rm Rm and decays when magnetic diffusion dominates at low rm Rm. By fitting the magnetic-energy growth rate as a function of rm Rm, we measure rm Rmᵣₘ cᵣᵢₜ=190⁺²¹₋₁₇ and 198⁺¹⁶₋₁₈ for the initially magnetised and unmagnetised plasma, respectively. These values are the same within their uncertainties, indicating that the initial plasma magnetisation does not significantly affect rm Rmᵣₘ cᵣᵢₜ in the supersonic regime. The measured values are higher than those previously obtained for the subsonic weakly-collisional dynamo, showing that increasing compressibility makes weakly-collisional turbulent dynamo action more difficult to excite. The measured values are also approximately 1.5 times higher than the rm Rmᵣₘ cᵣᵢₜ value reported for supersonic MHD turbulence.

articles.title: Quantum-Correlation-Based Multi-Emitter Localization in Information-Limited Regimes via Learned Inference
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24457v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum correlation measurements have emerged as a powerful tool for localizing multiple emitters with subwavelength separation. Multi-emitter localization consists of two distinct tasks: identifying the emitter count N and estimating their positions leftxⁱright. Existing fit-and-select frameworks fit the measured intensity and autocorrelation data using several models corresponding to different values of N and then select the best-supported model. This procedure lets errors from the multi-parameter optimization of emitter positions propagate into the choice of model, degrading performance under photon-limited and high-background conditions. We propose a method that directly infers the emitter count and positions from the multimodal data via learned inference. Learned inference improves both the emitter-counting accuracy and localization precision compared to the fit-and-select method. It achieves more than tenfold improvement in precision and requires up to five times fewer photons to achieve practically meaningful localization with the largest gains observed under low photon counts, strong background, narrowly spaced emitter configurations, and spatially truncated data. This photon-efficient quantum-assisted localization framework offers a promising route toward real-time biological imaging and single-particle tracking in densely labeled samples.

articles.title: Spherical Physics-informed Neural Operator with Multi-scale Coupling for Meteorological Downscaling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24708v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Meteorological downscaling is crucial for high-resolution regional climate forecasting and disaster early warning. While neural operators have emerged as a promising paradigm for modeling complex spatiotemporal mappings, existing frameworks often struggle with spherical manifold geometric distortions, inherent atmospheric multi-scale coupling mismatches, and lack of explicit atmospheric laws. We propose the Spherical Physics-informed Neural Operator, which utilizes a Spherical Laplacian Decomposition to partition atmospheric fields into hierarchical frequency components, maintaining exact point-wise correspondence across scales. To evaluate these representations at arbitrary locations, we introduce a localized spherical integral operator that approximates continuous kernel transforms via geometry-aware attention. Dynamical consistency is further enforced by embedding differentiable constraints into the learning process. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our framework attains superior accuracy and zero-shot generalization across various meteorological variables and unseen queries, representing a robust and interpretable solution for global-to-regional meteorological downscaling.

articles.title: A 4-20 GHz Superconducting 90deg Hybrid Using Capacitively Loaded Coupled Lines for 2SB Heterodyne Receivers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24859v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We report the design and cryogenic characterisation of a broadband superconducting 90deg intermediate-frequency (IF) hybrid covering 4 to 20 GHz for sideband-separating (2SB) heterodyne receivers. The hybrid is implemented in thin-film niobium using capacitively loaded edge coupled transmission lines, avoiding the air-bridge interconnections required in Lange-coupler layouts while retaining a compact superconducting implementation with low loss and good quadrature balance. Cryogenic measurements using Vector Network Analyser (VNA) show amplitude and phase imbalance better than 0.6 dB and 6deg, respectively, across the full band. When used in a 2SB receiver, this level of IF balance is consistent with the observed image-rejection performance in the 10-20 dB range, for the full receiver. The design supports the development of wide-instantaneous-bandwidth 2SB receivers for millimeter and submillimeter observatories, improving spectral grasp for broadband line surveys and high-redshift line searches.

articles.title: Spontaneous brain-wide rotational dynamics constrain cue-evoked behavior
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.25061v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Uncovering low-dimensional representations of brain-wide neural dynamics and their relationship to behavior remains a central challenge. Here, we show that spontaneous brain-wide rotational dynamics constrain cue-evoked behavior and learning. To systematically establish these findings, we developed a dimensionality-reduction technique called Rotational Component Analysis (RCA) that optimizes the detection of low-variance rotational modes even within individual trials. We applied RCA to motor-cortical spike-train data from monkeys and humans, mouse cortex-wide calcium imaging, and human functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and magnetoencephalography (MEG). In mice, a rotational mode identified from activity recorded at rest predicts cue-evoked behavior: the phase of rotation when a randomly timed cue arrives predicts whether the animal subsequently pulls the lever. We explain this surprisingly strong correlation using both a recurrent neural network (RNN) and a minimal two-dimensional model of response learning, in which the intrinsic rotational mode serves as a dynamical constraint on response and learning. We further identify double-rotation modes containing two centers of rotation that separate preparatory from task dynamics in both mouse and human data. Remarkably, corresponding modes also organize neural dynamics during a non-motor human task, and rotational irreversibility captures early psychosis even when principal component analysis shows no group difference. Our work establishes rotational dynamics as low-dimensional coordinates that constrain how ongoing brain states are converted into behavior. More broadly, RCA provides a versatile tool for detecting hidden nonreciprocal dynamics in biological and physical datasets.

articles.title: Measurement-efficient energy estimator for quantum chemistry of photodynamic materials
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26689v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Accurate modelling of chemical reaction rates requires precise correlated energy differences. Quantum computing offers a potential route to their determination, but extracting energies from quantum-prepared states can demand prohibitive sampling. We demonstrate measurement-efficient correlated energy estimation using an electronically challenging H₂DBB--Ru model derived from a Ru-functionalized hafnium metal-organic framework relevant to radiodynamic and photodynamic therapies. The mixed estimator combines a quantum-prepared target with sparse multiconfiguration references and recovers ground-state corrections using magnitude-only compute-uncompute measurements. Analytical variance estimates predict 1.6 mHa precision with a few hundred shots, about 100 times fewer than the single-determinant formulation and three orders of magnitude fewer than optimized Hamiltonian-term sampling. With approximate targets, it reaches comparable accuracy using simpler state preparation than direct expectation-value estimation. Emulator and trapped-ion experiments on Quantinuum Helios validate the approach up to (10,10), including a 50-qubit circuit combining AI-assisted state preparation with error detection, providing a measurement-efficient route to correlated energy differences for challenging chemical problems.

articles.title: The hidden spin-momentum locking and topological defects in unpolarized light fields
articles.abstract: arXiv:2309.13997v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Electromagnetic waves characterized by intensity, phase, and polarization degrees of freedom are widely applied in data storage, encryption, and communications. However, these properties can be substantially affected by phase disorders and disturbances, whereas high-dimensional degrees of freedom including momentum and angular momentum of electromagnetic waves can offer new insights into their features and phenomena, for example topological characteristics and structures that are robust to these disturbances. Here, we discover and demonstrate theoretically and experimentally spin-momentum locking and topological defects in unpolarized light. The coherent spin is locked to the kinetic momentum except for a small coupling spin term, due to the simultaneous presence of transverse magnetic and electric components in unpolarized light. To cancel the coupling term, we employ a metal film acting as a polarizer to form some skyrmion-like spin textures at the metal/air interface. Using an in-house scanning optical microscopic system to image the out-of-plane spin density of the focused unpolarized vortex light, we obtained experimental results that coincide well with our theoretical predictions. The theory and technique promote the applications of topological defects in optical data storage, encryption, and decryption, and communications.

articles.title: SynradG4: A Geant4-Based Extension for Synchrotron Radiation Background Studies in the ePIC Detector at the Electron-Ion Collider
articles.abstract: arXiv:2408.11709v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) will operate at high luminosity with multi-GeV, high-current electron beams, resulting in substantial synchrotron radiation (SR) emission in the electron storage ring (ESR). A detailed understanding of SR photon transport in the complex three-dimensional interaction region (IR) geometry is critical for estimating backgrounds in the ePIC detector and for developing effective shielding and masking strategies. This paper presents SynradG4, an EIC-specific extension of Geant4 for fast photon tracking in vacuum based on established models of SR reflection and rough-surface scattering.
