An application is provided for a bi-directionally stiffened panel and the influence of reduction parameters is discussed, as well as the robustness of the numerical results.

articles.title: Terabit-scale wavelength-multiplexed transmitter enabled by thin-film lithium tantalate
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26674v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial-intelligence systems face a growing data-movement bottleneck and require higher interconnect bandwidth without a proportional increase in electrical power consumption or the number of laser sources and fibre connections. Moving optical interfaces closer to computing chips reduces electrical transmission loss, while demanding optical engines that combine high channel capacity, broadband modulation and simple packaging. Although wavelength multiplexing relieves pressure on the fibre budget, integrating shared multi-wavelength sources with dense wavelength routing and broadband modulation in a compact format remains challenging. Here we demonstrate a monolithic transmitter that brings these functions together on a single material platform, enabled by the low birefringence and native Pockels response of thin-film lithium tantalate. The device separates, independently modulates and recombines eight wavelength channels between one optical input and output. This architecture retains a two-fibre interface as the channel count grows, directly addressing the packaging burden of parallel optical links. Measurements across the eight channels establish an aggregate line rate of 1.6 Tbit s⁻¹. Operation with a shared optical frequency comb achieves an estimated net data rate of 0.58 Tbit s⁻¹ across four channels, demonstrating compatibility with a common multi-wavelength source. Scaling this architecture into multiple wavelength-multiplexed engines offers a path towards 10 Tbit s⁻¹ optical interfaces with high bandwidth per unit package edge, positioning thin-film lithium tantalate for the next generation of co-packaged optical interconnects.

articles.title: QRecoupling.jl: numerical and exact computation of classical and quantum recoupling coefficients
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24074v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: QRecoupling.jl is a Julia package for numerical, exact and symbolic evaluation of classical and quantum recoupling coefficients and generic finite sums of quantum factorials, with one interface across the classical limit, principal unitary levels and real or complex deformation. A compact factorial rule and its cyclotomic exponents expose factor cancellation, polynomial structure and level support. The package covers quantum Clebsch-Gordan coefficients, 3j and 6j symbols and user-defined sums. Its adaptive numerical evaluation is combined with exact decisions for sums that cancel to zero. Classical 3j and 6j symbols are evaluated at a speed comparable to that of WIGXJPF, which is based on prime factorization tables, at the smallest spins, and about 6 and 10 times faster at spin cutoff 500. Under real, root-of-unity and complex deformation, the largest relative error measured against independent high-precision references is 3.5 × 10⁻¹⁴ for spins up to 400. Fusion matrices with 401 channels are computed about 100 times faster than by loops over their entries.

articles.title: Probing wetting and solidification dynamics of neon thin films with a high-T_c superconducting circuit
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24167v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Integrating condensed noble gases with superconducting circuits offers new opportunities for operating hybrid quantum devices. In particular, electrons on solid neon have recently emerged as exceptionally coherent charge qubits, however the growth of the underlying neon films on patterned devices remains poorly controlled. We monitor neon films near the triple point using a multimode resonator fabricated from high-T_c YBCO, which remains superconducting at temperatures where the liquid phase exists and whose geometry sets a thickness-sensing window near 1 μm. In the liquid state we observe rich film dynamics: uniform wetting that saturates near 20 nm, drainage of thicker films, and spontaneous thickness oscillations, reflecting the extreme sensitivity of thick films in this regime. A galvanic connection to our sensing volume enables in-situ electrostatic tuning of the liquid film thickness. Statistics of freezing the neon across various liquid levels reveal variations of the solid film thickness by approximately an order of magnitude. We also observe a two-fold increase in the quality factor of the resonators at the level of 10³ with added neon and rule out dielectric loss as the limiting factor. Our results demonstrate that hermetic packaging facilitates the investigation of both rich non-equilibrium fluid dynamics and the impact of condensed noble gas films on microwave loss in superconducting circuits, but may not be the best modality for growing solid neon films with precisely controlled thickness.

articles.title: Intermittent turbulence as the driver of stochastic heating in the near-Sun solar wind
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24296v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Understanding the mechanism by which the energy is dissipated at small scales to heat the outer corona and expanding solar wind, is a primary goal of the Parker Solar Probe (PSP) mission, and an outstanding question in heliophysics. Recent observational case studies have suggested that the dominant dissipation mechanism(s), stochastic heating (SH) or resonant heating (RH), may be modulated by the Alfvén `surface' (M_A = 1), while theoretical and simulation works predict that the mechanism should be modulated by the level of turbulence imbalance. We measure the local energy transfer (LET) rate from 9.8 to 55 solar radii from PSP observations, showing that the LET rate peaks at M_A sim 0.4 - 0.9. We connect enhanced LET rates to signatures of intermittency, highlighting the key role that intermittent fluctuations play in heating the near-Sun solar wind. We compare the LET rate with estimates of the SH rate, finding that below sim 15 solar radii the SH heating rate matches the LET rate provided intermittency is accounted for, regardless of M_A, while farther from the Sun, SH is unable to account for the observed LET rate. In contrast to predictions by recent theoretical works, this implies that `imbalanced' intermittent stochastic heating may be a viable mechanism to heat highly imbalanced, low-β collisionless plasmas, and is likely an important mechanism of dissipation in the outer solar corona and near-Sun solar wind.

articles.title: Adaptive Model-Switch Thermodynamic Integration: A Bayes Factor Estimator
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24354v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bayes factors are a widely used model comparison criterion, but are often quite challenging and computationally expensive to estimate well. We propose a variation of the model-switch thermodynamic integration method for estimating Bayes factors that decreases the variance of the estimator and essentially eliminates integration error. We choose samples whose density in β is proportional to the standard deviation of previously drawn samples. Rather than averaging many samples at each β, we use a very dense set of β values, collecting one sample at each in order of increasing β and one sample at each in order of decreasing β to minimize "thermic lag". We study our procedure with a toy model (based loosely on some signal recovery problems). In this model we find that adaptive sampling gives us a 2.7-fold decrease in the spread of the estimated Bayes factor. We test our procedure both drawing directly from the posterior distribution and using a Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampler.

articles.title: Squeezing and Decoherence of Axion Dark Matter
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.25466v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bosonic particles beyond the Standard Model, such as axions, are among the leading candidates for dark matter. If such particles have a small mass, they are usually described as a purely classical field. However, it was recently shown that this description is incomplete: their inherent gravitational self-interactions can squeeze the field, producing a quantum feature beyond the classical description. Here we analyze squeezing of light dark matter in the presence of decoherence. We show that squeezing is continuously generated, and rapidly enough to survive dissipation, and may also remain present under thermal fluctuations and dephasing. Our results demonstrate that dark matter might possess persistent quantum features and motivate further investigation of their implications for dark matter detection.

articles.title: Measuring the Quantum Phase of Multiphoton Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.25727v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The quantum phase of a multiparticle system has remained a long-standing mystery in quantum physics. The absence of a phase operator that faithfully represents this physical quantity has prevented the formulation of a meaningful uncertainty relation with particle number. Here, we resolve this problem by measuring, for the first time, the quantum phase of multiparticle systems containing up to fifteen particles. We achieve this through a new quantum state tomography scheme that combines homodyne interferometry with photon-number-resolving detection. This approach enables us to reconstruct complementary photon-number and phase representations and establish the corresponding number-phase uncertainty relation. Our measurements further provide access to the mutually unbiased basis of a multiparticle system, a fundamental resource for multiparticle quantum information processing. Furthermore, we report the spatially resolved characterization of the quantum phase. These results provide an operational framework for measuring quantum phase in multiparticle systems, with implications for fundamental quantum physics and scalable multiparticle quantum technologies.

articles.title: Time-resolved transient absorption spectroscopy with quantum light
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26041v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a fully quantum theory of time-resolved transient absorption spectroscopy, providing a general framework for describing the linear response of a nonequilibrium target to quantum probe fields beyond the semiclassical approximation. We elucidate how quantum correlations between probe-field frequency modes couple to coherences in the target and derive a simple expression for computing the resulting spectroscopic signals. We identify conditions under which quantum light can modify transient absorption spectra beyond the limits achievable with classical fields. Our work establishes a theoretical foundation for exploiting quantum light in ultrafast spectroscopy and suggests new routes for resolving dynamics in matter on timescales shorter than the duration of the probe pulse.

articles.title: Sensitive dependence of the motion of a legged robot on granular media
articles.abstract: arXiv:0905.4950v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Legged locomotion on flowing ground (em e.g. granular media) is unlike locomotion on hard ground because feet experience both solid- and fluid-like forces during surface penetration. Recent bio-inspired legged robots display speed relative to body size on hard ground comparable to high performing organisms like cockroaches but suffer significant performance loss on flowing materials like sand. In laboratory experiments we study the performance (speed) of a small (2.3 kg) six-legged robot, SandBot, as it runs on a bed of granular media (1 mm poppy seeds). For an alternating tripod gait on the granular bed, standard gait control parameters achieve speeds at best two orders of magnitude smaller than the 2 body lengths/s (approx 60 cm/s) for motion on hard ground. However, empirical adjustment of these control parameters away from the hard ground settings, restores good performance, yielding top speeds of 30 cm/s. Robot speed depends sensitively on the packing fraction φ and the limb frequency ω, and a dramatic transition from rotary walking to slow swimming occurs when φ becomes small enough and/or ω large enough. We propose a kinematic model of the rotary walking mode based on generic features of penetration and slip of a curved limb in granular media. The model captures the dependence of robot speed on limb frequency and the transition between walking and swimming modes but highlights the need for a deeper understanding of the physics of granular media.

articles.title: Nanoparticle arrays levitated in a cavity for quantum sensing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2406.00366v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Levitated nanoparticles are being investigated as ultrasensitive quantum sensors of forces and accelerations, with applications ranging from fundamental physics phenomena such as dark matter or quantum gravity to real world applications. Attention is now turning to multiparticle regimes, and an important question is whether collective effects offer advantages for sensing. We investigate here the spectral characteristics of collective motion of N  trapped nanoparticles interacting via the optical mode of a cavity. We find the collective motion typically exhibit two generic spectral features: a broad spectral feature, the collective bright mode (CBM) which has been previously studied; but we find also a new structure of sharp peaks , the mechanical mode comb (MMC). We can describe all the detailed spectral features of the system, with a simple closed-form expression, by reducing the motion to a 1D generic collective mode which is non-Hermitian. We show that the MMC is more advantageous than the usual CBM for increased sensitivity in force sensing. We find that the mechanical comb can autonomously repair loss of `teeth' due to particle loss, a feature that may offer robustness in sensing.

articles.title: IRENE: a fluId layeR finitE-elemeNt softwarE
articles.abstract: arXiv:2506.17827v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a finite-element software library, IRENE, which allows to solve numerically the dynamics of a viscous fluid layer embedded in three-dimensional space. Unlike finite-element libraries present in the literature, IRENE can handle two-dimensional open surfaces with a wide range of boundary conditions, and inter-surface obstacles with any shapes, and is built upon the user-friendly and versatile finite element computational software (FEniCS). Also, the library can describe a wide range of physical regimes--both low-Reynolds-number and inertia-dominated ones--capturing the complex coupling between in-plane flows, out-of-plane deformations, surface tension, and elastic response. We validate IRENE against known analytical and numerical results, and demonstrate its capabilities through physical examples. Overall, IRENE provides a versatile and efficient tool for understanding fluid-layer dynamics on multiple physical scales, from flows of lipidic membranes on a microscopic level, to fluid flows on a macroscopic scale, to atmospheric air flows on a planetary level.

articles.title: An Algebra Bundle for Non-Composable Coincidence Probabilities in Gamma-ray Spectroscopy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2512.00095v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Understanding nuclear level schemes from the detection of emitted gamma-rays is, at its core, a combinatorial problem. The transition matrix formalism that treats nuclear decay as a Markov process is a well established treatment for the prediction of emitted and detected gamma-rays. However, with the path algebra being the underlying algebra of such matrix methods, the formalism is restricted to calculating probabilities only for composable paths through the decay. This paper presents a new algebra that allows for the calculations of non-composable coincidence probabilities offering a more complete formalism for the prediction of gamma-ray spectra. The aim of this coincidence algebra is to provide a general treatment for predicting all full energy summing peaks for composable and non-composable transitions. Non-composable summing peaks often corrupt peaks of interest by creating doublets in the energy spectra. The coincidence algebra serves as a tool for investigating any possible doublets produced from full energy coincidence summing. This formalism is tested for the prediction of gamma-ray peaks in the electron capture of ¹³³Ba and compared to the results a Geant4 simulation of the decay within the GRIFFIN spectrometer. It is also shown how the path algebra formalism may be useful for understanding uncertainty propagation in nuclear level schemes.

articles.title: From Poincare Invariance to Gauge Theories: Yang-Mills and General Relativity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2512.02052v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article is founded on two fundamental principles: the principle field equations introduced in Refs. citeS, S1, S2 and the Fock-Ivanenko covariant derivatives citeFI, F. The former yields the equations of motion for free fields of arbitrary spin and helicity. In the massless case, it also dictates that Lorentz transformations for tensor fields acquire an additional term, which takes the form of a gauge transformation citeW, S1. The latter principle, the Fock-Ivanenko derivative, introduces interactions based on the intrinsic and Poincare groups. This framework allows us to recover a complete Yang-Mills theory, as well as general relativity in the connection-based formulations of Palatini and Ashtekar, both of which are theories with local gauge symmetries. While the standard approach begins with the symmetries of a matter action, we will instead derive dynamics directly from Poincare invariance. This perspective reveals that for free fields, Lorentz invariance induces the gauge symmetry of massless tensors. A proper definition of these gauge transformations, in turn, requires the covariant derivatives provided by the Fock-Ivanenko approach. Considering matter fields, we derive the interacting Dirac equation in the presence of Yang-Mills and gravitational fields from its free counterpart.

articles.title: A Level Set Method on Particle Flow Maps
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.09939v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Accurate interface tracking is central to numerical simulations involving moving boundaries, including multiphase flows, free-surface dynamics, phase-change problems, and other interface-driven processes in computational mechanics. Although level set methods provide a flexible implicit representation of evolving interfaces, their grid-based advection and reinitialization procedures often introduce numerical diffusion, volume loss, and degradation of thin or highly curved structures. This paper introduces a Particle Flow Map Level Set (PFM-LS) method that addresses these limitations by transporting interface geometry through particle-carried bidirectional flow maps. In contrast to particle level set methods that use particles mainly as corrective markers, PFM-LS uses particles as primary carriers of level-set values, gradients, and Hessians within a narrow band around the interface. The method combines long-range flow-map transport, high-order particle-grid reconstruction, adaptive particle control, and a hybrid particle-grid redistancing scheme to preserve both signed-distance consistency and sub-grid geometric features. Numerical benchmarks in two and three dimensions, including topology-change tests, chamfer and Hausdorff shape-error metrics, and coupling to an incompressible free-surface flow solver, show that PFM-LS achieves strong volume preservation, high shape fidelity, and near fourth-order convergence, outperforming a broad range of existing level set and reference-map-based methods.

articles.title: SECURE-AI: Multi-Signal Uncertainty Quantification for Trustworthy Acoustic Cough Detection
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Acoustic models for cough detection achieve high accuracy on curated benchmarks but fail silently in deployment, where speech, environmental noise, and audio unlike the training data induce confident misclassifications. In health monitoring, a confidently wrong prediction is worse than no answer at all. We present SECURE-AI (Self-aware Estimation of Cough Uncertainty for Reliable Evaluation of AI), a multi-signal uncertainty quantification framework that wraps a frozen MobileNetV3 cough classifier and estimates when its predictions should not be trusted, combining Monte Carlo Dropout, Temperature Scaling, and Mahalanobis distance in the embedding space. On a held-out split of 12,161 Coswara recordings, the probability-space methods are individually insufficient: Monte Carlo Dropout assigns lower uncertainty to incorrect than to correct predictions, and temperature scaling improves calibration but not discrimination. The strongest signal is embedding-space distance: Mahalanobis distance separates true positives from false positives (means 44.7 versus 63.4; Cohen's d = 0.94; AUROC 0.86) and, among predicted non-coughs, false negatives from true negatives (AUROC 0.82), so the same signal can flag both false alarms and missed coughs. At a descriptive operating point selected from labeled test data, retaining 90 percent of true-positive detections removes about two-thirds of false positives and raises precision from 59.9 to roughly 80 percent. A rejection threshold tuned on one split does not transfer to another (validation F1 of 82 percent falls to 34 percent on test), so we report threshold-independent AUROC as the main measure. An error taxonomy shows that failures are systematic, with most false positives related to speech. The pipeline runs on Raspberry Pi hardware costing 30 to 90 US dollars. Probabilistic calibration alone is thus inadequate for reliable cough detection.

articles.title: EdgeKernelBench: Unified LLM-Driven Kernel Generation for Edge Backends
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24648v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent works show that LLMs can generate kernels with strong performance on server GPUs. Edge deployment presents distinct challenges because the hardware is heterogeneous, the software stacks are fragmented, and the resource budgets are tight. LLM kernel generation across diverse edge backends has yet to be studied systematically. We introduce EdgeKernelBench, which combines a unified IR deployment framework with a hierarchical benchmark for edge workloads. The unified IR captures reusable computation, scheduling, and memory decisions and connects to each target backend through a compiler interface. The benchmark spans progressively larger program scopes, from individual operators to compact model graphs, across representative edge application domains. We instantiate the design with TVM as a reference compiler and validate it across heterogeneous edge backends. With a single generation attempt, the best model achieves 64.5% Correct@1 but only 25.5% Fast@1.0. This gap shows that functional correctness does not consistently translate into performance gains. We therefore introduce the Layered Edge Kernel Agent (LEKA), which organizes optimization through a layered IR. On the agent evaluation subset, LEKA achieves 43.5% Fast@1.0, compared with 13.0% for direct generation and 26.1% for Claude Code. LEKA and Claude Code use the same base model and optimization budget. Together, EdgeKernelBench and LEKA support unified evaluation and layered optimization of kernels generated by LLMs across edge backends.

articles.title: FlowMaker: From Tasks to Cost-Efficient Generative AI Workflow Deployments
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24861v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative AI workflows execute user tasks by composing sequences of LLM calls, where each call performs a sub-task (e.g., summarization or translation), forming a workflow. Executing such workflows requires decisions over workflow structure, model assignments, and deployment configurations, which jointly determine latency, cost, and accuracy under dynamic workloads and resource constraints. Existing systems optimize these decisions in isolation or fix them early, leading to suboptimal cost and goodput. We make two key observations. First, efficient serving requires jointly exploring all combinations of workflows, model choices, and deployment configurations under dynamic cluster state. Second, reuse of deployed LLMs is critical for reducing cost, but must be performed on-the-fly, as reuse depends on current load and resource availability. Together, these make selecting a workflow-variant-a combination of workflow, models, and deployment configuration-a time-critical problem. We present FlowMaker, which exposes a task-level interface and selects workflow-variants on behalf of users. To realize this, we design a constraint-guided load-aware pruning algorithm for fast, on-the-fly decisions. FlowMaker improves goodput by up to 10.14× and reduces cost by up to 2.77× compared to state-of-the-art baselines, including Murakkab.

articles.title: T-MUON: Tensorizing Muon via t-SVD for Large Language Model Pre-training
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24938v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Muon has recently emerged as a strong optimizer for large language model pretraining by exploiting matrix structure through polar orthogonalization. However, it processes each parameter matrix independently, whereas recent tensor-aware extensions of Muon jointly update groups of eligible matrix parameters through matrix unfoldings. In contrast, we propose T-MUON, a t-SVD-based generalization that groups structurally related Transformer gradients into third-order tensors and defines the corresponding Muon-style update directly through the M-transform. We show that the exact T-MUON update is a steepest-descent direction under the star_M-spectral norm and establish a convergence guarantee. Across GPT-2-style and LLaMA-style models from 51M to 1.3B parameters trained on FineWeb and FineWeb-Edu, head-wise T-MUON with the identity transform consistently achieves lower validation perplexity than AdamW, Muon, and variants using DFT, DCT, or DST transforms. These gains persist in additional experiments with longer context lengths and larger token budgets, although the preferred tensorization mode varies across settings.

articles.title: Conjugate Compilation: Self-Improving Agentic Co-Compilation for Speculative Decoding
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.25012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As LLM adoption surges, scaling model serving requires unlocking stranded GPU capacity alongside deploying more GPUs. Speculative decoding brings two models into the serving process: a small draft model proposes tokens that a larger target model verifies. Yet compiling these models individually leaves their shared execution outside the compiler's optimization boundary. We introduce CONJUGATE COMPILATION, which reframes speculative decoding as a cross-model compilation problem and jointly optimizes the draft and target models within their shared execution rather than treating each in isolation. Our key insight is that cross-model compilation should be informed by the measured performance of the co-located shared execution it produces: an optimization that improves a kernel in isolation need not improve the models when they execute together. To expand cross-model opportunities, we devise operand layouts that interleave blocks from both models within common tiles, co-locating GEMM and non-GEMM work while preserving their mathematics. We realize CONJUGATE COMPILATION through a self-improving agentic search system in which an LLM edits cross-model optimization plans using the compiler and GPU execution as its environment. Each proposed plan is compiled and evaluated through its co-located shared execution, whose measured score, together with kernel-level verdicts and compiler feedback, informs subsequent proposals, while Monte Carlo tree search accumulates rewards to guide exploration. Across six single-GPU speculative-decoding configurations on NVIDIA B300 and RTX 5090 GPUs, CONJUGATE COMPILATION achieves a geometric-mean per-round speedup of 1.37x over conventional execution. Interleaved kernels raise this speedup to 1.45x, reaching 1.59x in the best case. CONJUGATE COMPILATION also improves GPU utilization on average by 1.46x on RTX 5090 and 1.50x on B300.

articles.title: Multifidelity Monte Carlo Estimator for High-Dimensional Quantities of Interest
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.25016v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multifidelity Monte Carlo (MFMC) reduces the cost of estimating the statistics of quantities of interest (QoIs) computed via expensive high-fidelity model by using cheaper low-fidelity models as control variates. We extend MFMC to vector-valued QoIs by replacing the scalar control-variate coefficients with matrices and minimizing a weighted mean-squared error. The optimal full-matrix coefficients are available in closed form, and their variance reduction is summarized by an effective correlation that takes the place of the squared Pearson correlation in the closed-form MFMC design. Restricting the coefficients to block-diagonal, diagonal, and scalar classes gives a nested hierarchy of estimators with increasing variance reduction and increasing pilot-data demand, with closed-form coefficients for compatible weightings. For a scalar QoI obtained by linearly projecting the state, correcting the full state before projecting is never worse at the population level. Experiments on a Gaussian problem, a reduced-order model of an advection--diffusion problem, and a coarse-grid two-phase flow problem show that the best class depends on the pilot size relative to the number of covariance quantities it must estimate, and that reusing the pilot samples lowers the mean-squared error.

articles.title: Martingale Posterior Cox Processes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24787v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cox processes provide a principled Bayesian nonparametric framework for modeling event-based data through an underlying intensity function. However, existing inference methods for estimating the intensity typically rely on computationally expensive Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling or approximate inference techniques. In addition, to ensure tractability, these methods often define priors over indirect latent structures, making them challenging to interpret. In this paper, we introduce the Martingale Posterior Cox Process (MPCP), which recasts Bayesian intensity estimation as inference over unobserved events given the observed event history. This perspective avoids the need to define complex priors while retaining the flexibility of nonparametric modeling. We propose a scalable, GPU-friendly copula-based predictive update, and provide strong theoretical guarantees for the convergence of the predictive resampling algorithm. Empirically, we show that MPCP provides excellent performance in both simulations and real data at a fraction of the computational cost of competing Bayesian approaches.

articles.title: Decision-Target Reversal under Informative Label Missingness
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.25128v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Informative label missingness can improve classification efficiency because the pattern of label availability may itself contain information about the discriminant structure. We show that this advantage need not persist across deployment objectives: with the data-generating model and statistical experiments held fixed, informative partial classification can be favourable under one loss and unfavourable under another. We call this phenomenon decision-target reversal. For binary Gaussian discrimination, we derive a local cost-sensitive excess-risk expansion and, in one dimension, obtain explicit critical cost ratios at which the first-order risk ordering reverses. We show that the required covariance geometry arises under finite uncertainty-dependent missingness mechanisms with a fixed marginal missing-label proportion. We then extend the analysis to multiclass finite-action problems through loss-specific active-boundary curvature, yielding a general decision-target frontier. Monte Carlo experiments illustrate the predicted reversals, and a descriptive gastrointestinal-lesion application with agreement-defined label availability illustrates sensitivity to deployment costs. The results show that favourable informative missingness is a property of the statistical experiment relative to the deployment decision, rather than of the experiment alone.

articles.title: Keep the Lineages Alive: Diversity-Preserving SMC for Diffusion LLM Decoding
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.25932v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Inference-time sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) decoding can improve the reasoning accuracy of masked diffusion language models (diffusion LLMs) without post-training by resampling a population of partial generations according to a reward. Its effectiveness therefore depends on the resampling step, which must concentrate computation on promising candidates while retaining enough diversity to explore alternative reasoning paths. The reward can be internal, the decoder's own confidence on the committed prefix, or external, a process reward model scoring that prefix. Under either reward, multinomial resampling can disrupt this balance by duplicating high-weight particles and discarding lineages that may still reach a correct solution. The effective sample size (ESS) does not register this loss: multinomial resampling resets it to its maximum even as distinct lineages disappear. To retain such lineages, we introduce lineage-preserving SMC (LP-SMC), which combines Chopthin resampling with an input weight floor. Instead of equalizing weights, Chopthin bounds the ratio between the largest and smallest weights it returns and carries the unequal weights forward. The floor limits how far below the maximum a weight may fall before resampling so that lineages with low early weight keep a chance to recover. Across mathematical-reasoning and code-generation benchmarks on two base models, LP-SMC raises oracle coverage, the fraction of problems with at least one correct particle, in every setting, by 1.8 to 25.6 points, and raises end-to-end accuracy under a common reward-model selector in eleven of twelve settings, by up to 7.9 points on LLaDA-1.5 and 18.3 on Dream-7B. The coverage gain persists under the external reward model, which suggests that diversity-preserving resampling and the guidance signal contribute separately to inference-time search.

articles.title: Control Variate Design for Score-Function Gradient Estimators in Importance-Weighted Variational Inference
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.01412v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Importance-weighted variational inference approximates intractable densities by optimizing multi-sample Monte Carlo objectives whose tightness increases with the number of importance samples N. When reparameterization is unavailable, optimization relies on score-function (REINFORCE) gradient estimators. In this paper, we provide a comprehensive analysis of score-function gradient estimators for importance-weighted objectives by characterizing their asymptotic expectation and variance. We establish that standard variational inference for Monte Carlo objectives (VIMCO) gradient estimators suffer from a vanishing signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) as N increases, which arises from a suboptimal control variate choice and can impair optimization. To address this issue, we derive a general mechanism for constructing VIMCO gradient estimators that avoid SNR collapse. We identify the High-Effective Sample Size optimal variance importance sampling estimator as belonging to this category of estimators and establish its sqrtN SNR scaling. This estimator does not, however, have zero variance at optimality and achieving its sqrtN SNR rate may require prohibitively large N when the importance weights are degenerate. We overcome these limitations by introducing VIMCO gradient estimators that attain zero variance at optimality and support importance weight tempering. Experiments with discrete latent-variable and state-space models validate the theoretical predictions and illustrate the benefits of our estimators.

articles.title: Interacting Annealed Importance Sampling via Population-Based MCMC Kernels
articles.abstract: arXiv:2401.15645v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Sampling from a multimodal distribution is a fundamental and challenging problem in computational science and statistics. Among various approaches proposed for this task, one popular method is Annealed Importance Sampling (AIS). In this paper, we propose an interaction-based version of AIS by combining it with population-based Monte Carlo methods to improve its efficiency. By keeping track of an ensemble instead of a single sampler along some continuation path between the starting distribution and the target distribution, we take advantage of the interaction within the ensemble to encourage the exploration of undiscovered modes. Specifically, our main idea is to utilize either the snooker algorithm or the genetic algorithm used in Evolutionary Monte Carlo. We discuss how the proposed algorithm can be implemented and derive a partial differential equation governing the evolution of the ensemble under the continuous time and mean-field limit. We also test the efficiency of the proposed algorithm on various continuous and discrete distributions.

articles.title: Solving Inverse Problems via Diffusion-Based Priors: An Approximation-Free Ensemble Sampling Approach
articles.abstract: arXiv:2506.03979v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Diffusion models (DMs) have proven to be effective in modeling high-dimensional distributions, leading to their widespread adoption for representing complex priors in Bayesian inverse problems (BIPs). However, current DM-based posterior sampling methods proposed for solving common BIPs rely on heuristic approximations to the generative process. To exploit the generative capability of DMs and avoid the usage of such approximations, we propose an ensemble-based algorithm that performs posterior sampling without the use of heuristic approximations. Our algorithm is motivated by existing work that combines DM-based methods with the sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) method. By examining how the prior evolves through the diffusion process encoded by the pre-trained score function, we derive a modified partial differential equation (PDE) governing the evolution of the corresponding posterior distribution. This PDE includes a modified diffusion term and a reweighting term, which can be simulated via stochastic weighted particle methods. Theoretically, we prove that the error between the true posterior and the empirical distribution of the generated samples can be bounded in terms of the training error of the pre-trained score function and the number of particles in the ensemble. Empirically, we validate our algorithm on several inverse problems in imaging to show that our method gives more accurate reconstructions compared to existing DM-based methods. Our code is available at the following Github repository~url{https://github.com/HaoxuanSteveC00/AFDPS-TMLR}.

articles.title: Doing Less with More: A First-Principles Exploration of the Suitability of Agentic Computing over Alternative Architectural Choices
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23921v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: There is growing interest in automating business activities with Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) due to latter's seeming ease of use. Never has it been easier, or costlier, to do less with more. However, little is known about when agents are preferable to established alternatives such as local computation, Representational State Transfer (REST), the Simple Object Access Protocol (SOAP), and the Model Context Protocol (MCP), particularly when development speed, performance, and operational cost are considered. We investigate this question using a controlled mathematical task that compares seven methods on a benchmark of 1,000 arithmetic expressions where semantics of operator precedence has to be preserved. We ran this setup across a native Function Calling baseline (Python library), REST, SOAP and MCP microservice architectures, direct responses from large language models (LLMs) using a Groq cloud API and five locally deployed Ollama models, and agentic systems in which five local LLMs invoke MCP tools. The deterministic methods achieve 100% accuracy with negligible latency. Direct LLM evaluation achieves at most 92.9% accuracy at over 22,000x the latency of a native function call. With MCP tools, the best agent reaches 99.9% accuracy, but incurs nearly 1,000,000x the baseline latency. These results demonstrate that LLMs approaches are poorly suited for exact arithmetic evaluation and motivate an informed architectural decision framework (ADF) for choosing an architecture based on accuracy and throughput requirements. We recognize that an actual interaction with an agent may span both reasoning and linguistic tasks. Hence our recommendation is to explore multiple architectural choices (based on task type) rather than one-size-fits-all solution (LLMs). Code is available at - https://github.com/Ritvik-G/adf/

articles.title: Cortex: A Fixed-Point Theory of Governed Coding Agents - Technical Report
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24255v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A coding agent combines a large language model (LLM) with a harness that plans, edits, and executes code. We study Cortex, a supervisory layer for pre-execution governance, requirement tracking, and iterative validation and repair. We formalize requirement closure on a finite lattice. For a fixed requirement set and a sound, monotone validation rule with persistent evidence, exhaustive iteration reaches the least fixed point with no more strict increases than there are requirements. Fair consequence scheduling reaches the same closure. A separate stochastic model bounds expected completion time under a uniform positive-progress assumption. These results depend on their stated assumptions; artifact repair, fallible validation, and finite execution budgets do not satisfy them automatically. We define Gauntlet's trajectory-similarity and build-gated scores, attack-success estimators, Wilson intervals, and case-cluster bootstrap summaries. Effective-feedback accounting counts newly certified requirements, rather than estimating their information value or utility. The five evaluation families support raw-versus-governed comparisons. We report retained benchmark observations, including rescoring of existing artifacts; constructed outcomes are excluded. Unequal observation sets and incomplete provenance prevent causal claims about governance or measured long-horizon scaling.

articles.title: IndustrialCAD-1400: Benchmarking Detailed Industrial Assemblies from Text
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24789v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Industrial assemblies require more than a recognizable shape: functional parts, interfaces, dimensions and service features must satisfy a detailed request together. We introduce IndustrialCAD-1400, a text-to-CAD benchmark for this industrial setting. Its 1,400 requests combine 400 equipment categories across 40 domains with 250 four-case design families. Family requests specify a median of 17 named component or configuration roles and six explicit numeric targets; controlled variants test whether dimensions change while shared structure is retained. Task construction draws on documented manufacturer information, owner specifications and engineering guidance. Models generate geometry programs from requests, and a common Blender environment executes them to produce scenes, optional measurements, and standardized views for evaluation. A request assessment of front, isometric, and top views measures visible component, arrangement, and interface fulfillment without requiring a single reference geometry. Five stratified panels preserve complete families while covering the benchmark exactly once, enabling balanced comparisons and separating industrial breadth from controlled numerical responsiveness. In conclusion, IndustrialCAD-1400 extends text-to-CAD from recognizable part geometry to industrial assembly synthesis under joint component, interface, spatial, and numerical specifications.

articles.title: OpenSaC: A Python Library for Search as Code in Deep Research Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.25779v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep research agents investigate complex questions through iterative search, source examination, and evidence synthesis. A conventional workflow alternates reasoning with individual search and reading actions. Search as Code introduces a new paradigm: agents write programs that compose search, source reading, reranking, model calls, and local processing, returning selected observations for further reasoning. To support this workflow in existing coding agents, we present OpenSaC, an open-source Python library with a companion Search as Code skill. Configurable capability interfaces let agents combine these operations while retaining evidence for inspection and reuse. Compared with standard Codex using its built-in web search, the OpenSaC configuration uses less execution time and fewer model tokens on BrowseComp and WideSearch, with higher accuracy on BrowseComp and slightly lower row F1 on WideSearch. We aim to lower the barrier to adopting Search as Code and provide an open foundation for community development and transparent research on deep research agents.

articles.title: FrontierRefactor: Benchmarking Multi-Scale Performance-Oriented Codebase Refactoring
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.25834v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous codebase refactoring requires coding agents to restructure working software while strictly preserving externally observable behavior and prioritizing execution performance and compute efficiency over stylistic preference. Existing benchmarks: refactoring benchmarks assess functional correctness while overlooking runtime regressions, whereas code performance benchmarks target isolated micro-kernels that ignore codebase-scale complexity. We observe that refactoring scale is governed by the scope of the observable contract, the caller-visible interface fixing behavioral invariants while freeing private implementations for optimization. Building on this insight, we introduce FrontierRefactor, a benchmark of 60 qualified engineering tasks spanning four scales, from computational kernels to full repositories, across in-place optimization and cross-language rewriting. Evaluating frontier coding agents through a reference-free cascaded protocol across 1,080 execution runs reveals that correctness and speedup are largely decoupled: 41.2% of submissions satisfy functional equivalence yet fail to deliver verified performance improvements, with 19.3% suffering performance regressions and 21.9% trapped in measurement noise. Refactoring paradigms reveal orthogonal engineering bottlenecks: while cross-language rewrites gain speedups from native compilation after passing functional checks, agents struggle with contract fidelity, with pass rates dropping from 65.0% on modules to 32.6% at package scale; conversely, in-place optimization reliably preserves behavioral contracts at 86.5% but rarely achieves acceleration without physical performance profiling. Trajectory analysis shows that agents fall victim to uncalibrated micro-benchmarking illusions, an operational blind spot that multi-turn execution-timing feedback directly resolves, raising strict success from 16.0% to 40.0%.

articles.title: AuDQ: Auditable Data Quality through Agentic Rule Discovery
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26031v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-stakes tabular pipelines rely on scattered, static quality checks that are hard to evolve and audit against policy intent. Regulated domains particularly suffer as the LLM-era automation raises expectations for traceability and accountability. We propose a vision for an ontology-grounded, repository-native data quality layer in which rules are first-class artifacts: versioned, provenance-linked to governance texts, and re-playable through immutable execution traces. As a first step toward validating this vision, we present a concrete implementation of its agentic rule-discovery core with two rule acquisition modes (Full-Agentic and Guided) and a human-in-the-loop (HITL) review interface. We define an evaluation framework and run experiments addressing whether our fully autonomous, divide-and-conquer agentic rule discovery produces rules of the same quality and diversity as those specified by a human expert, reporting preliminary results on two real world industry datasets in the finance and retail domains.

articles.title: Decision4Rec: A Jev-Inspired Framework of Decision Models on Knowledge and Active Graphs for Multi-Agent Recommender Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26035v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decision models, such as the commercial Jev, are language models that return one probability for each option of a question instead of generating text. We present Decision4Rec, an open and modular framework that makes decision models useful for recommendation. A knowledge graph writes the logs of each recommendation scenario as short statements on a defined scale, such as "sold: top 10%". A pool of agents, proposes candidates, and a residual ranker keeps the best 30. A decision model, trained once on real choices of three scenarios, reads them through one interface of typed questions, and a fusion step combines its answers with the score of the ranker. Any model with this interface can be used, and we run the commercial Jev, the released open Kev and Kev models trained by us on recommendation requests. The framework with a trained 4B decision model is 25 to 36% above the best trained baseline in NDCG@10 in three sparse Amazon catalogues, one of them never used to train the decision model, and almost tie with baselines on the dense Steam dataset. Most of the gain comes from the pool, and with a trained recommender it comes from what the agents know about its candidates rather than from new candidates. The 27B decision model adds to the pool 5 to 6% above the 0.8B model in three of four domains. A trained 0.8B open model beats the released Jev in eleven of fifteen settings and is never worse. On MovieLens-1M, a dense domain never seen in training, the gain is 5 to 7%. Code, configurations and trained models are available at https://github.com/marcopoli/decision4rec and https://huggingface.co/m-polignano.

articles.title: CUA-Lite: An Open Platform for Computer Use Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26071v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Open resources for computer use agents (CUAs) -- environments, datasets, and models -- remain scattered: without a standard, these resources cannot be integrated and scaled; additionally, evaluation, RL, and SFT cannot share one infrastructure. We present CUA-Lite, an open platform for developing CUAs, built around three standardized abstractions: (1) Unified environment interface, under which we integrate 12 benchmarks across desktop, browser, and mobile, plus lightweight VM-free sandboxes that replicate OSWorld's desktop at much lower cost, providing over 30,000 verifiable tasks. (2) Unified supervised data format, into which we convert the major public CUA datasets, from GUI grounding and understanding to full rollouts, and record our fresh rollouts from frontier CUAs on these verifiable environments. (3) Model harnesses shared across evaluation, RL, and SFT, one per model and implemented for 14 model families. Each harness runs its model in these computer environments, producing the rollouts that evaluation and RL consume, or renders stored supervised data into the model's own training format for SFT. We release reference scores across the integrated benchmarks, and show that RL and SFT through the same harness improve open-weight models. We release our dataset, code, and models, and the platform is open to contributions.

articles.title: GPU-native extension of a high-order compressible solver to multicomponent reacting flows
articles.abstract: We present an extension of STREAmS-2.0, a GPU-accelerated solver for direct numerical simulation of compressible turbulent flows, to multicomponent chemically reacting gas mixtures. Three principal numerical contributions are introduced. First, the energy-preserving split discretization of the convective fluxes is reformulated forvariable-composition mixtures, with an eigenvalue structure extended to the additional species advective branches; species diffusion is modeled via the Hirschfelder--Curtiss approximation with a mass-conservation corrector. Second, a chemical kinetics module supporting Arrhenius, three-body, and pressure-dependent fall-off reactions is integrated through a custom interface with Cantera, with transport and kinetic properties pre-tabulated at runtime for GPU execution. Third, chemical stiffness is handled through an operator-splitting strategy coupling the explicit three-stage Runge--Kutta flow integrator with a four-stage fouth-order implicit Rosenbrock method. The extended solver is validated against nine standardized benchmark cases, from zero- to three-dimensional configurations, covering multicomponent transport and chemical kinetics, showing excellent agreement with reference solutions. Weak-scaling efficiency exceeds 99% up to 512 NVIDIA A100 GPUs, while strong scaling up to 64 GPUs is governed by per-GPU memory usage, with a critical threshold near 10% of memory capacity below which efficiency degrades sharply. Profiling shows that chemical source-term evaluation accounts for approximately 40% of the per-step wall time.

articles.title: Surface texturing of cutting inserts for turning of aluminium – Study of cutting forces, wear, chip formation and tool-chip contact
articles.abstract: This paper presents wet machining of wrought aluminium alloys with textured and non-textured tools. To improve the machining performance, textures were produced on rake face of uncoated cemented carbide by using femtosecond laser machining. Experiments were conducted on a computer numerical controlled lathe with each textured tool and then compared to conventional cutting tool. To evaluate the cutting performance of tested tools, the following criteria were considered: cutting forces evolution, rake face wear, flank face wear and chip formation. In parallel, simulations based on boundary elements method (BEM) were used to analyse the local effects of the texture in the contact. A significant decrease of flank wear about 90% is observed with textured tools with nanometric Laser Induced Periodical Surface Structures (LIPSS) and of 80% with double-scale structure (LIPSS + Dimples). Double-scale structured tool presents a lower cutting force in comparison with conventional cutting tool. An increase of shear angle value with tool textured with micrometric structure (Lines) is observed. A lower height of adhesion on rake face of the tool with LIPSS compared to other tested tools is found too. These results constitute another step in the purpose to design a new generation of tools for precision turning of aluminium alloys.

articles.title: State-of-the-Art Image Recognition for Surface Water Garbage Detection, Classification, and Counting
articles.abstract: Garbage floating on rivers, lakes and ponds harms water life, blocks drains and spoils the look of public places. Checking it by eye is slow and tiring. This paper builds a simple image-based system that finds floating garbage in a photo, tells what type it is, and counts how many pieces of each type are present. A small YOLOv8 model (YOLOv8n, about 3.0 million parameters) was trained on a public water-garbage image set with 371 training images, 105 validation images and 7 labels. Counting is done by adding up the boxes the model draws for each class. In the training log used for this paper (24 completed epochs), the model reached a best mAP50 of 0.244, with precision of 0.624 and recall of 0.276 at that point, and it took about 155 ms to process one image on a CPU. These scores are modest. They show that the idea works even with very little data and no GPU, and they point clearly to what must improve: more labelled images, cleaner class labels, and a longer training run.

articles.title: Ultra-Broadband Thermal Radiation Management Using a Plasmonic Metamaterial Absorber for Thermophotovoltaic Applications and Solar Sails
articles.abstract: Metamaterial absorbers show a path towards produce greener energy without noise, toxic waste, or carbon dioxide emissions. Optical metamaterial absorber can achieve significant absorption with compact dimensions. However, achieving high efficiency, with an average rate of 97% and ultrabroadband absorption from UV to IR, using a three-layer sandwich structure is still under research. In this work, we present a compact three-layer metal-dielectric-metal absorber that achieved a total 98.43% average absorption rate. This efficiency remains stable from 230 nm to 4000 nm. In this region, the absorption remains above 92%. Our study shows its suitability at higher temperatures, as we have used low-cost, high-temperature-stable materials: tungsten and silicon dioxide. Polarization angle and incident angle also varied from 0º to 70º, and showed no variation. Under AM 1.5 irradiance, the absorber performs also evaluated. Under 973K temperature the MMA shows 96.7% thermal conversion efficiency at C= 400 which maintains 97.41% at C= 2000. We verified the absorption with the interference theory model, which shows almost similar results. We also conducted a comparative analysis of the last two years' work, where our present work significantly stands out in terms of efficiency and bandwidth. The demonstration of solar absorber implementation illustrates how this MMA can be used for solar energy harvesting.

articles.title: Staged liquefaction: reaction pathway and mechanism of corn stalk hemicellulose in 1,2-propylene glycol / diethylene glycol under acid catalysis
articles.abstract: To promote full-component utilization of lignocellulosic biomass and reduce petrochemical reliance for “dual carbon” goals, this experiment studied the liquefaction of hemicellulose directly separated from corn stalk by 1,2-propylene glycol (PG) and diethylene glycol (DEG) mixture with acid catalysis at different reaction times. By investigating the variations in composition, structure, and distribution of liquefaction products under varying reaction times, the study aimed to elucidate the formation pathways of active functional groups and the liquefaction reaction mechanisms, thereby establishing the fundamental reaction patterns of the process. The time-dependent analysis revealed that the liquefaction reaction of hemicellulose proceeded in stages (the highest liquefaction yield of 87.02% at 0 min). Notably, ‘0 min’ indicated the moment when the target temperature of 170°C was reached. The hemicellulose degradation process was dominant and primarily completed during the heating phase (prior to 0 min), while polymerization reaction predominantly occurred during the holding phase (0–150 min). In the heating stage, hemicellulose degraded into pentoses/hexoses, then into oligosaccharides/monosaccharides under acid. These sugars formed corresponding PG/DEG-glycosides, further transformed into low molecular weight (LMW) compounds such as furfural and levulinic acid. In the holding stage, abundant degradation-generated LMW organics (alcohols, ketones, aldehydes, acids, ethers, esters, hydrocarbons, etc.) underwent polymerization among themselves, intermediates, and PG/DEG, forming higher molecular weight substances (liquefaction residue).

articles.title: Computationally guided inhibition of the HIF-1α–CBP/p300 coactivator interface suppresses hypoxia signaling in Caki-1 renal carcinoma cells
articles.abstract: Hypoxia-inducible factor 1 (HIF-1) drives adaptive transcription through recruitment of the homologous coactivators CBP and p300, but this interface remains difficult to modulate with small molecules. We combined virtual screening of approximately 250,000 ZINC natural-product-like compounds against the CBP CH1 domain (PDB 1L8C), molecular docking and a 100-ns molecular dynamics simulation to identify candidate interface binders. SIHC926 (ZINC000097971950) remained within the predicted pocket, and MM/PBSA analysis produced a negative total binding-free-energy estimate dominated by favourable van der Waals contributions. In a homogeneous time-resolved fluorescence assay using the p300 CH1 domain, SIHC926 inhibited HIF-1α–coactivator association with an IC₅₀ of 1.88 µM, compared with 4.72 µM for YC-1. SIHC926 also inhibited hypoxia-response-element-dependent transcription (IC₅₀ 2.52 µM), reduced Caki-1 cell viability under hypoxia (reported GI₅₀ 2.29 µM), decreased vascular endothelial growth factor secretion, increased Annexin V-positive apoptosis and elevated intracellular reactive oxygen species. These findings nominate SIHC926 as a candidate scaffold for modulating HIF-1 coactivator recruitment. Direct intracellular target engagement, coactivator selectivity, complete compound characterization and validation in additional renal carcinoma models remain necessary.

articles.title: A Compact Open Encoder Model for Calibrated Typed Decisions on Unseen Tasks
articles.abstract: Many software systems need quick, structured judgments: choose an option, estimate a yes/no probability, or assign an ordinal score. Decision models produce these answers in one forward pass, avoiding the cost and fragility of generating and parsing text. We present typic-bert, an open 396M-parameter decision model built on the Ettin encoder. The model places a [MASK] marker before each option, scores the marker states with a small head, and returns a calibrated probability distribution. We train it on 50,000 examples drawn from 25 public datasets and vary the question wording, labels, option count, and polarity to reduce surface-level shortcuts. Training takes 46 minutes on one free Kaggle T4 GPU. Across four tasks excluded from training (2,000 questions), typic-bert achieves 69.9% accuracy, compared with 56.7% for Laya (421M) on the same inputs. It nearly matches Laya on intent routing (81.2% versus 82.0%) and answers in 29 ms per question. It also retains 85-90% accuracy when the request follows up to 7,000 unrelated tokens, while both tested Laya checkpoints fall to 25-30%. We release the model openly and discuss important limitations, including task selection and single-seed training.

articles.title: Performance of abaca fiber geotextile as perforated pipe geo-envelope for agricultural subsurface drainage systems
articles.abstract: Waterlogging, defined as the complete saturation of the crop’s root zone, is a widespread problem in agricultural areas. This problem has been exacerbated in recent years by extreme weather conditions caused by climate change. Currently, the most common solution to waterlogging is the installation of subsurface drainage systems, which consist of perforated pipes wrapped in geotextiles. However, due to most geotextiles being synthetic, there has been emerging research interest in manufacturing these from sustainable sources, one of which is abaca. This study evaluated the performance of manually fabricated nonwoven geotextiles produced from 3% NaOH-treated S2-grade abaca fibers as geo-envelopes. To this end, a customized sand tank with a removable perforated pipe attachment was fabricated to simulate in-situ waterlogged conditions. The geotextiles were first wrapped around the perforated pipe prior to gradually filling the tank with pre-saturated sand. A constant head of water was supplied, and hydraulic readings were obtained only after the piezometric water levels had stabilized. One, two, and three-layer abaca geo-envelope configurations and a one-layer commercial geo-envelope configuration were each tested five times. Experimental testing found that the three-layer abaca geo-envelope had the highest, statistically significant, average drainage intensity among the four configurations. Furthermore, the one-layer commercial geotextile performed roughly in line with the one-layer abaca geotextile. The results indicate that as the thickness of the abaca geo-envelope is increased, its water entrance resistance decreases and its effective radius increases, leading to increased drainage performance. Lastly, the abaca geotextile underwent scanning electron microscopy (SEM) before and after it had been used as a geo-envelope. SEM results revealed that although fine soil particles adhered to the fibrous surface, pore spaces remained visible. These findings highlight the material’s soil retention ability and clogging resistance. Overall, the study concludes that abaca fiber geotextiles are suitable for subsurface drainage systems.

articles.title: Modeling Galactic Rotation Curves to Map Dark Matter Distribution in the Galaxy: A Comparative Bayesian Analysis of Cuspy and Cored Halo Profiles Across the Sparc Database
articles.abstract: The observed rotation curves of spiral and irregular galaxies do not decline at large radii as Newtonian dynamics predicts for a mass distribution concentrated toward the centre. Instead, they remain approximately flat, implying the presence of an extended, unseen mass component generally attributed to dark matter. The precise inner structure of this component remains disputed: Cold Dark Matter (ΛCDM) N-body simulations predict a steeply rising central density, or “cusp,” whereas a large body of observational work instead favours a flatter, constant-density “core.” This discrepancy, known as the Cusp-Core problem, has remained unresolved for more than two decades. In this study, rotation curves for a sample of late-type galaxies drawn from the Spitzer Photometry and Accurate Rotation Curves (SPARC) database were decomposed into their baryonic components (stellar disk, bulge, and gas) and a residual dark matter contribution. Baryonic mass was estimated from 3.6 µm near-infrared photometry and 21-cm HI radio data, applying standard Freeman-disk and Sérsic-bulge formalisms. Two competing halo models, the cuspy Navarro-Frenk-White (NFW) profile and cored alternatives (Pseudo-Isothermal, Burkert, DC14), were fit to each galaxy using Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) Bayesian inference, with priors placed on the stellar mass-to-light ratio. Standard fitting procedures assume that the uncertainty at each radial data point is statistically independent of its neighbours, an assumption that does not hold well for rotation-curve data in practice. A Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) extension was therefore incorporated to model correlated systematic residuals jointly with the physical halo parameters. Under the standard independent-error assumption, cored profiles outperformed NFW across most of the sample, particularly in gas-dominated dwarfs such as DDO 154. When the GPR covariance term was included, however, this advantage shrank sharply. The results suggest that a considerable portion of the historical observational evidence favouring cored profiles may be attributable to unmodelled correlations in the data rather than to a genuine absence of central cusps, and that resolving the Cusp-Core problem conclusively will likely require higher-resolution instrumentation and full three-dimensional kinematic modelling, not further one-dimensional curve-fitting.

articles.title: Assembly of Graphene on SAMs and their performance to ORR.
articles.abstract: Here we present a new class of molecularly assembled electrode systems, composed of  chemically reduced oxidized graphene (CRGO). The hydrophobic immobilization between this  graphitic nanostructure on terminal groups (CH3) of molecular spacers was carried out using  monolayers of self-assembled molecules (SAMs) of 4-Methylbenzenethiol (4-MBT), obtaining  thus the [Au/4-MBT/CRGO] electrode system. On the other hand, the electrochemical  characterization that is carried out through cyclic voltammetry and Electrochemical Impedance  Spectroscopy (EIS) shows how the presence of CRGO reestablishes the electronic transfer and  reduces the charge transfer resistance between the redox probe [Fe (CN)6]3-/4- and the electrode  surface. Besides, the conductive images of AFM (AFM-c) reveal that the areas of greatest  conductance are presented by CRGO nanostructures, immobilized on the graft of SAMs molecules  in Au (111). Likewise, the characterization through Raman Spectroscopy indicated the presence  of structural imperfections of this crystal lattice of carbon atoms, and a high number of localized  defects on the surface of CRGO, due to the interaction that the CRGO nanostructure presents,    when the assembly is established with the graft of SAMs in Au. The catalytic activity of this  electrode system was examined for the reduction of O2 in aqueous media of NaOH and compared  with that of Au (111) bare and Au (111) coated directly with Fe-phthalocyanine (FePc) molecules.  The electrocatalytic studies carried out with [Au (111)/FePc] and [Au/4-MBT/CROG/FePc]  electrodes show that the O2 reduction takes place by transferring 4-electron to give water. In this  paper, the characterization and application of a CRGO modified gold electrode, a novel electrode  system, are proposed.

articles.title: From Money to Prompt Laundering: CLEANSE*, a Risk-Calibrated Multi-View Detector
articles.abstract: Prompt laundering disguises disallowed instructions through narrative framing, translation, formatting, role-play, or other surface transformations while preserving harmful intent. This paper introduces CLEANSE*, a risk-calibrated multi-view detector that combines semantic intent proximity, narrative and role–action structure, cross-lingual round-trip stability, and stylometric and markup cues. These signals are fused into a calibrated anomaly score. Evaluation covers risk at fixed false-positive rates (Risk@FPR), attack success rate (ASR), discrimination, calibration, normalized probabilistic error, latency, and external benchmarks. On the in-distribution test set, CLEANSE* reduces Risk@FPR by 0.7, 0.8, and 1.0 units relative to Semantic-only at 0.5%, 1%, and 2% FPR, respectively. ASR falls from 11.6% to 8.4%; AUROC reaches 0.967, AUPRC 0.871, and expected calibration error (ECE) 1.8%, with p50/p95 latency of 15/28 ms. On the laundering-frontier slice, risk at 1% FPR falls from 6.2 to 4.9, ASR from 18.4% to 12.7%, and ECE from 3.2% to 2.1%. The reported miss-band area decreases by 37%. In-distribution relative Brier score, Brier Skill Score, and normalized cross-entropy are 0.42, 0.58, and 0.49, respectively. On JailbreakBench, CLEANSE* records risk of 5.3 and an ASR/miss rate of 14.8%, below the evaluated Llama Guard 3-8B, WildGuard, ShieldLM, and Semantic-only baselines. In the RAG/agent stress test, combined pre- and post-gate scoring records risk of 5.4, an ASR/miss rate of 15.1%, and an unsafe tool-pass rate of 3.6%, with p95 latency of 36 ms. The results support further evaluation of multi-view detection for prompt laundering. Limitations include adaptive attacks, sensitivity to graph extraction, restrictions on reproducibility materials, and limited coverage of low-resource languages. Future work will examine adaptive red-teaming, multimodal laundering, and subgroup calibration.

articles.title: The Effect of Gas Migration From Deep Geological Formations Into Mine Workings During the Evolution of Mining-Induced Seismicity
articles.abstract: From the experience of coal mining, there are known cases of gas emissions into mine workings and onto the surface, the volumes of which greatly exceed the calculated expected values. In this work, we link the intensification of gas emissions to mining workings with the process of transition of the coal strata deep sections to a critically stressed state, which is accompanied by deformation of the rock mass and is recorded by seismic activity. Seismic activity at depths exceeding the depths of mining operations has now been detected at many deposits by means of seismological monitoring. On this basis, we accept the working hypothesis that the evolution of the critically stressed state of the earth's crust in areas of mining operations manifests itself as its spread to ever deeper horizons. As the area of mining operations increases, this process proceeds from top to bottom, covering ever deeper horizons of the earth's crust, accompanied by fracture formation, contributing to their degassing and the flow of gases into mine workings from deep parts of the subsoil. Computer modelling illustrates how an increase in rock-mass permeability may facilitate gas migration from deeper horizons towards mine workings and the surface. The model provides a simplified representation of the proposed mechanism under the adopted assumptions. Using the situation in Kuzbass as a case study, the paper demonstrates a gradual increase in the depth of seismic activity manifestation, reaching depths of 5–6 km beneath the Bachat open‑pit mine. The scenario‑based methane‑volume estimate indicates the possibility of methane migration from depths of several kilometres, with quantities comparable to the emissions from the seams recently under development.  The results support consideration of this mechanism as a possible explanation for reported gas anomalies in Kuzbass mining areas.

articles.title: Numerical and Experimental analysis of interlaminar stresses in bonded composite patch repairs
articles.abstract: This study investigates the tensile behaviour of laminated composite plates repaired with bonded composite patches. The material consists of an epoxy matrix reinforced with carbon fibres, offering superior mechanical properties. Experimental and numerical analyses were performed to evaluate the repair efficiency and restore structural performance. A 3D finite element model was developed using two complementary approaches: a UMAT subroutine based on the maximum stress criterion and a progressive damage model implemented in ABAQUS/Implicit. To predict fracture modes, the extended finite element method (XFEM) was combined with cohesive zone modelling (CZM) to simulate adhesive debonding between substrates and plies, using both meshed (UMM) and meshless techniques. The simulation results agreed closely with experimental data, showing less than 5% deviation in ultimate load. The composite patch significantly reduced stress concentration, except for the GFRP plate repaired with a GFRP patch in the (− 45/45) stacking sequence, which exhibited a more favourable stress distribution at 5 MPa. The validated model optimises patch design, enhancing performance, durability, and strength of repaired aeronautical composite structures.

articles.title: Agents Can Build Benchmarks. Approvals Missed What Probing Found: 22 Cases
articles.abstract: We report 22 agent benchmarks built by AI coding agents on one shared TypeScript engine. No test job failed on the last commit of any of the 123 merged feature pull requests, and the LLM council that reviewed them approved 94 of them. A later probing review still found defects in all 22: each needed at least one fix round (median 3, maximum 9), the first 12 shipped a release whose changelog marks earlier scores incomparable (a sentence the fix briefs required), and at least 13 packages record a strategy that ignored the task and still earned credit. A preregistered check then played 8 generic trivial policies against the first 12 packages before and after the fixes: the best trivial score fell in only 2 packages, a null that suggests generic policies miss most of the logged defects. The approvals were real reviews: the council flagged defects that were then fixed, including the published hidden seed in sycophancy's pull request 20 and gaps in pelican's SVG scan. And 2 approved requests are documented holding defects a later review found: pelican's pull request 4, approved by the chair alone after the other members timed out, shipped a grader that scored a memorised SVG 1.0 on every task (issue 8), and sycophancy's pull request 20 was approved while a publishing leak and a grading-note claim the code did not back were still in the tree, both fixed after the approval. The artifact behind the suite is benchmark-core: one defineBenchmark call builds a task runner, a deterministic grader, and four runnable surfaces (SDK, CLI, MCP, HTTP) per package, and a mock provider separates an oracle script from a trivial script. We release the engine, the packages, the re-review protocol and review log, and the defect counts with their public sources. This release reports no real-model results and keeps no leaderboard; the registered real-model arm is still running.

articles.title: Polaron localization modulates lattice-oxygen transfer in Pd/CeO₂ methane oxidation
articles.abstract: Lean methane oxidation over Pd/CeO2 depends on oxygen exchange across the metal-support interface, yet descriptors that connect the electronic structure of reducible supports to catalytic oxygen supply remain elusive. Here, we isolate the effect of ceria faceting using PdOx/CeO2−y catalysts with comparable PdOx particle sizes and loadings. Contrary to the commonly reported preference for CeO2(111)-rich nano-octahedrons, catalytic activity follows the order nanocubes > nanorods > nano-octahedrons. Kinetic isotope measurements show that C-H activation remains rate determining across all morphologies, whereas microkinetic analysis identifies a support-assisted pathway involving molecular O2 activation at ceria vacancies and oxygen transfer to PdOx. Density functional theory reveals that the open (100) and (110) surfaces stabilize localized Ce3+ small polarons, while the close-packed (111) surface delocalizes vacancy-derived charge over a Ce trimer, increasing the energetic penalty for oxygen removal and transfer. These findings suggest that polaron localization can be a mechanistic descriptor linking ceria faceting to lattice-oxygen availability and methane-oxidation activity, beyond conventional measures based solely on vacancy concentration. Reactor-scale simulations using the validated microkinetics translate these intrinsic energetics into design requirements, showing that more favorable ratios between the Gibbs free energy of activation and that of oxygen transfer from the support to the PdOx (ΔG‡/ΔGlattice−oxygen transfer) enable comparable conversion with reduced catalyst inventory. This framework links defect electronic structure to catalyst selection and reactor performance and may extend to oxidation catalysis over other reducible supports.

articles.title: Enhanced Localized surface plasmon resonance and Interfacial Charge Transfer in Cu/ZnO Nanosphere Heterostructures: Insights from Combined DFT and FDTD Simulations
articles.abstract: Localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) enhances light absorption and quantum conversion efficiency in photocatalysts. The LSPR mechanism in Cu nanospheres loaded on ZnO nanospheres was investigated using FDTD simulations, while DFT was used to analyze interfacial charge transfer in Cu/ZnO heterostructures. Structures include A, a Cu nanosphere on ZnO; B, a partially embedded Cu nanosphere in ZnO; and C, a Cu/ZnO core-shell structure. Cu nanoparticles exhibit a response around 570nm.
