articles.title: A novel freshwater PP-like cyanophage with an unknown source endonuclease VII gene
articles.abstract: In this study, a novel cyanophage, designated PP-DH22, infecting Plectonema boryanum IU594 and Phormidium foveolarum IU427, was successfully isolated from a water sample collected from the surface waters of East Lake in Wuhan. Subsequent genomic sequencing and comparative analysis revealed that PP-DH22 shares significant organizational similarities with the previously reported cyanophage PP, including an endonuclease VII gene. However, a pivotal and unexpected divergence was discerned specifically within its 39th open reading frame. Detailed BLAST analysis showed that this gene exhibits a relatively high nucleotide sequence identity (45.65%) to the endonuclease VII gene encoded by the Escherichia coli-infecting phage HZP2. This stands in stark contrast to the extremely low identity (30.66%) observed when the same gene is compared to its putative homolog in the cyanophage PP reference genome. Collectively, these findings indicate that PP-DH22 might possess a broader and potentially more diverse host range beyond the currently identified cyanobacterial strains, possibly encompassing other bacterial phyla.

articles.title: Oxygen plasma-engineered resin–carbon interfaces in 3D-printed hollow microneedle electrodes for IL-6 detection
articles.abstract: A stereolithographically fabricated hollow microneedle carbon electrode (HMNE) was developed as an integrated platform for interfacial electrochemistry and impedimetric biosensing. The device consisted of hollow resin microneedles with internal channels filled with carbon paste, providing a continuous conductive pathway while preserving the microneedle architecture and structural integrity during insertion. Oxygen plasma treatment markedly modified the resin–carbon interface, decreasing the water contact angle from 79.4° to 15.7° and the apparent charge-transfer resistance from ~120 to 32 kΩ. The heterogeneous electron-transfer rate constant increased from 1.26 ´ 10-3 to 2.62 ´ 10-3 cm s-1, while voltammetric and Raman measurements indicated improved electrolyte accessibility and modification of the local interfacial environment without extensive structural transformation. After anti-IL-6 functionalization, the HMNE enabled label-free impedimetric detection of IL-6, producing an approximately fourfold higher response than for TNF-α, IFN-γ, and IL-17. The immunosensor showed a concentration-dependent response from 0.5 to 7.5 ng mL-1, with a limit of detection of 0.178 ng mL-1. The immunosensor also retained its response in simulated interstitial fluid and diluted human plasma, preserving approximately 91% of its initial signal after 40 days of storage at 4 °C. These results demonstrate the potential of oxygen-plasma-engineered resin–carbon hollow microneedles as integrated three-dimensional interfaces for minimally invasive cytokine biosensing.
authors: Ana Carola D. L. V. Reis

articles.title: Quantum Vault: Symmetric No-Cloning Protection for Token Issuer and User (Benchmarked on IBM Quantum)
articles.abstract: Quantum tokens are underlying primitives for quantum money and network proposals, which leverage the no-cloning theorem to realize unforgeable authentication. A relevant but overlooked type of attack to such architectures is one in which a hacker steals the classical side information about the token states from the issuing agent (e.g., a bank), enabling the forgery of fake tokens without violating the no-cloning theorem. Our proposal addresses this threat by removing the classical side information about the token states, where instead a copy of the token is stored at the bank, i.e. a quantum vault. This copy can be accessed by anyone to perform authentication, consuming the token pair in the process. We benchmark the protocol and identify quality parameters within a hardware agnostic framework employing IBM Quantum processors, such that the protocol is applicable to arbitrary quantum platforms. By comparing the efficiency with which genuine tokens are produced and authenticated against a possible estimate-and-forge attack, we quantify the security of the protocol. We achieve probabilities lower than 10-4 for false-negative errors (Type 1) and 10-10 for successful attacks (Type 2) when considering quantum bills composed of 200 tokens, even in the worst performing processor and a conservative uncertainty estimate. The quantum vault not only protects both user and bank symmetrically with the same quantum principles, but provides a step towards public key authentication, since any untrusted party can have access granted by the bank to the tokens' authentication interface without being able to clone them. Besides this bank-mediated form of publicly accessible verifiability, our proposal achieves traceability and revocability, since the bank retains the vault copy of the tokens.

articles.title: Dimensional effects on breakthrough behavior and pore-scale residence time distributions
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional pore-scale models are widely used as computationally efficient alternatives to three-dimensional simulations. To assess the effects of this reduction in dimensionality, we use Lattice Boltzmann simulations to compare two dimensional (2D) and three dimensional (3D) permeability, breakthrough curves, and fluid age distributions for three types of porous media across a range of porosities. Permeability calculations show that 2D slices systematically underestimate the true (3D) permeability, with the magnitude of the discrepancy depending on pore geometry and being strongest at low porosity, indicating that out-of-plane connectivity drives the dimensional bias. Consistent with this, the pore-normalized Euler characteristic χ̃, a topological measure of pore connectivity, largely tracks the 2D-vs-3D permeability difference across all three media and every porosity, pointing to its potential to indicate when 2D simulations may be suitable proxies for full 3D simulations. Dimensional effects on transport metrics show distinct medium-specific patterns. In the Fibrous porous medium, 2D-3D differences in mean travel time and breakthrough spreading stay almost constant across the explored permeability range. In the Gaussian medium, differences decrease with increasing permeability, while in the Overlapping Spheres medium, the 2D vs 3D differences in mean arrival time are larger and go in both directions, with no clear trend with permeability. Conservative and reactive tracers show similar breakthrough times and tracer spreading in 2D and 3D simulations. These results demonstrate that pore geometry and connectivity primarily govern dimensional bias with only smaller effects of tracer reactivity. Mathematics Subject Classification (2020): 76S05 · 76M28 · 65Z05 · 55N31 · 86A05

articles.title: Conformalized Quantum DeepONet Ensembles: Towards Scalable Operator Learning with Distribution-Free Guarantees
articles.abstract: Operator learning enables fast surrogate modelling of high-dimensional dynam-ical systems, but existing approaches face two fundamental limitations: the quadratic cost of dense neural layers and unreliable uncertainty quantification in safety-critical settings. We propose Conformalized Quantum Deep Operator Network (DeepONet) Ensembles, a framework that addresses both challenges simultaneously. Using Quantum Orthogonal Neural Networks (QOrthoNNs), we characterize the resource regime in which their established˜︁established˜︁ O(n) hidden-layer running-time scaling improves on the O(n 2) cost of a classical dense layer. To quantify uncertainty, we combine ensemble predictions with split conformal calibration. For a new input–output function pair jointly exchangeable with the calibration pairs, we prove a finite-sample, distribution-free lower bound on the expected fraction of covered query locations. As a secondary proof-of-concept, we explore hybrid classical–quantum architectures and superposed execution to manage ensemble runtime and hardware requirements. Experiments on synthetic operator benchmarks and real-world power-system dynamics show accurate predictions under ideal simulation and empirical coverage near the target under both ideal conditions and selected compact-circuit simulations with depolarizing 1 or device-calibrated composite noise. Together, these results connect resource-aware scalability analysis with finite-sample uncertainty guarantees for quantum operator learning.

articles.title: Dynamic Ferroelectricity in Antiferroelectric Hafnia-Zirconia Thin Films at Cryogenic Temperatures
articles.abstract: We report a novel, dynamic, ferroelectric response in ultrathin tetragonal-phase-rich antiferroelectric (AFE) Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 (HZO) films at cryogenic temperatures. At room temperature, AFE switching in these films arises from a field-induced tetragonal-to-orthorhombic (t-to-o) transformation followed by rapid o-to-t back-switching during each switching cycle, retaining little-to-no polar o-phase after applied electric field removal. However, upon cooling, the o-to-t back-switching during each bipolar voltage cycle becomes kinetically suppressed, allowing the field-induced polar o-phase to persist over the measurement timescale and at zero bias, resulting in dynamic ferroelectricity. At 12.5 K, the switchable polarization exceeds 20 µC/cm2, despite quasi-static tetragonal phase structure of the films at this temperature, verified by capacitance–voltage measurements. In-situ cryogenic grazing incidence X-ray diffraction confirms no structural transformation at cryogenic temperatures. Unlike conventional polarization “wake-up”, this high-polarization state is reversible upon thermal cycling and remains stable after 1010 polarization reversals at 12.5 K. Temperature- and frequency-dependent measurements link the enhanced polarization to the kinetics of o-to-t back-switching rather than an irreversible structural transformation. These results establish a novel mode of dynamic ferroelectricity achieved in nominally antiferroelectric hafnium zirconium thin films and tunable by temperature and operating frequency. We report a novel dynamic ferroelectric response in ultrathin tetragonal-phase-rich antiferroelectric (AFE) Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 (HZO) films at cryogenic temperatures. At room temperature, AFE switching arises from field-induced tetragonal-to-orthorhombic (t-to-o) transformation followed by rapid o-to-t back-switching during each switching cycle, retaining little-to-no polar o-phase after field removal. Upon cooling, o-to-t back-switching becomes kinetically suppressed, allowing the field-induced polar o-phase to persist over the measurement timescale and at zero bias, resulting in dynamic ferroelectricity. At 12.5 K, switchable polarization exceeds 20 µC/cm2 despite a quasi-static tetragonal structure, verified by capacitance-voltage measurements. In-situ cryogenic grazing incidence X-ray diffraction confirms no structural transformation. Unlike conventional “wake-up”, this high-polarization state is reversible upon thermal cycling and remains stable after 1010 polarization reversals at 12.5 K. Temperature- and frequency-dependent measurements link enhanced polarization to o-to-t back-switching kinetics rather than irreversible structural transformation, establishing a novel mode of dynamic ferroelectricity, tunable by temperature and operating frequency.

articles.title: Physics-guided machine learning for trochoidal milling: force and power prediction and limits of cross-diameter generalisation
articles.abstract: The growing demand for lightweight aerospace structures has made trochoidal milling an increasingly important strategy for the high-efficiency machining of large pockets and thin-walled features in structural frames. Specifically mechanistic force prediction in trochoidal milling requires a continuously updated description of cutter–workpiece engagement and uncut chip thickness, which complicates its application across varying toolpath and tool geometries. This paper presents an experimental and data-driven analysis of trochoidal milling of AA7075-T651 aluminium alloy using three end-mill diameters (8, 10 and 12 mm). Cutting forces and spindle power were acquired synchronously with a piezoelectric dynamometer and the machine monitoring system across 72 tests, and post-processed in MATLAB to extract five robust indicators: mean in-plane force (Fxy,mean), maximum in-plane force (Fxy,max), robust peak-to-peak in-plane force (Fxy,ptp), maximum axial force (Fz,max) and mean spindle power (Pmean). Three physics-informed input structures – a minimal 5-variable model, a hybrid 5 + 2 model adding the maximum uncut chip thickness (hmax) and a simplified severity descriptor (MRR*), and an enriched 5 + 4 model – were compared using boosted regression trees (LSBoost) with 5-fold cross-validation. The hybrid 5 + 2 model gave the best overall compromise, improving R2 from 0.241 to 0.364 for Fxy,mean and from 0.374 to 0.473 for Pmean relative to the minimal model, while the enriched model added redundancy (correlations up to r = 0.93) without consistent gains. Average, system-level responses were substantially more predictable than peak-based ones: all three structures returned negative R2 for Fz,max, showing that test-level descriptors cannot capture the transient, local origin of axial force peaks. The results indicate that compact, physically motivated feature sets can support preliminary screening of trochoidal milling conditions without recourse to larger or less interpretable models.

articles.title: Medial Prefrontal and Orbitofrontal neural-ensemble interactions reflect decision updates differently upon surprises versus uncertainty
articles.abstract: Temporal integration and correct interpretation of anomalies are important for decision stability and flexibility. Their impairment is a hallmark of many cognitive disorders and has been linked to dysfunction of medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) and orbitofrontal cortex (OFC). How these regions coordinate event-by-event preference updating following outcomes remains unclear. Using ultraflexible electrodes, we simultaneously tracked the same neurons in mPFC and ventrolateral OFC (vlOFC) across days while rats performed a two-armed bandit task with unsignaled reward reversals. Neural choice representations were temporally stable during high-certainty states (inferred from exploitative behavior), but exhibited rapid beta-range-timescale alternations between competing choice signals during low-certainty states characterized by subsequent exploratory switching. Before action execution, choice-selective, certainty-modulated inter-areal ensembles were preferentially dominated by mPFC neurons and more strongly represented the eventual choice under high certainty. Upon losses, however, vlOFC exhibited sequential activation of purely loss-specific ensembles throughout the post-outcome period. Furthermore, when losses followed high-confidence choices, vlOFC-preceding mPFC outcome dynamics were selectively associated with subsequent switching. Thus, OFC ensembles monitor failures under both exploratory and exploitative conditions. Yet, pre-decision-confidence dependent coordination of post-decision mPFC–vlOFC population helps interpret whether negative outcomes should be tolerated as stochastic feedback or treated as policy-relevant failures.

articles.title: Even or odd numbers: A single molecule makes all the difference in the quantum world
articles.abstract: The researchers in the Quantum Detection Microscopy group at CIC nanoGUNE, in collaboration with chemists at CiQUS of the University of Santiago de Compostela, have demonstrated that adding or removing a single molecule from a quantum chain can fundamentally change its interaction with a superconductor.

articles.title: New spectroscopy method enables direct comparisons of nuclear sizes across heavy elements
articles.abstract: The size of a nucleus (nuclear charge radius) is an important physical quantity that reflects the arrangement of protons and neutrons within the nucleus. Particularly in deformed nuclei, such as those of rare-earth elements, examining changes in the charge radius can deepen our understanding of nuclear structure and nuclear deformation.

articles.title: Silicon qubits surpass 99.99% gate fidelity while operating three at once
articles.abstract: Silicon spin qubits are a promising platform for building scalable quantum computers as they are compatible with the semiconductor manufacturing technologies used to produce today's computer chips. However, they have an important weakness: silicon spin qubits typically lose accuracy when several qubits are under parallel control. To be useful, quantum computers will need to operate many qubits simultaneously without compromising the accuracy of their operations.

articles.title: Laser pulses bring order to a quantum material's tiny electrical regions
articles.abstract: Physicists at Auburn University have used flashes of laser light to bring order to tiny electrically charged "islands" inside a crystal. The discovery helps answer a decades-old question about how the material organizes itself and shows how light could be used to control its behavior—a step toward exploring new technologies for processing and storing information.

articles.title: Transport in multilayer graphene: resistance from stacking faults
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multilayer graphene exhibits rich possibilities for stacking. While natural bulk graphite predominantly occurs in the Bernal structure, where layers are stacked in an -ABAB- pattern, rhombohedral stacking has sprung to prominence recently. It is well known that Bernal graphite exhibits anisotropic transport, with high resistance to currents along the stacking axis. Careful experiments using pillar geometries have measured out-of-plane resistance, attributing it to stacking faults where planes slip out of the nominal ABAB sequence. The observed resistance shows anomalously large, non-Gaussian, sample-to-sample variations. In this article, we build a theoretical framework to calculate c-axis resistance of graphene stacks with an arbitrary stacking arrangement. Our approach builds on the idea that, regardless of stacking sequence, we have in-plane translational symmetry. With in-plane momentum as a good quantum number, c-axis transport reduces to an effectively one-dimensional problem that can be addressed using the Landauer paradigm. We calculate the resistances of a variety of simple stacking faults in both Bernal and rhombohedral systems. We also calculate the resistance of a rhombohedral 'slab' embedded between Bernal leads. Remarkably, despite both Bernal and rhombohedral graphite being metallic, the system exhibits insulating behaviour. We attribute this to Fermi surface mismatch. We next calculate the resistance of a multilayer sample with stacking disorder. Resistance is non-self-averaging, akin to a one-dimensional wire where disorder has a strong localizing effect. The median resistance grows exponentially with stack size, indicating insulating character driven by localization. Our results demonstrate that transport measurements on mesoscopic graphitic pillars serve as signatures of stacking faults, and in particular, probe localization-driven physics.

articles.title: Long-lived local coherences at high temperature from frozen domain walls
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20724v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Local coherences between distinct charge sectors--measured by the single-particle Green's function or the transverse spin autocorrelation function--do not overlap with hydrodynamic modes. At finite temperature, therefore, they decay faster than any power law in generic chaotic systems. We present a mechanism by which these coherences can persist anomalously long, for integrable and chaotic spin chains (including the XXZ and Fredkin spin chains) that obey a quantum group symmetry. We show--using a Mazur bound derived from the quantum-group symmetry, together with locality and a "non-undershoot" assumption--that the transverse spin autocorrelation function C(t) equiv langle σ⁻ₓ(t) σ⁺ₓ(0)rangle can decay at most algebraically: C(t) gtrsim 1/t². This bound is not tight: in the large-anisotropy limit of the XXZ spin chain, at infinite temperature, we explicitly compute C(t) sim sqrt3/(18 sqrtt). We also compute this decay rate in the XXZ spin chain for general easy-axis anisotropy, and estimate it to scale as C(t) sim t⁻²/z (for transport exponent z) in the chaotic models.

articles.title: Grain-Size Dependence of Thermal and Electrical Properties in (Cr,Mo,Ta,V,W)C1-δ High-Entropy Carbide Ceramics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thermal and electrical transport in high-entropy carbides can be influenced by grain-boundary scattering, but the relevant microstructural regime remains uncertain. Here, near-fully dense (Cr,Mo,Ta,V,W)C₁₋δ ceramics were densified by spark plasma sintering at 1750-1950 degC, producing average grain sizes from 9.3 ± 4.9 to 28.8 ± 15.3 μm while retaining the rock-salt phase. Heat capacities were measured experimentally and estimated by the Neumann-Kopp law with the latter used to calculate thermal conductivity. Thermal conductivity values were in the range of 6.8-7.1 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ at room temperature, but showed no systematic dependence on grain size within the investigated range. Room-temperature electrical resistivity values were in the range of 151.9 to 177.0 μΩ cm and likewise showed no grain-size dependence. The electron contribution to room-temperature thermal conductivity was estimated to be approximately 58-68% of total thermal conductivity as estimated using the Wiedemann-Franz law and the theoretical Lorenz number. The results indicated that processing-induced grain coarsening did not produce clearly resolvable transport-property changes under the conditions investigated leading to the conclusion that intrinsic disorder and defect chemistry may exert stronger influences on properties.

articles.title: Material dependence of direct light-induced charge injection from metallic nanoparticles into adsorbates
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20886v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Direct injection of charge from metallic nanoparticles into adsorbed molecules via the chemical interface damping of localized surface plasmons has emerged as a promising avenue to avoid the rapid thermalization of hot carriers. In this paper, we develop an approach for predicting hot-electron and hot-hole injection rates from large spherical nanoparticles into adsorbed carbon monoxide (CO) molecules. The approach combines a detailed description of the adsorbate-metal interactions via ab initio density functional theory with a macroscopic electrodynamics treatment of the localized surface plasmon. We apply this approach to nine different metals including both traditional (Ag, Au, Cu) and emerging (Al) plasmonic metals as well as non-plasmonic metals (Ni, Rh, Pd, Ir, Pt). For all metals, hot-electron injection is larger than hot-hole injection. This is a consequence of the alignment of the CO frontier orbitals, with the CO lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) being closer to the metal Fermi energy than the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO). The largest electron injection rates in the optical photon ranges are obtained for Al, Ag, Cu and Au, with Cu and Au showing significant plasmonic enhancement. The non-plasmonic metals show weak electron injection as a consequence of their high LUMO energies relative to the metal Fermi level. The results of our study pave the way towards a rational design of metallic nanoscale photocatalysts for specific chemical processes.

articles.title: Denser-than-crystalline disordered polydisperse ellipse packings
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By employing SWAP Monte Carlo moves during slow Lubachevsky-Stillinger-like particle growth, we generate well-thermalized disordered jammed ellipse packings for a wide range of particle aspect ratios α and maximum/minimum particle-diameter ratios λ. For λ > λᵣₘ ₓₜₐₗ(α), the packings are denser than the perfect monodisperse ellipse crystal (φᵣₘ ₓₜₐₗrm moⁿo = π/2sqrt3 simeq 0.9069) despite lacking any obvious long-range structural order; we find that λᵣₘ ₓₜₐₗ(α) remains below 2.88 over the range 1 ≤ α ≤ 5, and drops below 1.65 for α simeq 1.2. These disordered φ > φᵣₘ ₓₜₐₗrm moⁿo packings are the first of their kind reported for anisotropic particles. Multiscale analyses reveal that their characteristic structural motifs are strongly α- and λ-dependent, but none of the examined metrics change sharply as the λ = λᵣₘ ₓₜₐₗ(α) boundary is crossed. For example, we find that packings with α simeq 1.2 and λ simeq λᵣₘ ₓₜₐₗ(α) exhibit a fractionated-hexatic-plastic-polycrystalline structure that (like that of the recently-reported ideal disk glasses) can be exactly-isostatic, triangulated, and effectively-hyperuniform with respect to packing-fraction fluctuations. In contrast, even-denser packings with larger α and λ have none of these properties.

articles.title: The Blume-Capel Model as a φ⁶ Field Theory: A Monte Carlo and Flow Model Study
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20982v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report Monte Carlo simulations of a continuous spin variant of the Blume-Capel model. We compute the phase diagrams in the crystal-field-temperature plane, as a function of the softness of the spins. We show that normalizing flows, a class of generative models capable of direct sampling without autocorrelation, are effective samplers across the phase diagram, including in the first-order transition region and in the vicinity of the tricritical point. Finite-size scaling analyses of flow samples locate the first- and second-order transitions as well as the tricritical point with accuracy comparable to canonical and extended-ensemble Monte Carlo.

articles.title: MASON: Materials Atomistic Structure builder Operated in Natural language
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.21015v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Building reliable atomistic models is a critical and often challenging step in first-principles calculations. Although large language model agents can assist with structure generation, they lack direct capabilities for crystallographic operations and therefore struggle to construct complex structures reliably. Here we present MASON, an AI-native toolkit for atomistic structure construction that can be invoked by agents through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). In an end-to-end example, an agent builds a CO/Pt(111) adsorption model from a natural language request. By equipping agents with dedicated structure-building tools, MASON enables reliable and efficient atomistic model construction and provides a foundation for autonomous first-principles workflows.

articles.title: Large Language Model-Assisted Systematic Study of Anomalous Adsorption Phenomena
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.21050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Soft porous crystals can undergo guest-induced structural transitions producing unconventional adsorption isotherms, which are valuable for gas separation and storage applications. However, the evidence for these transitions is scattered across the literature in narrative form and has not been aggregated. Here we use a large language model pipeline to mine the literature for anomalous adsorption, extracting phase-transition events together with material, adsorbate, temperature and pressure metadata and classifying each into an established behavioural class. Benchmarked against human annotation, the extraction stage attains an F1 score of 0.96. When applied at scale, the pipeline yields a curated corpus of 547 transitions across 240 distinct materials, drawn from 200 of 4,252 screened publications, which we further link to crystallographic structures. Analysis of this database shows that the principal behavioural classes, gate-opening and breathing, are distinguished by their functional response. Gate-opening frameworks transform at a significantly lower pressure than breathing frameworks (p = 3.8E-3). In contrast, no difference in pore size, void fraction, linker chemistry or metal identity was detected between the classes. Our findings argue for a functional rather than purely structural description of responsive porous materials. They also highlight the need for a community database that records the guest, temperature and pressure of every reported transition of these materials.

articles.title: Strain-enhanced superconductivity in RuO₂ thin films: Joint experimental and theoretical studies
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.21163v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the superconducting properties of RuO₂ films grown on TiO₂ substrates by combining film fabrication and transport measurement with ab initio calculation. Experimentally, we grow several RuO₂ (110) thin films on TiO₂ (110) substrates and observe superconductivity with critical temperature (T_c) of sim2.0 K in 20-nm and 30-nm RuO₂ (110) thin films. Theoretically, we study the superconductivity in both RuO₂ (110) and RuO₂ (100) epitaxial films within McMillan formalism of isotropic Migdal-Eliashberg theory. Among the salient results, the calculated phonon dispersion relations of all the considered RuO₂ films show that the epitaxial films are dynamically stable. Importantly, our ab initio calculations reveal that independent of the film orientation, the [001] compressive strain ϵ[₀₀₁] pushes the flat Ru dz^₂-dominant bands towards the Fermi level (E_F), and significantly soften the out-of-plane acoustic phonon mode near the R point in the Brillouin zone, which substantially enhances the electron-phonon coupling (EPC) strength λ and hence the calculated T_c in the RuO₂ films. Remarkably, the amount of the phonon softening and the enhanced T_c increase almost linearly with the increasing ϵ[₀₀₁]. The calculated T_c for the films with thickness of ≥ 20 nm agree well with the experimental T_c. These findings demonstrate that among other things, lattice mismatch strain provides an effective route for tuning phonon-mediated superconductivity in RuO₂ and other thin films.

articles.title: Plasmon Collapse in a Directional Strange Metal
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.21209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Strange metals are widespread in strongly correlated quantum matter and closely intertwined with high-temperature superconductivity and quantum criticality, yet their microscopic charge dynamics remain fundamentally unresolved. Whether well-defined collective modes survive in an incoherent electronic fluid or dissolve into overdamped continua remains intensely debated. Here, employing high-momentum-resolution inelastic electron scattering complemented by direction-resolved transport, we show that the van der Waals compound MoOCl₂, a "bad" metal known to host unusually "good" plasmons, exhibits a striking dichotomy in electronic coherence and charge dynamics. Transport reveals coherent Fermi liquid behavior along one in-plane crystallographic axis and an incoherent strange metal response along the orthogonal axis. This dichotomy extends directly to the charge response. The Fermi liquid direction supports a well-defined, long-lived plasmon, whereas the strange metal direction exhibits an overdamped excitation that progressively loses its collective character with increasing momentum. Beyond a critical momentum (q_c approx 0.008 mathringA⁻¹), the mode undergoes a reversal into negative dispersion and ultimately collapses into a broad, nearly featureless continuum with a robust high-energy boundary (E_c approx 1.75 eV). Remarkably, thickness-dependent measurements show that both q_c and E_c remain nearly unchanged despite substantial modifications of Coulomb screening, revealing them as intrinsic scales of incoherent charge density fluctuations. These results establish a unique single-material platform in which coherent and incoherent electronic states are partitioned into in-plane orthogonal channels, and demonstrate that incoherent electronic fluids retain intrinsically structured charge dynamics beyond the quasiparticle paradigm.

articles.title: Unique Charge-density-wave Order and Fluctuation-induced Phonon Softening in the Optimally-doped Trilayer Cuprate Bi₂Sr₂Ca₂Cu₃O₁₀₊δ
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.21305v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Charge-density-wave (CDW) order is a ubiquitous feature of cuprate superconductors that competes with superconductivity. However, its behavior remains poorly understood in trilayer compounds, which contain the optimal number of CuO₂ layers for superconductivity. Here, we report Cu L₃- and O K-edge resonant inelastic x-ray scattering (RIXS) measurements of optimally-doped Bi₂Sr₂Ca₂Cu₃O₁₀₊δ (Bi2223), the trilayer cuprate with the highest superconducting transition temperature (T_c) among Bi-based cuprates. We observe CDW order with a single in-plane wavevector of bm qCDW = (0.25, 0), demonstrating that a coherent CDW order is formed across the trilayers. We also resolve CDW fluctuations emanating from the static order, whose profiles differ between the Cu L₃ and O K edges. The phonon softening occurs where these CDW fluctuations interact with the phonon branch, indicating that the RIXS phonon anomaly is driven by the coupling between CDW fluctuations and the phonon branch.

articles.title: Imaging defects in two-dimensional crystals by convergent beam electron diffraction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.21542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Convergent beam electron diffraction (CBED), recently demonstrated on two-dimensional (2D) materials, offers a number of interesting applications such as imaging atomic in- and out-of plane shifts, interlayer distances, and individual adsorbates. In this study, we show how CBED allows for atomic-precision imaging of individual defects in 2D materials using one single-shot intensity measurement. In combination with structural calculations using density functional theory, we present simulated CBED patterns for various defects in graphene, each of which exhibits a unique fingerprint distribution. We also show how atomic positions, including the individual atomic defects in graphene, can be reconstructed by iterative phase retrieval from a single CBED pattern.

articles.title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.21563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While graphene/n-type silicon (Gr/n-Si) and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si solar cells offer a cost-effective alternative to conventional photovoltaics, achieving simultaneous high power conversion efficiency (PCE) and long-term environmental stability remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report the synergistic enhancement of both performance and stability in a planar trilayer PEDOT:PSS/Gr/n-Si Schottky junction architecture. By systematically benchmarking this hybrid device against pristine Gr/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si reference cells fabricated on untextured substrates, we isolate the fundamental optoelectronic and barrier functions of the carbon lattice. Comprehensive analyses reveal that the PEDOT:PSS layer simultaneously functions as an anti-reflection coating, a moderate p-type dopant for the underlying graphene, and a conductivity enhancer, collectively optimizing interfacial charge transport. Consequently, the trilayer device achieves a PCE of 8.52%, markedly outperforming the pristine Gr/n-Si reference cell (4.56%). Crucially, the atomic impermeability of the graphene sheet serves as a robust environmental barrier. While bare PEDOT:PSS/n-Si junctions retained only ~29% of their initial efficiency after 75 days of ambient exposure, graphene shields the active junction from moisture-induced degradation of the hygroscopic PEDOT:PSS overlayer. This enables the trilayer device to retain approximately 90% of its initial efficiency over the same 75-day period. The complementary roles of graphene as both a highly crystalline charge transport interface and an impermeable protective barrier establish a highly effective strategy for engineering high-efficiency, environmentally stable hybrid photovoltaics.

articles.title: Defect Candidates for Single-Photon Emission in Monolayer GaS and GaSe
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.21670v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the spin-resolved electronic structure of native vacancies and substitutional defects in monolayer GaS and GaSe using an anisotropic screened-exchange functional developed for two-dimensional material systems. By combining an energy-based classification of defect-associated states with spatially resolved projections and partial charge densities, we examine how these defects modify the in-gap electronic structure and assess their relevance for defect-based single-photon emission. The results identify gallium vacancies, particularly in GaS, as candidates single-photon emitters.

articles.title: Novel high-pressure silicon allotrope with quartz topology from first principles
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.21683v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A novel silicon allotrope, qtz Si, with quartz topology is proposed and investigated alongside four known allotropes (dia Si-I, lon Si-IV, bsn Si-II, and gsi Si-III) using first-principles density functional theory. qtz Si is found to exhibit the smallest atom-averaged volume (18.06 A3), highest density (2.582 g/cm3), highest bulk modulus (98 GPa), and highest maximum phonon frequency (16 THz) among the five, while showing the lowest shear modulus (37 GPa). All five allotropes are confirmed to satisfy the Born stability criteria and to display positive phonon frequencies throughout the Brillouin zone, i.e., they are mechanically and dynamically stable. Electronic structure calculations show that qtz Si is a semimetal with a vanishing gap, whereas dia Si and lon Si are semiconductors, and bsn and gsi allotropes are weakly metallic. Energy-volume equations of state place gsi and qtz 0.11-0.15 eV/atom above dia, bsn, and lon, consistent with their identification as high-pressure or metastable phases.

articles.title: Bond-informed search for ordered configurations in multi-principal element alloys
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.21718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ordered configurations in multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) control their local structure and influence a broad range of mechanical and thermodynamic properties. Yet they are notoriously difficult to identify. Locating low-energy ordered candidates requires exploring a configurational space that grows combinatorially with the number of elements, and Monte Carlo searches driven by density-functional theory (DFT) need a new electronic-structure calculation at every trial step. Here we introduce MECx (Minimum Energy Configuration eXplorer), a framework that guides Monte Carlo searches with a surrogate energy model trained on configurations stratified in bond-count space. Applied to ternary, quaternary, and quinary BCC alloys using compact training sets of 100 DFT-labeled configurations, MECx identifies ordered configurations with lower energies than those found by direct DFT-based Monte Carlo within practical computational limits. These configurations exhibit distinct pair-specific ordering, including B2- and B32-like motifs, and undergo progressive disordering as temperature increases. The MPEA-trained models also transfer to selected binary subsystems without retraining. The resulting ordered configurations agree with those obtained by direct DFT-based Monte Carlo and produce experimentally distinguishable superlattice reflections in simulated neutron diffraction patterns.

articles.title: Large in-plane optical anisotropy in epitaxial CrN(113) films
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.21856v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: CrN, a transition-metal nitride crystallizing in the cubic rocksalt structure, exhibits a unique combination of mechanical robustness, semiconducting behavior, and thermoelectric functionality. To date, however, CrN has been synthesized primarily as polycrystalline material or as epitaxial films grown along high-symmetry orientations such as (001) and (111). Here, we prepare epitaxial CrN(113) films on AlN(11bar22) templates by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy. The low-symmetry interface and highly direction dependent lattice mismatch are expected to modify the physical properties of CrN relative to the bulk material. Indeed, variable-angle spectroscopic ellipsometry in the photon-energy range from 1.25 to 5 eV reveals a surprisingly strong polarization dependence of the optical response despite the nearly strain-free cubic crystal structure of the films. The pseudo-optical constants n and k differ by more than 10% for orthogonal in-plane polarizations throughout the investigated spectral range. We evaluate possible origins of this effect and conclude that it most likely arises from anisotropic surface morphology of CrN(113), which creates a metasurface acting as a subwavelength grating in the strongly absorbing regime.

articles.title: Microwave spectroscopic evidence of a moiré-commensurate electron crystal in monolayer graphene
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.21875v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We probe the conductivity of the lowest Landau level of a moiré-aligned monolayer graphene device by broadband microwave transmission through a coplanar waveguide (sim50 mK, 15.4--18 T), isolating the longitudinal channel through a low-minus-high frequency band difference D(ν). We resolve a series of minima in D(ν) that drift with field along lines of fixed carrier density rather than fixed Landau filling, the hallmark of moiré-commensurate electron crystals. The strongest minimum is present at every field and matches no fractional quantum Hall or integer Hofstadter state. It lies at band filling s=1/3, one electron for every three moiré cells---the generalized Wigner crystal that DaSilva, Jung, and MacDonald predict as the most favorable fixed-density (t=0) commensuration. The weaker minima fall near neighboring commensurate fillings.

articles.title: VoroTypes: automated enumeration of Voronoi cell topologies for structural identification of complex crystals in atomistic simulations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.21911v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: VoroTypes enumerates, for an arbitrary crystal structure, the complete family of Voronoi cell topologies that can arise under small generic perturbations of atomic positions, and exports it as a topological filter for the VoroTop framework. This extends per-atom structural identification in molecular dynamics simulations, previously limited to a handful of simple reference structures, to complex crystals such as Frank--Kasper and Laves phases, with per-sublattice resolution. The package takes a standard crystallographic description (a CIF or POSCAR file) as input, applies exact symmetry reduction and validity pruning to accelerate the enumeration, and produces filters that load directly into the standalone VoroTop program or into OVITO. A library of pre-computed filters covers over a thousand structures from the Materials Project.

articles.title: Phase coexistence and nucleation of aging condensates
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.21917v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Biomolecular condensates form by phase separation and often age over time by transitioning from liquid-like droplets to solid-like states. To capture the fundamental behavior of aging condensates, we connect the Flory-Huggins model of phase separation with the trap model of aging dynamics. This combined model yields a rich phase diagram, including a regime of metastable coexisting liquids. Interestingly, the dense metastable liquid serves as an intermediate state in the nucleation pathway of the glass, which thus nucleates in two steps. Our results are generic, since they follow from a basic free-energy structure, providing a unified foundation for describing the thermodynamics and kinetics of aging biomolecular condensates.

articles.title: PANDA-D: Interface-free determination of two dynamic contact angles
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.21996v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Contact angles are central descriptors of wetting and capillary behavior at solid--fluid interfaces. Dynamic contact angles in molecular simulations are commonly extracted from two-dimensional liquid--vapor contours and near-wall tangent fits. We introduce PANDA-D, an extension of Predicting Angle from Nanoscale Density Analysis (PANDA) that determines both contact angles of a driven liquid roll without extracting an interface. The density profile measures occupied layer width but does not identify which meniscus is advancing. The method resolves this ambiguity by jointly fitting density and the layerwise center-of-mass displacement relative to the roll. A circular-meniscus model maps these profiles to receding and advancing angles and an effective near-wall offset. On synthetic rolls with prescribed angles, the reconstruction error is 0.29^circ root-mean-square. We then analyze force-driven Lennard--Jones rolls between crystalline walls. Joint fits reproduce both measured profiles, whereas density-only fits can match density while assigning incorrect asymmetry. The resulting angles agree with independently determined circle-fit angles to 0.84^circ root-mean-square. Across four wall--fluid attractions, the receding angle decreases and the advancing angle increases with force, approximately linearly over the studied ranges. By eliminating contour thresholds and near-wall tangent extrapolation from the primary estimate, the two-profile approach enables reproducible, automated angle analysis across molecular trajectories.

articles.title: Coherent and Incoherent Time-Resolved Diffuse Scattering Intensity from First Principles
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22006v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time-resolved diffuse scattering from X-ray free-electron lasers and ultrafast electron diffraction gives access to the nonequilibrium lattice dynamics of photoexcited solids in reciprocal space. Existing interpretations have often relied on simplified models. Here we present a first-principles formulation of the time-dependent first-order diffuse intensity in which coherent and incoherent contributions emerge on equal footing. By assuming the probe-pulse coherence time to be longer than the characteristic electronic timescales, but shorter than those of the ionic motion, we work in the density-matrix formalism and derive equations of motion for the displacement-displacement correlators in a basis of instantaneous, out-of-equilibrium Born-Oppenheimer normal modes. We show how the incoherent contribution, governed by the phonon occupations, and a coherent contribution, governed by the anomalous phonon correlators, emerge. The non-trivial coherent dynamics is shown to be induced both by the photoinduced phonon-frequency shift and by electron-phonon scattering off the nonequilibrium carrier distribution. We implement the resulting equations using Wannier interpolation in the textscEPIq code and apply them to photoexcited germanium. The calculated diffuse intensity reproduces both the oscillation frequencies and the rising incoherent background observed experimentally, opening the way to a systematic interpretation of time-resolved diffuse scattering in ultrafast experiments.

articles.title: Putting a Temperature on Electron Correlation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22134v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is common wisdom that a better understanding of how to quantify electron correlation should lead to more efficient treatments of the correlation problem. Here, we not only substantiate this view but turn it into a concrete, systematic framework for ground states. Since prominent correlation measures such as the nonfreeness depend only on the one-particle reduced density matrix, modeling the correlation energy as a function of such a measure naturally places the framework within reduced density matrix functional theory, while keeping the cost at mean-field level. Strikingly, the variable conjugate to the measure emerges as a ``correlation temperature'', thereby connecting correlation measures, functional theory, and effective temperatures. The framework rationalizes methods such as i-DMFT, and we illustrate its key concepts analytically for the Hubbard dimer and numerically for small molecular systems. This brings a fundamental question within reach: how much of the correlation problem can be solved at mean-field cost?

articles.title: A rigid commensurate host and a defect that switches: vacancies in the frustrated alternating spin-(1, 1/2) Heisenberg chain
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The alternating spin-(1,tfrac12) Heisenberg chain with a frustrating next-nearest-neighbor coupling J₂ loses its Lieb--Mattis moment through a discontinuous transition to a singlet whose nature was left open. Using an SU(2)-symmetric density-matrix renormalization group, in which the total spin is a quantum-number label, we identify that phase and follow a single vacancy through it. The total spin collapses directly from S=L/4 to S=0, with no partially polarized window. The singlet phase is critical: its singlet--triplet gap closes as 1/L, its entanglement entropy grows logarithmically with a central charge csimeq1.8, and its modulation wavevector, extrapolated from L=80 to 200, is commensurate at 3π/4 and independent of J₂ to 5×10⁻⁵. Removing the central S=1 site switches the ground state of the doped chain from a triplet to a singlet at J₂ast=0.3068(3), where the host shows no feature; the triplet is not bound to the vacancy but spread over one of the two segments it leaves. The transmission of correlations through the vacancy saturates at a finite value below J₂ast, T(infty)=0.102(15) and 0.036(9) at J₂=0.28 and 0.30, and the cut-chain law Tpropto L⁻¹ is excluded on both sides. We also show that the longitudinal correlator is not an observable in a triplet sector.

articles.title: d-wave superconductivity in quintuple-layer bulk superconductor La₆Ni₅O₁₂
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22212v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The recent realization of bulk superconductivity in the quintuple-layer nickelate La₆Ni₅O₁₂ opens new opportunities to probe the pairing symmetry of the reduced Ruddlesden--Popper (RP) nickelate family. Using an effective five-layer Hubbard model and variational Monte Carlo calculations, we find that a spin-singlet dₓ^₂₋y^₂-wave state is energetically favored, while extended-s-wave pairing is strongly suppressed. Based on the optimized superconducting state, we further calculate several experimentally accessible observables. The tunneling density of states exhibits a characteristic V-shaped low-energy spectrum, the superfluid density shows a linear low-temperature depletion, the Knight shift decreases below T_c, and the spin-lattice relaxation rate follows 1/T₁Tpropto T², together providing consistent signatures of a clean nodal superconductor. Extending the same framework to related reduced RP nickelates, we find a robust d-wave tendency in infinite-layer LaNiO₂, while trilayer La₄Ni₃O₈ at its nominal filling lies close to the boundary between d-wave superconductivity and a non-superconducting state. These results establish bulk La₆Ni₅O₁₂ as a promising platform for determining the pairing symmetry of nickelate superconductors and suggest a common dₓ^₂₋y^₂-wave pairing tendency across the reduced RP nickelate family.

articles.title: Local wave-packet spectroscopy of the Drude weight in Tomonaga-Luttinger liquids
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22257v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate wave packets generated by a local pulse electric field in a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid (TLL) with a U(1) charge q. Bosonization shows that a local pulse field creates two counterpropagating packets with opposite accumulated charges ± qK and velocity v, where K and v are the TLL parameter and velocity. The packet motion produces a linearly growing charge polarization P(t)=2 qDt in the conducting TLL at non-equilibrium, allowing the Drude weight D=vK to be extracted from real-time local dynamics. We test this local-packet description by time-dependent variational principle simulations of the spin-1/2 XXZ chain. The simulations visualize the density, current, energy, and entanglement profiles in the space-time plane and confirm the predicted packet charge and propagation velocity. We also show that excess energy and entanglement remaining near the pulse region are suppressed in the weak-pulse limit. Finally, the Drude weight obtained from the packet-induced polarization agrees with the exact Bethe-ansatz result, demonstrating local-packet spectroscopy of intrinsic transport in a TLL.

articles.title: Extended strange metal and superconductivity in partially filled moiré Hubbard bands
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22307v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Moiré semiconductors provide a physical realization of the Hubbard model. Bandwidth-tuned Mott transitions and complex phase diagrams mimicking those of high-temperature superconductors have been demonstrated near a weak Mott insulating state at half-band-filling. The platform also provides an opportunity to explore the physics of a partially filled Hubbard band at doping densities far away from the Mott insulator, a regime that has remained largely unexplored. Here we report the emergence of an extended strange metal (ESM), in both doping density and twist angle, in a partially filled Hubbard band of twisted bilayer WSe2. The ESM is in the clean limit, persists down to 100mK, and spans over multiple symmetry-breaking ground states; it also appears only at small twist angles, where electronic correlations are strong. These observations distinguish the state from the reported strange metals associated with quantum criticality and favor the viewpoint that it is an intrinsic state of matter. We also report the observation of a new superconducting dome being developed from the ESM but far away from both the Mott insulating state and the van Hove singularity of the material. Our work opens the door to exploring the new regime of partially filled Hubbard bands in the clean limit.

articles.title: Quantum Work Statistics from Entanglement-Assisted Invariance
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20528v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We demonstrate that the one-time measurement scheme is more consistent than the standard two-time measurement scheme with respect to the fundamental symmetry of entanglement, namely entanglement-assisted invariance (envariance). In particular, the work statistics obtained from the one-time measurement scheme arise naturally as a direct consequence of envariance for any driving unitary, without involving an explicit measurement postulate, whereas the analogous identification for the two-time measurement scheme is possible only for a Haar-measure-zero set of unitaries. This envariance-based formulation eliminates the ambiguity in work statistics related to the energetic cost of measurement.

articles.title: Second-Order Homogenization of Particulate Elastomeric Composites for Structural-Scale Damage Analysis
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20624v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Damage prediction in particulate elastomeric composites is challenging due to the strong material heterogeneity, nearly incompressible behavior of the matrix, and the presence of localized stress concentrations arising from matrix-inclusion interactions. In the present work, a computational framework is developed for damage propagation analysis of particulate elastomeric composite structures. The effective constitutive response of the heterogeneous material is first determined using the second-order homogenization method. The resulting homogenized response is subsequently used to identify equivalent hyperelastic material parameters for structural simulations. A three-parameter isotropic damage model is incorporated to capture damage-induced softening. A mixed displacement-pressure finite element formulation, is used to alleviate volumetric locking associated with nearly incompressible property of elastomers. The proposed framework is validated through full-scale simulations and homogenized response involving composites with varying inclusion volume fractions. Numerical investigations demonstrate that the homogenized models is able to reproduce the global force-displacement response within 2% error and damage evolution characteristics of the heterogeneous composites while significantly reducing the computational cost.

articles.title: The noise cost of reservoir locality in broadband quantum amplifier chains
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20654v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Directional quantum amplifiers enable weak-signal readout while protecting the source, but reservoir noise limits sensitivity. Finite-band suppression must reconcile frequency-dependent responses with fixed local couplings and finite rates. We construct adjacent-site loss channels attaining the known single-frequency minimum under local compatibility conditions, as an uncapped benchmark. For specified uniform and dimerized chains, we compare fixed reservoirs at matched drift, ports, high-gain band and complete gain/loss rate caps. At the representative cap R=8 and halfwidth Ω=0.05, nearest-neighbor arithmetic band average noise exceeds the unrestricted optimum by more than 1.01265 quanta in the uniform chain for every finite Nge64. Boundary-response bounds give necessary rates and targets requiring range two. At N=64, finite-auxiliary calculations retain a noise advantage under matched total coupling budgets; response bounds quantify noise-resolution tolerances. These theoretical results guide reservoir design and noise calibration for a proposed cryogenic microwave array with a 100 kHz design band.

articles.title: Surviving readout errors and incomplete postselection in monitored quantum circuits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20712v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study how readout errors affect dynamics in monitored quantum circuits. Such errors make postselection effectively incomplete, conditioning trajectories on imperfect rather than true records. Focusing on U(1)-symmetric circuits, we find that the charge-sharpening transition survives at a finite error rate, with the sharp phase's vanishing fluctuations replaced by a finite steady-state plateau. The charge fluctuations show a shallow minimum near the ideal transition point as a function of measurement rate, signaling the competition between measurement-induced purification and noise-induced mixing. By decomposing the fluctuations into quantum and classical contributions, we show the minimum marks where incomplete postselection still retains enough trajectory memory to attenuate noise-induced mixing, leaving a detectable signature of the transition even in a noisy setting. Mid-circuit measurements are far harder to mitigate against readout errors than standard end-of-circuit ones, because the errors corrupt the postselection itself; the decomposition therefore offers a minimal mitigation framework and a route to locate the transition directly from experimental data. Our results show that charge sharpening survives readout errors in a quantitative and experimentally accessible way.

articles.title: monoprop: Scaling Pauli and Majorana propagation via Anticommutation Indices
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.21000v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce monoprop, an open-source, massively parallel operator-propagation framework for fermion and qubit bases. For N qubits or modes, existing codes represent each of the K tracked operator terms (Pauli strings or products of Majorana operators) as a 2N-bit string, testing each for anticommutation with the gate at O(KN) cost per gate. Here, we introduce the anticommutation index which rapidly looks up the terms anticommuting with a gate. A local gate changes only the terms that touch its sites, and when terms are truncated to act on few sites, only a fraction sim1/N touch any given qubit or mode, and we use this to prove the time per gate scales as O(K/N). This counterintuitive result tells us that for a fixed number of terms, increasing the number of sites can make things faster. We demonstrate this numerically, and show monoprop scales almost ideally to 8192 cores, tracking 9.5×10¹⁰ terms. Beyond propagation, we present memory-efficient surrogate graphs, which record one propagation and replay it at new angles, for fast energy re-estimation and parameter gradients, and an efficient method for finding energy-minimising gates and optimal angles for simulating adaptive quantum-chemistry circuits.

articles.title: Casimir forces on suspended thin dielectric membranes covered with graphene
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.21437v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the Casimir force on thin suspended dielectric layers covered with graphene, both theoretically and experimentally. Thermal effects of the Casimir force on graphene occur at separations significantly smaller compared to ordinary metals and dielectrics. At such small separations, the Casimir force is sufficiently strong to be measured experimentally. However, the presence of substrates to support the graphene significantly reduces the enhancement. We show theoretically that replacing the solid substrate beneath graphene with a thin dielectric membrane partially restores this strong thermal dependence. One of the interacting objects is a solid gold plate. The other object is a suspended dielectric membrane made of either 15 nm of silicon oxide or 13 nm silicon nitride, covered with graphene. At a separation of sim500 nm, theoretical predictions yield changes in the Casimir pressure of up to 54 % and 40 % for silicon oxide and silicon nitride, respectively, when the temperature is increased from 10 K to 294 K. Measurements were performed for graphene on a suspended silicon nitride membrane at room temperature, using a gold-coated sphere attached to a cantilever as the force sensor. The measured force gradient is consistent with the theoretical prediction, although the thermal dependence could not be resolved, in part because of uncertainties in the optical properties of silicon nitride. Replacing a bulk substrate with a thin dielectric membrane covered with graphene provides a substantial reduction of the Casimir force, which may facilitate the stable operation of neutral nanomechanical elements at small separations.

articles.title: Difference between pair creation and anomaly matching: Nontrivial aspects of invertible symmetries and defects in SU(N) models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.21478v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the connection between the SU(N)K Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW) model and SU(N)K' WZW models, enforcing the unbroken ZN symmetries. The fundamental underlying structures are the (half-)integer spin simple currents in the topological quantum field theories and anomaly matching conditions in conformal field theories. For the (half-)integer spin simple current condition of the folded models SU(N)Kboxtimes_ZN overlineSU(N)K' or SU(N)Kboxtimes_ZN SU(N)K', we obtain the generalized pairing condition K= ± R²K' (mod.N) with gcd(R,N)=1. On the other hand, the anomaly matching condition results in the weaker condition K= ± RUK' (mod.N) with gcd(R,N)=gcd(U,N)=1. Surprisingly, the anomaly matching without the pairing condition results in the intrinsic mismatch of the preservation law of the ZN defects and symmetries. The pairing condition canonically relates symmetries and defects, as in category theory, whereas it is unclear whether it can be a guiding principle in prohibiting the massless renormalization group flows.

articles.title: Operator-Space Entanglement Entropy in Random Fermionic Gaussian Dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.21723v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the von Neumann operator-space entanglement entropy (OSEE) of initial product operators evolved under random gaussian dynamics, as modeled by a Brownian SYK₂ model. By exploiting a mapping to a domain-wall melting problem, we derive an exact expression for the time-dependent bipartite OSEE in the thermodynamic limit, and obtain an analytic characterization of the corresponding gaussian Page curve emerging at late times. Our results build on recent work on the entanglement dynamics in the all-to-all quantum simple exclusion process, leveraging tools from RMT, including the Coulomb-gas approach and a mapping to the free Jacobi process. Finally, based on our results, we discuss the possibility of relating the OSEE with non-gaussianity measures in the Heisenberg picture.

articles.title: Grain Boundary Anisotropy and Its Influence on Helium Bubble Nucleation, Growth, and Decohesion in Polycrystalline Iron
articles.abstract: arXiv:2509.07197v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The accumulation of helium bubbles at grain boundaries (GBs) critically degrades the mechanical integrity of structural materials in nuclear reactors. While GBs act as sinks for radiation-induced defects, their inherent structural anisotropy leads to complex helium bubble evolution behaviors that remain poorly understood. This work integrates accelerated molecular dynamics simulations and a novel atomic-scale metric, the flexibility volume (V_f), to establish the interplay between GB character, helium segregation, and bubble growth mechanisms in body-centered cubic iron. We demonstrate that V_f, which incorporates both local atomic volume and vibrational properties, qualitatively predicts deformation propensity. Our results reveal that the atomic-scale segregation energy landscape dictates initial helium clustering and subsequent bubble morphology, with low-energy channels in tilt Σ5 boundary facilitating one-dimensional migration while isolated deep traps in twist Σ13 boundary promote larger, rounder bubble morphology. Critically, besides gradual bubble growth via trap mutation mechanism, we identify two distinct stress-relief mechanisms: loop punching in anisotropic tilt Σ5 boundary and interfacial decohesion in twist Σ11 boundary, with the dominant pathway determined by the interplay between bubble morphology and local mechanical softness. This study establishes a fundamental connection between GB crystallographic and energetical anisotropy and helium bubble evolution, providing critical insights for designing radiation-tolerant microstructures.

articles.title: Fluctuation-Induced Supersolidity at the Superfluid-Solid Interface
articles.abstract: arXiv:2512.08739v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Supersolidity, combining superfluid and crystalline orders, has been realized in dipolar Bose-Einstein condensates by tuning interatomic interactions. Here we show that supersolidity can also emerge from mode coupling at a superfluid-solid interface, without modifying bulk interactions and for a broad class of superfluids. Using an analytical and numerical treatment of the coupled superfluid and phonon fields, we derive the criterion for a density-modulation instability driven by interfacial coupling and dependent on dimensionality. In superfluid helium, the instability first appears at the roton mode, while in a Bose-Einstein condensate with contact interactions it occurs at the lowest accessible wave vector set by the system size. Beyond the threshold, the ground state acquires an interfacial density modulation while the bulk remains superfluid, forming a hybrid superfluid-supersolid phase. Our results identify interfacial mode coupling as a promising route to supersolidity, enabling the simultaneous exploitation of interfacial supersolid and bulk superfluid quantum properties.

articles.title: Quantum geometry, localization, and topological bounds of spin fluctuations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2512.17454v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study how topological crystalline defects--dislocations--reshape the real-space quantum geometric tensor and act as tunable sources of quantum geometry. We show that dislocations strongly enhance the quantum metric, establishing a direct link between lattice topology and the Hilbert-space geometry of states. We characterize the quantum geometry of topological magnons in ordered arrays of dislocations, demonstrating that defect-induced geometric enhancement controls their localization and topological protection. In disordered arrays, dislocation-driven geometry expands the accessible topological phase space and enables transitions to disorder-induced topological phases. Our results identify the quantum metric as a tunable bridge between crystalline topology, magnonic excitations, and emergent topological matter in aperiodic solid-state and synthetic systems.

articles.title: Signatures of Dynes superconductivity in the THz response of ALD-grown NbN thin films
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.15003v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The frequency-dependent complex optical conductivity reflects key properties of superconductors, such as the energy gap in the density of states (DOS) and the superfluid density. For disordered superconductors, the optical conductivity often can be described within Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) theory, while in corresponding tunneling experiments, deviations in the observed DOS typically require modelling by the phenomenological Dynes formula. The implications of such Dynes DOS for optics were rarely discussed so far. Here we probe the terahertz conductivity of superconducting NbN thin films with thicknesses ranging from 4.5 to 20nm, which were grown by atomic layer deposition (ALD). Our frequency range from 0.3 to 2.1 THz covers energies below and above the spectral gap. For 20nm thick NbN, we find in the optical conductivity distinct deviations from the BCS model, including a step-like characteristic in the absorption at half the zero-temperature spectral gap. These observations can be fully captured by Dynes electrodynamics with a small and temperature-independent pair-breaking rate. For the other films, we also observe signs of Dynes electrodynamics, and we discuss the evolution of the energy gap, the superfluid density, and the pair-breaking rate as function of film thickness.

articles.title: Quantum Many-Body Mpemba Effect through Ruelle-Pollicott Resonances
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.11788v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Relaxation towards equilibrium is often assumed to be slower when a system starts farther from equilibrium, but this intuition fails in the Mpemba effect. Recent advances in controllable quantum platforms have enabled the exploration of its quantum analogue, the quantum Mpemba effect (QME), yet its microscopic origin remains largely unclear. Here we provide a general framework for understanding the QME in closed quantum many-body chaotic systems by reformulating the equilibration process of local subsystems in terms of Ruelle-Pollicott (RP) resonances. We show that suppressing the initial-state overlap with the dominant RP resonant mode accelerates subsystem equilibration and thereby yields the QME. We further uncover that a novel type of strong QME can occur via complete translation-symmetry breaking of initial states. We substantiate our predictions using the prototypical kicked Ising chain and a quantum automaton circuit. These findings cast the QME in closed many-body systems into a unified framework with open-system analogues and provide experimentally accessible signatures on state-of-the-art quantum platforms.

articles.title: Quantum Monte Carlo calculations in the nuclear shell model by the complex Langevin method
articles.abstract: arXiv:2508.15116v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The nuclear shell model is known to describe the properties of various nuclei extremely well. However, the auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo calculations cannot be applied to it with general interactions due to the sign problem. The model has therefore been investigated primarily by variational methods, where the accuracy of the results depends crucially on the ansatz for the wave function. Here we perform the auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo calculations in the case of small systems at finite temperature using the complex Langevin method (CLM), which has been successfully applied to various interesting systems with the sign problem over the decade. In particular, we show the existence of a parameter region in which the validity criterion for the CLM is satisfied and the expectation value of the energy obtained by exact diagonalization is correctly reproduced. Thus the CLM can be a complementary approach to the variational method for large systems.

articles.title: Entanglement and apparent thermality in simulated black holes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2509.22774v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the apparent thermality of Hawking radiation in the semi-classical limit of quantum black holes using the mean-field limit of a chiral spin-chain simulator, which models fermions propagating on a black hole space-time in the continuum. In this free-theory regime, no genuine thermalisation occurs. Nevertheless, we show that a bipartition across the event horizon yields a reduced density matrix whose mode occupations follow an apparent thermal Fermi-Dirac distribution. In contrast, partitions away from the horizon do not exhibit such thermal distributions, reflecting the absence of thermal behaviour. Our results demonstrate that Hawking radiation appears thermal only with respect to horizon bipartitions in free theories, with genuine thermal behaviour expected to emerge only in the presence of strong interactions deep in the black hole interior, a study of which we leave for future work.

articles.title: Simulation of topological superconductors and their competing orders using photon-mediated interactions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2512.17889v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Realizing and controlling the unconventional pairing featured by topological superconductors remains a central challenge. We introduce a cavity QED quantum simulator that engineers competing chiral pₓ+ip_y and dₓ^₂₋y^₂+idₓy orders by tailoring cavity-mediated couplings between atomic pseudospins that emulate momentum-dependent pairing channels. The desired spatially inhomogeneous cavity-mediated couplings can be engineered in a 2D optical lattice using incommensurate cavity-lattice wavelengths naturally occurring in cavity QED systems. This minimal and fully tunable platform enables controlled state preparation and continuous measurement of superconducting order parameters. To probe this competition, the platform enables selective excitation and direct time-domain detection of Bardasis-Schrieffer modes---collective excitations of the subdominant pairing channel. The same competing channel can have an even stronger impact out of equilibrium, where a sudden quench can drive its growth and abruptly reshape the dominant superconducting order, despite the stability of the dominant order in equilibrium. Together, these results establish cavity QED as a controlled setting for revealing hidden competing orders and exploring nonlinear dynamics of topological superconductivity that remain elusive in solid-state and ultracold-atom systems.

articles.title: Representation-split Carleman lattice Boltzmann with near-unit step success probability on quantum computers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Carleman lattice Boltzmann method replaces the quadratic collision of the lattice Boltzmann equation by a linear map on a lifted state. Existing block encodings of this map succeed with probability 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻² per step, so that the probability of a multi-step evolution decays exponentially with the number of steps. This study develops multi-relaxation-time Carleman lattice Boltzmann, a representation split in which the Carleman-lifted collision is performed in a moment basis on the amplitude-encoded state, while streaming remains a permutation in population space. The level-2 hierarchy closes under collision but not under streaming, which generates the work of pressure, advection and stress on the momentum flux. The state therefore remains the full pair array, and the moment representation is an orthogonal change of basis of the population one, with identical dynamics and truncation error. The operator to be block encoded changes with the basis, and with it the success probability of a quantum step. In the weighted Hermite basis with the amplitude encoding fᵢ/sqrtwᵢ, the relaxation is a diagonal operator of norm one, and the level-2 collision stage becomes this diagonal plus a sparse coupling from products of conserved moments. A structured block encoding of this form raises the single-step success probability on the D2Q9 lattice from 10⁻² for the best population encoding to 0.98. With the pair sector in relative coordinates and scaled, one step requires O(log² N) Toffoli gates and is verified by statevector simulation. The encoding and readout overhead of a T-step run is then polynomial in T and N rather than accumulating a factor p^T. For resolved flows, the remaining exponential loss in coherent multi-step Carleman lattice Boltzmann evolution is set by the non-equilibrium norm relaxed by dissipation rather than by the block encoding.

articles.title: Schrödinger's unpublished hidden-variable model in the 1944-45 debate over the "Collapse of Determinism"
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20752v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the mid-1940s, the question of whether quantum mechanics could be supplemented by deterministic hidden variables resurfaced in a debate in ^textitNature. I show that Erwin Schrödinger drafted a hitherto unpublished response to this controversy. In it, Schrödinger provided an explicit hidden-variable model, thereby showing that such models could not be ruled out. I reconstruct the historical context of this forgotten manuscript and publish here the first transcription and analysis. Importantly, Schrödinger's proposal should be understood as a proof of principle rather than as evidence of his commitment to determinism.

articles.title: Vibrational Dressing of Collective Molecular Polaritons: A Scalable Green's-Function Theory
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a scalable Green's-function theory of vibrationally dressed molecular-polariton absorption in the Holstein--Tavis--Cummings model. Within the self-consistent Born approximation (SCBA), the ground-state linear response of N identical molecules coupled to one cavity mode follows from a 2×2 cavity--bright matrix, while scattering through the N-1 dark states remains in the molecular self-energy. The number of self-consistent equations is independent of N, allowing large ensembles to be treated without explicitly resolving the dark manifold. Benchmarks against hierarchical equations of motion show that the theory captures collective linewidth narrowing and an N-dependent minimum in the lower-polariton linewidth as its exciton fraction varies, beyond a Hopfield-weighted linewidth estimate. Comparisons with exact diagonalization for discrete local vibrations show weaker vibronic progressions and better overall SCBA agreement as N increases at fixed single-molecule coupling. The resulting framework connects microscopic vibrational scattering to collective absorption spectra without introducing fitted polariton linewidths.
