In this work, we demonstrate that active biomolecular condensates enable the self-propulsion of micron-sized objects in otherwise homogeneous, isotropic, and autonomous environments. Our proposed minimal mechanism consists of phase-separating proteins, the enzymes that passivate them, and complementary enzymes isotropically anchored to a spherical-colloid surface which reactivate the proteins. This passivation-activation cycle gives rise to a symmetry breaking wherein a single biocondensate is stabilized near the colloid surface, which in turn exerts a repulsive force on the colloid. We numerically demonstrate that this mechanism can propel micron-sized colloids at speeds of up to a hundred microns per second. This propulsion mode is strongly resistant to Brownian fluctuations and external forces. Propulsion mechanisms based on biomolecular condensates may thus offer a complementary, motor-free route to biological transport.
articles.abstract_zh: 生命系统通常消耗能量来实现运动，通常使用复杂的生物分子机器。在这项工作中，我们证明了活性生物分子冷凝物能够在均匀、各向同性和自主的环境中实现微米级物体的自我推进。我们提出的最小机制包括相分离蛋白质，钝化它们的酶，以及各向同性地锚定在球形胶体表面的互补酶，其重新激活蛋白质。这种钝化-活化循环产生对称性断裂，其中单个生物冷凝物在胶体表面附近稳定，这反过来对胶体施加排斥力。我们数值证明，这种机制可以以高达每秒100微米的速度推进微米大小的胶体。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 生命系统通常消耗能量来实现运动，通常使用复杂的生物分子机器。在这项工作中，我们证明了活性生物分子冷凝物能够在均匀、各向同性和自主的环境中实现微米级物体的自我推进。我们提出的最小机制包括相分离蛋白质，钝化它们的酶，以及各向同性地锚定在球形胶体表面的互补酶，其重新激活蛋白质。这种钝化-活化循环产生对称性断裂，其中单个生物冷凝物在胶体表面附近稳定，这反过来对胶体施加排斥力。我们数值证明，这种机制可以以高达每秒100微米的速度推进微米大小的胶体。这种推进模式对布朗波动和外力具有很强的抵抗力。因此，基于生物分子冷凝物的推进机制可以为生物运输提供互补的、无马达的途径。

articles.title: The thermopower properties of interacting systems
articles.title_zh: 相互作用系统的热电特性
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.14225v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Seebeck coefficient quantifies the voltage generated across a material in response to a temperature gradient. Recent studies have shown that strong electronic correlations can enhance this coefficient, producing anomalous behavior near half-filling associated with the Mott plateau. This raises the possibility that other interaction scales, not necessarily originating in Mott physics, could give rise to similar enhancements. Here, we investigate the Seebeck coefficient in the presence of attractive interactions, nearest-neighbor interactions, sublattice potentials, and electron-phonon coupling. The Seebeck coefficient is obtained via the Kelvin formula, using entropy data derived from density calculations within determinant quantum Monte Carlo (DQMC). We find that these additional interaction scales can indeed enhance the Seebeck coefficient and further induce multiple sign changes as a function of doping. We show that this anomalous behavior is associated with the opening of a gap in the ground state, as computed via cluster perturbation theory (CPT). Moreover, electron-phonon coupling alone-even in the absence of on-site repulsion-can produce a Seebeck anomaly. We relate these sign changes to a restructuring of the Fermi surface and an accompanying change in its topology, an effect commonly observed in cuprates.
articles.abstract_zh: Seebeck系数量化响应温度梯度在材料上产生的电压。最近的研究表明，强大的电子相关性可以增强这一系数，从而在与莫特高原相关的半填充附近产生异常行为。这提出了其他相互作用尺度（不一定源于莫特物理学）可能产生类似增强的可能性。在这里，我们研究了在存在有吸引力的相互作用、最近邻相互作用、亚晶格电位和电子-声子耦合的情况下的塞贝克系数。塞贝克系数通过开尔文公式获得，使用从行列式量子蒙特卡罗（ DQMC ）内的密度计算得出的熵数据。
authors: Willdauany C. de Freitas da Silva
articles.abstract_zh_full: Seebeck系数量化响应温度梯度在材料上产生的电压。最近的研究表明，强大的电子相关性可以增强这一系数，从而在与莫特高原相关的半填充附近产生异常行为。这提出了其他相互作用尺度（不一定源于莫特物理学）可能产生类似增强的可能性。在这里，我们研究了在存在有吸引力的相互作用、最近邻相互作用、亚晶格电位和电子-声子耦合的情况下的塞贝克系数。塞贝克系数通过开尔文公式获得，使用从行列式量子蒙特卡罗（ DQMC ）内的密度计算得出的熵数据。我们发现，这些额外的相互作用量表确实可以增强塞贝克系数，并进一步诱导多种征象变化作为兴奋剂的函数。我们表明，这种异常行为与基态间隙的开放相关，如通过聚类扰动理论（ CPT ）计算的那样。此外，单独的电子-声子耦合-即使没有现场排斥-也会产生塞贝克异常。我们将这些符号变化与费米曲面的重构以及随之而来的拓扑变化联系起来，这种影响通常在铜酸盐中观察到。

articles.title: Topological zero-reflection points in multi-terminal quantum wire junctions
articles.title_zh: 多端量子线结中的拓扑零反射点
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.31586v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study scattering in noninteracting multi-terminal quantum wire junctions and show that junctions with dihedral symmetry can exhibit exact zero-reflection points for N ge 4 terminals. By analyzing the scattering matrix, we identify these reflectionless points in the (E,t') parameter space, where E is the incident particle energy and t' is the junction hopping amplitude. These points exhibit an even-odd dependence on N and converge asymptotically to a common limiting value in the large-N limit. We show that the reflectionless points are characterized by an integer winding number associated with the phase of the reflection amplitude, providing a topological description for their stability against weak on-site disorder. We also consider junctions with broken time-reversal symmetry and find that a magnetic flux can induce additional reflectionless points, including for the N = 3 case. For a four-terminal junction threaded by a π-flux, we identify a unique parameter regime in which the reflection amplitude vanishes over the entire energy band. Finally, we discuss experimental signatures through the behavior of Friedel oscillations and examine the stability of these reflectionless points in the presence of weak interactions.
articles.abstract_zh: 我们研究了非相互作用多端子量子线结中的散射，并表明具有二面体对称性的结可以为N ge 4端子呈现精确的零反射点。通过分析散射矩阵，我们在(E, t ')参数空间中识别这些无反射点，其中E是入射粒子能量， t'是结跳幅度。这些点表现出对N的偶数依赖性，并渐近收敛到大N极限中的公共极限值。我们表明，无反射点的特征在于与反射幅度的相位相关的整数绕组数，为它们对弱现场障碍的稳定性提供了拓扑描述。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 我们研究了非相互作用多端子量子线结中的散射，并表明具有二面体对称性的结可以为N ge 4端子呈现精确的零反射点。通过分析散射矩阵，我们在(E, t ')参数空间中识别这些无反射点，其中E是入射粒子能量， t'是结跳幅度。这些点表现出对N的偶数依赖性，并渐近收敛到大N极限中的公共极限值。我们表明，无反射点的特征在于与反射幅度的相位相关的整数绕组数，为它们对弱现场障碍的稳定性提供了拓扑描述。我们还考虑了具有断裂时间反转对称性的结，并发现磁通量可以诱导额外的无反射点，包括N = 3的情况。对于由π通量螺纹连接的四端结，我们确定了一种独特的参数机制，其中反射幅度在整个能带上消失。最后，我们通过弗里德尔振荡的行为来讨论实验特征，并检查这些无反射点在弱相互作用下的稳定性。

articles.title: Floquet spin-group theory for light-tailored spin splitting in collinear magnets
articles.title_zh: 共线磁体中轻量化自旋分裂的Floquet自旋群理论
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.02393v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Spin groups have emerged as a fundamental symmetry framework for spin-splitting antiferromagnets, including altermagnets. For periodically driven magnets, where new spin-splitting electronic structures can emerge beyond equilibrium, an analogous symmetry theory is still lacking. Here, we develop a Floquet spin-group theory for optically driven collinear magnets by combining the static spin group of the magnetic crystal with the dynamical symmetry group of the light field. This theory determines the symmetry-allowed parity, momentum dependence, and nodal structure of light-induced spin splitting under general periodic driving. We show that odd-, even-, and mixed-parity spin splittings can be selectively switched within the same material by tailoring the drive symmetry, accompanied by distinct symmetry-allowed transport responses. We further uncover higher-order h- and k-wave Floquet spin splittings unique to three-dimensional systems. Our work extends spin-group theory from static magnets to periodically driven systems, providing a general symmetry principle for engineering light-controlled nonequilibrium spin-resolved electronic structures.

articles.title: Dynamic Magnetic Pair-Density Function of a One-Dimensional Ferromagnet
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.21759v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The dynamic magnetic pair-density function (DymPDF) Dᵣₘ M(r, E) is derived by extending the static magnetic pair distribution function (mPDF) to finite energy transfer. The analytical DymPDF of a one-dimensional Heisenberg ferromagnet is obtained from the magnon dispersion and compared with simulations performed using textsc SpinW. Excellent agreement is achieved for energy dependence of the nearest-neighbor spin-pair correlation, demonstrating that the DymPDF changes sign at the magnon-mode transition occurring at one-half of the maximum magnon energy. The r-dependence of DymPDF at low energy is also reproduced with a model including magnon correlation length and Fourier-termination effects. These results establish the theoretical foundation of DymPDF analysis for investigating local spin dynamics in magnetic materials.

articles.title: Microscopic Theory of Drag in a Bose Condensate Interacting with a Moving Reservoir
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.27898v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive a microscopic theory of drag for a Bose-Einstein condensate interacting with a moving reservoir. Starting from interactions between a condensate and a drifting fermionic bath, we integrate out the bath degrees of freedom within the Born--Markov approximation to obtain an effective Gross--Pitaevskii equation with a drag potential. From this potential we derive an effective drag force and obtain a closed expression for the drag coefficient, determined by the reservoir density fluctuations and the condensate density profile. As an application, we simulate the drag for an exciton--polariton condensate interacting with a drifting electron gas.

articles.title: Continuum Limit of Nonlocal Electrostatics in Random Media
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.06354v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive a two-scale continuum limit for the electrostatic energy of random charge density fields that are stationary and ergodic under lattice translations. Each microscopic cell is charge neutral in every realization, while its dipole moment may fluctuate and have a nonzero mean. Under assumptions on the stationary microscopic potential and the finite-volume fields, the local and nonlocal energies converge almost surely to deterministic limits. The local limit consists of the ensemble-averaged microscopic Coulomb energy and a cell-depolarization term, whereas the effective polarization determines the nonlocal limit. The cell-depolarization terms cancel in the total energy, which consists of the ensemble-averaged microscopic cell energy and the macroscopic electrostatic field energy. The deterministic specialization recovers the periodic two-scale limit. For an independent-cell random-displacement model, we verify the assumptions of the continuum-limit theorem and show that centered microscopic fluctuations can change the local energy without changing the effective polarization or the nonlocal energy.

articles.title: High-fidelity k·p representations of first-principles electronic band structures through covariant renormalization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.11861v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The k·p method can be applied directly to first-principles energies and momentum matrix elements, but the resulting models converge slowly with the number of bands and are inexact wherever the underlying Hamiltonian is nonlocal. We show that both limitations can be largely removed by renormalizing the eigenvalue spectra of the Hermitian momentum matrices. These spectra are gauge invariant, and are identical along symmetry-related directions; hence scaling the recurring magnitudes provides a modest set of parameters that preserves degeneracies and crystal symmetry without needing to construct a symmetry-adapted basis. We choose to renormalize the models against reference eigenvalues and band velocities on rays out of a high-symmetry point. For GaP, a 15-band model can reproduce the band structure in the near-gap reference regions within a few meV. For zincblende and wurtzite AlN, similar accuracy requires 30- or 85-band models, which in the case of zincblende is traced to the strong warping in the [110] direction. The scheme readily generalizes to rocksalt PbTe, which includes spin-orbit coupling, and has L-centered valence- and conduction-band extrema. Further, we demonstrate, for GaP, how compact four-band Hamiltonians can be obtained by downfolding within the same renormalization scheme. Moreover, by changing the fitting regime to encompass the entire Brillouin zone, the scheme can be used to generate full-zone models that reproduce the density of states. A practical use of the method is illustrated with a 59-band k·p model for GaP, which can be evaluated on meshes far denser than the reference calculation, that in turn can be used both to resolve fine features in the density of states and to compute the hole conductivity at low temperature.

articles.title: Neural-Network Solutions to Real-Space Charge Density and Generalization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.14906v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Hohenberg-Kohn theorem establishes that, in principle, the ground state (GS) charge density contains all GS information of a many-electron system, such that all GS observables can be expressed as functionals of the GS charge density. Conventional Kohn-Sham density functional theory requires iterative solution of the self-consistent-field equations at substantial computational cost, motivating the development of deep learning surrogates for electronic structure calculations and, in turn, accelerating computer-aided materials design. Here, we propose AIDEN, an Atomic-Interaction Density Equivariant Network for solving real-space charge density. AIDEN separates the element-dependent one-center density from environment-induced density redistribution and represents the latter through complementary atom- and edge-centered tensor correlations. A continuous low-rank Gaussian decoder then reconstructs the density at arbitrary spatial coordinates while reusing atomic encodings independently of the evaluation grid. AIDEN achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on periodic crystal benchmarks while remaining competitive for molecular systems, and further demonstrates zero-shot transferability across several structurally distinct out-of-distribution case studies. Furthermore, AIDEN provides substantially faster inference than both baseline models and full SCF calculations, enabling efficient charge density reconstruction for large-scale electronic structure calculations.

articles.title: Correlative Microstructural Analysis of a Weathered Nantan Meteorite Fragment
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.14187v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The weathering of iron-rich phases within meteorites is a multi-stage process that significantly alters the microstructure and chemical composition based both on the environmental condition at the location of landing and the exposure time since the fall. This work investigates the resulting phases of this process in a correlative and comparative manner using a naturally weathered Nantan meteorite fragment. Techniques including X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS), Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (EDS), and X-ray Fluorescence Spectroscopy (XRF) were used for chemical and compositional determination and X-ray Diffraction (XRD) and Electron Backscatter Diffraction (EBSD) for phase determination and microstructural analysis. The combination of these techniques revealed the meteorite matrix to be predominantly composed of magnetite, with goethite and maghemite present as secondary phases. The meteorite had two pairs of distinct regions, one separated by Ni content and the other by grain size and Cl distribution. The Ni content regions are believed to have formed from a former Widmanstätten pattern, with the high (≥2.6 at%) and low (≤0.9 at%) Ni regions from plessite and kamacite, respectively. The kamacite and taenite within the plessite are suggested to have weathered through distinct mechanisms. The grain size regions were separated by a visible boundary 100-200 μm wide where grains transitioned rapidly from fine to elongated grains and the Cl content changed from low and dispersed to concentrated spots. Lastly, a brecciated phase was found within the sample and was identified as a large cohenite grain which exhibited signs of weathering, including vein-like extensions of the matrix composed of NiO and magnetite, and deposits of iron and nickel carbonates.

articles.title: Magnetic domains stabilized by symmetry-protected zero modes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.15510v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Understanding mechanisms for the breakdown of thermalization in closed quantum systems is a central problem in quantum many-body physics. We demonstrate strong nonergodic behavior in the XX model on coupled chains, where domain-wall initial states retain an inhomogeneous magnetization profile for arbitrarily long times. We find that this effect arises due to zero modes protected by chiral symmetry. Using an analysis based on the Lanczos algorithm, we identify evidence for a localization transition in the thermodynamic limit at a critical coupling between the chains. We further show that antiferromagnetic defects in the initial state and symmetry-breaking perturbations restore slow thermalization, whereas it remains robust for symmetry-conserving perturbations. These results establish that degenerate, symmetry-protected subspaces can give rise to thermodynamically stable nonergodic dynamics in experimentally accessible quantum systems.

articles.title: S-duality, boundary states, and higher-form symmetries on ALE spaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.26224v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study Abelian S-duality of Maxwell theory on A-type asymptotically locally Euclidean (ALE) spaces. Unlike on closed four-manifolds, the Maxwell path integral on an ALE space is not naturally a scalar partition function. Rather, it decomposes into theta-function blocks labeled by flat U(1) holonomy sectors on the asymptotic lens-space boundary. We interpret these blocks as components of the Hilbert-space boundary state prepared by the ALE path integral. With this interpretation, the apparent failure of ordinary modularity is replaced by vector-valued modular covariance under the action of the modular group. We test this picture explicitly for Eguchi-Hanson space by gluing it to its orientation reversal. The resulting closed four-manifold is diffeomorphic to S²× S², and the natural pairing of the two ALE boundary states reproduces the standard Maxwell partition function on S²× S². We then refine the construction by turning on electric and magnetic 1-form symmetry backgrounds. In their presence, the ALE theta blocks are not ordinary functions, but sections of a line bundle over the Cartan torus associated with the AN₋₁ root lattice, reflecting the mixed electric-magnetic 1-form anomaly. We also discuss gauging discrete mathbb Zₖ subgroups of the 1-form symmetries and show that the vector-valued boundary-state structure remains the natural covariant framework after gauging. In this sense, ALE spaces behave as chiral building blocks for four-dimensional Maxwell theory: individual ALE blocks carry sector-resolved boundary data, while gluing pairs these sectors to produce an ordinary closed-manifold partition function, much like the pairing of left- and right-moving conformal blocks in two-dimensional CFT.

articles.title: TorchSpin: Differentiable Electron Paramagnetic Resonance Simulation in PyTorch
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.18924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interpreting electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectra commonly requires repeated forward simulation and optimization of spin Hamiltonian parameters. Established software provides mature simulation and fitting methods, but these calculations are not generally available as differentiable components within machine-learning workflows. We present TorchSpin, an open-source PyTorch framework that ports the organization and numerical conventions of EasySpin into a tensor-based computational environment. Representative calculations spanning continuous-wave EPR, ENDOR, pulse EPR, spin dynamics, trajectory simulation, and magnetometry closely reproduced corresponding EasySpin results. In matched benchmarks, TorchSpin CPU execution was faster than EasySpin for six of nine workloads although performance depended strongly on the calculation. We therefore focused on the capabilities enabled by automatic differentiation in PyTorch. In a Cu(II) powder-spectrum demonstration, feedback propagated through TorchSpin improved the quality of a supervised convolutional neural network (CNN) without using parameter labels during refinement. Models trained from randomly initialized CNNs using only noisy spectra and TorchSpin reconstruction loss achieved median similarities of ≥ 0.99. CNNs trained on TorchSpin-generated libraries also transferred without adaptation to independently generated EasySpin spectra with performance comparable to EasySpin-trained controls. Once trained, the CNN produced initial parameter estimates in approximately 1 ms per spectrum while a batch of 512 was processed in approximately 1.3 ms with GPU acceleration. TorchSpin therefore provides both a tested Python implementation of established EPR calculations and a differentiable physical layer for rapid learned inference, spectral refinement, and parameter-label-free training.

articles.title: Coulomb collision operator
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.18988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Properties of the Coulomb collision operator that have been found useful in plasma kinetic theory and plasma transport theory are gathered and reviewed, with derivations. The use of velocity-space coordinates appropriate to a magnetized (drift-kinetic) plasma is emphasized. Little of the material is new, although the derivations may be more detailed than is customary.

articles.title: A deep energy method formulation for phase-field modelling of ductile fracture
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19094v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work extends the Deep Energy Method to phase-field modelling of ductile fracture in elasto-plastic solids. Its key contribution is an incremental DEM-based formulation that couples history-dependent J2 plasticity and plasticity-dependent fracture toughness with separate energy-optimised displacement and phase-field representations. The formulation combines the second-order Ambrosio-Tortorelli phase-field fracture model with small-strain J2 plasticity and linear isotropic hardening. A volumetric-deviatoric split defines the elastic crack-driving energy, while accumulated equivalent plastic strain governs the degradation of local fracture toughness. Plastic internal variables are updated locally through radial return. The reduced energy is minimised alternately with respect to the displacement and phase fields, represented by a ReZero residual neural network and spatially localised Gaussian radial basis functions with trainable centres, respectively. This split addresses the diffuse phase-field profiles observed in preliminary calculations with a shared global network. Alternating optimisation is combined with transfer learning to reuse trainable parameters and optimiser states across loading increments, while the converged constitutive history is carried forward separately at quadrature points. The numerical results demonstrate close agreement with finite-element reference solutions in predicting force-displacement responses, energy evolution, plastic deformation and crack propagation. The framework captures the main features of ductile fracture, although accuracy becomes more sensitive to loading increments near abrupt fracture events.

articles.title: Physics-based deep learning for non-stationary adaptive multiple suppression
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19147v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Surface-related multiple elimination (SRME) is an indispensable processing step in marine seismic exploration, comprising two main components: multiple prediction and adaptive subtraction. While the multiple prediction is theoretically data-driven and relies on the data itself, the adaptive subtraction step requires a fairly subjective manual control. Our approach introduces a purely data-driven and physics-based deep learning (PDL) algorithm for improving the adaptive multiple subtraction to significantly enhanced performance. There are two main innovations in the proposed deep-learning (DL) multiple subtraction approaches: first, being data-driven and self-supervised, which removes the dependence on inflexible label preparation and model training processes; secondly, being governed by the adaptive matching filtering (AMF) equation to guide the training process. The DL module serves as a strong regression filter analogous to the traditionally known AMF. We segment a moderately sized seismic profile and an initial multiple model into a large number of patches using a patching scheme for self-contained training. The number of patches is controlled by the patch size and the shift size to enable a sufficient number of training samples required by mainstream DL platforms. The patching-based self-training and regression approach, PDL, is inherently a non-stationary matching approach that aims to obtain a globally optimal matching from the initial multiple models to the input full wavefield data through iterative patching-based training. It is also closely connected with the non-stationary regression approach, which was developed almost two decades ago. However, the PDL approach achieves even stronger regression performance due to the backpropagation-based optimization mechanism in DL, and has shown significantly improved multiple subtraction performance over a number of examples.

articles.title: Dual-Resonator Organic Microcavities for Triplet-Triplet Annihilation Upconversion
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Solid-state triplet-triplet annihilation upconversion offers a compelling route to harvest sub-bandgap photons to increase the efficiency of photovoltaics, but low sensitizer doping required to suppress non-radiative aggregation quenching severely restricts light absorption. Here, we present a dual-resonator planar silver microcavity housing a thermally co-evaporated rubrene:palladium phthalocyanine (PdPC) active layer designed to simultaneously enhance triplet-sensitizer absorption and out-couple upconverted emission. By aligning a dispersive cavity mode with the PdPC absorption peak at 32^circ, we achieve a 12-fold enhancement in absorptance at 665 nm. This absorption boost, combined with directional outcoupling through a second cavity mode, outweighs cavity-induced reabsorption losses to yield a 22-fold peak and 4.5-fold integrated enhancement in detected upconversion emission. Overall, this work highlights the potential of microcavity integration to substantially enhance solid-state upconversion performance across low-intensity optoelectronic applications.

articles.title: Topologically Protected Surface Acoustic Wave Edge States in Phononic Integrated Circuits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19259v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phononic integrated circuits enable the development of compact systems to manipulate radio frequency signals through interconnected networks of acoustic waveguides. Introducing topologically protected robustness in these circuits to counter fabrication imperfections and local perturbations, remains a challenge. This work presents a validated modeling framework for topologically protected edge states using surface acoustic waves in etch-defined waveguides consisting of scandium aluminum nitride on silicon carbide, directly comparing analytical, full-wave numerical simulation, and laser Doppler vibrometer measured experimental approaches and their agreement. This work represents the first experimental demonstration of topological edge states on a ScAlN on SiC platform, validated through direct quantitative comparison with analytical and numerical analyses, with future implications for topological protection in phononic and optomechanical integrated circuit platforms.

articles.title: Strong field confinement in air and enhanced optical Kerr nonlinearity of high-index star-shaped pore membrane metasurfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19412v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The optical Kerr effect in high-refractive-index membrane metasurfaces patterned with a square lattice of five-pointed star-shaped pores is investigated numerically using gallium phosphide as a model material. The star geometry supports resonances with pronounced electromagnetic energy confinement, including an anapole state. The sharp tips of the star-shaped pores concentrate the electric energy density in air, exceeding that of Mie voids by a factor of seven. The effective second-order refractive index is enhanced by up to three orders of magnitude relative to bulk GaP, with the largest values obtained near the anapole resonances. The nonlinear response remains stable under polarization rotation and random misalignment of the nanoholes, indicating tolerance to fabrication imperfections. These results establish star-shaped pore lattices in freestanding membranes as a promising platform for nonlinear optics exploiting strong field confinement.

articles.title: GeONet: Geometry-Encoded Operator Network for Predicting Flow in Heterogeneous Porous Media
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rapid prediction of pressure-driven flow in microfluidic porous media is important for experimental design, tracer-test interpretation, and digital-twin development for subsurface energy and critical mineral applications. High-fidelity simulations resolve geometry-controlled flow but are computationally expensive across large geometry ensembles. Here, we introduce GeONet, a Geometry-Encoded Operator Network that predicts steady-state pressure fields by jointly representing material properties, spatial coordinates, and solid--void geometry. GeONet extends the Branch--Trunk architecture with a dedicated Leaf Network encoding the binary domain mask through multiscale features. The Branch Network represents porosity and permeability, the Trunk Network combines coordinates with local geometric descriptors and random Fourier features, and a gated DeepMixer integrates these representations to predict pressure. GeONet was trained and evaluated using 5,000 PFLOTRAN simulations of heterogeneous Reduced Complexity Platform domains, comprising nearly 30 TB of data. Comparisons with pore-scale Stokes solutions across three geometries yielded Pearson correlations of 0.987--0.991 and R² values of 0.974--0.982, supporting PFLOTRAN as reference data. Under matched partitions and two-stage hyperparameter optimization, GeONet substantially outperformed a boundary-condition-aware DeepONet baseline. Across three held-out domains, GeONet achieved NRMSE of 0.0381--0.0500, MAPE of 1.76--2.59%, and R² of 0.9673--0.9822, versus 0.1483--0.2040, 7.81--10.45%, and 0.5658--0.7126 for DeepONet, respectively. On three additional unseen geometries, GeONet achieved NRMSE of 0.0448--0.0676 and R² of 0.9511--0.9770. These results demonstrate improved accuracy, pressure-range preservation, and cross-geometry generalization through explicit geometry encoding.

articles.title: A compact six-beam 3D magneto-optical trap based on multifunctional metasurface chips
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19504v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magneto-optical traps (MOTs), indispensable to cold-atom-based quantum computing and quantum precision measurement, are increasingly desired in compact and stable form. Particularly, the six-beam 3D-MOT, distinguished by symmetric geometry and superior trapping performance, finds particularly broad applications. Conventional implementations, however, rely on complex and bulky free-space optics, hindering miniaturization, practical assembly, and long-term stability. Here, we demonstrate a compact six-beam 3D-MOT system that employs two multifunctional optical metasurface chips to implement the optical-field functionalities required for cooling and trapping atoms. By combining two metasurface chips and a vacuum cell, a photonic-integrated cell module (PICM) is implemented as the core assembly and the volume is only" 73*73*107 mm³" . In success, 1.3 * 10³ Rb atoms are trapped and cooled to the temperature of ~183 μK. It should be noticed that the laser beam is guided to the metasurface through optical fiber, thus such fully fiber-coupled architecture enables straightforward and stable operations. We believe that this work would pave a practical route toward compact and portable 3D-MOT.

articles.title: Preservation of photon statistics upon selective molecular modulation in hollow-core fibers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Preserving the underlying statistical properties of light during frequency transduction is essential for interfacing spectrally disparate quantum systems. To do this successfully, the process needs to be highly efficient, broadband and noiseless. Despite significant progress in this field, satisfying all these conditions remains challenging. Recently, molecular modulation-based transduction in hollow-core fibers has emerged as a promising approach, where biphoton correlations were proven to be preserved during frequency up-conversion. However, beyond this previous demonstration of correlation-maintaining conversion, whether molecular modulation can preserve more general statistical properties of light remains experimentally unexplored. Here, we demonstrate the conservation of photon-number statistics during selective frequency transduction by Raman molecular modulation in a hydrogen-filled hollow-core fiber. As a proof of concept, weak 585-nm signals are selectively converted to 773 nm in the near-infrared and to 471 nm in the blue spectral region with near-unity efficiencies. Phase matching between the generated coherence waves and the transitions of interest is achieved through the effective dispersion of the system, enabling independent selection of the frequency up- and down-conversion processes. The preservation of the photon-number statistics of the shifted signals, along with the large frequency shifts, broad tunability and compatibility with quantum-optical fields, provides a versatile fiber-based platform for quantum frequency transduction. In particular, the demonstrated interfacing between visible and near-infrared wavelengths using low pump energies and low gas pressures offers a route towards connecting spectrally distinct quantum systems, including quantum emitters, sensors and atomic quantum memories, within hybrid quantum networks.

articles.title: Inferring Transition-Dipoles from Two-Dimensional Infrared Spectroscopy with Deep Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19972v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two-dimensional infrared (2D IR) spectroscopy is a powerful nonlinear technique for probing vibrational couplings, anharmonicities, coherence, and molecular dynamics. Among the microscopic parameters encoded in 2D IR spectra, transition dipoles are fundamental quantities that characterize molecular structure and govern light-matter interactions. However, reconstructing these quantities from spectroscopic data remains a challenging inverse problem. Here, we introduce a physics-informed convolutional neural network (CNN), Spec2DipoleNet, trained on 2D IR spectra generated via the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian (NHH) method. This multi-task CNN reconstructs the transition dipole matrices under physically-motivated masking constraints. On the validation set, the model achieves a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.085, an R² of 0.97, and a normalized cross-correlation of 0.98. It reliably recovers matrix elements associated with allowed transitions, while larger deviations are observed for nominally forbidden transitions. Our results suggest that transition dipole operators can be quantitatively inferred from 2D IR spectra, highlighting the potential of physics-informed deep learning for extracting microscopic quantum parameters from multidimensional spectroscopic data.

articles.title: A low-cost compact muon detector for millikelvin operation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20132v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ionizing radiation produces correlated errors in superconducting qubits, posing some challenges to quantum error correction. In addition, it causes background events in other superconducting cryogenic devices, such as kinetic inductance detectors and superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors. Cosmic muons are a component of this background that can only be partly shielded against at ground level, but can be tagged by an independent detector inside the cryostat, so that the affected data can be vetoed, or the muon tags incorporated into error correction. We present a low-cost, compact muon detector consisting of two plastic scintillator modules, each read out by a silicon photomultiplier (SiPM), operated in coincidence. We characterize the SiPMs from room temperature down to 10 mK, including the breakdown and upper-limit voltages that define the operating bias range. Operated as a muon counter, the detector measures a coincidence rate that, as expected, is independent of temperature within uncertainties and agrees with analytical and Monte Carlo predictions. Below approximately 8 K, each muon event produces two pulses, one narrow and one broad, an effect that, to our knowledge, has not been reported before. Coincidences with an independent muon detector outside the cryostat confirm that muons are still counted reliably in this regime. By studying the appearance of double pulses as a function of temperature and magnetic field up to 4.5 T, we find a behavior consistent with the phase diagram of a type-II superconductor. This links the double pulses to a superconducting material in the SiPM, likely an adhesion layer or diffusion barrier introduced during manufacturing. The mechanism by which the superconducting state produces the second pulse is not yet understood.

articles.title: Fine-structure Raman interferometry with metastable barium for magnetically resilient inertial sensing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20168v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Atom-interferometric quantum inertial sensors are promising candidates for inertial navigation systems owing to their high sensitivity and intrinsically low drift. However, their application to next-generation inertial navigation, targeting a drift below 100 m/month, requires exceptionally stringent inertial-sensor bias stability. In conventional Raman atom interferometers based on ground-state hyperfine transitions, suppressing inertial-sensor biases arising from quadratic Zeeman shifts requires highly optimized magnetic shielding. In this work, we propose a Raman atom interferometer based on fine-structure transitions between metastable states of barium, which exhibit a quadratic Zeeman sensitivity approximately three orders of magnitude lower than that of conventional alkali-atom Raman transitions. We show that the proposed scheme increases the allowable spatial gradient of the magnetic-field magnitude by a factor of several tens, thereby relaxing the magnetic-field-control requirements from highly optimized shielding and compensation systems to standard magnetic-field-control techniques. Furthermore, we experimentally demonstrate Mach--Zehnder interference between metastable fine-structure states of barium, validating a key building block of the proposed inertial-sensing scheme.

articles.title: Learning to reconstruct Germano Differential Filtered Fields with Convolutional Neural Networks for Large Eddy Simulation of Plasma Turbulence
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20204v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a novel method which combines the invertibility of the differential filter of Germano, with convolutional networks to accelerate plasma turbulence simulations. Rather than learning the mapping from coarse-grid LES fields to fine-grid DNS, the proposed method learns the mapping from coarse LES fields to the differential-filtered DNS fields. We then use the inverse of Germano's filter to reconstruct the fine-scale details and hence calculate exactly the nonlinear terms in the governing equations and subgrid-scale terms in the LES equations. The method is tested on the 2D Hasegawa-Wakatani (HW) and modified Hasegawa-Wakatani (mHW) plasma turbulence models at 256² and 512² DNS resolutions using 2, 4 and 8 times smaller LES grids in each direction. We compare the model with DNS results on energy, enstrophy, spectra, probability distributions, poloidal and radial fluxes and computational cost. Validation extends to 1000 simulation time units for HW and 100 for mHW, whose faster dynamics lead toward laminarization. For the 256² cases, the finer LES meshes preserve several integral and spectral features, whereas the coarsest mesh yields unphysical behavior. In contrast, for the 512² cases, even the coarsest LES mesh preserves the turbulent character of the flow and maintains acceptable statistics for both the HW and mHW models. Moreover, we show how our methodology is superior to traditional algebraic numerical LES models, which traditionally fail to capture important design features. Finally, benchmarks show an MPI task-time reductions of 4.82--49.45, with a maximum wall-clock speedup of 1.55× when compared to full CPU socket.

articles.title: Post-Optimization Subspace Corrections to Quantum Ansätze
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19109v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Circuit depth and measurement count are the main limitations for chemical applications of the leading variational quantum algorithms on quantum computers. We show that both resource requirements can be reduced by augmenting adaptive variational quantum algorithms with post-optimization corrective techniques. We focus on two such techniques---Hamiltonian-moment Krylov subspace diagonalization and the identity-augmented quantum self-consistent equation of motion (q-sc-EOM)---applied to optimized ADAPT-VQE states without further ansatz growth or nonlinear optimization. Across molecular systems studied with up to 20 qubits, first-order Krylov correction reduces the optimized iterations (and the corresponding number of adaptive layers) needed to reach the 1.6~mEₕ threshold by up to approximately sixfold, with a general trend toward larger reductions at higher determinant Rényi entropy. We also find measurement-cost reductions of up to approximately fortyfold using a suitable resource-cost model. Identity-augmented q-sc-EOM improves molecular potential-energy curves obtained from truncated ADAPT-VQE ansätze with limited expressivity and recovers accuracy from states produced by sampled operator ranking without additional gradient-based operator selection, providing an advantage when small pool gradients make selection measurement intensive. Together, these post-optimization corrections offer routes to improve energy accuracy and reduce adaptive circuit growth in quantum algorithms as quantum hardware advances.

articles.title: Structure-aware Bayesian full waveform inversion via diffusion-regularized Stein variational gradient descent
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19187v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Full waveform inversion (FWI) is a powerful tool for high-resolution subsurface model reconstruction, but it remains highly nonlinear and ill-posed, especially when the initial model is inaccurate or the acquired data are noisy and incomplete. Annealed Stein variational gradient descent (ASVGD) provides a particle-based Bayesian framework for FWI by approximating the posterior distribution with an ensemble of velocity models, thereby enabling uncertainty quantification beyond a single deterministic solution. However, conventional ASVGD-FWI commonly relies on simple handcrafted priors, such as Gaussian or smoothing assumptions, which are often insufficient to represent complex geological structures. To address this limitation, we introduce a learned diffusion model (DM) as an implicit regularization mechanism within the ASVGD-FWI framework. Instead of explicitly evaluating the diffusion prior density, the trained diffusion model acts as a learned geological projection operator that guides updated particles toward the distribution of plausible velocity models. In this way, the proposed method combines data consistency from FWI, posterior diversity from ASVGD, and structural realism from the diffusion prior. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the diffusion-regularized ASVGD-FWI produces more geologically consistent mean models, suppresses nonphysical artifacts, and yields uncertainty estimates that are more concentrated around structurally complex and poorly constrained regions. These results suggest that learned diffusion priors can effectively enhance Bayesian FWI by improving both inversion stability and the interpretability of posterior uncertainty.

articles.title: Magnetic Reconnection Governs the Entire Lifecycle of Solar Eruptive Magnetic Flux Rope
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19348v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While magnetic flux ropes (MFRs) are widely accepted to exist prior to many solar eruptions, the physical mechanism responsible for triggering and subsequently driving their eruptions remains debated. Classical models commonly attribute eruption onset to ideal magnetohydrodynamic instabilities, particularly the torus instability, while magnetic reconnection is often regarded as a secondary process. Using high-resolution three-dimensional MHD simulations, we investigate the eruption of an MFR that forms self-consistently through flux cancellation driven by converging motions and photospheric diffusion following an initial shearing phase. The pre-eruption MFR rises quasi-statically and reaches a height where the decay index exceeds the classical torus instability threshold, yet the system continues to evolve quasi-statically without eruption. Instead, eruption begins only when the current sheet beneath the MFR becomes sufficiently thin for magnetic reconnection to set in. Increasing numerical resolution systematically delays the eruption onset, whereas the decay index at eruption onset remains nearly unchanged, demonstrating that the onset is governed by reconnection rather than torus instability. During the eruption, magnetic reconnection continuously converts surrounding sheared arcades into newly reconnected twisted flux that merges with the pre-eruption MFR and continuously to build the erupting MFR. A component-resolved analysis of the Lorentz force work further shows that the newly reconnection flux contributes predominantly to the main acceleration phase. These results demonstrate that magnetic reconnection plays a central role throughout the entire lifecycle of the eruptive MFR: it builds the MFR, directly triggers its eruption, and provides the dominant driving of the eruption.

articles.title: MoEDAL-MAPP: the first dedicated search experiment at the LHC
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19959v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This special issue brings together a collection of original research articles and review papers addressing topics directly related to the MoEDAL-MAPP experiment at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). The experiment is designed to search for (meta-)stable, anomalously ionising particles predicted by theoretical extensions of the Standard Model. Several contributions explore the theoretical and phenomenological aspects of models of particular relevance to the experiment, including scenarios involving magnetic monopoles, highly electrically charged particles, and millicharged particles. Other contributions focus on experimental developments, highlighting novel detection techniques and technological advances aimed at identifying these unconventional signatures and probing new phenomena beyond the Standard Model.

articles.title: Stationary Resistive MHD Solutions Near an Isolated Three-Dimensional Magnetic Null
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20015v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Magnetic null points define the magnetic field topology in stellar coronae, planetary magnetospheres, and astrospheres, and are commonly associated with magnetic reconnection. We investigate the local structure of stationary three-dimensional (3D) resistive, incompressible magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) flows in the vicinity of an isolated magnetic null and an isolated velocity stagnation point, assuming that the two nulls are colocated. The governing MHD equations are solved self-consistently using a first-order local expansion of the magnetic and velocity fields about the null. For any given magnetic-null configuration, the equations admit a two-parameter family of stationary solutions, comprising multiple solution branches with distinct velocity topologies. Along these families, the velocity-null polarity can change at bifurcation points where the flow becomes effectively 2.5D. A single magnetic null can therefore support positive-radial, negative-radial, and spiral stagnation flows, with qualitatively different inflow, outflow, and rotational properties. The associated pressure and resistivity distributions are likewise determined self-consistently and vary across the solution family, demonstrating that they are coupled to the flow topology rather than prescribed independently. The generic solutions do not require the velocity and magnetic separatrices to coincide, allowing plasma to cross the magnetic fan separatrix and providing a local reconnective flow. These results demonstrate that, in the presence of nonuniform resistivity, the magnetic topology alone does not uniquely determine the associated stationary flow, pressure, or resistivity structure around a 3D magnetic null, revealing the nonlinear feedback between all macroscopic variables and resistivity. The constant-resistivity field-aligned and spiral field-crossing solutions identified previously are recovered as special cases.

articles.title: Tracking a solar energetic eruption and associated energetic particles from Sun to spacecraft
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20026v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Context. Solar energetic particles (SEPs) in the heliosphere are produced by flaring processes on the Sun or shocks driven by coronal mass ejections (CMEs). Electrons, in particular, are regularly detected remotely as electromagnetic radiation (X-rays or radio emission), which they generate through various processes, as well as in situ by spacecraft monitoring the Sun and the heliosphere. Aims. We aim to combine remote-sensing and in situ observations of an energetic solar eruption to link energetic processes in the solar corona to energetic particles observed in situ in the heliosphere. This will be done using the tools developed in the Horizon Europe SOLER project. Methods. Here, we investigate a solar energetic eruption at the Sun together with its associated signatures of accelerated electrons observed at radio and X-ray wavelengths and combine these remote observations to in situ particles observed by spacecraft on 10 March 2024. These observations are combined with a magneto-hydrodynamic (MHD) model of the solar corona in order to make the remote to in situ connections. Results. We observe a high-energy SEP event at multiple spacecraft (>25 MeV protons and 1 MeV electrons), despite the event being associated with a slow white-light CME. Remote observations of the Sun show that the event was associated with a fast large scale coronal wave (1400 km/s) and also multiple regions where electrons are accelerated around this large scale wave observed as type II radio bursts. In addition, we observe a strong coronal dimming away from the main flaring region, providing evidence of field lines getting opened to interplanetary space, dislocated from the flare site.

articles.title: Flares and flux ropes: an entangled story
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20056v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Solar flares serve as standard candles for all magnetic-reconnection-based energy releases, and their consequences into the heliosphere can be modeled from first principles. This review presents the latest developments in modeling solar flares and their associated flux rope expulsions with state-of-the-art multidimensional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) descriptions. Observationally established ingredients beyond a single-fluid, thermal plasma evolution have been incorporated to varying degrees, and we highlight self-consistent efforts realized in "standard flare" setups.

articles.title: Demonstration of a mobile ion-trap quantum device
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20487v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Trapped-ion devices are being investigated for transportable applications, including the transfer of exotic charged particles between laboratories and the development of portable quantum technologies. To date, ion transport has been demonstrated only in magnetic (Penning) traps, whereas radiofrequency (Paul) traps are the predominant platform in quantum science. Here, we report the first transport of a few thousand ions confined in a linear Paul trap over distances of several kilometers, with transport durations of 15 and 45 min. These results establish a foundation for mobile trapped-ion quantum devices capable of operating while in motion and may enable the transport of exotic ions in Paul traps between experimental facilities.

articles.title: Revealing the Spatial Distribution of Dust and Plasma Solitary Waves in Jupiter's Innermost Magnetosphere Using Juno Waves Observations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20541v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Jupiter's faint ring system contains micron- and submicron-sized dust whose dynamics are influenced by the planet's rapidly rotating magnetic field. Optical observations have established the morphology of the main ring and halo, but tenuous dust close to Jupiter remains difficult to characterize. We analyze nearly a decade of in-situ Juno Waves electric-field measurements using a two-stage convolutional neural network to identify and classify dust impacts, solitary waves, and other plasma waves. These in-situ dust-impact detections reveal a radially evolving structure extending well inside the traditionally observed halo. In the innermost region, dust is concentrated in a compact, equatorially symmetric layer, indicating that the optical inner boundary does not mark the end of the dust population. Farther outward, the layer expands vertically into a broad halo before contracting toward the main ring, directly revealing the toroidal morphology of the Jovian halo. Dust number density is enhanced within the halo and near the main-ring--halo transition. The vertical distribution also develops hemispheric asymmetries that vary with radial distance, consistent with an influence of Jupiter's magnetic geometry on charged-dust dynamics. In contrast, solitary waves occur predominantly at high latitudes, and their mapped magnetic footprints show a strong spatial correspondence with Jovian auroral structures, particularly the main auroral oval. Together, these in-situ measurements extend the remote-sensing picture of Jupiter's rings and reveal previously unresolved dust and plasma structures in its innermost magnetosphere.

articles.title: Structured-Light Magnetometry in a Coherently Controlled Atomic Medium
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.25781v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A structured-light-based approach to magneto-optical rotation (MOR) magnetometry is proposed, in which magnetically induced polarization rotation is converted into a directly observable spatial displacement. A radially polarized Laguerre--Gaussian beam propagating through cold ⁸⁷Rb atoms in the presence of a longitudinal magnetic field experiences circular birefringence, which induces a relative phase shift between the σ₊ and σ₋ polarization components. This phase shift manifests itself as the angular rotation of a petal-shaped interference pattern, enabling the MOR angle to be determined directly from the spatial intensity distribution. Unlike conventional MOR detection techniques based on balanced polarimetry or Stokes-parameter reconstruction, the proposed method requires only a fixed-axis polarization projection and avoids computationally intensive polarization analysis. By translating polarization rotation into a topology-dependent spatial observable, the scheme enables direct and spatially resolved magnetic-field measurements. Furthermore, the use of electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) allows low-loss operation while preserving high sensitivity. These characteristics make the proposed technique a promising platform for optical magnetometry and structured-light-based quantum sensing.

articles.title: Interfacial waves from pressure forcing: role of the transients
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.12254v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A localised overpressure translating at a uniform speed greater than a critical value acts at the interface between two deep fluid layers with different densities. We analyse the resulting wave patterns using an initial-value problem formulation within the linearised, inviscid, potential flow framework. The steady-state interface exhibits short capillary waves ahead of the forcing and long gravity waves behind it, arising from an asymmetric cancellation of Fourier components in the far field. The time-dependent part of the solution, decaying algebraically with time, plays a crucial role in this mechanism. This contrasts with classical steady approaches, which require additional conditions to select a unique solution. We extend this approach to a two-fluid interface and validate the predictions against nonlinear simulations.

articles.title: Resonant photoionization dynamics during optical trapping of lithium atoms
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.09549v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Photoionization induced by trapping and auxiliary laser fields is an inherent feature of many laser-cooling and optical trapping experiments, yet its microscopic dynamics are rarely investigated directly. In this work, we employ a reaction microscope implementing an event-by-event photoionization time retrieval technique to extend momentum-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy to continuous-wave laser--atom interactions. We investigate low-intensity multicolor photoionization of laser-cooled lithium atoms confined in an all-optical trap. Complete three-dimensional electron momentum distributions and kinetic-energy spectra recorded for different laser wavelengths and polarization configurations identify resonant excitation of the 5p and 5f states and reveal an additional ionization channel following spontaneous decay from the 5f to the 4d state. A pronounced polarization dependence of the photoionization yield is explained by magnetic-sublevel selection rules and the coherent interference of different virtual excitation pathways. These results demonstrate that reaction microscopy combined with event-by-event time reconstruction provides a powerful approach for investigating microscopic electronic dynamics in laser-cooled atomic systems and offers new insight into photoionization processes occurring during optical trapping.

articles.title: A Magnetothermodynamic Theory of Energy Transport In Collisionless Plasmas
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.01471v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Presented here is an exploratory conceptual framework with the aim of describing electromagnetic and thermal energy transport and transfer in collisionless plasmas in a coherent way, starting from an arrow-of-time perspective. That is, arguments about the transport of energy are fundamentally based on the idea that systems tend to fill the phase space available to them. First, we describe electric fields, magnetic fields, and plasma particles as interacting subsystems that are thermodynamically linked in specific ways. Second, we discuss the importance of the stochastic electric field in the transport of plasma particles down energy density gradients until the energy flux contributions from so-called electrothermodynamic (ETD) interactions become sufficiently uniform. Third, the logic of ETD transport is extended to a magnetized system invoking 2 types of magnetothermodyamic (MTD) transport: 1) transport of electromagnetic energy through stochastic Poynting flux and 2) plasma energy transport through stochastic drift energy fluxes associated with local ExB drift motion. The magnitudes of the ETD and MTD mechanisms are tied to local characteristic scales of the electric field fluctuations and critical scales are derived beyond which ETD mechanisms dominate MTD mechanisms. Finally, we discuss the interplay between electrothermodynamic and magnetothermodynamic equilibria (ETE and MTE), dynamics in the small critical scale (MTD) limit, and the potential relevance of this type of description to the problem of reconnection onset and scale coupling.

articles.title: Assessing the effect of error field penetration during plasma current ramp-up in the DIII-D tokamak
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.04546v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work provides evidence that established error field penetration threshold scalings remain applicable during plasma current ramp-up. In dedicated DIII-D experiments with imposed n=1 perturbations during extended Iₚ ramps, an apparent empirical threshold is found between 2 and 3~kA of applied 3D coil current, above which MHD modes are seeded. The imposed perturbation couples to the rational surfaces present during the ramp, seeding near the q=4 surface and penetrating as an m/n=3/1 mode by the end of the perturbation phase. To interpret these observations, multi-machine penetration threshold scalings are combined with equilibrium-based overlap metrics from the GPEC code, including the in-situ error fields of the device. This modeling reproduces the observed onset in the amplitude scan and classifies mode seeding across a database of 12 ramp-up discharges spanning a range of plasma currents and densities. Across this database, the seeding appears to be controlled primarily by the applied 3D coil current rather than by the plasma current or its ramp rate. Accounting for the in-situ error fields is found to be important for reliable prediction. These results are consistent with the robustness of scaling-based penetration metrics when coupled to detailed 3D field modeling under transient ramp-up conditions, and suggest the importance of accounting for in-situ error fields when assessing additional externally induced perturbations. This work is motivated by future tokamaks in which transient, non-axisymmetric error fields can arise during startup, for example from runaway electron mitigation coils.

articles.title: Generalized Noether theorem in the realm of Hamiltonian point dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:1206.4449v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Noether's theorem in the realm of point dynamics establishes the correlation of a constant of motion of a Hamilton-Lagrange system with a particular symmetry transformation of its action functional. Although usually derived in the Lagrangian formalism, the Hamiltonian formalism provides a natural context for this correlation. Canonical transformations preserve the canonical form of the action up to a boundary term. Within the class considered here, a symmetry additionally preserves the functional form of the specified extended Hamiltonian. Every smooth phase-space first integral admits locally a corresponding canonical Noether symmetry when momentum-dependent transformations and boundary terms are allowed. In order to represent symmetry mappings that include a transformation of time, we use the extended Hamiltonian formalism. This formalism enables us to define generating functions of canonical transformations that also map time and energy in addition to the conventional mappings of canonical space and momentum variables. The physical energy hypersurface and the choice of the evolution parameter are distinguished from identities on the full extended phase space. As an example, a manifest representation of the symmetry transformation associated with the Runge-Lenz invariant of the Kepler system is derived. A suitable choice of evolution parameter makes its time-shifting representative a symmetry of the specified extended action.

articles.title: Searching for Ultra-Light Axions with Twisted Cavity Resonators of Anyon Rotational Symmetry with Bulk Modes of Non-Zero Helicity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2208.01640v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Möbius-ring resonators stem from a well-studied geometrical structure with a one-sided topology, the Möbius strip, and have been shown to exhibit fermion rotational symmetry with respect to an untwisted ring resonator, which exhibits boson rotational symmetry [1]. Here, we present twisted hollow resonators with equilateral triangular cross-sections, leading to cavities with anyon rotational symmetry. Unlike conventional cavity resonators, these structures permit bulk resonant modes with a non-zero complex electromagnetic overlap mathcal Cₚ=int_VEₚcdotBₚ^*,dτ. The real and imaginary parts of this overlap couple to different observable quadratures. Although the negative-frequency component of a real axion field is immaterial for haloscopes employing a static DC magnetic field, it must be retained for a pumped resonator because the complex forms of Maxwell's equations differ for positive and negative frequencies and produce distinct upper and lower mixing branches. Retaining both branches shows that the real overlap produces amplitude-modulated sidebands, whereas the imaginary helicity of the modes studied here produces phase-modulated sidebands through the axion-photon chiral anomaly. A sensitive ultra-light dark-matter experiment may therefore be realised with an ultra-stable oscillator and a phase-sensitive readout. The sensitivity curves calculated here require the assumed noise floor to be interpreted as phase-modulation noise rather than amplitude-modulation noise, and consequently require sufficiently low residual oscillator phase noise at the axion Fourier frequency. The scheme removes the usual requirement for an external magnetic field and permits superconducting resonators with reduced surface loss and enhanced axion sensitivity.

articles.title: Tracking large chemical reaction networks and rare events by neural networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2512.10309v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Chemical reaction networks are widely used to model stochastic dynamics in biophysical processes. Their exact probabilistic description via the chemical master equation becomes intractable for high-dimensional systems due to the exponential growth of the state space. This difficulty is further exacerbated when metastable transitions and rare events dominate the dynamics. Here, we present an advanced neural-network approach that effectively tackles large reaction networks and rare-event dynamics within a unified framework. Building on autoregressive representations of the full joint probability distribution, we achieve efficient training through second-order optimization methods, including natural gradient descent and the time-dependent variational principle. We leverage enhanced-sampling strategies that enable accurate resolution of low-probability regions governing rare transitions. We demonstrate the method on a multistable genetic toggle switch and a mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) cascade consisting of 16 species and 35 reactions with dense coupling. We further quantify rare events in spatially extended Schlögl models in both one- and two-dimensional lattices, reaching system sizes with extremely large state spaces up to 3×10¹⁵. These results highlight the potential of neural modeling as a flexible and scalable framework for studying high-dimensional chemical reaction networks and rare events.

articles.title: Heterogeneous entanglement between a trapped ion and a solid-state quantum memory
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.05836v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Hybrid quantum networks offer a promising architecture for scalable quantum information processing and a future quantum internet, as they can combine the complementary strengths of disparate physical platforms. While single-atom systems provide deterministic quantum logic gates, atomic ensembles enable large-capacity quantum storage. However, generating entanglement between such heterogeneous systems has remained an open challenge, primarily due to fundamental spectral mismatches and system complexity. Here, we demonstrate a hybrid quantum network that entangles a single trapped mathrm¹⁷¹Yb⁺ ion and a quantum memory based on rm ¹⁵³Eu³⁺colon!Y₂SiO₅ crystal over a 75-m separation. Using polarization-maintaining quantum frequency conversion, we map spin-photon entanglement onto a hybrid entanglement between a single spin qubit and a collective excitation of the quantum memory. The resulting entangled state achieves a fidelity of (89.21 ± 2.23)% and violates the CHSH-Bell inequality by 6 standard deviations (S = 2.328 ± 0.055), confirming nonlocality between two heterogeneous nodes. This work establishes entanglement between a quantum processing module with a multiplexed quantum memory node, representing a key step toward a scalable, multifunctional quantum internet.

articles.title: Njord: A Probabilistic Graph Neural Network for Ensemble Ocean Forecasting
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.15470v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Ocean dynamics are inherently chaotic, yet existing machine learning ocean models produce only deterministic forecasts. We introduce Njord, a probabilistic data-driven model for ocean forecasting, applicable to both global and regional domains. Njord combines a deep latent variable framework with a graph neural network architecture, enabling sampling each forecast step in a single forward pass. We apply Njord globally at 0.25deg resolution and regionally to the Baltic Sea at 2 km resolution. To scale to these large ocean grids we introduce K-means cluster meshes that adapt to irregular sea surface geometry. Experiments demonstrate strong performance on both domains compared to deterministic machine learning baselines, while also providing uncertainty estimates from the sampled ensemble forecasts. On the global OceanBench benchmark, Njord achieves the lowest errors on average across upper-ocean variables when evaluated against real-world observations, with the largest improvements in surface temperature prediction.

articles.title: Structured Multi-Level-Set Inversion for 3-D Electromagnetic Inverse Scattering
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.08594v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Many dielectric targets encountered in 3-D electromagnetic inverse scattering exhibit piecewise-homogeneous material distributions, which provide useful structural information for inversion. To exploit this property, this paper proposes a structured multi-level-set inversion (SMLSI) method within a physics-driven neural network (PDNN) framework. Instead of directly parameterizing the contrast distribution, SMLSI represents it in terms of object support and material distribution. Multiple level-sets are mapped to soft-support functions and combined through a soft-union operation to construct the object support. The normalized contributions of these soft-support functions, together with trainable complex relative permittivities, determine the material distribution within the support. The level-set residuals are parameterized by a coordinate-based neural network, and the trainable parameters are optimized from scattered field data. Structure-aware regularization terms are introduced to promote binary object support and spatially coherent material regions while reducing material mixing and redundant activation of level-set supports. Adaptive regularization weighting is further employed to reduce the dependence on manual parameter tuning. Numerical experiments demonstrate that SMLSI improves reconstruction accuracy over direct contrast parameterization and enables the recovery of irregular 3-D geometries, closely spaced objects, and multiple material regions. Compared with CSI and L₂/₃-FBE-WCIE, SMLSI achieves more accurate reconstructions on representative synthetic targets. Experimental validation using 3-D Fresnel data further demonstrates its applicability to measured scattering data.

articles.title: Spectral Theory of an Exactly Solvable Quantum-Optical Oscillator
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.18421v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study a one-dimensional single-excitation model of a scalar photon field coupled to a continuum of two-level atoms with quadratic density. The resulting matrix Hamiltonian has an unbounded spatially varying coupling and is not semibounded. We prove that it is essentially self-adjoint and determine its spectrum explicitly. The continuous spectrum is the half-line (-infty,Ω], where Ω is the atomic resonance frequency, while the spectrum above Ω consists of a strictly increasing sequence of simple eigenvalues. These eigenvalues are characterized by the interlaced zeros of the Airy function and its derivative and satisfy beginalign* ωₙ = left(frac3π g n4right)¹/² + fracΩ4 + O(n⁻¹/²). endalign* The analysis is based on a nonlinear spectral reduction that yields a confining massless relativistic oscillator above Ω and an inverted oscillator below Ω.

articles.title: Theoretical and Practical Advances in Hierarchical Bayesian Deep Learning Methodology
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19074v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reliable uncertainty quantification remains an important challenge in AI. Hierarchical Bayesian methods provide a principled framework for this by representing unknown quantities through posterior distributions. Joint inference of neural-network parameters and prior hyperparameters is challenging for conventional Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods due to strong dependencies. In this work, we introduce the multilevel particle marginal Metropolis-Hastings (MLPMMH) method, which combines pseudo-marginal inference for the hyperparameters with coupled sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) across hierarchy of network-width truncations for conditional parameter inference. The hierarchy is induced by a trace-class neural network (TNN) prior with width-dependent decay, motivated empirically by the compressible structure observed in trained neural-network parameters. Under standard multilevel coupling assumptions, we establish that MLPMMH achieves mean-square error (MSE) O(ε²) at expected computational cost O(ε⁻²), and verify the predicted rate on a Bayesian regression problem. To address larger-scale applications, we further introduce S-MLPMMH, a practical approximation that replaces the exact sampling components with a PCA-based hierarchy and scalable Bayesian Monte Carlo. Experiments on MNIST demonstrate competitive predictive performance and uncertainty quantification while exploiting the parallel structure of the approximation. Software has been made publicly available at https://github.com/submission-code-anon/mlpmmh-anon.

articles.title: Beyond Time Induction: Structured Conditional Neural Solvers for Parametric Stochastic-Volatility Pricing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19254v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks provide a flexible framework for learning parametric PDE solution families without labeled data, yet preserving accurate derivatives across heterogeneous regimes remains challenging. Structured neural solvers offer compact representations, but restrictive conditional parameterizations can limit adaptation across the solution family. We introduce BeTINN, a structured conditional architecture extending time-induced modulation through multi-directional time-parameter conditioning and a joint residual pathway. We evaluate BeTINN on the Heston stochastic-volatility PDE, a demanding parametric problem with mixed derivatives and economically relevant first- and second-order sensitivities. BeTINN improves joint accuracy across normalized option value and key sensitivity metrics relative to our baselines. Controlled ablations characterize the roles of its architectural components. We further find that validation physics loss is informative but does not fully determine differential fidelity, and that accurate solution values can coexist with localized derivative errors. These results support structured conditional adaptation and motivate derivative-aware evaluation when sensitivities are downstream quantities of interest.

articles.title: Exact Scaling Laws for a Random-Features Bigram Model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19281v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding neural scaling laws is increasingly important for theory and practice, yet first-principles explanations remain limited even in simple settings. In this work, we study capacity-limited scaling in a bottlenecked bigram model with power-law (Zipf) token statistics, viewed as an analytically tractable toy model of a large language model. Fixed random embeddings serve as a proxy for representational capacity and induce an explicit bottleneck of width, allowing us to derive scaling laws for prediction regret as a function of model width, vocabulary size, and the Zipf exponent. Our results complement recent theoretical accounts based on optimization dynamics by isolating scaling due purely to representational constraints. In the appropriate regime, the theory recovers the functional form of classical neural scaling laws and suggests that heavy-tailed language statistics may underlie both optimization- and capacity-driven scaling. Experiments natural language datasets (WikiText2, OpenWebText) closely match the predicted curves.

articles.title: Train to Stitch: Topology-Preserving Regularization for Interoperable Representations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As large, powerful pre-trained models become more prevalent, there is growing interest in developing methods that allow different neural networks to be seamlessly combined with little or no direct communication between them. Take autoencoder-based data compression as an example: the ability to independently choose architectures and train encoder and decoder models, while still ensuring they work together, could fundamentally transform how such models are built, deployed, and updated. In this work, we introduce a novel approach that leverages topological regularization to align the latent spaces of two independently trained autoencoder models, entirely eliminating the need for coordination during training. We provide a conditional theoretical analysis showing how the structural agreement encouraged by our regularizer can translate into approximate geometric compatibility between independently learned representations. Reconstruction experiments validate this approach empirically, substantially narrowing the interoperability gap across multiple datasets.

articles.title: HankelKANet: Lightweight Path Loss Estimation via Physics-Inspired Hankel Convolution
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19524v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate path loss (PL) estimation is essential for wireless network planning and optimization. This paper proposes HankelKANet, a lightweight physics-inspired network for PL estimation that structurally embeds electromagnetic propagation characteristics into the neural architecture. Built on a single residual UNet backbone, the proposed model integrates urban layout features with a convolutional Kolmogorov-Arnold network(KAN). Specifically, the convolutional kernels are parameterized by the radial amplitudes of the zeroth- and first-order Hankel functions. This formulation acts as a physics-inspired nonlinear distance encoding, enabling the network to capture dominant attenuation characteristics directly without requiring additional physics-based loss terms. Experimental results demonstrate that HankelKANet achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and efficiency on both the simulated RadioMapSeer dataset and the real-world Huawei RSRPSet.
