Compared with the leading baseline, PEFNet, it reduces the parameter count by 78% and lowers the RMSE by 16.96% on the simulated data, while further exhibiting robust cross-dataset transferability and high data efficiency during target-domain adaptation. To interpret these empirical gains, we mathematically establish a parameter-conditional spatial gradient bound. Using discrete Dirichlet energy (DDE) and Jacobian sensitivity heatmaps, we empirically verify that this physical encoding intrinsically constrains the network's spatial derivatives. This structural smoothness effectively eliminates non-physical spatial ripples, preventing overfitting to simulator artifacts and serving as the fundamental driver for robust real world generalization.

articles.title: Learning Across Temporal Graph Representation Silos
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19576v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Temporal graph data are recorded in different representations, but whether these differences also determine the scope of learned knowledge reuse remains unclear. This study investigates whether predictive structure learned from relational histories can be reused between continuous-time dynamic graphs (CTDGs) and temporal knowledge graphs (TKGs). Bidirectional reuse emerges while retaining distinct input and prediction interfaces and independent vocabularies, and sources with the same representation are not always more useful. Controlled reorganizations of source histories show that the organization contributing to reuse varies across source-target conditions. We show that learned aspects of Relational Dynamics, the predictive structure present in relational histories, can be reused across conventional representation boundaries. Independently pretrained TKG and CTDG learners can also be fused at the score level to improve prediction on a third dataset without entity or relation-semantic alignment. Two proofs of concept in recommendation and security detection illustrate that external temporal sources without direct alignment can also become useful pretraining resources.

articles.title: Asymptotically Exact Negative Guidance of Diffusion Models via Positive-Unlabeled Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19802v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Negative guidance of diffusion models generates samples that avoid an undesired condition, specified either by reference samples or by a conditional score alongside an unconditional model. Existing methods inject repulsive terms derived from local information at each sample, so the resulting sampler does not target an explicit density, and its bias cannot be systematically reduced by increasing computation. We instead present a negative-guidance method that samples from an explicit target density, which uniformly handles both reference-sample and score-based specifications and suppresses probability mass near the undesired condition with an avoidance strength that parametrizes the target density itself. Realizing this target requires estimating, at each diffusion timestep, how likely each sample is to belong to the undesired condition. We cast this estimation as a Positive-Unlabeled learning problem that admits lightweight online training along the diffusion trajectory, using condition samples as positives and diffusion particles as unlabeled data. Because the guided particles drift from the unconditional marginal, we further correct the residual mismatch via Sequential Monte Carlo, yielding a sampler that is asymptotically exact in the particle limit and that turns any existing negative-guidance method into its proposal kernel. Empirically, our method approaches the ground-truth target on Gaussian mixtures and Pareto-dominates existing methods on trade-offs between avoidance and generation quality, distributional bias, and diversity, including in an image-generation setting with a pretrained score network.

articles.title: Sequential Learning-Based Physics-Informed Neural Network Modeling for Parameter Estimation on a Power Converter
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20041v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A staged physics-informed neural network (PINN) is proposed for identifying the inductance, capacitance and parasitic resistances of a DC buck converter from time-domain data. Gradients are released in the order of L to C to rL to rC, a sequence derived from sensitivity analysis. The five-stage schedule recovers L and C to within 5% and the series ESR to 10%, while a three-stage variant attains the same accuracy 11% faster. An 84 factorial sweep confirms that the trained PINN remains accurate for simultaneous 8% perturbations of all four components, achieving a waveform RMSE of 2.6 x 10-2 over 5 ms-an order-of-magnitude better than a simultaneous-training baseline.

articles.title: Trainable at Depth, Solvable at Small Size: What the Loss Surface of a Polynomial Activation Dictates for Designing, Initializing and Training Networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20069v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: What makes a deep network train, and what shape is its loss surface? We answer both with one construction at two scales: a polynomial activation f (z) = z + λz 3 , clamped and projected onto the unit sphere, plus an unnormalized identity path. As a deep stack it trains to one hundred layers on MNIST with no normalization machinery; as a small model its square loss is a polynomial system we solve exactly. The small scale explains the large one: it prescribes how to design, initialize and train the stack.

articles.title: HGRP: Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network for Routability Prediction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Routability prediction enables rapid evaluation of placement quality without routing, providing effective feedback for routability-driven placement optimization. Recent machine learning methods have achieved efficient routability prediction through data-driven approach. However, their prediction performance highly depends on the capability of input representations to capture essential circuit information. To address the limitations of existing circuit representations in simultaneously preserving logical topology, physical layout and routing resource information, this paper proposes HGRP, a heterogeneous graph neural network for routability prediction. HGRP models the cells, nets, and routing grids as distinct types of nodes and explicitly represents topological connectivity, spatial mapping, and grid adjacency, thereby constructing a heterogeneous graph representation that preserves multi-level circuit semantics. Based on the representation, a heterogeneous message passing mechanism is developed to enable information interaction and feature fusion among distinct types of nodes, effectively learning the complex correlations between circuit structures and routing behaviors. Experimental results on the CircuitNet dataset show that HGRP improves F1-score by 18.69% relative improvements compared with the state-of-the-art in the congestion prediction task. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/ShenShan123/HGPR.

articles.title: FUSE: Fairness-aware Update Screening against Byzantine Exploitation in q-Fair Federated Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20264v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Client-level fair federated learning, in the form of q-fair federated learning (q-FFL), agnostic federated learning, or tilted empirical risk minimization, has emerged as an attractive solution to equalize utility across heterogeneous clients. This paradigm grants high-loss clients greater relative influence, while a central server aggregates their loss-weighted updates into a single shared model. Yet, the Byzantine robustness of q-fair federated learning has been largely neglected, leaving the server unable to tell legitimate fairness-induced amplification from malicious update scaling. To address this critical gap, we formalize the problem of Byzantine-robust q-fair federated learning under an emphupdate-only interface, in which the server observes nothing but the fairness-scaled client updates. Our analysis under shared class-conditional label skew shows that fairness scaling preserves the nonnegative class-mixture structure of honest updates, while replacing their unit-sum constraint by a client-dependent radial scale. Moving beyond magnitude-based screening, we show that this warped geometry supplies two complementary tests, one radial and one structural, that a single norm cannot provide. We then introduce FUSE, a structure-aware robust aggregator that uses a small trusted labeled dataset for coefficient recovery, scale and cone-consistency screening, and post-screening step-size control. Across four benchmarks and seven Byzantine attacks, FUSE improves seed-wise worst-attack accuracy over the strongest baseline on each benchmark by 3.9--30.1 percentage points, while largely preserving the influence of the high-loss honest clients that fairness is meant to protect.

articles.title: SpectrumQuant: Spectrum Alignment for LLM Quantization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Orthogonal transforms have emerged as an effective tool for low-bit quantization of large language models (LLMs), as they reshape activation distributions without changing the underlying model function. Existing approaches typically rely either on fixed data-agnostic transforms, such as Hadamard rotations, or on calibration-time optimization of learned rotations. We study rotation selection from first principles and show that maximizing covariance leads to spectral alignment and provides a principled criterion for constructing quantization-friendly orthogonal transforms. Based on this insight, we propose SpectrumQuant, a closed-form rotation method that estimates activation covariance from calibration data and uses it to construct a covariance-aware orthogonal transform for post-training quantization. Our formulation characterizes quantization-friendly rotations as compositions of alignment and mixing components, while recovering Hadamard matrices as a special case. Interestingly, a class of butterfly matrices belongs to this category. In the realm of LLM quantization, SpectrumQuant bridges the gap between data-agnostic structured rotations and learned rotations, providing an effective and efficient data-aware alternative for post-training quantization. Experiments on Llama and Mistral models show that SpectrumQuant is competitive with state-of-the-art rotation strategies while requiring less than one-third of the GPU memory and significantly less time than learned rotations approaches like SpinQuant and DartQuant.

articles.title: NeuroDETR: Multiscale Discrete Spatiotemporal Tokenization for Asynchronous EEG Event Detection
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20349v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Asynchronous EEG event detection supports practical brain-computer interfaces by identifying event classes and temporal boundaries directly from continuous recordings without predefined event boundaries at inference time. The primary challenge lies in extracting event-related patterns embedded in ongoing background activity. To address this, we propose NeuroDETR, a discrete spatiotemporal multiscale framework that combines structured tokenization with event-aware feature refinement. Multiscale temporal codebooks capture brief responses and sustained dynamics, while Spatial-Pyramid VQ hierarchically encodes spatial structure across EEG channels. These complementary representations form a compact event memory for jointly classifying events and estimating their onsets and offsets. Before tokenization, we apply FOCAL, an event-aware sparse attention module that uses predicted event presence to guide temporal feature refinement and spatial aggregation, emphasizing likely event periods while preserving context across the recording. Experiments on eight EEG datasets that span diverse paradigms demonstrate state-of-the-art performance. These findings provide a basis for the development of BCI systems that recognize meaningful neural activity during continuous interaction and monitoring.

articles.title: The Physics Is the Network: Fast, Training-Free Neural Emulation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20525v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural emulation need not require learning a substitute for known physics. We investigate PolyNets that couple a continuous-time neural representation of polynomial dynamics with a simple recurrent network for discrete-time integration. When the governing coefficients are known, the resulting tensor graph requires no training and preserves the prescribed numerical scheme while enabling efficient hardware execution and parallel simulation. Using the one-dimensional Korteweg-de Vries equation, we compare PolyNet with CPU and GPU finite-difference Runge-Kutta solvers and three trained neural models: a state-map emulator, a physics-informed predictor, and a learned-tendency integrator. Analytical soliton solutions provide a reference for amplitude and phase errors across grid resolutions, 10⁶ dispersively scaled time steps, ensembles of up to 10⁴ trajectories, and varying initial amplitudes. PolyNet achieves accuracy comparable to the numerical solvers, including at amplitudes outside the learned models' training conditions. It combines this fidelity with high GPU throughput, approximately constant over the tested resolution range, and favorable ensemble scaling.

articles.title: One Task, Many Interfaces: Simple Cross-Interface Consistency Training Improves LLM Agent Robustness
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20576v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Post-training binds the competence of an LLM agent to the interface it was trained on. Semantics-preserving perturbations of that interface, such as renaming an action or changing the notation, leave the underlying task unchanged yet make the agent worse at it. Scoring each sample independently means interface randomization only broadens this dependence from a single interface to the training interface distribution, so out-of-distribution perturbations still degrade the agent. We propose Cross-Interface Policy Regularization (CIPR), a self-supervised objective that replaces action names with uninformative identifiers and presents each training sample under two interfaces in which equivalent actions are identified by construction. CIPR penalizes the KL divergence between the action distributions induced under the two interfaces, so the policy behaves consistently across them. We evaluate CIPR in both supervised and reinforcement-learning post-training, where it improves robustness. On agentic function calling, held-out interface perturbations reduce the accuracy of a post-trained agent by nearly 25%, and CIPR recovers 10.5% while leaving accuracy on the unchanged interface intact.

articles.title: Risk-Controlled DFT Selection for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated materials discovery requires evaluating large pools of candidate configurations, with density functional theory (DFT) as a major throughput bottleneck. Pretrained machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) approximate DFT cheaply, but their errors vary by orders of magnitude across configurations, making it difficult to decide when to trust the MLIP predictions and when to fall back to DFT. We frame this decision as a risk-controlled selection problem and solve it within a conformal risk control (CRC) framework. Each configuration is mapped from atomic numbers and Cartesian coordinates to a fixed geometric descriptor, which a lightweight predictor uses to estimate an MLIP-DFT disagreement score in energy, average force, and maximum force. CRC then calibrates this score into a selection threshold for DFT labeling such that the MLIP error on the unselected configurations, which keep their MLIP labels, stays below a user-chosen fraction α of the expected error. Under an identical guarantee across eight dataset-MLIP pairs, our predictor routes 7% and 14% fewer configurations to DFT at α=0.3 than committee baselines. Because committee disagreement overlooks errors the MLIPs share, our gains are largest when the DFT labels and MLIP training data differ in DFT functional and basis set, and narrow when the two agree. Without model access, the structure-only predictor also ranks errors as well as the target MLIP's latent representation and outperforms widely used descriptors such as Smooth Overlap of Atomic Positions (SOAP) and Atom-Centered Symmetry Functions (ACSF).

articles.title: Calibration and Risk-Budgeted Decisions with System One Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM workflows and agents rely on a set of binary decisions like allow/block an input, or discard/retain a retrieved document. When human deferral is unavailable, uncertain cases must still receive an action. We study System One decision scores in this setting by defaulting to a conservative fallback when uncertain, and controlling the false omission risk within the subset of inputs assigned the utility-maximizing action. Across six datasets covering moderation, safety, and reranking, we compare general System One models with task baselines and a local open-weights fine-tuned System One model. We show that naive baselines for threshold selection exceed the target risk in roughly half of settings with defined test risk, compared with 7.8% for Learn Then Test (LTT), which leverages finite-sample statistical guarantees. Our results show why relying on a probability-like interface is insufficient for deployment decisions and how risk-budgeted selection trades useful action against observed error.

articles.title: A Falsifiable Topological Correspondence for the Standard Model Parameters from a G₂-Holonomy Manifold
articles.abstract: The Standard Model requires nineteen experimentally determined parameters that it does not explain. We investigate, in an exploratory and explicitly falsifiable spirit, whether these dimensionless parameters can be expressed as topological invariants of a *conjectural* compact seven-dimensional G₂-holonomy manifold K₇ with Betti numbers (b₂, b₃) = (21, 77), coupled to an E₈×E₈ structure, with nocontinuously adjustable physical parameter. We do not exhibit this manifold: its topological and lattice data are certified, while the full smooth analytic compact construction remains open, and every claim below is conditional on this clearlydelimited hypothesis. The framework's load-bearing claim is a*parameter-free core* of exact rational relations among topological integers:for instance sin²θ_W = b₂/(b₃+dim G₂) = 3/13, the Koide relationQ = dim(G₂)/b₂ = 2/3, mₛ/m_d = 20, and Ω_DM/Ω_b = 43/8, which cannot be tunedand are individually correct or wrong; all are machine-checked in Lean 4 (zero'sorry'). The geometric substrate is independently anchored by an interval-rigorous, machine-checked bound on the Calabi–Yau residual of anexplicit closed-form metric on the K3 fibre (a variance Var(log R) ≤ 1.32×10⁻⁴, certified box-locally over the surface, not merely at sample points). Against adeliberately generous null model that draws random algebraic formulas from the *same* constants, no set among three million random formula sets reproduces the framework's joint precision profile, indicating strong over-determination rather than curve-fitting. The decisive falsifier is the leptonic CP phase δ_CP = 7×14 + 99 = 197°, compatible with the spread of recent global fits (which have ranged over 177°–212° between releases) though no longer at the central value of the latest, and to be tested definitively by DUNE; a fourth fermion generation, or a measured δ_CP outside[182°, 212°] at 3σ, would falsify the framework. We claim no correctness: only a sharp, testable correspondence, and we are explicit about where geometric derivation ends and empirical correspondence begins.

articles.title: Preparation and Electrochemical Performance of N,S,F Co-Doped Porous Carbon Derived from FCC Slurry via Synergistic Doping and Pore Regulation for High-Performance Supercapacitors
articles.abstract: Utilizing fluid catalytic cracking (FCC) slurry as a carbon precursor represents a promising approach for the high-value conversion of industrial by-products, yet its application is restricted by inorganic impurities, limited pore accessibility, and insufficient active sites. In this work, a synergistic strategy combining ammonium sulfate-assisted in-situ N,S co-doping, KOH activation, and lithium fluoride–hydrochloric acid etching is developed to fabricate high-performance porous carbon. The incorporation of (NH4)2SO4 enables simultaneous pore formation and heteroatom doping, while KOH activation constructs a hierarchical porous structure with enhanced surface area and ion transport pathways. Meanwhile, LiF–HCl etching effectively removes residual inorganic species and introduces fluorine functionalities, thereby modulating surface chemistry and pore architecture. Comprehensive structural analysis confirms the formation of a defect-rich carbon framework with uniformly distributed N, S, and F heteroatoms. The optimized sample (CNK-2) exhibits a high specific surface area of 2847 m2 g-1 and a well-developed pore structure. Electrochemical measurements reveal a high specific capacitance of 401 F g-1 at 1 A g-1 with excellent rate capability and 87% capacitance retention after 10,000 cycles. These results highlight the synergistic effects of hierarchical porosity and multi-heteroatom doping, demonstrating significant potential for advanced supercapacitor applications.

articles.title: Ab initio study of magnetic Cu 2 Sb compounds related to antiferromagnetic CuMnAs
articles.abstract: The antiferromagnetic metal CuMnAs has become a workhorse of antiferromagnetic spintronics. A broad range of phenomena has been demonstrated in this material, most notably current-induced switching and heat-driven quench switching, both first realized in CuMnAs. CuMnAs belongs to a much larger family of intermetallic compounds sharing the tetragonal Cu2Sb-type structure, yet the magnetic properties of most of its members, and their potential for spintronics, have not been studied. Here we report a systematic density functional theory (DFT) study of the magnetic and electronic structure of more than 50 compounds of this family, intended to guide future theoretical and experimental work toward spintronic applications. We find a wide range of magnetic ground states, among them over 20 new antiferromagnetic candidates.

articles.title: Multi-Parametric Characterization and DFT Analysis of L-Proline-Doped Strontium Nitrate (LPSN) Single
articles.abstract: The Mounting demand for advanced optoelectronic devices has generated curiosity over the optical and functional nature of crystalline structures. The present work focuses on synthesizing and evaluating the structural, thermal, optical, electrical, and quantum chemical properties of semi-organic L-proline-doped strontium nitrate (LPSN) single crystals. Single crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD) analysis revealed that LPSN crystallizes in the cubic centrosymmetric Fm(:stackrel-3)m space group, while powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) verified phase purity. Fourier-Transform Infrared spectroscopy identified key functional groups and conformed structural interaction between the L-proline component and nitrate-bearing host lattice. Thermogravimetric and Differential Thermal Analysis (TG-DTA) revealed exceptional thermal stability up to 550°C before decomposition. Kinetic parameters of major decomposition process studied using Coats-Redfern Method yielded activation energy of 304.01kJ mol-1. UV-Vis-NIR analysis showed significant transparency within the region of wavelength investigated. Results of scanning electron microscopy coupled with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy analysis verified a smooth surface morphology, besides confirming the presence of strontium, nitrogen, carbon and oxygen. Complex impedance analysis confirmed a bulk relaxation mechanism, characterized by an ohmic resistance of 50 Ω, a charge-transfer resistance of 970 Ω and a low AC conductivity of (1.25×10− 2 Ω. m)−1. Density Functional Theory (DFT) and molecular electrostatic potential (MEP) analyses were employed at the B3LYP/LANL2DZ level to investigate electronic properties of the LPSN crystal. High global electrophilicity and extremes of electrostatic potential indicated strong regional reactivity and intermolecular hydrogen-bonding capability. These combined findings highlighted the suitability of LPSN crystals for next generation optoelectronic devices like, optical modulators, photodetectors, optical sensors, organic LEDs, signal detectors and generators.

articles.title: Secure Key Relaying in Quantum Key Distribution Networks with Malicious Relay Nodes
articles.abstract: Secure key distribution is crucial for maintaining communication confidentiality in networks with multiple communicating partners. Asymmetric key algorithms are vulnerable to quantum attacks because of the computational advantage offered by quantum computers, whereas symmetric key algorithms with sufficiently large keys remain comparatively more resistant. Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) has emerged as a promising quantum-secure key distribution technique based on the principles of quantum physics. However, practical QKD networks often rely on relay nodes to extend communication distance, and malicious relay nodes can compromise quantum keys during the relaying process. This study proposes a secure key relaying approach based on Shamir's Secret Sharing to mitigate this vulnerability. The proposed method uses a probabilistic behavioural model to assess relay nodes according to their curiosity and collaboration tendencies. By splitting a quantum key into multiple shares and routing them through paths with minimum compromise risk, the approach reduces exposure to malicious or colluding relay nodes. The proposed algorithm assigns risk to network paths by evaluating node-level curiosity and collaboration potential, determines the appropriate number of shares, and selects secure routing paths to minimise key compromise. The study further analyses the parameters influencing the ideal number of shares for a given network, thereby offering a resilient mechanism for quantum-safe communication in QKD networks with malicious relay nodes.

articles.title: Making the most from abrupt and sparse data: Data-driven interpolation from sporadic sensors of contaminant concentration with extreme spatial gradients in saturated porous media
articles.abstract: Soil and aquifer contamination is difficult to map because sampling is costly, invasive, and sparse, while subsurface heterogeneity drives non-Fickian, sharp-gradient concentration fields channelled along narrow preferential pathways. This study introduces a data-driven method that reconstructs the full contamination field from sparse measurements by casting interpolation as a signal reconstruction problem: sparse soil samples form an encoded input, and a decoder trained on simulated transport reconstructs the dense field. The framework is adapted from an encoder--decoder method originally developed for air pollution and is here extended to saturated porous media, broadening it from smooth, continuous atmospheric dispersion to abrupt, channelled subsurface migration and establishing it as a medium-agnostic approach to interpolation. A synthetic dataset is generated with a contaminant transport simulator and a particle tracker following the simulated flow and stochastic diffusion, so the decoder learns the statistical dependencies between sampling points and the underlying field without requiring boundary conditions, gradient bounds, or the conductivity field as input. On the test set the method reaches a mean correlation of 0.72 with the ground truth, while classical interpolators including Universal and Ordinary Kriging remain near zero, and it reproduces the steep gradients they smooth away. A sensor-density analysis shows that usable reconstruction is obtained well below the 30-sensor configuration studied. The results also reveal a subsurface-specific behaviour: contaminant streams merge and coalesce as they migrate. Together these findings support the method as a general tool for dense field reconstruction in data-limited settings.

articles.title: Overcoming Material Trade-Offs in MEMS Transducers via Lateral Ferroelectric–Piezoelectric Thin-film Integration
articles.abstract: Piezoelectric microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) transducers are constrained by a fundamental materials trade-off. Materials that enable strong electromechanical actuation typically exhibit high dielectric permittivity and loss and in contrast, materials optimized for electrical sensing generally provide weaker piezoelectric coupling. Here, we overcome this limitation through the first extensive experimental demonstration of a laterally integrated ferroelectric–piezoelectric resonator architecture designed to enhance transceiver efficiency and figure of merit (FoM). Lead Zirconate Titanate (PZT) and Aluminum Nitride (AlN) are integrated with equal area coverage within the same resonator plane. In this configuration, the high piezoelectric coefficient of PZT enables efficient electromechanical actuation, while the low permittivity and dielectric loss of AlN enable high-voltage sensing. The second resonant mode is used to directly compare actuation and sensing performance under identical strain conditions. This allows material-dependent transduction effects to be isolated. Experimental results demonstrate an approximately 10× increase in electrical output voltage when PZT is used for actuation and AlN for sensing, compared with the reverse configuration. This enhancement is observed across devices spanning frequencies from the kHz to MHz range and results in a substantial improvement in FoM. The architecture also enables DC-bias tunability and enhanced performance through ferroelectric poling of PZT while preserving low-loss AlN sensing. These results establish lateral material integration as an effective strategy for combining complementary ferroelectric and piezoelectric functionalities within a single MEMS resonator for sensing, signal processing, and ultrasonic applications.

articles.title: Geochemistry of Alluvial Deposits from the Mouanko Region (Littoral Basin, Cameroon): Implications for Provenance, Depositional Environment, and Associated Mineralizations
articles.abstract: The siliciclastic sedimentary formations of the Cameroonian Littoral Basin preserve crucial indicators of the paleoclimatic and geodynamic evolution of the Central African Atlantic margin. This study focuses on the lithogeochemical characterization of clays, sandstones, and conglomerates from the Mouanko region (Douala sub-basin) to determine their provenance, reconstruct their depositional environment, and evaluate the potential of associated mineralizations. In the absence of X-ray diffraction (XRD) data, a quantitative multi-element approach using X-ray fluorescence (XRF) and inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) was applied. The results reveal three distinct geochemical poles. The first, an aluminous pole (residual clays), displays high Al2O3 contents (23.1–25.5%) and high loss on ignition (LOI: 12.4–13.7%), associated with an extreme Chemical Index of Alteration (CIA) exceeding 99%. This signature reflects complete continental hydrolysis under a hot, super-humid paleoclimate, which promoted the neoformation of kaolinite. The second, a potassic-alkaline pole (arkosic sandstones), exhibits a moderate CIA (55–60%), indicating chemical immaturity linked to rapid mechanical erosion and short transport distances from the crystalline (basement) during local tectonic reactivations. The third pole is distinguished by high secondary Fe2O3 concentrations (17.9–19.7%), reflecting supergene lateritic induration processes or diagenetic cementation in an oxic to suboxic environment. Although the potential for base and precious metals (Au, Ag, Cu, Pb, Zn) is negligible, the explored area holds significant economic potential for non-metallic substances. The characteristics of the aluminous pole open concrete perspectives for the local industrial valorization of ceramic materials and construction eco-materials.

articles.title: Coconut Shell Biochar as a Sustainable Amendment for Soil Quality and Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.) Plant Growth
articles.abstract: Growing concerns about environment sustainability and food security have encouraged the adoption of sustainable soil amendments that enhances soil quality and improve crop growth. This study assessed the effect of coconut shell waste derived biochar as a sustainable soil management strategy to improve tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.) growth while supporting agricultural resource utilisation. Following controlled slow pyrolysis of coconut shell waste, the resulting biochar was comprehensively characterised to assess its physiochemical properties, such as surface morphology, porosity, pH, and nutrient availability. The experiment was designed and set up as a randomised complete block design with 3 replicates per treatment. Tomato plants were cultivated under greenhouse conditions for 120 days and subjected to four biochar application rates 0%, 2%, 4% and 6%, designated as T1 (control), T2, T3 and T4, respectively. The coconut shell-derived biochar (CSB) exhibited a mildly alkaline nature (pH 7,23), whereas the experimental soil was moderately acidic (pH 6.16). The ANOVA (Analysis of variance) indicated that biochar application significantly influenced soil quality and tomato plant growth, indicating its potential for sustainable crop production. Consequently, tomato plants exhibited better growth, stronger root development, and higher fruit yield and quality than those grown in untreated soil, highlighting the potential of biochar to better crop yield and soil management.

articles.title: Comparative genomics reveals the adaptive evolutionary basis of golden-yellow coloration in the large yellow croaker
articles.abstract: The golden-yellow pigmentation on the body surface of adult large yellow croaker (Larimichthys crocea) is hypothesized to play roles in conspecific recognition, environmental adaptation, and visual signaling in natural ecosystems, while also constituting a key trait affecting its commercial value. In this study, we integrated genomic resources from eight species, including Sciaenids, and conducted homologous gene family clustering, phylogenetic reconstruction, divergence time estimation, and chromosome-level synteny analysis to assess genomic structural conservation. Furthermore, gene family expansion/contraction analyses, positive selection detection using branch-site models, and functional enrichment (GO/KEGG) were systematically employed to screen candidate genes and pathways associated with body coloration, alongside amino acid site comparisons and protein structural localization analysis of the candidate gene npc1l1. Our results revealed that while the sciaenid genomes are generally conserved at the macro-structural level, the L. crocea lineage exhibits specific evolutionary signals related to golden pigmentation. A total of 11,470 shared gene families were identified across the eight species, with only four unique families in L. crocea. Phylogenetic and syntenic analyses confirmed the closest relationship with L. polyactis and demonstrated overall genomic stability among closely related Sciaenids. In the L. crocea lineage, 88 gene families showed significant expansion and 22 showed contraction; expanded genes were enriched in pigmentation regulation and lipid metabolism, yielding candidates such as cers2, cers3, hspa8, and bax. Positive selection analysis detected 688 genes under selection, significantly enriched in intestinal cholesterol absorption, lipid digestion, and organic hydroxy compound transport, from which candidates including npc1l1, npc1, bscl2, elovl5, mc1r, edn1, cd63, bloc1s5, and ltk were identified. Notably, among the two positively selected sites in npc1l1, the 77th amino acid resides within the Niemann-Pick C1 N-terminus domain, suggesting a potential role in the adaptive evolution of carotenoid absorption. Collectively, these findings imply that the golden coloration in L. crocea may result from a combination of optimized carotenoid uptake, transport, and storage, alongside melanin regulation and optical enhancement mediated by iridophores. This study provides comparative genomic insights into the evolutionary characteristics of coloration‑related genes in L. crocea, enriches the molecular understanding of fish pigmentation mechanisms, and lays a foundation for future research and selective breeding targeting body color traits in this species.

articles.title: Investigation of the Performance of Machine Learning Algorithms of Casson-Micropolar Nano Particles Around a Cylindrical Shape: ANN and PINN
articles.abstract: Present study deals with a comprehensive analysis of Micropolar-Casson fluid model in two dimensional through a porous cylinder. In order to represent an accurate complex transport scenario encountered in Industrial and engineering applications formulated mathematical model incorporates Joule heating, heat source, mixed convection, chemical reaction and radiation. Convective boundary conditions were assumed. Non-similar transformations were employed to proposed system of nonlinear equations to get ordinary equations. Transformed system of nonlinear differential equations were resolved via two intelligence-based approaches i.e. Physics-informed neural network and artificial neural network. PINN based predictivity is examined at different number of iterations i.e. 1000-20,000. Mean absolute error decays as we increased number of epochs. ANN and PINN based highly authentic and stable solutions compared with BVP4c solutions were obtained. Comprehensive analysis of ANNPINN and BVp4c shows overlapped, stable, authentic and convergent outcomes at 20,000 epochs. It guarantees efficient, robustness and reliable approach for solving nonlinear system of equations alternate to conventional numerical approaches.

articles.title: Design, Physical Modeling, and Circuit Verification of a 4-Bit Quasi-Delay-Insensitive (QDI) Room-Temperature Molecular Processor
articles.abstract: As silicon CMOS technology approaches thermodynamic and quantum scaling limits, room-temperature molecular electronics represents a promising Beyond-CMOS paradigm. However, designing reliable computing systems at the single-molecule scale faces critical challenges, including stochastic channel variations, absence of global clock distribution networks, and quantum transport sensitivities. In this paper, we present the design, quantum physical transport modeling, and circuit-level transient verification of a 4-bit asynchronous Quasi-Delay-Insensitive (QDI) molecular processor. The architecture leverages quantum interference (Fano resonance) within single-molecule junctions to implement the core logic gates (AND, OR, XOR, NOT, ADD, SUB), dynamic latches, and a 4-bit Ripple Carry Adder (RCA). Computational sequencing is governed by a 4-phase Return-to-Zero (RTZ) dual-rail handshake protocol, eliminating global clock dependencies and ensuring strict delay insensitivity under wire-length and quantum transport variations. Comprehensive physical-to-circuit co-simulations confirm an active hardware core area of 0.0216 µm2 (147 nm × 147 nm across 1,296 molecular switches), an active dynamic power of 116.43 mW at 300 K, an energy efficiency of 4.93 pJ/token, and an Energy-Delay Product (EDP) of 116 aJ·ns. Verilog-A behavioral transient modeling validates physical noise margins (SNML = 3.12 mA, SNMH = 9.26 mA), an on/off switching ratio of ION/IOFF = 7.55, an SNR of 60.1 dB across a 50 GHz bandwidth, and an ultra-low Bit Error Rate (BER = 1.05 × 10− 12).

articles.title: Chiral Cartograph3R: A Quick Filtering Framework for Stereochemical Enumeration Integrating Chemistry Rules, 3D-Aware SDF Atom Mapping, Chirality Validation, and Spectral Geometry Features
articles.abstract: Stereochemical enumeration pipelines often overproduce candidate structures that are topologically admissible yet chemically impossible, mechanistically implausible, or silently corrupted by atom-order mismatch between canonical molecular representations and three-dimensional embeddings. These failure modes become increasingly costly in workflows that must explore large stereochemical chemical spaces, preserve chirality, and feed candidates into expensive downstream quantum-chemical, docking, or machine-learning stages. We present Chiral Cartograph3R, a correctness-first quick-filter framework that integrates literature-grounded chemical feasibility rules with a three-dimensional, chirality-preserving atom-mapping and validation layer operating directly on SDF-style structural assets. The system first enumerates candidate stereochemical states and then applies a hierarchical filter stack comprising structural impossibility checks, aromaticity validation, ring-closure feasibility logic, stereochemical preference heuristics, and kinetic-versus-thermodynamic plausibility weighting. Surviving candidates are passed to a 3D-aware graph isomorphism mapper that reconstructs connectivity from coordinates, enumerates graph-consistent atom correspondences against canonical structures, and scores mappings using a directional N×N×3 coordinate-difference tensor, topology-versus-geometry agreement, bond-length consistency, and collapse detection. Final validation uses signed tetrahedral volumes and related orientation tests to preserve chirality and detect hidden inversions. Spectral or distance-geometry embeddings are then emitted as downstream descriptors for equivariant graph neural networks or reranking modules. We ground the manuscript using stereoisomer SDF exemplars containing 196 atoms and 196 bonds each; they exhibit identical elemental composition and near-identical pairwise distance spectra while differing in local stereochemical flags, illustrating the exact regime in which global geometry can be similar while local chirality remains decisive. Compared with current mainstream capabilities in RDKit, OMEGA, ChemAxon, StereoMolGraph, and recent chirality-aware molecular models, the proposed framework occupies a distinct role: not as a replacement conformer generator or end-to-end GNN, but as a fast stereochemical correctness filter that reduces wasted downstream computation, broadens practical exploration of stereochemical chemical space at fixed budget, and improves trustworthiness of ML-ready molecular representations [1–12].

articles.title: Machine Learning for Gene-Expression-Based Prediction of Alcohol Use Disorder with an Integrate Web-Based Dashboard
articles.abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a complex condition associated with molecular alterations in brain regions involved in reward, motivation, and behavioral regulation. Gene-expression profiling can provide valuable molecular information for studying AUD; however, the high dimensionality and correlation structure of transcriptomic data present challenges for predictive modeling and interpretation. This study develops a machine-learning approach for predicting AUD status from gene-expression profiles and introduces GENO, a web-based dashboard designed to support laboratory users in interpreting the resulting predictions. Publicly available bulk RNA-sequencing data from postmortem brain tissue of 114 individuals, including 58 AUD cases and 56 non-AUD controls, were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus repository (GSE253155). Gene-expression data were standardized, and dimensionality was reduced using ANOVA F-test and mutual-information-based feature selection. An Elastic Net logistic regression model was then developed to manage high-dimensional and correlated predictors while maintaining model interpretability. On the held-out test set, the model achieved an accuracy of 86%, an F1-score of 0.865, and a receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.895. For each input profile, the model generates a probability-based prediction of membership in the AUD class and estimates gene-level contributions to the prediction. GENO integrates this predictive pipeline into a web-based interface that supports data upload, automated analysis, result visualization, and structured report generation. A preliminary task-based usability assessment with laboratory users further demonstrated the feasibility of completing the platform’s primary workflow. These findings provide preliminary evidence that interpretable regularized machine learning can predict AUD status from postmortem gene-expression profiles within the analyzed dataset.

articles.title: Physics-Informed Dual-Modality Monitoring for GNSS Spoofing Detection
articles.abstract: Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) underpin positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT), but open civil signals remain exposed to jamming and spoofing. When neither the radio-frequency configuration nor the attack is known in advance, the receiver must still identify the spoofed satellite channels before those measurements can be mitigated. Physics-informed dual-modality cross-attention networks (PI-DMCANs) are introduced for this channel-wise task. A short tracking-feature sequence and a local cross-ambiguity-function image are fused by causal cross-attention, and a residual bank—code–carrier consistency, signal-quality monitoring (SQM), peak walk, a secondary peak, and clock drift—sets the weight of each stream. On TEXBAT, OAKBAT, and the multi-constellation dataset MuCoGS, PI-DMCANs were compared with five baselines. Within-scenario accuracy at a Neyman–Pearson threshold was 0.965. Under within-dataset cross-scenario evaluation and cross-dataset evaluation, accuracy was 0.928 and 0.932 respectively, about 3.5 and 5.1 percentage points above the strongest baseline. Ablations of modality fusion and of the gate confirm that dual-modality residual gating is most helpful under hold-out. The resulting channel flag marks which satellite a GNSS receiver should de-weight or exclude, and thereby supplies a basis for interference mitigation.

articles.title: Cybersecurity and Digital Forensics for Multimodal Transport Accident Investigation: A Governance, Risk and Compliance Framework
articles.abstract: Multimodal transport accident investigations increasingly depend on digital control systems, networked communications, and sensor-rich operational data across aviation, rail, maritime, and road domains. This dependence expands the evidentiary surface and creates cyber-enabled failure modes that can alter records, undermine evidence integrity, and complicate attribution. This study develops a Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) framework that integrates cybersecurity and digital forensics across the accident-investigation lifecycle. A structured conceptual synthesis of 34 academic, professional, and standards-oriented sources was used to identify recurring governance, threat, evidence-handling, and compliance requirements. The framework was then operationalised in a deterministic prototype using 10,000 synthetic access requests. Under the baseline configuration, 61.13% of requests passed the governance gate; final decisions comprised 52.65% permits, 38.87% governance denials, 4.33% multi-factor authentication challenges, 3.08% algorithmic-risk denials, and 1.07% compliance denials. The prototype is illustrative rather than a measure of field performance. Its contribution is a traceable decision architecture that links authority, contextual cyber risk, evidentiary integrity, and lawful handling. The framework supports earlier preservation of volatile evidence, clearer decision rights, and more defensible cyber-aware investigations across transport modes.

articles.title: From Hours to Daily Extremes: Evaluating ERA5 and ERA5-Land Biases Across Morocco’s Diverse Climates
articles.abstract: Reanalysis products increasingly serve as ground-truth references and training/verification data for statistical and machine-learning applications in regions with sparse in-situ networks. This study evaluates ERA5 and ERA5-Land against 36 quality controlled synoptic stations over Morocco, across hourly, seasonal, Köppen-climate, and daily-extreme timescales, from 2016 to 2024. Both reanalysis reproduce the mean diurnal and seasonal cycle of near-surface variables with high fidelity (Pearson r frequently > 0.9 for temperature), and the two reanalysis products are broadly interchangeable for climatological applications, with small, systematic differences per variable (ERA5 ahead for temperature, humidity and wind bias; ERA5-Land ahead for wind-speed RMSE in complex terrain). Categorical verification of daily extremes reveals a threshold-dependent, rather than uniformly poor, skill: moderate warm/cold/wind thresholds are detected well by both products, but skill collapses specifically at the most extreme, rarest thresholds (POD falling from ∼0.85 to ∼0.4 for the hottest T2M_MAX class; near-zero for the strongest WS_MAX class), a pattern consistent with the known degeneracy of traditional contingency-table scores for rare events rather than with a specific flaw of either reanalysis. We additionally document a structural ERA5-Land limitation: its land-only grid leaves no valid nearest-neighbour match at some coastal/island-adjacent stations (e.g. Dakhla), a gap that is easily mistaken for missing observations if not checked explicitly. The results argue for anomaly- or percentile-based extreme definitions, and for explicit reporting of land-mask coverage, when ERA5/ERA5-Land are used for impact studies or as an AI-model verification baseline over Morocco’s complex, station-sparse terrain.

articles.title: Enhanced Electrical, Dielectric, and Optical Properties of Fe₂O₃-Decorated MWCNT/Epoxy Nanocomposite Thin Films
articles.abstract: In this study, Fe₂O₃ nanoparticle-doped epoxy/multi-walled carbon nanotube (Fe₂O₃@CNT/EP) nanocomposite thin films were fabricated, and their structural, electrical, dielectric, and optical properties were investigated. EP/CNT nanocomposites containing different MWCNT concentrations (0.1, 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5 wt%) were prepared, followed by the incorporation of Fe₂O₃ nanoparticles into the EP/CNT matrix. The structural, chemical, and morphological characteristics of the prepared nanocomposites were investigated using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The electrical and dielectric properties were evaluated using impedance spectroscopy over a broad frequency range, while the optical properties were investigated using UV–visible absorption and photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy. The results demonstrated that the incorporation of MWCNTs significantly modified the electrical and dielectric properties of the epoxy matrix. Among the investigated CNT concentrations, the 1.0 wt% CNT-loaded EP/CNT nanocomposite exhibited a high capacitance of 8.1 × 10⁻⁹ F, dielectric constant of 71.5, and AC conductivity of 6.7 × 10⁻⁸ S m⁻¹. Further incorporation of Fe₂O₃ nanoparticles into the EP/CNT matrix resulted in a further enhancement of the electrical and dielectric responses. The optical absorption measurements revealed a decrease in the optical band gap from 4.15 eV for pristine EP to 3.86 eV for EP/CNT and 2.69 eV for Fe₂O₃@CNT/EP nanocomposites. The observed changes in the electrical, dielectric, and optical properties demonstrate the potential of these hybrid nanocomposite thin films for applications in electronic and optoelectronic devices.

articles.title: Mechanism and Inhibition of Preferential Corrosion of Cold-Sprayed Copper in Dilute Nitric Acid
articles.abstract: Cold-sprayed copper is a promising additive manufacturing material for a range of applications, including used nuclear fuel containers. Under aggressive dilute nitric acid conditions, it exhibits preferential corrosion associated with the oxide network incorporated during fabrication, a phenomenon that remains poorly understood. Here, we systematically investigate the mechanism of this preferential corrosion by varying the presence of dissolved oxygen and the concentrations of copper ions and chloride. By exploiting the inhibitive effect of chloride on nitrate reduction, we show that nitrate reduction is necessary before the initiation of preferential attack at the oxide-rich particle-particle boundaries can occur. In addition, dissolved copper ions substantially accelerate corrosion, providing direct experimental evidence for their proposed catalytic role. Material loss is ultimately dominated by particle detachment following preferential dissolution along the oxide network. These findings provide new insight into the corrosion mechanism of cold-sprayed copper in dilute nitric acid and indicate that preferential corrosion is specific to nitrate-containing, chloride-free environments.

articles.title: Termination controlled Phase-Pure Ti3C2Tx MXenes Towards Efficient Electrocatalysis
articles.abstract: MXenes are promising electrocatalysts for sustainable hydrogen generation, but establishing reliable structure–activity relationships to achieve phase purity and control surface terminations remains challenging. Here, we report phase-pure Ti3C2-F and Ti3C2-O MXenes synthesised via a molten-salt process, achieving purities >99.6%. Ti₃C₂-F exhibits excellent performance in the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in acidic solutions, with a very low overpotential of 86 mV at 10 mA cm-2 and a Tafel slope of 55 mV dec-1. Ti₃C₂-O shows bifunctional catalytic activity in alkaline conditions, with HER and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) overpotentials of 76 and 134 mV at 10 mA cm⁻², and Tafel slopes of 86 and 102 mV dec⁻¹, respectively. Their outstanding activities and stabilities are attributed to phase-purity and tunable surface terminations, enabling different pathways for hydrogen and hydroxide activation. These findings not only elucidate the underlying reaction mechanisms but also demonstrate the potential of termination-controlled MXenes for efficient energy conversion.

articles.title: A Hybrid High-Spin Molecular Magnet for an Integrated Sensing–Storage Quantum Register
articles.abstract: Hybrid quantum molecular systems combining high-spin electrons and nuclear spins possess enlarged Hilbert spaces that can encode multiple qubits within a single molecule and therefore hold great promise for constructing quantum registers. However, the full potential of their multilevel spin manifolds remains underexplored. Herein, we synthesize P@C60 (electron spin S = 3/2, nuclear spin I = 1/2), a representative hybrid high-spin molecular magnet, via an improved, hazard-free synthetic route and systematically investigate its full electron–nuclear spin manifold. All ten spin transitions within an eight-dimensional Hilbert space, separated by hyperfine coupling and zero-field splitting, are individually addressed using pulsed electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR). We demonstrate coherent control across multiple electron-spin levels, quantitatively characterize the multi-quantum coherence times of the high-spin electron system, and reveal that such coherence enhances sensing of the surrounding magnetic environment, increasing the signal-to-noise ratio by a factor of 2.4. We further demonstrate integrated quantum sensing and storage by transferring electron-spin sensing information to the 31P nuclear spin, where it is preserved beyond the electron-spin coherence time. Finally, we quantify nuclear-spin storage by transferring coherence from the electron spin to the 31P nuclear spin, obtaining a phase-memory time of 20.8 ms, approximately 1,300 times that of the electron spin. These results establish an electron–nuclear molecular spin register in which quantum sensing and storage are integrated within a single molecule.

articles.title: Quantum sensor could measure how Earth drags spacetime
articles.abstract: Einstein's theory of general relativity describes gravity as the bending of spacetime, a mathematical model that combines three-dimensional space and time into a single, four-dimensional continuum. The theory also predicts that a rotating object, such as Earth, slightly drags the surrounding spacetime as it rotates, a phenomenon known as frame-dragging.

articles.title: IBM executive warns of risk of quantum computing hacks
articles.abstract: Organizations are unprepared for the risks posed by quantum computing, IBM's Europe and Africa vice president Alessandro Curioni told AFP Wednesday, referring to the high-speed technology that could crack security encryptions and enable large-scale cyberattacks.

articles.title: Software advance brings complex quantum simulations to standard computers
articles.abstract: A major software advance could aid the creation of bigger, more reliable quantum computers, a study suggests. Researchers have developed an algorithm that enables off-the-shelf computers to run quantum simulations previously only possible using the world's most powerful supercomputers.

articles.title: Phase separating microdomains in highly coarse-grained lipids
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.18882v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A highly coarse-grained model for the lipid monolayer is formulated by considering a two-dimensional system of spherical particles with distinct types of S, U, and C, corresponding to the saturated, unsaturated, and cholesterol molecules. Their interactions are defined as modified Lennard-Jones type with distinct interaction strengths. The phase behavior of the system is studied for various cholesterol compositions, x ranging from 0.1 to 0.6. From the simulation results, we observe that the S- and C-type particles segregate together to form ordered microdomains, with U-type particles at their outer leaflet; consistent with observations in literature. An order parameter Φ is defined to quantify the extent of phase separation among the constituents. The time averaged value of Φ is found increasing with the x value. Radial distribution function calculations indicate the structural ordering within the phase separated domains.

articles.title: Mechanisms leading to axial segregation of bidisperse particles in rotating tumblers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.18885v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The origin of segregated axial bands for size-bidisperse particles in long rotating tumblers is a long-standing question in granular flows and a problem of both fundamental and practical interest. Using DEM simulations, we consider the streamwise and time-dependent development of the underlying instability as well as performing a broad parametric study over a wide range of particle size ratios, tumbler lengths and diameters, species fractions, and fill levels to determine the conditions under which axially segregated bands appear. We show that initial radial segregation of the small and large particles in the surface flowing layer results in a layer of mixed particles with a higher bulk density due to more efficient packing over a layer of nearly monodisperse small particles with a lower bulk density. This leads to a granular Rayleigh-Taylor-like instability that produces recirculation cells driving axial band formation. The appearance of a layer of high-density mixed particles over a layer of lower-density monodisperse particles can be directly connected to the operating conditions, explaining why axially segregated bands appear only under certain conditions. Typically, increasing the particle size ratio improves packing and increases the density of the mixed layer, enhancing the Rayleigh-Taylor instability and accelerating axial segregation.

articles.title: Full-Continuum Ultrafast Quantum Gas Microscopy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.18994v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum gas microscopy provides single-shot access to many-body configurations, but their microscopic reconstruction has so far largely relied on a predefined discrete spatial basis during fluorescence readout. Here we realize ultrafast atom-resolved fluorescence microscopy of an ultracold ¹⁶²Dy gas directly in continuous space, with all external confinement removed during imaging. Exploiting the large mass and broad optical transition of dysprosium together with a high numerical aperture in-vacuum objective, we detect single atoms within 4,mus while maintaining an effective point-spread function with a full width at half maximum of 254.8(3),nm, and an isolated single-atom classification fidelity of 99.72(3)%. We use the measured single-atom response to construct a statistical configuration-inference model that recovers atomic positions and multiplicities, coming from overlapping atoms, directly from single fluorescence snapshots. Benchmarking our model on Monte-Carlo generated images shows a total reconstruction fidelity of 98.7%. Our approach extends quantum gas microscopy beyond predefined detection lattices, enabling atom-resolved measurements of counting statistics and higher-order spatial correlations directly on the intrinsic length scales of continuum many-body systems.

articles.title: Electron-Mediated Phonon Polaritons in Quantum Cavities
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.18999v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phonon-photon coupling in quantum materials is commonly treated as an effective direct interaction, neglecting the crucial role played by electrons. Here we develop a gauge-invariant theory of cavity phonon polaritons that captures electronic screening, dissipation, and hybridization. We show that screening can suppress polariton formation in metals, severely constraining cavity control of phonon-mediated superconductivity. By contrast, interband electronic resonances in time-reversal-symmetric gapped systems can strongly enhance phonon-photon coupling, enabling robust polariton formation down to the monolayer limit despite electronic absorption. We illustrate these effects in NbSe2, hBN, and gapped graphene. Finally, we show that gauge invariance enforces photon decoupling from a critical soft phonon, establishing a general no-go mechanism for photon condensation.

articles.title: Viscous hydrodynamics from correlated losses
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19083v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interactions turn a gas into a fluid. We show that two-body loss can take their place. Correlated loss induces elastic scattering, as required by the optical theorem, which dominates at strong loss via the quantum Zeno effect. A nondegenerate gas with only two-body loss thus flows hydrodynamically, with viscosity and thermal conductivity close to those of the unitary Fermi gas. As loss heats the gas, both grow in time with a universal exponent 3/8. Unlike single-particle loss, two-body loss can engineer collisions, and hence transport, in quantum matter.

articles.title: Geometry-Encoded Hidden Orientational Memory
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19090v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Materials usually remember their past through dissipative changes of structure or through a net order. Simulations of caged colloidal ellipsoids at a fluid interface reveal a purely orientational memory. The particles stay in place, the layer has no net alignment, and a pattern written by a field is retained by capillary interactions between neighbors. It lasts hundreds of times longer than a particle takes to reorient, while every particle keeps rotating. The layer also remembers sequence: when two strong fields act one after the other on the same particles, it records which came last.

articles.title: Engineering Correlated Transparent Conductors via Metal-Insulator Transition Proximity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transparent conductors are key functional materials in modern optoelectronic devices. Their performance is governed by an inherent trade-off between optical transparency and electrical conductivity. Correlated metallic oxides offer an attractive workaround to this compromise, where narrow partially-filled bands provide high conductivity, while the absence of visible-range transitions enables optical transparency. Despite this promise, transparency and conductivity remain coupled through carrier density and electronic coherence. Here, we use proximity to a metal-insulator transition (MIT) as a design principle for engineering this balance in correlated-oxide transparent conductors. Epitaxial Ti-substituted SrVO₃ films serve as a model platform where the optical window and metallicity are tuned simultaneously. We demonstrate and explain a systematic broadening of the optical window to regimes relevant for silicon photovoltaics. This gain is counterbalanced by carrier depletion and disorder, which drive the loss of coherent transport near the composition-driven MIT. A Haacke figure-of-merit analysis identifies the optimal composition range near the MIT, where the loss of metallic transport is accompanied by persistent near-Fermi-level spectral weight, indicating disorder-assisted localization together with correlation-driven spectral-weight redistribution. These findings establish proximity to an MIT as a general materials-design strategy, using electronic filling as a tuning knob for the transparency-conductivity balance in correlated-oxide transparent conductors.

articles.title: Symmetry-selected extreme shear compliance in a stable carbon monolayer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19168v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Solids that are stiff to most loads and extremely compliant to one are normally built, not found. That internal atomic relaxation lowers elastic constants is textbook; what has remained untested is whether it can be driven far enough to separate the elastic scales of a crystal by an order of magnitude while leaving it mechanically stable. Density functional theory calculations of the complete in-plane elastic tensor of four non-hexagonal carbon monolayers sharing a square lattice metric show that it can: their longitudinal stiffnesses agree to within a factor of two while their shear constants span more than a factor of fifty. Twin T-graphene, previously reported as elastically isotropic from normal strains alone, is the extreme case, with C₆₆=3.03~N,m⁻¹, nearly fifty times below graphene, at an axial stiffness typical of semiconducting monolayers, and a soft Kelvin eigenvalue a factor of 29 below the others while the Born criteria hold. Symmetry confines the strain-induced relaxation to the B₂g sector, a counter-torsion of the carbon sublayers about the short mid-plane bonds that removes 96% of the clamped-ion shear stiffness with almost no bond stretching and leaves the semiconducting gap intact. Transverse acoustic phonons, finite-temperature dynamics, and large-deformation simulations show that the channel survives beyond the harmonic, zero-temperature limit. Because the selection rule is a point-group statement rather than a chemical one, it yields a screening criterion for other crystals and other strain components.

articles.title: Atomic ironing for conformal interfaces in freestanding oxide nanomembranes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19275v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Atomically well-defined interfaces are essential for realizing functional interlayer coupling in stacked and twisted oxide heterostructures, yet transferred freestanding oxides can develop structural inhomogeneities, including local curvatures, interfacial voids, and incomplete contacts with substrates. Here, we demonstrate that these transfer-induced structural disorders and imperfections evolve substantially and can be suppressed by post-transfer thermal treatments, yielding bulk-like crystalline freestanding oxide nanomembranes. Using freestanding SrTiO3 membranes as a model system, we report a systematic understanding of the role of "atomic ironing" and the associated evolution of lattice mosaicity, interfacial roughness, and optical bandgap. We further demonstrate atomically bonded conformal interfaces in twisted SrTiO3 heterostructures, highlighting the importance of post-transfer thermal processes. These results establish a synthetic strategy to restore the structural integrity and intrinsic bulk-like functionality of freestanding oxide nanomembranes, enabling stacked, twisted, and heterogeneously integrated oxide architectures with atomically well-defined interfaces for emerging quantum functionalities.

articles.title: Signatures of symmetry-stabilized Dirac fermions in correlated oxide CaNbO3 thin films
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19276v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Symmetry-protected electronic states in correlated oxides offer a route to combining topology, lattice tunability, and many-body interactions, but creating such topological electronic states in complex oxides remains challenging. Here, we show that oxygen octahedral rotations provide a symmetry-control parameter for stabilizing Dirac-related electronic states in epitaxial CaNbO3 films. By comparing compressively strained tetragonal films and relaxed orthorhombic films, we demonstrate that distinct octahedral rotation patterns preserve nonsymmorphic symmetry and lead to distinct transport signatures consistent with Dirac-like electronic states. The films exhibit metallic transport with high mobility of 138,000 cm2 V-1 s-1, multichannel conduction, and Shubnikov-de Haas oscillations from small high-mobility Fermi pockets. Landau-fan diagram analysis indicates finite Berry-phase contributions, while first-principles calculations reveal a strain-driven evolution from nodal-line band crossings in the orthorhombic phase to Dirac-electron band features in the tetragonal phase. These results establish oxygen octahedral symmetry as a design knob for engineering topological electronic states in correlated perovskite oxides.

articles.title: Chern insulator optics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19284v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chern insulators have optical properties that are strikingly different than ordinary chiral media. Unlike the natural optical activity of the latter, which is a finite-wavelength effect arising from spatial dispersion, the optical activity of a Chern insulator is already present in the long-wavelength limit, and exhibits a striking directional asymmetry in the propagation of circularly polarized light. We study this unnatural optical activity using a recently developed field theory for Chern insulators. For bulk Chern insulators, we derive the normal-incidence transmission and reflection coefficients of multilayer structures, identify the associated Faraday and Kerr angles, and show that these optical rotations provide a direct optical signature of topology at low frequencies. We also show that an interface between bulk Chern insulators can act as a kind of mirror, completely reflecting light at normal incidence when the Chern invariants have opposite signs. Moving to a more realistic model of a two-dimensional current sheet, we study the Faraday and Kerr effects in a thin film of MnBi₂Te₄ in its Chern insulator phase. The predicted rotations are many orders of magnitude larger than those of optically active media of comparable thickness that are topologically trivial.

articles.title: Odd-to-Even-Layer Switch of Spontaneous Excitonic State in rmTiSe₂ Thin Films
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: rmTiSe₂ is a candidate of high temperature excitonic condensates with spontaneous exciton formation in addition to its charge density wave (CDW). However, direct observation and manipulation of this electron-hole paring state formation is still lacking. Here, using varying-temperature angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (VT-ARPES), we observe a distinct odd-to-even-layer switch of spontaneous exciton state formation with the evident correlated band structure in rmTiSe₂ thin films. While the odd-layer rmTiSe₂ films show a sharp band structure in single-particle picture superimposed by CDW renormalization, in the even-layer rmTiSe₂ films, the full-filling valence band (VB) opens a distinct notch at the top, and the conductive band (CB) shows a significant extra signal extending above Fermi level with spectra broadening. These features indicate that the extra holes (notched VB) and electrons (broadening CB above Fermi level) form spontaneous excitons in even-layer rmTiSe₂. Based on a correlated electron-hole model extracted from the tight-binding description, we reproduce the characterized band structures with spontaneous exciton formation, where the interlayer inter-band coupling in rmTiSe₂ plays a key role, which leads to an odd-to-even-layer switch of the excitonic state formation. Our results provide direct evidences of the spontaneous exciton formation, promising an excitonic condensate as versatile platform for realizing Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) and investigating novel correlated phenomena.

articles.title: Seismology of Glasses
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19602v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Aging and relaxation of glasses proceed through localized rearrangements that also generate long-ranged mechanical responses in their surroundings. We develop a theory that treats these rearrangements as internal microseismic sources, and thereby separates the direct effects emerging from an event from the effects from the far-field displacements it generates. These far-field disturbances propagate and relax through the viscoelastic medium through which they move, producing a stochastic background of weak but numerous perturbations at any given location. Combining the description of local events from the Random First Order Transition theory with this propagating background, we derive a unified equation for the dynamical structure factor of a relaxing glass. The theory identifies a finite wave-vector and time window in which the growing viscoelastic far-field disturbances can produce compressed exponential relaxation, which has been observed using X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy. At higher wave vectors that resolve local jumps, heterogeneity of the local event dynamics instead produces stretched exponential relaxation. The crossover between these behaviors depends on the event statistics and the scattering phase accumulated across the region reached through viscoelastic propagation from the numerous distant sources.

articles.title: Active Sculpting: morphodynamics of internally stirred active vesicles
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Active flows are often confined by soft, deformable boundaries that they can push against, reshape, and in turn get reorganized by. Motivated by this interplay, we combine theory and numerical simulations to analyze the morphodynamics of an elastic vesicle enclosing a dilute suspension of extensile active particles. We model the two-dimensional vesicle as a weakly extensible elastic ring with bending rigidity, immersed in a Stokesian fluid, and describe the confined active suspension using a kinetic theory. The vesicle and the suspension are coupled hydrodynamically, through the kinematic and dynamic boundary conditions at the interface, and energetically, through a single alignment interaction that simultaneously aligns active particles with the membrane and the membrane with the particles. We show that this interaction reduces to a weak-anchoring boundary condition familiar from passive liquid crystals and derive a closed-form quiescent equilibrium state in which the nematic order in the suspension organizes into a vortex with a +1 defect core. A stability analysis of this state predicts an ordered hierarchy of activity thresholds at which successive shape modes of the vesicle are destabilized, as well as a purely passive, anchoring-driven instability of floppy vesicles. Nonlinear simulations, performed with a volume-conserving immersed boundary method, reveal that each threshold crossing gives rise to a distinct emergent state: a static spindle with boundary-pinned defects, a rotor that tank treads against its own rotation, a fluctuating spinner, and a turbulent state in which the vesicle acts as a self-stirring compartment. Beyond demonstrating how boundary deformability sculpts, and is sculpted by, confined active matter, our results open the door to study hydrodynamic interactions between such active vesicles and to use membrane fluctuations as a probe of activity of suspensions.

articles.title: Nonadiabatic dynamics under slow parametric modulation in nonlinear graphene resonators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19816v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Resonantly driven nonlinear systems, from superconducting circuits to nanomechanical resonators, are often described in a rotating frame, where amplitude and phase evolve slowly within a fixed landscape of stable and unstable states. How such systems behave when this landscape moves on their intrinsic timescale remains to be understood. Here, we exploit the strong tension sensitivity of a graphene drum's resonance frequency to reshape the rotating-frame phase space of a bistable mechanical mode in real time, combining an MHz-frequency resonant drive with kHz-frequency tension modulation. When the modulation rate becomes comparable to the mechanical relaxation rate, adiabatic tracking of the fixed points breaks down. Instead, parametric instabilities emerge in the slow dynamics at frequencies set by libration around these points rather than by the mechanical resonance; stronger modulation drives period doubling and chaos. A slow-variable theory predicts where the instabilities occur, and Melnikov analysis captures the onset of chaos. These results show that the rotating frame itself can be parametrically driven, offering a general route to controlling nonadiabatic dynamics in systems ranging from Josephson bifurcation amplifiers to cold atoms.

articles.title: Andreev-reflection spectroscopy of SrPt3P single crystals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19851v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The interplay between inversion symmetry breaking and superconducting pairing mechanisms is a long-standing puzzle of solid-state physics. Ternary platinum phosphide SrPt₃P is an excellent case study in this regard, since it shares the distorted anti-perovskite crystal structure of non-centrosymmetric superconductor CePt₃Si but preserves the inversion symmetry center, enabling a direct comparison between the two compounds. Despite intense scrutiny, the superconducting pairing strength, gap symmetry, and magnitude of SrPt₃P remain an open question. Here, we study the gap structure of high-quality SrPt₃P single crystals with T_c = 8.6 K by using point-contact Andreev-reflection spectroscopy. The spectra systematically showed symmetric conductance maxima and a zero-bias minimum, as is typical of fully gapped superconductors, and dips at finite voltage V_dip due to the local transition of the contact region to the resistive state. In contacts with high resistance, where the dips fall sufficiently far from the gap features, the conductance curves can be well fitted with a single isotropic s-wave gap. The temperature dependence Δ(T) of the gap amplitude extracted from the fit is in good agreement with the one predicted by the BCS theory, with a zero-temperature mean value Δ(0)=1.88±0.08 meV, and a mean gap ratio 2Δ/k_BT_c = 5.2±0.2.

articles.title: Observation of correlations beyond the single-particle picture in fermionic counting statistics
