articles.title: Fast Monte Carlo calculation of multiple scattering in resonant neutron capture
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20435v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A fast Monte Carlo code has been developed to calculate multiple neutron scattering in a sample. Good agreement with an independent Monte Carlo calculation using SAMMY is obtained for neutron capture in ¹⁹⁷Au over the energy range 50--300 eV. For capture following two or more scattering events, a difference is found between the direct Monte Carlo calculation and the analytical approximation in SAMMY. The computational speed allows the scattering correction to be recalculated whenever trial resonance parameters are changed during parameter estimation. The computational core is implemented in C++, while data preparation, calculation control and analysis are performed in Python. Model studies examine how Monte Carlo statistics affect the accuracy with which neutron and radiative resonance widths are recovered.

articles.title: A heuristic sketch how it could fit all together with time
articles.abstract: arXiv:2405.10335v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: On a scientific meta-level, it is discussed how an overall understanding of the physical universe can be built on the basis of well-proven theories, observations, and recent experiments. In the light of almost a century of struggle to make (common) sense of Quantum Mechanics and to reconcile it with General Relativity, it is proposed to (for some time) forget about quantizing gravity or striving for one Theory of Everything or 'Weltformel', which would describe the whole of reality seamlessly without any joints or suture marks. Instead of one single monolithic formalism, a three-legged compound approach is argued for. Quantum Mechanics, Relativity and Thermodynamics are proposed as the main pillars of reality, each with its well-defined realm, specific features, and clearly marked interfaces between the three of them. Not only classical reality, which is rather directly accessible to us, is then comprehensively modelled by their encompassing combination. Quantum phenomena are understood as undoubtedly lying at the bottom of classical physics and at the same time, they become 'fully real' only when embedded in classical frames, i.e., preparation and measurements in time. It is then where thermodynamics steps in and provides the mediating glue as it does at interfaces towards gravity. Decoherence is understood as a smooth way of gradually transferring information and basically dumping entropy to a suitable environment. The aim of this short contribution is not to deliver novel quantitative results but rather to propose a comprehensive research program and to coarsely lay out a very roughly coherent sketch starting from the beginning of the one universe, which we inhabit. The all-embracing picture is claimed to be one of ('mutually induced') emergence.

articles.title: High-level, efficient ocean modeling at all scales with Oceananigans
articles.abstract: arXiv:2502.14148v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We describe the user interface, governing equations, and numerical methods underpinning the ocean modeling software called "Oceananigans". Oceananigans development has been led by the Climate Modeling Alliance as part of a larger effort to build a trainable climate model with quantifiable uncertainty. Notably, Oceananigans is written in the Julia programming language, is optimized for GPUs, and can efficiently simulate all scales of ocean motion ranging from millimeter-scale turbulence in a small box to planetary-scale ocean circulation. We argue that this combination of capabilities is enabled by a design that combines a basic, easy-to-optimize, GPU-friendly structured finite volume algorithm exposed behind a high-level, programmable user interface. This design negotiates a dual mandate for highest-possible performance (to support state-of-the-art applications) and enhanced accessibility (to facilitate adoption and development). The dual mandate aims ultimately to accelerate the progress of Earth system science.

articles.title: The Soul of Waves: Physical Interpretation of Dispersion Relations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.17098v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This pedagogical paper presents a comprehensive framework for interpreting dispersion relations across fundamental physical systems. We adopt a novel approach that starts from the mathematical form ω(k) and systematically extracts its physical content, rather than deriving it from first principles. Through an in-depth case study of the massive Klein-Gordon dispersion relation ω² = ω₀² + c²k², we demonstrate how this single equation encodes phase velocity, group velocity, density of states, effective mass, and impedance. The analysis reveals the universal nature of this dispersion form, which manifests in quantum fields, plasmas, superconductors, and photonic crystals with different physical interpretations of its parameters. We complement this with detailed examination of classical systems including mass-spring chains and hydrodynamic waves, providing tangible analogies that bridge conceptual understanding between quantum and classical wave phenomena. The paper includes eleven carefully designed figures that visualize key concepts and a comprehensive catalog of dispersion relations in the Appendix. Aimed at advanced undergraduates and instructors, this work emphasizes conceptual understanding through physical interpretation, offering a unified pedagogical framework for teaching wave propagation across physics curricula while maintaining mathematical rigor and depth.

articles.title: Experimental observations of sub-threshold triadic resonances in internal wave beams
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.26689v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work examines sub-threshold triadic responses to a vortex-ring-induced perturbation of an internal gravity-wave field, using sparsity-promoting dynamic mode decomposition (spDMD) to diagnose wave structures from experimental observations. Compared with a standard approach to dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) that selects modes by truncation of the singular value spectrum, spDMD, an alternative approach that instead seeks to minimise reconstruction error, is shown here to robustly identify previously indistinguishable oscillatory signals of high frequency in cases of both triadic resonance instability (TRI) and sub-threshold sustained triadic response (STR). These signals are consistent with wave--wave interaction products composed of a primary internal wave with frequency ω₀, and secondary TRI waves with frequencies ω₁ and ω₂ respectively, leading to signals with frequencies ω₃ = ω₀ + ω₁ and ω₄ = ω₀ + ω₂. We show that these signals satisfy conditions for resonance, but fail to satisfy the dispersion relation for internal waves, indicating that they are confined, non-propagating oscillatory signals rather than freely propagating internal waves. A hierarchical analysis of wave--wave interactions provides evidence that feedback between both branches of the TRI secondary waves gives rise to these signals. Whilst we expect our observations to generalise to many classes of wave--wave interaction, we cannot exclude the possibility that the particular observations we make in the laboratory may arise due to reflections of the primary wave from a free surface. However, beneath strongly density-stratified regions of the ocean we would expect to find these interaction pathways faced with the same geometric configuration, so we are confident our findings will transfer directly to the natural environment.

articles.title: Fundamental Limits on QBER and Distance in Quantum Key Distribution
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.22319v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) enables information-theoretic secure communication, yet its ultimate tolerance to noise and achievable transmission distance remain fundamentally constrained. We establish the maximum quantum bit error rate (QBER) compatible with secure QKD and derive corresponding upper bounds on communication distance. Our results follow from a fundamental capacity threshold for qubit Pauli channels and apply to protocols based on two or more mutually unbiased bases, using either single-photon or weak coherent sources. By connecting information-theoretic limits to realistic physical noise models, we obtain universal bounds on achievable distances in fiber and free-space links, including diffraction-limited constraints relevant to deep-space quantum communications. These findings clarify the ultimate noise robustness of QKD and delineate the fundamental boundaries of secure quantum communication.

articles.title: Synthetic reaction data from transformation rules for graph-to-sequence pretraining in biodegradation pathway prediction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The scarcity of observed biodegradation reactions constrains the training of product and pathway predictors. We present enviGraph, a framework that generates and curates synthetic reaction data, uses these data to pretrain a graph-to-sequence predictor, and fine-tunes the predictor on observed environmental reactions for product and recursive pathway prediction. Applying inherited environmental transformation rules to structures from PubChem, NORMAN SusDat and EPA DSSTox, followed by curation, produces 776,851 canonical parent-product pairs for pretraining. We compare this dataset with three United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) reaction datasets: USPTO-50K, USPTO-MIT and USPTO-Stereo. We evaluate enviGraph and the sequence-based enviFormer using ten folds split by pathway on the EAWAG Biocatalysis/Biodegradation Database (BBD), regulatory pesticide biodegradation data (Soil) and activated-sludge biodegradation data (Sludge). For both predictors, synthetic pretraining gives the highest BBD mean precision-recall area under the curve (PR-AUC) among the evaluated pretraining datasets for single-generation and multi-generation prediction. enviGraph achieves BBD single-generation PR-AUC of 0.202 ± 0.050 with synthetic pretraining, compared with 0.169 ± 0.065 for the retrospectively selected strongest USPTO condition, USPTO-Stereo (mean ± sample standard deviation across folds). Its exact BBD top-1 and top-5 accuracies with synthetic pretraining are 0.355 and 0.594. The strongest USPTO conditions give higher PR-AUC means than synthetic pretraining in most Soil and Sludge comparisons. enviGraph has higher Soil multi-generation PR-AUC means than enviFormer under each of the four main pretraining datasets, and with synthetic pretraining it also leads enviFormer on BBD single-generation PR-AUC and exact top-1 and top-5 accuracy.

articles.title: From Plato to Aristotle: Toward a General Theory of Representation Hypotheses
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20286v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) holds that increasingly capable models converge toward a common representation. However, recent studies have shown different views on aligning representations via their neighborhoods, spanning trees, and distances. We show that these views can differ because the alignment criteria behind them sit at different points of one lattice, and we formalize this explanation as the Lattice Representation Hypothesis (LRH). Under the LRH, the convergence claimed by the PRH is agreement at the top of the lattice, whereas its evidence comes from neighbor overlap, a criterion near the bottom. The Aristotelian Representation Hypothesis (ARH) restricts convergence to local neighborhoods because calibration keeps the growth of neighbor overlap with model size but largely removes that of centered kernel alignment. We show that this removal can come from calibrating a maximum over layers, so global convergence remains open. Back into Plato's Cave (BPC) infers coarse shared structure from the collapse of neighbor overlap on larger evaluation sets, whereas we trace it at least partly to a fixed number of neighbors covering shorter distances. We show that the spanning-tree overlap used by Structure over Geometry (SOG) mostly repeats one-nearest-neighbor overlap. The LRH also extends to independently trained models, whose training procedure and objective decide the criteria met reliably across runs. We prove this claim for the training procedure in a linear autoencoder and for the objective in a finite contrastive Gibbs model. Experiments on dozens of pretrained vision and language models and thousands of runs of both theoretical models support these conclusions. We hope this work paves the way toward a general theory of representation hypotheses, with a framework to analyze them and compare their evidence. Project page: https://eethanshi.github.io/LRH

articles.title: Decoupled Marginal Sharpening for Training-Free Inference-Time Scaling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20483v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how to improve LLM reasoning at inference time without updating model weights or using external reward models. Recent reward-free power-sampling methods define the sequence-level power target π_α(ymid x)propto p₀(ymid x)^α, where α>1, which increases the relative probability of completions that are already likely under the base model. Existing methods use Metropolis--Hastings or Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) to approximately sample from this target. However, two challenges arise at different levels. At the target level, full-sequence sharpening can concentrate probability on a few exact reasoning--answer trajectories, suppressing alternative paths that support the same answer. At the sampler level, finite-particle SMC can suffer from path collapse when resampling repeatedly duplicates a few high-weight prefixes. To address these challenges, we propose Decoupled Marginal Sharpening (DMS), which separately controls how strongly the model favors particular reasoning paths and how strongly it favors final answers after aggregating support across those paths. At the target level, DMS first samples from a sharpened reasoning distribution, then marginalizes the model's answer probabilities over the resulting weighted reasoning population and sharpens the induced answer marginal. Separate exponents allow mild reasoning sharpening to encourage exploration of diverse paths, followed by stronger answer-marginal sharpening to concentrate probability on answers with greater aggregate support across those paths. At the sampler level, we develop Fully Adapted Annealed SMC, which combines an annealed sequence of power targets with locally fully adapted proposals and predictive ancestor resampling. Experiments on MATH500, GPQA-Diamond, HumanEval, and AIME24/25 across three base models show that DMS achieves the highest mean pass@1 among the compared methods in all tasks.

articles.title: Ore Loss Mechanisms in Diamond Layout Sublevel Open Stoping for Moderately Dipping Medium-Thick Orebodies
articles.abstract: The diamond layout sublevel open stoping (DLSOS) method enables efficient extraction of moderately dipping medium-thick orebodies through gravity-driven ore flow, while ore loss persists during lower stope extraction due to geometric and frictional constraints. This study elucidates these loss mechanisms via coupled physical experiments and Particle Flow Code (PFC) simulations, focusing on three governing parameters: footwall side-hole angle, surface friction coefficient, and ore-drawing crosscut spacing. Granular flow exhibits preferential hanging-wall mobility with marked footwall restriction, yielding three residual forms: surface residue, end-of-crosscut residue, and inter-crosscut ridge residue. The footwall surface residue increases as the side-hole angle decreases. Physical experiments (6 m spacing) demonstrate that peak recovery depends on both angle and friction: 83.61% at 40° under ore-fragment friction (µ = 0.95) versus 88.59% under fine-sandpaper friction (µ = 0.45). Numerical simulations confirm monotonic recovery increase with angle, validating the trend but omitting inter-crosscut ridge effects present in physical experiments. Extending spacing to 7.5 m reduces recovery to 80.2% at 40° under ore-fragment friction, with 6 m spacing consistently superior across all angles. These findings elucidate three distinct ore-loss mechanisms in DLSOS lower stopes and establish quantitative guidelines for angle-friction-spacing optimization.

articles.title: Ultrasound-Intensified Solvent-Free Lipase-Catalyzed Synthesis of 2-Phenethyl Octanoate: Molecular Docking and ANN-Based Process Optimization
articles.abstract: 2-Phenethyl octanoate (2-PO) is a food flavoring ester with a mild fruity, wine-like odor. This paper introduces an ultrasound-intensified solvent-free lipase-catalyzed process for 2-PO synthesis from 2-phenylethanol and octanoic acid using Novozym® 435. Under ANN-optimized conditions, the process achieved 87.01% molar conversion within 6.48 min, versus 45.84 ± 2.66% without ultrasound, confirming its benefit in the solvent-free system. ANN modeling (R² = 0.9974, RMSE = 0.5535) outperformed response surface methodology (RSM; R² = 0.9333, RMSE = 4.1984) in capturing nonlinear variable interactions, with a predicted optimum of 88.16% validated experimentally as 87.01 ± 1.02%. Docking analysis supported substrate positioning within the Ser105–His224–Asp187 catalytic triad, while the stronger predicted binding affinity of 2-PO (− 6.524 kcal/mol) may explain the product-associated active-site occupancy and kinetic plateau observed. Green metrics confirmed process sustainability, with an E-factor of 0.49 kg/kg and atom economy of 93.24%, reflecting minimal waste in the solvent-free system. After 10 cycles, Novozym® 435 retained 88.8% of its initial molar conversion, indicating operational stability. These findings establish a docking-guided, ultrasound-assisted framework for the scalable, sustainable biosynthesis of food-grade aromatic esters for natural flavor applications.

articles.title: Monocular Panoramic Imaging for High-Precision 3D Shape Reconstruction
articles.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction from two-dimensional (2D) images is a fundamental problem in computer vision with applications ranging from industrial inspection to virtual reality. Traditional methods often face challenges such as textureless surfaces and complex camera setups. Here, we present a novel monocular multi-view panoramic sensing system that captures multiple images of an object from varying perspectives within a single exposure, addressing these challenges. Our method generates accurate 3D point cloud data by traversing contour voxel polar coordinates, eliminating inconsistencies in color calibration and camera parameters. Experiments on foot shape reconstruction demonstrate the effectiveness and accuracy of our approach, achieving real-time performance with high robustness. We show that our method significantly reduces stereo matching complexity and improves reconstruction accuracy, contributing to the field of high-precision 3D shape measurement. **The source code and detailed documentation are publicly available at https://github.com/zlpan8848-gif/three-D to facilitate the reproducibility and evaluation of our work.**

articles.title: Riociguat Suppresses Osteoclastogenesis and Ovariectomy-Induced Bone Loss by Attenuating MAPK Signaling and PPARγ–PGC-1β Coupling
articles.abstract: Background Postmenopausal osteoporosis is driven in part by excessive osteoclast-mediated bone resorption. We investigated whether the soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator riociguat regulates osteoclastogenesis and protects against estrogen-deficiency-induced bone loss.Methods Riociguat was evaluated in RANKL-stimulated bone marrow-derived macrophages and ovariectomized mice using viability, differentiation, cytoskeletal, resorption, immunoblotting, immunofluorescence, micro-computed tomography, and histomorphometric assays. Computational target prioritization, public single-cell transcriptomic reanalysis, co-immunoprecipitation, rosiglitazone interaction experiments, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations were used to examine MAPK- and PPARγ–PGC-1β-associated responses. Group comparisons used analysis of variance or nonparametric alternatives as appropriate.Results Riociguat inhibited osteoclast formation without detectable cytotoxicity, disrupted F-actin-ring organization, reduced resorption-pit formation, and lowered the abundance of CTSK, integrin β3, c-Fos, and NFATc1. Riociguat attenuated RANKL-induced phosphorylation of JNK, ERK, and p38 and reduced PPARγ–PGC-1β association. Rosiglitazone partially counteracted several cellular and biochemical effects associated with riociguat treatment. Structural simulations associated modelled riociguat occupancy of the PPARγ ligand-binding pocket with reduced energetic favorability of a PPARγ–PGC-1β interface. In ovariectomized mice, riociguat preserved trabecular microarchitecture and reduced histological indices of osteoclast activity.Conclusions Riociguat suppressed osteoclastogenesis and preserved trabecular bone in an ovariectomy model. The data support involvement of early MAPK attenuation and reduced PPARγ–PGC-1β coupling, while direct target engagement, pathway necessity, and canonical sGC–cGMP–PKG dependence remain to be established.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption and the Within-Firm Labor Share: Evidence from Chinese Listed Firms
articles.abstract: Does artificial intelligence rewire the division of value added between labor and capital inside the firm? We answer this question using a staggered-adoption panel of 2,274 Chinese A-share listed firms over 2010–2024 (26,579 firm-year observations), measuring AI adoption with a Chinese-BERT classifier applied to annual-report text. Identification combines a two-way fixed-effects design, heterogeneity-robust estimators, and an instrument based on provincial program-controlled telephone switch capacity density in 1992. AI adoption lowers the within-firm labor share by 1.18 percentage points (2.8 percent of the sample mean). The decline reflects decoupling rather than immiseration: value added per worker rises 5.8 percent and average wages rise 2.1 percent while employment falls 3.2 percent—wages fail to keep pace with productivity. The wage-bill share of operating costs falls 0.92 percentage points and markups rise by 0.035. Estimates are stable across Callaway–Sant’Anna, Sun–Abraham, and Borusyak–Jaravel–Spiess estimators, a sixteen-specification robustness battery, and IV-2SLS (10 percent level with provincial controls). Task substitution, productivity-and-scale, and markup channels descriptively account for 97.5 percent of the effect, which is concentrated in labor-intensive firms. JEL Classification: J23, J24, J31, L25, O33, E25

articles.title: Carbon Support–Alkali Interplay Controls CO₂ Slip during Direct Air Capture and Methanation over Dual-Functional Materials
articles.abstract: Dual-functional materials (DFMs) combine CO2 capture from diluted sources with catalytic conversion to fuel. However, the contribution of the alkali phase is difficult to separate from that of reactive oxide supports. Here, Ru-Na and Ru-K DFMs were prepared on two carbon supports with different pore structures: mesoporous high-surface-area graphite (HSAG) and predominantly microporous activated carbon (AC). The materials were evaluated in cycles of CO₂ capture from humid air at 40 °C followed by methanation in 20% H₂/Ar during heating to 300 °C. Activated-carbon-supported DFMs showed higher CO₂ capture capacities than their HSAG-supported counterparts. The use of a chemically inert carbon support enabled the clear assessment of intrinsic role of the alkali metal. Alkali identity determined how efficiently the captured carbon was used: Ru-Na retained the captured species within the methanation temperature window and achieved nearly complete conversion to CH₄ with negligible CO₂ slip across the investigated loading range, whereas Ru-K released substantial CO₂ at higher loadings. RuNa(1:10) on AC maintained stable performance over 25 cycles after an initial conditioning period. Reducing the Ru content from 3 wt% to 1.5 wt% preserved negligible CO₂ slip but decreased capture capacity by about 20%. These results show that DFM optimisation requires matching the stability and reactivity of the captured species with the catalytic methanation window rather than simply maximising CO₂ uptake.

articles.title: Sampling Limits on Recovering Finite-Depth Double-Diffusive Interface Structure from Hydrographic Profiles
articles.abstract: Hydrographic profiles resolve only a sparse projection of a spatially organized double-diffusive interface. We quantify which scalar-interface properties survive that projection by sampling four controlled finite-depth salt-finger simulations with vertical profiles and section-like station arrays. The simulation labels are fixed by prescribed initial spectra, while the measured outputs are salinity-gradient width, gradient localization and entropy, temperature--salinity correlation, and horizontal interface scale. Ice-Tethered Profiler, Argo, and GO-SHIP records are screened independently with TEOS-10 Turner angle and buoyancy frequency to establish their thermohaline regimes and sampling characteristics. The retained ITP windows are predominantly diffusive-convective rather than salt-fingering-favorable, demonstrating why profile morphology cannot establish double-diffusive branch by itself. In the synthetic profiles, median salinity-gradient-width error remains at or below 0.229 for spacing bins wholly below one-half of the native interface width, but is at least 0.561 once spacing equals or exceeds that width. In section-like sampling, the exact dominant mode is recovered in 0.822 of deterministic phase evaluations when station spacing is no greater than one-half of the target wavelength and in none of the evaluations at coarser spacing. Retaining one, three, and five of nine aligned profiles gives median interface-width errors of 0.289, 0.150, and 0.093 and mean prescribed-family contrast-sign retention of 0.693, 0.792, and 0.856. These are deterministic information-retention measures, not predictive accuracies. The results provide scale-aware limits for observing scalar-interface structure; heat, salt, and buoyancy flux remain unobserved without additional velocity or microstructure measurements.

articles.title: Identifiability of battery fuel savings from sparse diesel engine fuel curves
articles.abstract: Sparse diesel fuel tables can support a fitted curve without identifying the direction of a battery fuel-saving claim. This analytical study derives sharp pointwise bounds over continuous, nonnegative, nondecreasing fuel curves that agree with reported knots. For a restricted storage-only transfer from a measured charging point, the bounds classify guaranteed saving, guaranteed fuel increase and an unidentified sign. A second result gives coupled bounds when both operating points are unreported in the same interval, and a conditional slope constraint shows what additional information can resolve ambiguity. The audit is applied to a Cummins mechanical-power table under a declared electrical conversion and to a Caterpillar electrical generator-set table. At 0.9025 round-trip efficiency, all six interval-midpoint comparisons remain ambiguous despite exact agreement at every source knot. At the unreported Cummins low-load point, the critical fuel rate is 31.23 L/h; two admissible extensions cross it. Constructive witnesses and independent linear programs verify the formulas. The contribution is a reproducible decision audit and measurement criterion; it does not establish field savings, economic payback or transient feasibility.

articles.title: Bench Testing of an 8 N Slip-Resistance Specification for the Handle–Shaft Locking Interface of an Articulated Laparoscopic Instrument
articles.abstract: Background Articulated laparoscopic instruments require a reliable mechanical connection between the handle and shaft to maintain the intended instrument configuration during surgical manipulation. The handle–shaft locking interface should resist unintended relative displacement under external loading. However, the appropriateness of a specific slip-resistance threshold must be evaluated in relation to the instrument design and intended conditions of use.Objective To evaluate the mechanical performance associated with an 8 N slip-resistance specification for the locked handle–shaft interface of an articulated laparoscopic instrument using a controlled bench model.Methods A bench-based mechanical evaluation method was designed using the instrument under test, mechanical fixtures, a calibrated force-measurement device, and displacement-measurement equipment. After engagement of the handle–shaft locking mechanism, external forces were applied to evaluate resistance to relative displacement. Testing included axial loading, loading in relevant transverse directions, and repeated locking–unlocking cycles. The primary outcome was the force corresponding to the onset of relative slippage at the locked interface. Secondary outcomes included displacement under load, complete locking failure, and changes in mechanical performance after repeated operation. Acceptance criteria should be established before confirmatory testing.Results All 30 instruments from three production batches met the 8 N axial requirement (30/30). The axial slip-onset force was 12.40 ± 0.97 N (range, 10.80–14.00 N). Under a sustained load of 8 N for 60 s, mean relative displacement increased from 0.06 mm to 0.10 mm, and mean residual displacement was 0.02 mm. After 1,000 cycles, the axial slip-onset force was 12.00 ± 0.97 N (range, 10.40–13.60 N).Conclusions This study provides a bench-testing framework for evaluating an 8 N slip-resistance specification for the handle–shaft locking interface of an articulated laparoscopic instrument. Whether this specification provides adequate mechanical stability can be determined only by comparing the measured performance with engineering acceptance criteria established in advance on the basis of the instrument’s intended use and foreseeable loading conditions.

articles.title: Molecular dynamics simulation of natural gas drag reducing agents on iron surfaces under the dual-carbon background
articles.abstract: To address the issues of high energy consumption and significant carbon emission intensity in long-distance natural gas pipelines, a molecular dynamics simulation of natural gas drag-reducing agent adsorption on iron surfaces and a numerical simulation of agent-added transportation were conducted to meet the low-carbon demands of oil and gas surface processes under the dual-carbon strategy. The Materials Studio software was utilized to construct the solid-liquid interface models of the iron atomic layer with three representative drag reducing agents, namely CPA, BIB, and corrosion-inhibiting G10, and the adsorption energies of the drag reducing agent molecules on the Fe surface under different mass fractions were calculated. The ANSYS Fluent software was employed to simulate the flow field characteristics inside the pipeline before and after agent addition, and to analyze the intrinsic correlation among the drag-reducing agent, iron surface adsorption, and macroscopic drag reduction. The results indicate that as the mass fraction of the drag reducing agent increases from 10% to 20%, the adsorption energies of CPA, BIB, and G10 on the Fe atomic layer increase by 53.84%, 26.87%, and 60.98%, respectively. The G10 drag reducing agent, containing siloxane groups, forms Si-O covalent bonds on the iron surface, and its adsorption energy improvement is significantly superior to that of CPA and BIB containing carboxylic acid groups. After the addition of CPA and G10, the average flow velocity in the pipeline increases from 10.183 m/s to 10.637 m/s and 10.943 m/s, the throughput increases by 12.37% and 14.79%, respectively, and the average turbulence intensity decreases by 37.4% and 59.6%, respectively. The research results provide theoretical support for the molecular structure design of natural gas drag-reducing agents and for energy conservation and emission reduction in pipeline transportation under the dual-carbon target.

articles.title: Laser Travel Speed, Interfacial Reaction-Layer Thickness, and Tensile-Shear Performance in DP600–AA6061-T6 Lap Joints: A Critical Process-Window Assessment
articles.abstract: The joining of advanced high-strength steel with aluminium alloy has led to a new method for constructing energy efficient, weight-reduced structures especially in the automotive and transportation industry. However, joining these two different materials is difficult due to differences in their thermo-physical properties, melting mechanisms and chemical affinity. The formation of brittlediron – aluminium intermetallic compounds (IMC) as well as poor wetting and melting performance along with inhomogenous heat distribution remains the greatest challenge. This study investigates how the laser travel speeds affect the heating cycles, interfacial microstructures, IMC thickness, and tensile-shear properties of lap joints between 1.2 mm DP600 and 1.5 mm AA6061-T6 aluminium alloy by using the 2.2 kW continuous wave fiber laser. The laser travel speeds were 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0, and 1.2 m/min. The results indicate that 0.8 m/min appears to produce the best overall compromise, with a tensile-shear strength of 218 ± 9 MPa and IMC thickness of 3.8 ± 0.5 µm. Reaction layer thickness was greater at lower travel speeds due to slower reaction kinetics, which led to poorer joint strength; thinner reaction layers at higher speeds led to poorer joints due to deficient bonding, not necessarily thinner reaction layers. This suggests that improvement in reaction layer thickness alone will not produce better joints. The present work proposes to optimize the process window assuming raw measurements have been validated, interaction time calculated, thermal-model output and Fe-Al phases identified.

articles.title: Asymmetric day–night warming across Pakistan, 1980–2025: diurnal temperature range compression in the irrigated Indus plains and expansion in the Karakoram
articles.abstract: Warming is rarely symmetric between day and night, and the sign of diurnal temperature range (DTR) change is regionally specific. We analyse 46 years (1980–2025) of ERA5 daily maximum and minimum temperature over Pakistan, for the country and its six first-order administrative regions, using Mann–Kendall tests with the Hamed–Rao serial-correlation correction, Sen's slope, and Benjamini–Hochberg control of the false discovery rate. Pakistan contains two opposing regimes. In the irrigated Indus plains, minimum temperature rose (Punjab + 0.33, Sindh + 0.28°C decade⁻¹) while maximum temperature did not change significantly (+ 0.04 and + 0.02°C decade⁻¹), compressing DTR by 0.28 and 0.27°C decade⁻¹, some 1.2°C over the record. In the Karakoram–Himalaya, maximum temperature rose faster than minimum temperature and DTR widened (Gilgit-Baltistan + 0.11°C decade⁻¹). The station-based HadEX3 data set independently reproduces the plains compression but has no usable coverage in the mountains. Compression is strongest in the monsoon and post-monsoon seasons and is absent in winter and early spring, when both extremes warm together. Warm nights (TN90p) increased nationally from 7.8% to 20.5% of nights, faster than warm days (8.1% to 15.4%). Warming increases with elevation in maximum temperature only, so the near-surface lapse rate flattened by 0.062°C km⁻¹ decade⁻¹. Detrended correlations link plains compression to declining surface solar radiation and rising water vapour, and mountain expansion to low-cloud loss. Because minimum and maximum temperature are changing at different rates and in different directions, mean temperature alone misrepresents Pakistan's warming for agriculture and health.

articles.title: Diffusion-Based Super-Resolution of Adriatic Sea Oceanographic Fields
articles.abstract: High-resolution oceanographic fields are critical for resolving mesoscale and sub-mesoscale coastal dynamics, yet their generation remains constrained by both computational cost and observational sparsity. We present OcDiffSR, a conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) for oceanographic super-resolution that reconstructs high-resolution sea-surface fields from coarse-resolution reanalysis inputs. The model is trained on ten years (2011--2020) of paired low-resolution (GLORYS12V1, 1/12degree) and high-resolution (Mediterranean Sea Physics Reanalysis, Med MFC, 1/24degree) data, and evaluated on an independent test year (2009) over the Adriatic Sea. OcDiffSR employs a conditional U-Net augmented with multi-scale low-resolution encoders, cross-attention bottleneck layers, and sinusoidal seasonal embeddings via Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM), enabling joint super-resolution of sea-surface temperature (SST), salinity (SSS), and horizontal velocity components with visually coherent circulation patterns. Benchmarked against bilinear interpolation and the state-of-the-art residual diffusion model CorrDiff, OcDiffSR achieves substantially lower reconstruction errors for scalar fields (RMSE((SST))=0.477degree C, RMSE((SSS))=0.346 psu), near-unity Pearson correlation (PCC ((≥)) 0.999), and high structural similarity (SSIM ((≥)) 0.964). For dynamical vector fields, OcDiffSR outperforms both baselines in absolute error and spatial coherence, though moderate correlation (PCC = 0.64) reflects the intrinsic stochasticity of oceanic velocity fields. Daily and monthly evaluations confirm temporal robustness across all seasons. These results establish OcDiffSR as a reliable framework for high-fidelity oceanographic downscaling and reanalysis enhancement, producing fields that are visually consistent with known ocean dynamics.

articles.title: Lithostratigraphic Control of Vertical Water Fluxes in Chalk Aquifer Systems: An Integrated Geophysical and Sedimentological Approach
articles.abstract: Chalk aquifers represent a major groundwater resource in northwestern Europe, yet the role of superficial formations in controlling recharge processes remains poorly constrained. This study investigates how lithostratigraphic successions, at the loess–chalk interface, regulate vertical water fluxes in the Senonian-Turonian chalk aquifer of northern France. An integrated approach combining electrical resistivity surveys (Vertical Electrical Soundings and Electrical Resistivity Tomography), sedimentological analyses, and hydro-mechanical characterization was applied across an urbanized sector of the Artois–Picardie Basin. Results identify three main lithostratigraphic successions controlling subsurface hydrological connectivity: loess over Senonian chalk (LSC), loess-tuffeau-chalk (LTC), and loess over Upper Turonian chalk (LUT). These successions influence the development of perched water bodies within the loess cover and regulate vertical transfers toward the regional chalk aquifer. Weathered interface facies “marnettes”, formed by the periglacial reworking and admixture of chalk debris with loessic sediments, locally act as semi-permeable layers that reduce hydraulic conductivity and promote water retention in the superficial formations. These findings highlight the key role of lithostratigraphic architecture and weathered interfaces in controlling groundwater recharge pathways in loess-covered chalk systems and emphasize the need to integrate these features into hydrogeological models under increasing hydroclimatic variability.

articles.title: A settlement currency to finance climate restoration and human prosperity
articles.abstract: Restoring the climate and meeting basic human needs draw on the same scarce public finance. We ask what one settlement mechanism would have to earn to fund both. In the 841-member FaIR ensemble, holding carbon dioxide removal (CDR) at 9.5 GtCO₂ per year after 2183, without global solar geoengineering, returns median atmospheric CO₂ to 280 ppm in 2300. We cost that removal, ending hunger and Gavi's 2026–2030 vaccine target against Carbonite, a hypothetical tree-backed settlement stablecoin whose fees fund a treaty-governed restoration fund. At US200 per tonne these commitments need US3.1 trillion per year, an effective fee of 13 basis points on all foreign-exchange turnover, attainable only if settlement volume falls by less than 2.9% per basis point of fee. Universal health care fits only if its incremental cost is near published estimates; at US2,500 per uncovered person it needs four to five times as much revenue.

articles.title: Control of Thermochemical Expansion in Perovskite Oxides via Octahedral Tilting and High-Entropy A-sites
articles.abstract: The durability of solid oxide cells is critically limited by the overall thermochemical expansion of perovskite electrodes, exacerbated by the formation of oxygen vacancies with increasing temperature. This creates a fundamental trade-off, where oxygen vacancies enhance electrochemical functionality at the cost of thermomechanical stability. We independently study thermal and chemical expansion of fifteen perovskite oxides with complex A-site cation mixtures using synchrotron X-ray diffraction, dilatometry, thermogravimetry, and density functional theory. We demonstrate that the Goldschmidt tolerance factor governs both thermal and chemical expansion through octahedral tilting dynamics, which offset bond-stretching vibrations and compensate for vacancy-induced strain. We identify that high-entropy A-site mixing also suppresses chemical expansion via "strain containment", where larger cobalt sites with increased bond covalency locally absorb vacancy-induced strain. This lowers the chemical expansion coefficient by up to 29% relative to the benchmark electrode. Together, these correlations and mechanistic insights map structural and compositional descriptors onto expansion behaviors, providing targeted design principles to tune thermochemical expansion without sacrificing functional defects.

articles.title: Gold-Atom-Mediated Charge Transfer in Plasmonic Picocavity- Enabled CO2 Dissociation
articles.abstract: Plasmonic picocavities enable extreme light confinement at the atomic scale, making them highly promising for solar photochemical reactions. Here, ultrafast dynamics of CO2 dissociation in a plasmonic picocavity is explored using time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT). Atomic-scale structure in the picocavity has a strong influence on plasmon-driven reaction, and introducing a gold adatom significantly lowers the dissociation threshold. We identify that the reaction is dominated by direct charge transfer (DCT) rather than local field enhancement (FE). The gold adatom in the picocavity not only acts as a direct electron donor but also establishes a critical charge-transfer bridge across the gap, strongly enhancing transient population of CO2 antibonding (AB) orbitals and thereby facilitating the reaction. Time-resolved analysis further reveals sequential charge-transfer channels between the nanoparticles (NPs), adatom, and CO2, clarifying how atomic-scale junction structure controls the reaction dynamics. These findings uncover a single-atom-regulated plasmonic catalytic mechanism and provide microscopic insight into ultrafast photocatalytic processes in picocavities.

articles.title: Field performance and seasonal energy yield of a residential photovoltaic prosumer in Romania over three years
articles.abstract: Published real-world performance datasets for residential photovoltaic systems in Central-Eastern Europe remain scarce. This study analyses 37 months of continuous production data (January 2023 to January 2026) from a residential grid-tied PV installation in Romania, equipped with a Growatt inverter and monitored via the ShinePhone cloud platform. Monthly totals were extracted from application screenshots and cross-validated against annual platform totals. The system produced 3,195.0 kWh (2023), 3,171.3 kWh (2024), and 2,883.7 kWh (2025), with a three-year mean of 3,083.3 kWh per year. Quarter 3 contributed 33–37% of annual yield, and Quarters 2 and 3 together accounted for 68–70%. A 9.7% year-on-year decline in 2025 is attributed primarily to inter-annual meteorological variability. The Mann-Kendall trend test on the 36-month series returned p = 0.376, indicating no significant monotonic trend; pairwise inter-annual seasonal profile correlations exceed r = 0.88, confirming structural conservation of the production pattern. Grid import and export were zero throughout the monitoring period, indicating complete self-consumption matching across all seasons. The findings provide field-validated PV performance evidence for Romanian residential prosumers and a reproducible methodological template for similar studies across Central-Eastern Europe.

articles.title: Complementary bodies in sphere packing
articles.abstract: Symbolic and graphical tools, such as Mathematica, enable precise visualization and analysis of void spaces in sphere packings. In the cubic close packing (CCP, or face-centred cubic packing; FCC) arrangement these voids can be partitioned into repeating geometric units we term spherically truncated polyhedra - bodies analogous to plane-truncated polyhedra but bounded by both planar and spherical surfaces. They can also be grouped under the more general class of sphero-planar polyhedra. These structures are relevant in geometric studies and applications such as modelling diffusion in porous media and biological tissues. This work examines the properties of these complementary bodies, deriving their surface area-to-volume ratios, which are significant in physical contexts; and we establish a result concerning the packing density of truncated tetrahedra and octahedra, demonstrating how they tile the interstitial space surrounding packed spheres. These findings contribute to a deeper understanding of classical packing problems and their geometrical complements.

articles.title: Revisiting magnetoelectric response in collinear antiferromagnetic zigzag chains: A downfolding approach beyond conventional low-energy models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.07118v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Magnetoelectric (ME) effects in antiferromagnets provide a fertile platform for exploring symmetry-driven cross-correlated responses. However, their microscopic origin remains elusive and is often obscured in simplified low-energy descriptions. In this study, we revisit the microscopic mechanism of the ME effect in a collinear antiferromagnetic zigzag chain by employing a multi-orbital tight-binding model that explicitly includes both s- and p-orbital degrees of freedom. Using analytical and numerical calculations based on the Kubo formula, we demonstrate that the ME response is governed by orbital degrees of freedom activated through s--p hybridization, while the spin contribution vanishes due to spin conservation. To elucidate the low-energy description, we derive an effective Hamiltonian projected onto the s-orbital subspace using the Schur complement. We show that a naive application of the Kubo formula within this effective model fails to capture the ME response. This issue is resolved by systematically incorporating vertex corrections in terms of orbital hybridization into the response functions. Furthermore, by introducing a quasiparticle renormalization scheme, we formulate a renormalized Kubo formula that preserves conservation laws and accurately reproduces the full multi-orbital results. Our analysis revisits the conventional low-energy perspective and reveals that the ME effect originates from virtual interorbital processes encoded in vertex corrections, rather than from the bare low-energy Hamiltonian. The effective framework developed here provides a unified microscopic understanding of orbital-driven ME responses and offers a systematic route to incorporate hybridization effects beyond simple low-energy models.

articles.title: Classical Cellular Automaton for Measurement-Only Entanglement Transitions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.28743v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a generalized classical long-range stochastic cellular automaton that exactly captures the entanglement dynamics and transitions of a measurement-only monitored quantum system. The corresponding quantum model consists of a one-dimensional qubit chain subject to competing single-site and long-range Bell measurements, with separations drawn from a power-law distribution. At every step of each trajectory, the state remains a tensor product of Bell pairs and unpaired qubits, with bipartite entanglement entropy fully encoded in a classical matching of the sites. This exact representation allows us to solve the dynamics analytically in several limits and to determine the steady-state scaling of the entanglement entropy. We find volume-law, fractal, and area-law regimes. Numerical results show that these regimes persist beyond the analytically solvable limit. Because Bell measurement outcomes change only the Bell-state labels and leave the matching unchanged, all subsystem entropies are outcome independent, avoiding the exponential cost of trajectory postselection often encountered in experimental studies of measurement-induced entanglement dynamics.

articles.title: A symmetry-field theoretical framework for quasi-stationary interfaces in fully miscible fluids
articles.abstract: Long-lived sharp interfaces in fully miscible fluids exhibit a transient quartic excess free-energy landscape and a Fermi–Dirac logistic concentration profile, whose microscopic statistical-mechanical origin has remained unresolved. Here, we develop an independent statistical-mechanical theory based on a microscopic pair Hamiltonian and the corresponding grand partition function. Exchange symmetry naturally introduces the invariant p=c1−c, whose regular local expansion uniquely generates the quartic excess free-energy density as the leading nonvanishing contribution after coarse-graining the microscopic Hamiltonian. The resulting free-energy functional completely determines the Euler–Lagrange equation of the quasi-stationary interface, whose exact solution is the Fermi–Dirac logistic profile. The independently derived microscopic formulation converges to the same quartic free-energy functional obtained previously from a continuum variational approach, thereby establishing a unified microscopic statistical-mechanical framework for quasi-stationary interfaces.

articles.title: Ultrafast coherent vibrational dynamics and structural rearrangement following photodetachment of the aqueous adenine anion
articles.abstract: Understanding the elementary processes that follow the interaction of ionizing radiation with biomolecules is of fundamental importance in radiation chemistry and radiation biology. Nucleobases are a class of biomolecules that are of particular interest in these fields due to their significance as the building blocks of DNA and the role of nucleobase radicals in DNA damage. Here, femtosecond optical pump–probe spectroscopy is employed to study the ultrafast vibrational wave packet dynamics of the aqueous adenine radical (Ade[-H] • ) induced by photodetachment. Strong-field photodetachment of the aqueous adenine anion (Ade[-H] − ) by intense, few-cycle pump pulses drives the formation of the hydrated electron and aqueous Ade[-H] • . Absorption signatures of the hydrated electron and Ade[-H] • are observed in the transient absorption spectra, probed in the visible–near-infrared and ultraviolet range. The pronounced modulations present in the transient absorption spectra encode vibrational wave packet dynamics of aqueous Ade[-H] • . This vibrational wave packet motion is resolved into ten vibrational modes along which structural reorganization occurs upon photodetachment. Density functional theory calculations assign the observed vibrational modes and quantify the extent of structural rearrangement following photodetachment. This work provides insights into the ultrafast structural dynamics that accompany the ionization of biomolecules in an aqueous environment.

articles.title: Hydroxyl-terminated carbosilane dendrimer films at water–toluene and water–air interfaces
articles.abstract: We report a fully atomistic molecular dynamics study of fourth-generation amphiphilic carbosilane dendrimers adsorbed at water–toluene and water–air interfaces across a wide range of surface densities. The dendrimers, featuring a tetrafunctional silicon core, trifunctional =Si(CH 3 )– branching units, and terminal hydroxyl groups, adopt a characteristic “umbrella” conformation at low coverage, with hydrophilic termini anchored in water and the hydrophobic core aligned with the nonpolar phase. Interfacial chemistry fundamentally modulates this architecture: favorable toluene–core interactions promote core swelling and homogeneous lateral dispersion, whereas the sharp hydrophobic mismatch at the water–air interface drives dendrimer aggregation. Lateral compression induces a systematic transition from flattened, anisotropic conformations to more isotropic, near-spherical geometries, accompanied by redistribution of hydrogen bonds from dendrimer–water to intra- and interdendrimer contacts. Under strong confinement, steric crowding and transient interdendrimer hydrogen bonding lead to dynamic arrest, with lateral diffusion suppressed by orders of magnitude. These findings establish a unified molecular picture of how surface density and solvent compatibility jointly control conformation, interactions, and mobility in amphiphilic dendrimer monolayers, providing design principles for tunable interfacial materials with tailored mechanical and transport properties.

articles.title: Ab initio study of gas phase HClSO 2 : Building up the molecular complexity of candidate UV-absorbers in Venusian clouds
articles.abstract: Sulfur–chlorine–oxygen-containing species have an indispensable role in chemistry in the Venusian atmosphere. Here, the detailed electronic structure and spectroscopy of the [H, Cl, S, O, O] molecular system are explored using Density Functional Theory, coupled cluster theory [CCSD(T)], and multireference configuration interaction theories [MRCISD+Q]. Equilibrium geometries, rotational constants, harmonic vibrational frequencies, and thermodynamic data of the ground state isomers of [H, Cl, S, O, O] are presented. The meta-stable van der Waals system (complex 1 ; HCl + SO 2 ) is identified as the lowest energy isomer, possessing a noncovalent O⋯H interaction between SO 2 and HCl fragments. The thermodynamics and kinetics of dissociation of HClSO 2 isomers into HCl and SO 2 fragments are explored in detail. From computations, complex 1 is not thermodynamically stable in the upper cloud of the Venusian atmosphere where UV absorbers are present, as it is predicted to spontaneously dissociate into HCl and SO 2 fragments at temperatures above 100 K. Calculated vertical excitation energies of the low-lying isomers using equation-of-motion CCSD (EOM-CCSD) and MRCISD+Q levels of theory are also reported. Our analysis showed that all excited state transitions from the ground state of the lowest energy isomers were below 280 nm and thus might not be candidates for the UV absorber(s). As the lowest energy isomer of [H, Cl, S, O, O] is a van der Waals complex, we expect larger van der Waals clusters with more favorable intermolecular interactions than complex 1 to be plausible candidates for the near-UV absorber(s) observed in the Venusian atmosphere.

articles.title: Electronic stopping power of protons in transition metals: Bragg peak
articles.abstract: For the electronic stopping power of protons in period-6 transition metals, the Bragg peak positions measured in experiments are nearly independent of the element for lanthanides and suddenly show a linear growth for non-lanthanides, while the Bragg peak magnitudes monotonically decrease with increasing atomic number. These observations can be partially explained qualitatively by the velocity-matching criterion. In this study, we reproduce experimental results by using the dielectric response models. To interpret them, we develop approximate analytical models of the Bragg peak position and magnitude for specified shells, which are correlated to both the ionization energy and average electronic density. It is found that for inner shells, the element-independent Bragg peak position for lanthanides is due to a weak variation of ionization energies and average densities, and a strongly dependent relationship for non-lanthanides is attributed to a distinctly remarkable increment of ionization energies. In addition, it shows that the consideration of the electronic density, a factor neglected in the velocity-matching formula, is essential for reproducing the element-dependent peak positions for inner shells. For valence shells, a uniform density is the unique factor, which almost remains unchanged for lanthanides but can be increased by about an order of magnitude for non-lanthanides. An analytic simplification of the Bragg peak magnitude reveals that the maximal stopping cross section is inversely proportional to the Bragg peak position for inner shells, and it is determined by the atomic number density for valence shells, which well explains the experimental results in period 6.

articles.title: Quaternion Dirac–Coulomb–Breit integral transformation for relativistic four-component correlated electronic structure theory
articles.abstract: High-accuracy correlated four-component relativistic electronic structure methods are typically formulated in terms of integrals over molecular orbitals (MOs). Consequently, an efficient and scalable strategy is required to deal with the complexity of transforming relativistic two-electron integrals from the atomic orbital (AO) to the MO basis. The transformation bottleneck is particularly acute for approaches that include Breit interaction integrals, whose computational and memory demands further exacerbate the transformation cost. To overcome this challenge, we develop a quaternion-based, AO-driven direct integral transformation scheme. The method operates on scalar AO integrals and combines quaternion density-based contractions with direct Cauchy–Schwarz screening to systematically exploit integral locality. As a result, the proposed framework substantially lowers the practical computational scaling and provides an efficient, memory-conscious, and highly parallelizable pathway for the routine inclusion of relativistic Dirac–Coulomb–Breit integrals in large-scale four-component correlated calculations.

articles.title: Coupled plasmon modes and constituent-selective refractive-index sensing in silver sphere–torus heterodimers
articles.abstract: Attributing a confined dielectric change to one constituent of a composite nanostructure requires each plasmon resonance to be tied to its mode identity and to the region dominating its shift. We establish this link using boundary-element calculations for silver particles of 40 nm fixed outer diameter along a continuous sphere-to-torus path and the corresponding sphere–torus heterodimers. The transformation reorganizes the spherical dipole and quadrupole manifolds into toroidal modes. Mode labels follow from the symmetry of the quasistatic eigencharge distributions; the corresponding eigenvalues guide assignment of the retarded electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) branches, and cathodoluminescence under matched trajectories assesses radiative character: E 1 u is strongly radiative, A 1 g is dark, and A 2 u is weakly radiative. As the torus aspect ratio e = R / r increases from 1 to 4, the monomer E 1 u and the dimer torus-parent E 1 u -like resonances redshift by about 1.3 eV, with wavelengths following a plasmon-ruler-inspired exponential form. In water, both E 1 u channels exceed 600 nm/RIU in bulk refractive-index sensitivity at quality factors of 18–20 and figures of merit near 13; the sphere-parent χ 1 -like branch is a second, less sensitive channel. Beam-position-resolved EELS shows preferential excitation of the E 1 u -like and χ 1 -like branches near the torus and sphere, respectively. Local dielectric perturbations quantify this constituent preference: the E 1 u -like shift is 9.9 times larger for torus than for sphere loading, and the χ 1 -like shift is 3.9 times larger for sphere loading. The two-channel response matrix reproduces all 15 pairwise wavelength differences among six simultaneously loaded states with maximum range-normalized residuals below 4.1%. A sphere–rod example shows that orientation-dependent excitation of different rod modes accompanies changes in local cross-response, illustrating the role of eigenmode assignment in interpreting the measured channels.

articles.title: Warming up ground-state orbitals: A route to excitation energies?
articles.abstract: Linear-response time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) is the workhorse of spectral prediction, yet it can struggle to predict or even describe important low-lying excitation energies. An alternative is to use static formalisms to target excited-state energies directly from variational density functional theory (DFT). This may involve using custom excited-state functionals or feeding excited-state orbitals and densities into standard ground-state approximations, and can often be effective, even for describing states for which adiabatic TDDFT fails. However, this comes at the cost of requiring specialized algorithms to find stationary points. In this exploratory work, we demonstrate that finite-temperature DFT can provide an effective auxiliary framework for generating excited-state-like orbitals from ground-state orbitals for modern ensemble and state-specific functionals, such as the GX24 ground-state (G) and excited-state (X) functional. Notably, the necessary fixed-point algorithms are already available and well optimized in many electronic-structure codes.

articles.title: Optical skyrmions can control the motion of magnetic skyrmions
articles.title_zh: 光学skyrmions可以控制磁性skyrmions的运动
articles.abstract: Magnetic skyrmions (MSks) are swirling patterns of magnetization that form inside certain magnetic materials. They can behave like actual particles in many ways, exhibiting a stable internal structure and distinct boundaries. Because they are extremely small and can be pushed around with relatively little energy, MSks are regarded as promising information carriers in emerging technologies, including low-power memories and logic circuits. However, a major goal in the field has been to find practical ways to control their motion with high precision.

articles.title: Platonic Projection Structures: Operator-Induced Observability in Representation Learning
articles.title_zh: 柏拉图投影结构：表征学习中的操作员诱导可观察性
articles.abstract: We introduce Platonic Projection Structures (PPS), an operator-theoretic framework for analyzing observability in representation learning systems. Rather than treating observable outputs as direct reflections of latent representations, PPS models observation as a geometry induced by a self-adjoint positive semidefinite operator acting on a latent Hilbert space. Within PPS, a system is represented as a triple (H, Π, O), where Hdenotes a latent representation space, Π ⪰0 is an observation operator, and O(v) = ⟨v, Πv⟩defines an induced observable quantity. The framework characterizes observability through the quotient geometry H/ ker(Π), which represents equivalence classes of latent states that are indistinguishable under observation. From this perspective, observable behavior is governed not by latent representations themselves, but by the geometry induced through the observation operator. We show that both quantum measurement and deep learning inference can be formulated within this common operator-theoretic structure while differing in the algebraic properties of their observation operators. Within this perspective, quantum measurement serves primarily as a mathematically canonical example of projection-mediated observability. The correspondence developed in PPS is therefore structural rather than physical. Within the same framework, representation transfer and knowledge distillation can be interpreted as approximate preservation of observable geometry through the intertwining condition ΦΠT ≈ΠSΦ. PPS further reveals a structural limitation of output-based interpretability: latent components contained in ker(Π) are fundamentally inaccessible from observables generated through the induced observation process. Accordingly, attribution and explanation methods inherit intrinsic constraints imposed by the observation geometry itself. We provide controlled empirical validations demonstrating kernel-invariant observability, projection-induced attribution gaps, and rank-controlled observable geometry in latent representation spaces. Overall, PPS provides a mathematically explicit operator-theoretic perspective for analyzing observability, interpretability, and representation transfer in projection-mediated learning systems
