Our code is available at https://github.com/TSUITUENYUE/The-Lattice-of-Transition-Laws.

articles.title: Automated Assembly Instruction Generation from CAD Models Using Grounded Large Language Models: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.11896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Assembly documentation is a downstream manufacturing artifact that is still usually authored by interpreting CAD models by hand. Structured product data and large language models are both available, yet studies of CAD interpretation, assembly sequence planning, instruction writing, and human oversight have largely proceeded separately. This paper formulates CAD-grounded assembly instruction generation: the production of natural-language assembly procedures constrained by structured engineering information extracted from CAD models. The proposed framework maps a STEP assembly to a typed ProductGraph intermediate representation, derives a precedence order by deterministic topological sorting, realizes each step as language conditioned only on selected graph context, attaches per-step visual documentation, and applies rule-based and model-assisted checks. PDF export remains disabled until a human reviewer resolves every quality flag. The case study establishes endto-end feasibility on a built-in six-part reference assembly: the pipeline preserves a reported assembly order and carries quantity, material, and torque into an exported manual page. Generalization and geometric validation remain open empirical questions. The contribution is an architecture that separates engineering state, deterministic reasoning, grounded language realization, verification, and human release.

articles.title: Verification and Self-Improvement in Agentic AI: Foundations and Limits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.10611v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic AI systems can improve by searching longer, receiving additional support, or modifying how they propose and verify outputs. A performance score does not distinguish these mechanisms. We compare these changes through bounded verification with hidden terminal randomness. A stage specifies admissible transcripts, polynomial bounds, an alternating verification protocol, and a terminal checker. Its native reach uses default support; its closure frontier permits all support already admitted by the interface. Under a uniform pointwise probability gap and task-relative soundness, these are well-defined languages. We prove that independent majority amplification preserves both languages, whereas existential acceptance over random tapes can admit incorrect outputs. Exact verification is the zero-randomness case, with placement and completeness results. The randomized-verifier classes satisfy ΣₖPsubseteqΣₖRVsubseteqΣₖ₊₁P; strict enlargement and depth separation require explicit complexity assumptions, while BPP=P yields exact companions with the same frontiers. Representation analysis separates invariant acceptance from core-versus-support labels that can change under refactoring. For recursive self-improvement, uniformly bounded self-modification under a common sound interpreter and fixed verification protocol remains within the same verification class. A separate conditional-error budget controls false selection across adaptively chosen candidates. A quota-enforced XOR-synthesis family separates unbounded ratios of search success from changes in the accepted languages; exact and probabilistic audits check the resulting evidence requirements. The framework ties self-improvement claims to obligations on correctness, admissible evidence, verification resources, and selection error.

articles.title: The Harness as the Only Mutable Surface: Compliance-Bounded Self-Evolution of LLM Agents in Credit Pipelines, with a Measured Admission Gate
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.10629v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-improving LLM agents can adapt a credit pipeline to a changed rule, but an agent that rewrites itself destroys the artefact a supervisor reviews: a named change, a recorded test, an approval. We argue that self-evolution is reviewable only if it is confined to the runtime harness (instruction text, tool-call logic and primitive composition) while model weights stay fixed, so that every adaptation is a diff with a cause and a test attached. We give a dual-loop engine built on that bound, with one admission gate that writes a hash-chained record before deployment, and we measure the gate in simulation, with a simulated agent and a seeded-search proposer rather than language models. Across three families of supervisory re-interpretation at three severities, 10 seeds each, the gated loop admitted 144 of 7,449 candidate changes, none of which worsened error on held-out history, and restored the false-positive rate to the oracle level without raising missed flags in every low- and mid-severity cell. With the gate replaced by the check an unbounded system applies (fewer errors visible in recent traces), the same loops admitted 309 harmful changes and left missed flags above 10% in 49 of 90 runs: false positives fell because the screen was loosened. Evaluated on pre-shift labels, the gate rejected every candidate, so a re-interpretation must be encoded as a rule that relabels history. Parametric and scope shifts were repaired locally, a structural one only by primitive replacement; at the highest structural severity the gate's fixed tolerance blocked the correct replacement in half the seeds. We map the mechanisms to the EU AI Act's provisions for high-risk credit scoring and note that the April 2026 US model-risk guidance excludes agentic AI from its scope.

articles.title: TypedBench: A Benchmark for Calibration, Framing Sensitivity, and Cost in System One Decision Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.11392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: System One models output calibrated probabilities over typed answers such as categorical choices, ordinal levels, or binary outcomes, via a non-generative interface. Software can act on these probabilities through thresholds, cost-weighted choices, and escalation rules. Consequently, if these probabilities are miscalibrated or wording-sensitive, the software ma take unintended actions leaving human operators with no textual rationale to inspect. Current evaluations largely report accuracy and calibration on public classification datasets without a clear reference. We present TypedBench, a benchmark for typed decision models like Jev built from seven policy-labelled generators and nine evaluation suites. We report accuracy as median and range across paraphrases, and calibration error relative to the finite-sample noise floor of a matched, perfectly calibrated predictor. We assess probability quality through selective prediction, ordinal proper scoring rules, and realised cost under asymmetric cost matrices. We evaluate a hosted model, an open encoder, and a family of open decoders spanning 0.8B-9B parameters on identical items. The hosted model follows the stated policy but is wording-sensitive and systematically underconfident; under asymmetric costs, using its probabilities can be worse than taking its top answer. Decoders route exactly and are slow as options or questions are added. The decoder is least accurate on policy questions and degrades with more options. Overall, typed decision models must be evaluated jointly on policy adherence, wording robustness, probability quality, and induced decision outcomes.

articles.title: AgentEvolver: System-Wide Self-Evolution Through Task Execution
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.11613v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An agent can complete a task without improving how it works. Turning task experience into reusable capability requires connecting the changed component to its evaluation and subsequent use. We present AgentEvolver, a system for developing capabilities during task execution while keeping the foundation model fixed. Eight entity families expose reusable operations, methods, agents, control flow, interfaces, and supporting state to revision through a common versioned lifecycle. A shared Runtime coordinates ongoing work, while persistent planning and recoverable context preserve task direction and supporting evidence. We evaluate task outcomes on SWE-bench Pro Public and examine capability changes in six application cases. The team reports an 82.08% resolution rate with evolution, exceeding its reported baseline without evolution. The cases show retained capabilities entering later website, game, and research work, while also documenting incomplete objectives and an unsuccessful strategy. These findings distinguish improvement in a reusable component from success on the final task. AgentEvolver provides a concrete basis for studying capability accumulation through execution; independent-task transfer and total development cost remain open questions.

articles.title: An Interpretable Approach to PDE Solution Discovery via Structural Experience Distillation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12003v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: PDE solution discovery aims to identify explicit symbolic expressions for unknown physical fields from observations under known physical constraints. Existing methods, however, collapse data fidelity and physical consistency into a single terminal score used as the sole feedback signal, providing little information about which subexpressions are responsible for a candidate's final performance. This opaque terminal feedback severely limits the interpretability of the search process itself, offering no insight into why a candidate succeeds or fails. Consequently, reusable structures in otherwise suboptimal candidates are often discarded, whereas incidental syntax along successful search trajectories may be repeatedly reinforced. We propose SED-MCTS, a Monte Carlo tree search approach that distills structural experience from evaluated expressions and reuses it to guide subsequent symbolic solution search. Through counterfactual subtree interventions, SED-MCTS estimates local structural contributions, routes reliable evidence to the responsible construction edges, and preserves useful components in a refined structural archive. The approach naturally extends to coupled multiphysics systems. Across a diverse suite of PDE benchmarks, SED-MCTS achieves strong performance under a fixed evaluation budget and improves search efficiency and robustness under noisy or scarce observations.

articles.title: Structure Tax: How Structured Output affects LLMs Performance
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12056v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deploying large language models in production often requires constraining outputs to structured formats such as JSON or XML, and prior work treats the resulting accuracy loss as an inherent `structure tax'. We re-examine this claim by evaluating a battery of models, datasets and schemas, measuring task accuracy, confidence calibration, and hidden-state geometry. The tax turns out to depend on schema design rather than on structure per se: reasoning-first field ordering matches or exceeds free-form accuracy, while answer-first ordering causes steep drops, particularly in smaller models. Format sensitivity scales inversely with a task's own structural constraints, and schemas that preserve reasoning order also improve calibration with CKA showing greater separability between correct and incorrect representations in middle transformer layers. Our findings indicate that properly designed structured formats can match or exceed free-form performance, reframing the critical question from `whether to structure' to `how to structure' for optimal reasoning preservation.

articles.title: RFChipAgent: Multi-Agentic AI Flow for Analog/RF Chip Design
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.10858v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Analog/RF circuits remain the critical interface between digital computation and the physical world, and emerging standards from Wi-Fi 7 to 6G place stringent demands on them, yet analog/RF design remains one of the most labor-intensive steps in chip development. We present RFChipAgent, a first-of-its-kind multi-agent flow of large language model (LLM) agents for end-to-end analog/RF circuit design automation, in which AI agents collaboratively orchestrate the complete design flow under human supervision. RFChipAgent is built around four technical pillars. First, a multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) subsystem with private per-document FAISS indexing extracts design knowledge from existing engineering documentation. Second, a topology agent drives topology selection, and a schematic and testbench agent automates circuit and testbench assembly. Third, a closed-loop hybrid circuit-sizing engine combines Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) and CMA-ES optimization, evaluating every candidate in a simulator-in-the-loop framework. Fourth, a trust-scored simulation database accumulates verified performance data and builds an adaptive optimization model that informs subsequent trials. We validate RFChipAgent on a family of GF22FDSOI 60 GHz wideband mm-wave low-noise amplifier (LNA) topologies, demonstrating automated topology generation, specification-driven design-space exploration, and simulator-guided optimization. Experimental results show substantial reductions in design effort while maintaining signoff-quality verification. This work establishes a foundation for LLM-driven multi-agent electronic design automation (EDA) for analog/RF circuits.

articles.title: Speedbumps: Rejection Attacks on Speculative Decoding
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.10929v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Speculative decoding is a popular technique for increasing the speed and reducing the costs of large language model (LLM) inference by verifying multiple draft tokens in a single target-model forward pass. The resulting benefit depends on the ability of the drafter to approximate the target model's distribution. In this work, we study Speculative Rejection Attacks (SRAs), a novel class of attacks that cause draft and target models to disagree more often, resulting in fewer draft tokens being accepted per draft cycle. This leads to more target model forward passes needed per generated token, slowing down inference and increasing costs for the victim. We introduce two attacks which append an adversarial suffix to attacker-controlled content to degrade speculative decoding on a victim's prompts. Both attacks optimise the expected length of the accepted speculative prefix, estimating per-depth acceptance from the target's probability of the drafted proposals (Speedbump-P) or from the overlap between the draft and target distributions (Speedbump-D). In some cases, attacks degrade speculative decoding to the point of being slower than autoregressive decoding. The degradation reduces the output quality - regularisation restores output quality but gives up most of the degradation, trading effectiveness for stealthiness. Additionally, the suffixes remain effective under sampling, and transfer across drafters (Speedbump-P) or across target models sharing a drafter (Speedbump-D). These findings identify the draft-target interaction of speculative decoding as a realistic attack surface through which adversarial inputs can inflate inference costs.

articles.title: Continuous Ground-Truth Construction and a Recovery Policy for Air--Water Robotic Tracking
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.11096v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Visual tracking across the air-water interface is challenged by splashes, bubbles, refraction, reflections, and abrupt appearance changes that can temporarily invalidate observations. This setting poses two coupled difficulties: first, for evaluation, image-only annotation cannot reliably describe the target's physical location during visual blindness; second, for online tracking, corrupted observations can contaminate motion estimates and appearance templates. We address the first difficulty with a construction pipeline that synchronizes camera frames with motion-capture poses, projects known target geometry, corrects underwater projection with a medium-gated residual, and subjects the annotations to manual review. This yields an evaluation-only cross-medium test set of 22,346 frames. We further introduce a Cross-Medium Recovery Policy (CMRP) centered on confidence-triggered template selection. It supplies MixFormerV2 with the fixed initial template, a window-best pre-trigger template, and a trigger-frame Kalman-guided image crop, together with their associated weights, without retraining the visual backbone. In the accuracy evaluation, CMRP achieves 49.90 Macro Success AUC, 2.95 points above MixFormerV2 Official. On selected cross-medium transition and occlusion-recovery intervals, CMRP increases MixFormerV2 tracking coverage from 47.91% to 50.43% relative to Official updating, while mean loss-to-recovery latency over successfully recovered videos decreases from 55.3 to 49.3 frames.

articles.title: Effect of Ionic Liquid Incorporation on Sodium-Ion Conducting Gel Polymer Electrolytes Based on PVDF-HFP and Sodium Triflate
articles.abstract: In this work, sodium ion conducting gel polymer electrolytes (GPEs) based on 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium trifluoromethanesulfonate (BMIMTf) ionic liquid (IL) and poly (vinylidenefluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) (PVdF-HFP) copolymer have been studied for their structure and physical properties. The salt, sodium triflate (NaTf) was used to facilitate the sodium ion conduction. All the samples are prepared using the well-known solvent casting method. The IL was added to the polymer-salt mixture in different concentrations to increase the Na+ ion conduction. The resulting membranes are free standing, flexible, non-volatile, and thermally stable up to 400 oC. Among the studied samples, the maximum room temperature ionic conductivity was 4.66 mS cm-1 for the GPE having 67 wt.% IL. The x-ray diffraction (XRD) spectra showed a reduction in the degree of crystallinity and an increase in amorphous phase content of IL added GPEs. In addition, the decrease of melting temperature (Tm) and glass transition temperature (Tg) values with the incorporation of IL seen in the differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) thermograms points towards the improved segmental flexibility of the polymer chains. These findings demonstrated that the addition of IL has a clear influence on the structure and physical properties of the PVdF-HFP: NaTf mixture, resulting in increased mobility of conducting ions via structural changes, as further confirmed by FTIR vibrational spectroscopy.

articles.title: Accelerated Early 21st-century Warming from Declining Aerosol Emissions and its Implications for Near-term Climate Change
articles.abstract: Global aerosol emissions have declined rapidly since peaking around 2005, substantially weakening the aerosol-induced cooling effect on climate. Using updated historical emissions, we show that this decline, driven primarily by reduced sulphur emissions, enhanced trends in global-mean surface temperature and Earth's energy imbalance by approximately 0.07oC decade-1 and 0.09~W~m-2decade-1, respectively, equivalent to 0.14oC of additional warming over 2005-2025. This rapid decline in aerosol emissions broadly aligned with the earlier strong-mitigation pathway, while greenhouse gas emissions remained close to the intermediate pathway. Analyses of newer emission scenarios indicate that, if these diverging aerosol and greenhouse gas emission trajectories persist, they could contribute an additional 0.1oC of warming by 2050, causing the 1.5oC and 2oC warming thresholds to be reached two to four years earlier. Therefore, limiting warming to below 2oC may require steeper greenhouse gas emission reductions if aerosol emissions continue to decline faster than projected in these new scenarios.

articles.title: Electrolyte and Voltage Operating Window for Reversible Plasmid Capture
articles.abstract: Electro-modulated separation enables ligand-free capture and release of charged biomolecules through electrically controlled interactions with conductive surfaces. This study defined the operating window for reversible capture of the model plasmid pVAX1 on non-functionalized pencil graphite electrodes by evaluating applied cell voltage, initial plasmid concentration, buffer composition, electrolyte conditions, and plasmid stability. In deionized water, increasing the applied voltage accelerated plasmid depletion, with +1.6 V providing the fastest capture within the investigated range. Near-complete depletion was obtained at initial concentrations up to 300 mg L⁻¹, whereas capture remained incomplete at 400 mg L⁻¹. Ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid-containing media generated voltage-dependent ultraviolet absorbance interference and were unsuitable for reliable plasmid quantification by absorbance. Higher electrolyte concentrations at +1.6 V were associated with visible precipitation, heterogeneous concentration readouts, bulk acidification, altered electrokinetic behavior, and reduced reversibility. In contrast, deionized water, 10 mM tris(hydroxymethyl)aminomethane, and 1 mM sodium chloride supported reversible capture without visible precipitation. In 10 mM sodium chloride, operation at +1.0 V was not accompanied by visible destabilization. These findings demonstrate that applied voltage and electrolyte composition jointly define compatible conditions for reversible plasmid capture and provide an experimentally grounded framework for further development of electro-modulated nucleic-acid separation.

articles.title: Microstructural and Mechanical Properties of Additive Friction Stir Deposited Aluminum 7050 Alloy
articles.abstract: Solid-state Friction Stir Additive Manufacturing offers a melt-free route to produce high-strength aluminum alloys by avoiding the solidification defects that limit conventional fusion-based AM. In this study, AA7050 was deposited by AFSD and subsequently subjected to hot isostatic pressing to eliminate the effects of defects/pores and unbonded regions on tensile behavior. As-deposited AFSD AA7050 retained most of the wrought tensile strength (UTS ≈ 404–468 MPa, versus ≈ 507 MPa for wrought AA7050) and exhibited comparable hardness (~ 175 ± 5 HV), yet failed with ~ zero uniform elongation compared with ~ 19% for the wrought AA7050. EBSD revealed a clear layer/interlayer hierarchy comprising coarse, elongated grains in the layer interiors and ultra-fine equiaxed grains concentrated in reheated interlayers. XRD showed an α-Al-dominated matrix in AFSD with the absence of discrete second-phase reflections. Fractography, however, demonstrated that macroscopic embrittlement was primarily governed by large pores and lack-of-bond defects at interlayer boundaries. Cracks initiated and propagated along these defects, while regions between them exhibited shallow dimples, characteristic of ductile micro-void coalescence in AA7050. Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP) removed the large defects and homogenized the microstructure, but also severely coarsened the η′/η precipitates. Consequently, HIPed AFSD AA7050 exhibited reduced strength (UTS ≈ 316–324 MPa) but showed improved ductility (~ 18–19% elongation) comparable to the wrought AA7050. The results quantitatively demonstrate a strong trade-off between defect elimination and precipitation, and highlight that AFSD process design for AA7050 must simultaneously control porosity, interlayer bonding, and precipitate stability to achieve wrought-like strength–ductility combinations without over-reliance on aggressive HIP treatments.

articles.title: Effect of Metal Transfer Mode on Local Chemical Inhomogeneity in Dual-Wire Electron Beam Additive Manufacturing of Nitinol
articles.abstract: Local chemical inhomogeneities are the primary obstacle to producing NiTi shape memory alloys with reproducible functional properties by dual-wire electron beam additive manufacturing (EBAM). This study investigates the mechanisms of their formation and identifies the technological conditions for their suppression. Using smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) simulation, high-speed videography, and metallographic analysis, the convergence angle β of the wire feed nozzles was found to be the key parameter controlling the metal transfer mode. At β ≥ 30°, droplet transfer of the nickel wire was observed, caused by the difference in surface tension coefficients of liquid nickel and titanium, resulting in asynchronous delivery of components to the melt pool and formation of zones with disrupted stoichiometry. At β = 15°, mixing was governed solely by the electron beam deflection pattern through two separate transfer bridges. At parallel wire feeding (β = 0°), component mixing began prior to entry into the melt pool, forming a single stable transfer bridge. Optical flow analysis of high-speed recordings showed that at β = 0° the time margin for convective homogenisation reaches ~ 67% compared to ~ 7% at β = 30°. The mean deviation of the chemical composition coefficient γ from the target value decreased from 3.6% at β = 30° to 0.4% at β = 0°. Metallographic analysis confirmed a uniform NiTi matrix and homogeneous hardness distribution (358–385 HV5) in samples produced at β = 0°.

articles.title: Crystallographic Orientation of the Substrate Enables Micromole-Level Lithium-Mediated Ammonia Synthesis at 500 mA cm-2
articles.abstract: The transition of the lithium-mediated nitrogen reduction reaction (Li-NRR) toward industrial application remains a formidable challenge. Achieving stable operation under ampere-level current density is particularly pivotal in this regard. An ideal solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) plays a decisive role in determining the overall efficiency and feasibility. Current research predominantly focuses on bulk electrolyte optimization for SEI control, leaving the direct tailoring of electrode interphase underexplored. This lack of fundamental understanding hinders the achievement of highly efficient and stable Li-NRR toward practical application. Here, we report a strategy to atomic-scale restructure the interfacial microenvironment by engineering Cu substrates with a predominant (220) facet, leveraging the crystallographic orientation to present a definitive pathway for stable interphase. The Cu (220) facet selectively promotes the specific adsorption of anions within the inner Helmholtz plane (IHP), establishing a locally concentrated anion microenvironment even within dilute electrolytes. This facet induced enrichment overrides conventional reduction pathways dominated by solvents, triggering a kinetically accelerated evolution of a thin, robust SEI rich in inorganic components composed primarily of LiF and Li2S. This tailored interphase architecture enhances the interfacial Li+ diffusion coefficient by two orders of magnitude and shortens the N2 transport pathway, effectively balancing the transport of Li+, N2 and H+, enabling the system to sustain a remarkable 1.1 µmol s− 1 cm− 2 ammonia production rate at a sustained current density of -500 mA cm− 2. This work demonstrates that atomic scale manipulation of substrate crystallography can dictate macroscopic interphase chemistry, charting a robust and scalable pathway for high flux electrochemical synthesis.

articles.title: Process-Structure-Property Relationships and Multi-Response Optimization of Z-Direction MEX-Printed Polyphenylene Sulfide
articles.abstract: Material extrusion (MEX) of polyphenylene sulfide (PPS) is strongly governed by interlayer consolidation, particularly under Z-direction loading. However, whether minimizing the overall apparent porosity also maximizes Z-direction mechanical performance remains unclear. This study investigates the effects of nozzle temperature (315–345°C), layer thickness (0.1–0.3 mm), and print speed (20–60 mm/s) on Young’s modulus, tensile strength, elongation at break, and density-derived apparent porosity using a face-centred central composite design and response surface methodology. Dynamic mechanical analysis and scanning electron microscopy were used to support the process–structure–property interpretation. The tensile responses were strongly affected by the investigated processing variables, whereas print speed had no significant effect on apparent porosity (p = 0.517). Importantly, the best measured mechanical response occurred at 345°C, 0.1 mm, and 20 mm/s, whereas the minimum apparent porosity occurred at 330°C, 0.2 mm, and 40 mm/s. This divergence demonstrates that minimum bulk porosity does not necessarily correspond to maximum Z-direction performance. The SEM images revealed that better mechanical performance correlates with lesser interlayer spaces as well as higher local fusion. The multi-response optimization method estimated an optimum value at 341.67°C, 0.1 mm, and 20 mm/s. It could be concluded that assessment of the structural integrity of 3D prints in PPS by means of MEX technology is defined by the defects' shape.

articles.title: Advancing Microplastic Analysis in Complex Matrices Towards Harmonization: Insights from an Interlaboratory Study Supporting the Development of a Standardized Extraction Protocol
articles.abstract: Reliable quantification of microplastics in complex environmental matrices remains challenging due to the lack of harmonized extraction procedures and matrix variability. To support standardization of a compost extraction protocol, we conducted an interlaboratory comparison across laboratories with diverse expertise and analytical capabilities. Compost samples were spiked with 33 mg of cryo-milled poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT) and 33 mg of low-density polyethylene (LDPE) particles (50–300 µm) and distributed with blank samples to participating laboratories. All laboratories applied an identical extraction protocol consisting of deagglomeration, Fenton oxidation, and calcium chloride density separation. Each laboratory then used their available technique, including µ-Raman, µ-Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (µ-FTIR), fluorescence microscopy, Pyrolysis-Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry (Py-GC/MS), and Thermal Extraction Desorption-Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry (TED-GC/MS) to identify and quantify the extracted microplastics. All laboratories detected and quantified both target polymers, demonstrating the applicability of the protocol. However, considerable inter- and intra-laboratory variability was observed for particles < 100 µm. Further investigations indicated that variability originated from compost subsampling, dispersion behavior of the particles, and non-harmonized analysis; rather than the extraction procedure. Despite differences in absolute particle counts, relative particle size distributions were comparable. Mass-based methods also identified and quantified both polymers, although recoveries varied across laboratories, reflecting differences in analytical workflows and quantification approaches. Feedback from participating laboratories enabled critical protocol improvements, including optimized Fenton conditions and modifications to the density separation procedure. Overall, this study shows that harmonized extraction of microplastics from compost is feasible and provides a foundation for the ongoing development of ISO/FDIS 24899 and future standardization of microplastic analysis in complex matrices.

articles.title: Beyond Decisionism: Spinoza’s Affective Logic of Political Foundation
articles.abstract: Modern constitutional theory has long been troubled by a foundational difficulty: how can a collective body be credited with the intentionality necessary for the exercise of constituent power? Since Sieyès, and through Schmitt’s decisionist framework, the doctrine has relied upon a sovereign subject capable of a foundational act. Yet the identity of this subject remains elusive. This paper proposes that Spinoza’s political thought provides the resources for overcoming this deadlock. By examining the mechanism of affective imitation (imitatio affectuum), we show that political association arises not from a sovereign decree but from the spontaneous alignment of passions through an impersonal, mimetic dynamic. The paper advances an original thesis: the formation of the legal order is not attributable to a constituent subject, but is rather the outcome of a subjectless process—a continuous interplay of affects that shapes and reshapes the political sphere.

articles.title: Photonic Quantum Simulation of Three-Body Non-Covalent Interactions Using a Generalized Quantum Drude Oscillator Framework
articles.abstract: Context: Non-covalent interactions, especially dispersion interactions, are crucial for defining the stability and structural characteristics of molecular systems, while accurately modeling them becomes increasingly complex for many-body arrangements. The Quantum Drude Oscillator (QDO) model offers a physically meaningful coarse-grained approach to dispersion interactions; however, previous photonic quantum simulations have primarily focused on pairwise interactions. In this work, we introduce an extended three-body Quantum Drude Oscillator (3-QDO) framework to represent geometry-sensitive non-covalent interactions in triangular molecular arrangements. This framework allows for the exploration of symmetric, asymmetric, angular-dependent, and custom-defined three-body geometries. Our simulations reveal that the interaction energy and optimal binding are highly influenced by intermolecular distances and angular arrangements. In the fully variable setup, the global minimum is found near a symmetric configuration, whereas changes in angular parameters can significantly strengthen, diminish, or even eliminate binding. These findings highlight the capability of the 3-QDO framework to advance photonic quantum simulations into the realm of more intricate many-body molecular dynamics. Methods: The three-body QDO system was formulated as three harmonically bound quantum oscillators coupled through pairwise Coulomb interactions and mapped onto a three-mode continuous-variable photonic quantum circuit. The circuit was initialized in the three-mode Fock vacuum and implemented using Gaussian beam-splitter, rotation, squeezing, and displacement operations together with non-Gaussian Kerr gates. Numerical simulations were performed using the Strawberry Fields photonic quantum computing platform with a Fock-space cutoff of 6 and an 81-point position-quadrature grid over X = −6 to 6. Dimensionless units with ℏ = ωᵢ = mᵢ = qᵢ = 1 and an effective Coulomb constant of 0.08 were employed. Binding energies were obtained from the expectation values of the harmonic and Coulomb contributions, and the resulting energy profiles were fitted using a pairwise-summed Morse function.

articles.title: Surface Adsorption to Bulk Storage: Integrating Experimental and Theoretical Insights into Hydrogen Behavior on Palladium
articles.abstract: The interaction of hydrogen with palladium (Pd) forms the basis of numerous applications, including catalysis, biosensing, gas detection, and hydrogen storage technologies, due to the exceptional characteristics of Pd to adsorb, dissociate, and transport hydrogen. In this study, experimental and density functional theory (DFT) analyses are employed to establish a unified understanding regarding the hydrogen adsorption and bulk diffusion in Pd foils and electrochemically fabricated Pd nanowires. Pd nanowires were synthesized using anodized aluminum oxide (AAO) templates, and subsequently characterized by FE-SEM, AFM, XRD and XPS analyses to evaluate their morphology, topography, crystallinity, and surface chemistry. Temperature programmed desorption (TPD) analysis revealed that after surface adsorption and saturation, hydrogen robustly diffuse into the Pd bulk under continuous exposure of hydrogen, with an experimentally determined diffusion barrier of 0.123 eV. However, the evolution of hydrogen is observed to follow zeroth-order kinetics. Despite the relatively rough morphology, Pd nanowires exhibited adsorption characteristics remarkably analogous to that of Pd foils, suggesting that the hydrogen uptake mechanism remains unchanged irrespective of the Pd architectures. DFT analysis provides atomistic insights into the dissociative adsorption of H2 over Pd surface. Furthermore, calculations reveal that the migration of resulting atomic hydrogen from surface to subsurface hollow site is essentially a barrier less (Ea » 0 eV) and thermodynamically exergonic process (DG = –0.53 eV), substantiating the experimentally observed transition from surface adsorption to bulk diffusion. Overall, this study provides a comprehensive framework for hydrogen interaction with Pd, offering guidance for the rational design of Pd-based materials for hydrogen dominated catalysis, sensing, separation, and energy storage applications.

articles.title: Dynamic fusion of displacement parallelism and mass conservation for landslide slip-surface depth inversion from SBAS-InSAR observations: a case study in the Wudongde reservoir area
articles.abstract: Accurate quantification of landslide slip-surface depth and volume is a cornerstone of hazard assessment and risk management, particularly in large reservoir basins where conventional borehole and geophysical surveys are logistically challenging or economically unfeasible. This study proposes a novel dynamic fusion framework that integrates the displacement parallelism principle and mass conservation law to invert the time-varying active thickness of landslides using multi-orbit Sentinel-1 Small Baseline Subset Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (SBAS-InSAR) observations. First, topography-constrained quasi-three-dimensional (quasi-3D) surface displacements are reconstructed from ascending and descending line-of-sight (LOS) measurements. Second, a spatially variable rheological coefficient is calibrated point-by-point using the static slip-surface geometry derived from the geometric method as a benchmark under quasi-steady-state conditions. This calibration enables the mass conservation equation to be solved without cumulative integration errors, yielding time-series slip-surface thickness fields anchored to the static geometric baseline. The framework is applied to active landslides along the Wudongde Hydropower Reservoir in southwestern China. The inverted slip-surface depths range from 15 to 85 m, and the volume of active Jinpingzi landslide is approximately 6.25 × 107 m³. Validation GNSS comparisons show root mean square errors (RMSE) values of 3D displacement is 7.8 mm, 4.2 mm and 2.4 mm in Vertical, Eastern and Northern, respectively. The proposed dynamic fusion approach mitigates the ill-posedness of pure mass-conservation inversion and the oversimplification of purely geometric methods, providing a physically consistent, spatially distributed tool for regional landslide characterization and reservoir hazard management.

articles.title: Terahertz Spectroscopy of Femtosecond-Laser-Induced Frequency Upshifts of the Transverse Optical Phonons in CuInSe2 Nanoparticles
articles.abstract: The impact of optically induced charge transfer between atoms in non-centrosymmetric crystals on theirtransverse optical (TO) phonons is probed using ultrafast terahertz (THz) radiation. By comparing theTHz response of optically excited and pristine CuInSe2 nanoparticles, clear frequency upshifts in the TOphonons are observed. A TO phonon model incorporating local-field corrections is analyzed to explainthese experimental observations. During charge transfer in non-centrosymmetric crystals, the ionicity ofthe individual atoms decreases, reducing the effective charges at the lattice sites. We attribute theobserved TO phonon frequency upshifts to this reduction in effective charge.

articles.title: Climate responses to Antarctic meltwater depend on the timing of meltwater release
articles.abstract: Increasing freshwater fluxes from the Antarctic Ice Sheet are widely recognised to have global impacts, including sea surface cooling extending into the Northern Hemisphere, and Southern Ocean subsurface warming. However, most simulations have imposed Antarctic ice loss rates that are unlikely in a pre-industrial climate, or 'high-end' in a warming climate. To ensure that freshwater forcing is consistent with a warming future climate, we here use historically-calibrated, highest-likelihood ice sheet projections to constrain Antarctic freshwater forcing in the Norwegian Earth System Model until 2300. In clear contrast to earlier studies, the projected freshwater forcing only induces weak global responses in sea-surface temperature and ocean circulation. Despite the weak global responses, Southern Ocean subsurface warming develops, albeit delayed until at least the late 21st century. Additional experiments with freshwater forcing increasing 40 years earlier or under pre-industrial conditions yield substantially stronger climate responses, and highlight that climatic impacts of Antarctic meltwater depend sensitively on the timing of meltwater increases relative to Southern Ocean precipitation increases. While our results suggest much weaker global responses than have previously been reported, Southern Ocean subsurface warming that threatens ice sheet stability underlines the importance of ongoing efforts to quantify ice-ocean feedbacks with coupled ice sheet - ocean modelling.

articles.title: Coupled structural evolution and elemental redistribution in zigzag Pt3Fe nanowires revealed by in situ electrochemical liquid-cell TEM
articles.abstract: Shape and compositional control are widely used to tailor electrocatalyst properties, yet how these deliberately engineered features evolve under operating conditions remains poorly understood, obscuring the relationship between the as-synthesized catalyst and its active state. Here, we directly track the evolution of shape-controlled zigzag Pt₃Fe nanowires during the hydrogen evolution reaction under weakly alkaline conditions using in situ electrochemical liquid-cell transmission electron microscopy (EC-TEM), complemented by in situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), elemental analysis, electron tomography, and electrostatic simulations. Operando EC-TEM reveals that the initially well-defined zigzag nanowires undergo spatially heterogeneous morphological evolution, including protrusion growth and nanoparticle formation preferentially at high-curvature regions. Correlated elemental mapping reveals selective Fe depletion and the formation of Pt-rich surface structures, while in situ XAS reveals increased Pt–Pt and decreased Pt–Fe coordination together with changes in the Fe chemical environment under HER conditions. Three-dimensional electron tomography resolves the zigzag nanowires as thin, plate-like structure rather than the previously proposed spiral-like geometry. Electrostatic simulations based on the experimentally determined geometry reveal electrostatic heterogeneity at high-curvature regions, providing a possible link between the nanowire geometry and the spatial preference of the observed morphological evolution. Together, these findings reveal coupled morphological evolution and elemental redistribution in shape-controlled alloy catalysts during electrochemical reactions. More broadly, these findings establish catalyst morphology as a dynamic parameter that not only defines the initial structure but also influences its subsequent evolution, highlighting dynamic structural evolution as an integral component of structure–property relationships in multicomponent electrocatalysts.

articles.title: Request Segmentation and Metadata Leakage in Low-Rate GPUPower Telemetry: A Single-Platform Audi
articles.abstract: Software-accessible graphics processing unit power telemetry can expose workload metadata, but request boundaries are often easier to obtain in an experiment than in an attack. We audit this distinction on one NVIDIA RTX 2080 Ti using continuous telemetry from two GPT-2 models. A post-hoc reanalysis preserves an archived development, validation, and test split comprising 36 sessions, including ten test sessions with 583 monitored requests. The archived passive detector and classifier achieve class-balanced correct identification of 0.076 over all requests. An oracle-window classifier trained on the identical 144 development events achieves 0.764; using all 1,043 observable development requests raises it to 0.887. The detected score exceeds its 0.052 coverage-adjusted random-label reference. Only 60 requests are matched, all generation requests. The duration and overlap rules mechanically exclude 110 of 117 prefill requests; relaxing duration alone still finds none. A validation-selected candidate-change detector, with its classifier retrained, increases the all-request score to 0.127 but produces more false alarms. Replacing degenerate normalization using development-derived scales yields 0.100 for the validation-selected pipeline. Amplitude-only and timing-only ablations both retain conditional signal. Two new ten-second hardware measurements observe approximately 9.8 power-value changes per second despite more than 1,000 interface calls per second. These results support evaluating detection coverage, false alarms, training supervision, and conditional inference together. They establish limitations of evaluated pipelines on one platform, rather than a general security guarantee.

articles.title: Thermodynamic landscapes of conformational regulation during intrinsically disordered protein fibrillation
articles.abstract: Amyloid fibrillation of intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) involves a disorder-to-order transition driven by complex sequence-dependent interactions. However, how amino acid sequences and conformational ordering reshape the multi-chain free-energy landscape during fibril formation remains poorly understood. Here, we combine the hybrid-resolution coarse-grained HyRes model with umbrella sampling to reconstruct the potentials of mean force governing successive stages of IDP fibrillation, including free-chain association, fibril-surface recruitment, and multilayer fibril growth. Using α -synuclein, transactive response DNA-binding protein of 43 kDa (TDP-43), and a fibrillar-core construct of fused in sarcoma (FUS-FC) as representative amyloid-forming IDPs, we demonstrate that sequence-encoded electrostatic interactions are a major determinant of association free energies. α -Synuclein exhibits the strongest attraction and salt sensitivity, whereas TDP-43 shows weaker electrostatically regulated interactions. Association of the isolated FUS fibrillar core remains thermodynamically unfavorable, whereas inclusion of nonfibrillar regions makes association favorable. Charge-neutralization simulations further reveal the critical role of electrostatics and charge patterning in controlling association. Conformational restraints and fibrillar surface organization further modulate the free-energy landscape in a protein-specific manner, with recruitment governed by the accessibility and arrangement of surface interaction sites rather than fibril thickness alone. These results provide a thermodynamic framework connecting sequence, conformation, and surface organization to the molecular mechanisms of amyloid assembly.

articles.title: Relaxation dynamics in strongly coupled spin systems in zero- to ultralow-field NMR spectroscopy
articles.abstract: Nuclear spin population lifetimes encode information regarding molecular-tumbling regimes and interatomic distances in solution with sub-nanometer resolution. In the zero- to ultralow-field (ZULF) regime, population and coherence decays reveal complex behavior due to strong coupling between nuclear spins. We describe herein polarization lifetimes measured for a 13 C-labeled formic acid sample, with an atomic-magnetometer-based ZULF setup, and present a theoretical framework to understand and model the observed effects. Individual peaks resolved by quadrature detection show different signal decay depending on the shuttling profile from a (pre)polarizing region to the detection region at ultralow fields, the strength of the measurement field, and the nutation angle induced by the excitation pulse. The relaxation model incorporates field-dependent dipole–dipole interactions and random field fluctuations. The multiexponential dynamics of spin populations is a general feature of any heteronuclear spin system at ultralow fields. The control of resonance peak lifetimes could be used for optimizing ZULF experiments, for spectral assignment, and for deriving structural and dynamical features of molecules by interpreting relaxation processes at nano- to microtesla magnetic fields.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Vibrationally inelastic scattering of NO from metal surfaces: A partial mean-field approach
articles.abstract: Vibrationally inelastic scattering of NO from metal surfaces probes electronically nonadiabatic molecule–surface dynamics. Experiments have reported multi-quantum relaxation and a work function dependence associated with transient charge transfer. In this work, we develop a partial mean-field approach for a Newns–Anderson model of NO scattering. The molecule–surface distance is treated classically using the mean-field approach, whereas the NO stretch, molecular electronic states, and metal electron bath are treated quantum mechanically with fermionic hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM). Benchmarks against fully quantum HEOM simulations show that the new approach reproduces transient electron transfer and mean vibrational–translational trajectories. It also reproduces the final vibrational distributions over a range of initial vibrational states, incident energies, hybridization widths, and coupling strengths. We then apply the method to NO( ν = 2) scattering from ultrathin Ag/Au(111) films. Both shifted and interpolated potential models reproduce the main work function dependence: lower work function increases transient NO − population and enhances relaxation, especially in the ν = 2 → 0 channel. Together, these results show that the partial mean-field approach can accurately describe direct NO scattering with a classical translational coordinate, provided that the NO vibration and electronic degrees of freedom are treated quantum mechanically.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Methods for inferring interaction potentials from cross-linking mass spectrometry data
articles.abstract: Cross-linking mass spectrometry (XL-MS) has emerged as a powerful quantitative technique for probing intra-protein structural information as well as protein–protein interactions at an unprecedented scale. XL-MS data yield information on the pairwise spatial proximity of proteins through intermolecular linkers. However, systematic methods for adapting such data for coarse-grained interacting particle models remain limited. Predominant focus has been put on directly fitting radial distribution functions (RDFs), while observables such as coordination numbers, as functionals of the RDF, cannot be uniquely inverted. In addition, complexities such as phase separation and mixing of multiple components make these methods largely unsuitable. In this work, we develop a framework for parameterizing interaction potentials in potentially phase-separated mixtures and demonstrate their applicability to XL-MS results. We establish a connection to the inverse Henderson problem and adapt algorithms such as Iterative Boltzmann Inversion and Iterative Monte Carlo for its numerical solution. We derive exact and low-density limit gradient approximations and propose new algorithms based on a predictor–corrector framework. We evaluate several optimization approaches in biologically realistic ten-component test systems and demonstrate exceptional efficiency and accuracy for homogeneous fluids by all methods. We further demonstrate successful potential parameterization in a three-phase system. Here, three algorithms, namely Adam and gradient descent employing the low-density derivative and Newton’s method with the exact gradient, reliably recover the correct parameters. These results establish a clear pathway from XL-MS experiments to coarse-grained protein models for systems where phase separation governs the biological function, potentially enabling new investigations of biomolecular condensates and protein aggregation.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Pressure–temperature phase diagram from global structure prediction and self-consistent phonon calculations based on polynomial machine learning potentials: Application to elemental silicon
articles.abstract: Polynomial machine learning potentials (MLPs) based on polynomial rotational invariants have been systematically developed for various systems and applied to efficiently predict crystal structures. In this study, we propose a methodology founded on polynomial MLPs to enumerate crystal structures under high-pressure conditions and evaluate their phase stability at finite temperatures. The proposed approach involves constructing polynomial MLPs with high predictive accuracy across a broad range of pressures, conducting reliable global structure searches for structures containing up to the specified number of atoms, and performing exhaustive self-consistent phonon calculations with reduced errors. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach by examining elemental silicon at pressures up to 100 GPa and temperatures up to 1000 K, revealing stable phases across these conditions. The framework established in this study offers a powerful strategy for predicting crystal structures and phase stability under high-pressure and finite-temperature conditions.

articles.title: Static vs Herzberg–Teller spin–orbit coupling under symmetry-reducing distortion in multi-resonance TADF emitters
articles.abstract: Multi-resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence emitters typically rely on rigid, symmetry-defined molecular frameworks to achieve narrowband emission and small singlet–triplet energy gaps (Δ E ST ), but such symmetry often suppresses static spin–orbit coupling (SOC), making reverse intersystem crossing (RISC) dependent on vibronic assistance. Here, the recently reported emitter 2S-BN was adopted as a model system to examine how molecular-symmetry reduction, accompanied by non-planar structural distortion, affects spin-conversion pathways. Two symmetry-reduced derivatives, A and B, were computationally designed through peripheral substituent removal and asymmetric framework modification. Density functional theory, SOC calculations, and thermal vibration correlation function simulations reveal that the C 2v -symmetric parent 2S-BN exhibits nearly vanishing Franck–Condon SOC, whereas the symmetry-reducing structural modifications make finite static FC-SOC contributions accessible in A and B, with values of ∼0.20 and 0.18 cm −1 , respectively. The absorption and emission energies remain comparable across the series, suggesting preservation of the essential multi-resonance character. Under the same computational protocol, the calculated k RISC values of A and B are only ∼3.3 and 2.2 times larger than those of 2S-BN. This modest increase is not caused by a larger total effective SOC; the effective SOC of 2S-BN exceeds those of A and B. In the present rate model, the k ISC values remain nearly unchanged, because a large FCWD-related factor offsets the smaller |SOCeff| 2 of A and B. The faster k RISC then follows mainly from their smaller ΔESTadi through the Boltzmann relation. Within this molecular series, symmetry reduction, inseparably accompanied by non-planar distortion, therefore provides a handle on the accessibility of static vs vibronic SOC contributions rather than a standalone control of the RISC rate.

articles.title: Fluorene radical anion isomers: Computed photodetachment spectra, singlet–triplet energy splittings, and computational thermochemistry
articles.abstract: Fluorene (FL) possesses a characteristic π-electron conjugation, resulting in its diverse utilization as a molecular scaffold in fields such as organic electronics, biochemistry, combustion science, and the synthesis of electroluminescent materials. Whereas the vibrational structures of the ground singlet (S 0 ) and the lowest-lying triplet (T 1 ) electronic states in 9H–FL have previously been investigated using techniques such as matrix-isolation Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, electron attachment to FL isomers remains largely unexplored. In this work, geometries and vibrational frequencies from the density functional theory B3LYP/6-311++G (2d, 2p) level of theory are utilized to predict the vibrational structures of the S 0 and T 1 states in 9H–FL, 1H–FL, 2H–FL, 3H–FL, and 4H–FL via the computation of the Franck–Condon factors. Whereas the S 0 state in 9H–FL is unbound, the 1H–FL, 2H–FL, 3H–FL, and 4H–FL isomers form stable anions and have calculated adiabatic electron affinity values of 0.990, 1.282, 0.569, and 1.561 eV. The adiabatic origins of the T 1 states in 1H–FL, 2H–FL, 3H–FL, 4H–FL, and 9H–FL lie at 2.350, 1.706, 2.271, 1.790, and 2.777 eV above their respective anionic states, yielding singlet–triplet energy splittings ΔEST of 1.360, 0.421, 1.701, 0.233, and 2.780 eV. The negative ion photoelectron spectra representing the electron detachment to form the S 0 and T 1 states exhibit pronounced 0–0 transitions that are suggestive of the subtle geometric changes between the anions and corresponding neutrals. The computed thermochemistry data reveal that the 9H–FL has the strongest sp 3 C–H bond dissociation energy and is the least acidic.

articles.title: Infrared spectroscopy of MO(CH 4 ) n (M = Ce, Y; n = 1–3) reveals two distinct adsorption configurations
articles.abstract: Investigation of the interactions of methane with metal oxides is crucial for elucidating absorption configurations at active sites of catalysts, which has proven to be a challenging experimental target due to the difficulty in size selection of neutral systems. In this work, the interactions of methane with rare earth metal oxides are studied by using size-specific infrared-vacuum ultraviolet spectroscopy and quantum chemical calculations. Two distinct configurations of methane adsorption are found in the MO(CH 4 ) n (M = Ce, Y; n = 1–3) complexes. In the first configuration, the C and H atoms of methane are positioned between a Lewis acid-base pair (M 2+ –O 2− ); in the second configuration, one H atom of methane is oriented toward a Lewis basic oxygen anion (O 2− ). Such adsorption features of methane on cerium and yttrium monoxides are dominantly governed by electrostatic interactions. These findings provide key microscopic information for methane adsorption on metal oxides that are helpful for understanding the crucial initial steps in the catalytic cycles.

articles.title: Rovibrational spectroscopy of 1,4-dioxane in the mid-infrared range from high resolution jet-cooled and long path cell measurements
articles.abstract: This study presents a high-resolution rovibrational investigation of 1,4-dioxane in the mid-infrared region, motivated by the need for accurate spectroscopic data in the context of atmospheric monitoring of this emerging pollutant. Jet-cooled spectra were recorded using two complementary setups: a continuous supersonic jet coupled to the Fourier transform spectrometer of the AILES beamline at the SOLEIL synchrotron facility (Jet-AILES) and a quantum cascade laser spectrometer coupled to a pulsed jet (SPIRALES). These measurements were combined with long-path cell spectra at room temperature and supported by anharmonic quantum chemical calculations. Four fundamental vibrational bands (ν 34 , ν 33 , ν 16 , and ν 15 ) were analyzed at high resolution, leading to the assignment of more than 6100 rovibrational transitions. A global fit yielded accurate ground- and excited-state rotational and centrifugal distortion parameters. The results significantly improve the spectroscopic characterization of 1,4-dioxane and provide reliable line lists for future atmospheric detection in the mid-infrared range.

articles.title: Study on the removal efficiency of Cr(VI) from corn cob biochar loaded with zero-valent iron on wastewater
articles.title_zh: 负载零价铁玉米芯生物炭对废水中Cr(VI)的去除效果研究
articles.abstract: In this study, the adsorption of Cr(VI) in wastewater by corncob biochar modified with zero-valent iron was evaluated. The results showed that zero-valent iron modification significantly improved the adsorption effect of Cr(VI) in wastewater. The main research contents and results were as follows:CBC-nZVI was successfully prepared by liquid-phase reduction method with grape seed extract as reducing agent under the optimal iron-carbon ratio of 1:1. The removal rate of Cr(VI) by CBC-nZVI was as high as 96.14%, and the adsorption capacity was increased to 24.04 mg/g, which was 22.59% higher than that of unmodified CBC. The results not only demonstrated the high efficiency of CBC-nZVI in treating wastewater containing Cr(VI), but also confirmed the potential application of grape seed extract as an environmentally friendly reducing agent in environmental treatment.The adsorption process of Cr(VI) by CBC and CBC-nZVI accords with pseudo-second order kinetic model and Langmuir adsorption isotherm model, and it is pointed out that the adsorption process is mainly monolayer chemisorption. In addition, after CBC-nZVI was recycled for 5 times, the removal rate of Cr(VI) remained at around 50%, demonstrating its good stability and reuse potential.The results of SEM, BET, FTIR, XPS and XRD show that CBC and CBC-nZVI have mixed microporous and mesoporous characteristics and amorphous structure, and CBC-nZVI reduces the problem of aggregation of nZVI. Meanwhile, abundant oxygen-containing functional groups endow CBC and CBC-nZVI with excellent adsorption performance, which mainly removes Cr(VI) through electrostatic action, coordination reaction and redox reaction. In addition, the water affinity and surface polarity of the adsorbent also affect the adsorption process.

articles.title: Magnetically Recoverable Fe 2 O 3 /ZSM-5 Composite for Fenton-Like Oxidation of Organic Dyes in Water
articles.title_zh: 磁性可恢复 Fe 2 O 3 /ZSM-5 复合材料用于水中有机染料的类芬顿氧化
articles.abstract: A magnetic Fe2O3-modified ZSM-5 catalyst was synthesized via excessive impregnation for heterogeneous Fenton-like degradation of Rhodamine B (RhB) in dye wastewater. The catalyst possesses well-dispersed iron oxide species and a stable structure, achieving 95.0% degradation efficiency under optimized conditions.It exhibits excellent magnetic recyclability, avoiding the generation of iron sludge, which is a major drawback of traditional Fenton systems.. Mechanistic studies confirm that hydroxyl radicals generated through Fe2+/Fe3+ cycling are responsible for RhB mineralization to CO2 and H2O. The catalyst maintains stable performance over multiple cycles. This work offers a sustainable, environmentally friendly solution for dye wastewater treatment with efficient catalyst recovery and reduced secondary pollution.
